name: Cheering Team card
head: Pays its own suit
a: Each scored card sharing this card's suit gains extra points
b: Each scored card sharing this card's suit gains extra points, scaling with how many of them there are
c: Each scored card sharing this card's suit gains extra points, and this card gains the same again

name: Crowd glow
head: The crowd trickles in regardless
a: On a low-scoring turn, a small amount of fame arrives anyway
b: On a turn that scores nothing at all, a small amount of fame arrives anyway
c: On a low-scoring turn, fame arrives inversely to what you scored, so the worst turns pay most

name: Extra Point
head: Gain extra flat points on score (+10)
a: +10 points when this card scores
b: +2 points for each card in the line this card scores in
c: +10 points when this card scores, doubling each further time it scores in the same show

name: The Pose (Sandow)
head: Scores by standing still
a: Scores by being spotlit and doing nothing, rather than by melding
b: Scores by being spotlit and doing nothing, paying more the longer it holds the pose
c: Scores by being spotlit and doing nothing, and cannot score by melding at all

name: The Sparkler
head: Straight into the column score
a: When this card scores, +10 flat points go to its column's score
b: When this card scores, flat points equal to its rank go to its column's score
c: When this card scores, +10 flat points go to whichever of its lines scored lowest

name: Bootstraps
head: Paid by what is in your pocket
a: Gains a multiplier for every fixed amount of gold you hold
b: Gains a multiplier for every fixed amount of gold, and spending gold mid-show lowers it immediately
c: Gains a multiplier for gold held, capped, and converts overflow gold into flat points

name: Combo card
head: Scored cards keep the hand's value
a: During scoring, each card gains temporary points equal to the hand it scored in
b: During scoring, each card gains permanent points equal to the hand it scored in, once
c: During scoring, each card gains temporary points equal to the hand it scored in, doubled if it scored in two lines

name: Diamond type
head: Twice the score, twice the price
a: Doubles this card's score, and costs 3 more when traded at shops
b: Doubles this card's score, and it cannot be sold at all
c: Doubles this card's score, and every other card of its suit costs more at shops

name: More Poker card
head: Poker hands pay double
a: Poker hands score double
b: Poker hands score double, but only the highest hand of each placement
c: Poker hands score double, and non-poker melds score nothing

name: Noble Family card
head: Face cards feed each other
a: Each scored face card raises the points of the next scored face card by 1
b: Each scored face card raises the next one by 1, and the chain resets at the end of each placement
c: Each scored face card raises the next by 1, with no reset, so the chain runs the whole show

name: Hoop tower
head: Same suit, stacked hoops
a: Consecutive same-suit cards in a line multiply their score together
b: Consecutive same-suit cards in a line multiply their score, and the multiplier grows with run length
c: Consecutive same-suit cards in a line multiply their score, counting across grid boundaries at the same row

name: Joker Stencil
head: Paid by the room you left
a: Gains a multiplier for every empty skill slot you are carrying
b: Gains a multiplier for every empty cell on the grid at scoring
c: Gains a multiplier for every empty skill slot, doubled if every slot but its own is empty

name: Pagliacci
head: Gains bonus multiplier while this card carries any debuff or negative status
a: Gains a multiplier while carrying any debuff or negative status
b: Gains a multiplier per debuff or negative status it carries, stacking
c: Gains a multiplier per debuffed card anywhere in its grid, whether or not it is one of them

name: Searing Knife
head: When scored, its column pays 3x this placement but is locked (no placement or grabs) for the next 2 turns
a: When this card scores, its column pays triple this placement and is locked against placement and grabs for two turns
b: When this card scores, its column pays triple this placement and is locked for the rest of the show
c: When this card scores, its column pays triple, and the column to each side is locked for one turn

name: Swashbuckler
head: Paid by what your collection is worth
a: Adds the total sell value of your other cards to the multiplier
b: Adds the total sell value of your other cards to the multiplier, and selling any of them lowers it at once
c: Adds the sell value of your single most valuable other card, doubled

name: The Advance Campaign
head: Cue before a show: spend N Gold tokens to multiply that show's fame payout by 1 + N/10
a: Cue before a show: spend N gold to multiply that show's payout by 1 + N/10
b: Cue before a show: spend all your gold to multiply that show's payout by 1 + gold/10, capped at triple
c: Cue before a show: spend N gold to multiply the payout by 1 + N/10, but the next show's goal rises by the same fraction

name: The Kecak Chorus
head: Paid by the low cards on the board
a: When any meld scores, gains a multiplier per rank-1 card on the board
b: When any meld scores, gains a multiplier per card on the board below rank 4
c: When any meld scores, gains a multiplier per card on the board whose rank is lower than this card's

name: The Wall of Death
head: Both neighbours pay, and both pay for it
a: Both adjacent columns gain a multiplier, and every card in them takes an Exhausted debuff at show end
b: Both adjacent columns gain a multiplier, and one random card in each is Exhausted at show end
c: Both adjacent columns gain a multiplier scaling with how many cards are in them, and all of those cards are Exhausted at show end

name: Abstract Card
head: Raises the score to a power
a: Raises the placement's multiplier to a power rather than adding or multiplying, with a chance of being destroyed each show
b: Raises the placement's multiplier to a power, with no destruction risk but a very small exponent
c: Raises the multiplier to a power that grows the longer this card survives, with a rising chance of destruction

name: Breaking Infinity
head: The ceiling itself becomes a thing you remove
a: Score is capped until an effect removes the cap, after which higher operators become available
b: Score is capped until an effect removes the cap; removing it also raises every goal to match
c: Score is capped, and each cap broken permanently unlocks the next operator tier for the rest of the run

name: Critical Deck
head: A coin flip on the exponent
a: After each placement, a small chance the multiplier is squared, and a smaller chance it is square-rooted
b: After each placement, a small chance the multiplier is squared, with no downside
c: After each placement, the multiplier is raised to a random power between a half and two

name: The Long Shot
head: After the Cryptid mod's Googol Play Card: a tiny chance at an absurd number
a: A small chance per Entrance refill of an enormous multiplier, and nothing otherwise
b: A small chance per Entrance refill of an enormous multiplier, with a modest one the rest of the time
c: A small chance of an enormous multiplier, and the chance improves each placement it fails

name: Double Trigger
head: All of this card's effects trigger twice, once per scoring pass
a: All of this card's effects trigger twice
b: All of this card's effects trigger twice, but only on the first line it completes each show
c: This card's effects trigger once more for each line it belongs to, so a card scoring in a row and a column fires three times

name: Echoing Trigger
head: All triggers on the grid repeat once, per card, per scoring pass
a: Every card's triggers on the grid repeat once per scoring pass
b: Every card's triggers in this card's own row and column repeat once
c: Every card's triggers on the grid repeat once, and this card is destroyed at the end of the show

name: Exposed
head: Retriggers the plain ones, kills the faces
a: Retriggers every scoring non-face card twice more, and debuffs every face card
b: Retriggers every scoring non-face card twice more, and face cards simply score normally
c: Retriggers whichever card type is rarer on the board, and debuffs the commoner one

name: Hanging Chad
head: Re-fires whichever card went first
a: Retriggers the first card of a scoring line two extra times
b: Retriggers the first and last card of a scoring line one extra time each
c: Retriggers the first card of every scoring line once, across every line that scores

name: Seltzer
head: Retriggers everything, then burns out
a: Retriggers every scoring card for the next ten placements, then is destroyed
b: Retriggers every scoring card for the next three scoring passes, then is destroyed
c: Retriggers every scoring card until it has retriggered a fixed total number of times, then is destroyed

name: The Aerialist
head: Once per placement, re-scores the topmost meld, but is destroyed permanently if her column ever fails to score
a: Once per placement, re-scores the highest meld; destroyed for good if her column ever fails to score
b: Once per placement, re-scores the highest meld; destroyed for good the first time her column fails to score twice running
c: Once per placement, re-scores any meld you choose; each use carries a 1-in-8 chance of destroying her

name: The Clock Hang
head: May be placed half-off the grid past the last column; while hanging it is double-spotlit (its skill fires twice), but any board-shift effect discards it
a: May be placed half off the grid past the last column; while hanging its skill fires twice, and any board-shift effect discards it
b: May be placed half off the grid past any edge; while hanging its skill fires twice and it cannot be part of any meld
c: May be placed half off the grid; while hanging it fires twice, and it falls off at the end of the placement unless a line scored

name: The Drone Swarm
head: Cue, once per show: re-triggers any formation bonus already scored this run, paying it again without needing the cards
a: Cue, once per show: re-trigger any formation bonus already scored this run, paying it again without needing the cards
b: Cue, once per show: re-trigger any formation bonus already scored this show, paying it again
c: Cue, once per show: re-trigger the highest-paying formation bonus of the run, at half value

name: The Encore
head: If this card's skill triggered this show, there is a seeded 50% chance it triggers once more at show end
a: If this card's skill triggered this show, a 50% chance it triggers once more at show end
b: If this card's skill triggered this show, it triggers once more at show end, guaranteed
c: If this card's skill triggered this show, a 50% chance per trigger that it fires again at show end, capped at three

name: The Fanchant
head: After all scoring resolves, each meld that raised the show's combo pays again at 25%
a: After all scoring resolves, every meld that raised the show's combo pays again at 25%
b: After all scoring resolves, the single highest meld that raised the combo pays again in full
c: After all scoring resolves, every meld that raised the combo pays again at 10% per distinct class involved

name: The Groundhog
head: Cue, once per show: replay the previous placement's entire effect sequence against the current board, same effects and order, targets resolved fresh
a: Cue, once per show: replay the previous placement's whole effect sequence against the current board, targets resolved fresh
b: Cue, once per show: replay only the effects of the previous placement that scored
c: Cue, once per show: replay the previous placement's effect sequence twice, and this card is discarded afterwards

name: The Seesaw
head: After the Cryptid mod's Broken Sync Catalyst: trades chips for mult
a: Swaps a tenth of the line's flat points into its multiplier
b: Swaps a tenth of the flat points into multiplier, or the reverse, whichever scores higher
c: Swaps a proportion you choose, up to a half, between flat points and multiplier

name: The Accountant
head: At payout, before row x column multiplication, shift up to 20% of the larger axis total onto the smaller, costing 2 combo to invoke
a: At payout, before row times column, shift up to 20% of the larger axis total onto the smaller, at a cost of 2 combo
b: At payout, shift up to 20% of the larger axis total onto the smaller, free of charge
c: At payout, the row and column totals are averaged and both set to that average, at a cost of 2 combo

name: The Credit Line
head: Points earned here are paid somewhere else
a: Cue: name another line; for the rest of the placement, everything this line scores is paid into that one instead
b: Cue: name another line; half of what this line scores is paid into that one, and the other half scores normally
c: Cue: name another card; everything this line scores is banked onto that card and pays out when it next scores

name: The Running Total
head: Every line shows what it is worth as you build
a: Each line's accumulating score is visible at its end while you build, not only when it completes
b: Each line's accumulating score is visible, and effects may read it mid-build
c: Each line's total is visible, and a line may be cashed out early at a discount

name: The Giant Killer
head: After the Cryptid mod's AP Joker: saves itself for the boss
a: Scores a large multiplier against bosses only
b: Scores a large multiplier against bosses, and nothing at all otherwise
c: Scores a multiplier that scales with how many bosses you have already beaten this run

name: Card Sharp
head: Paid for repeating yourself
a: Gains a multiplier if the hand it scores in has already been scored this show
b: Gains a multiplier if the hand it scores in has already been scored this placement
c: Gains a multiplier that grows each time the same hand type is scored again in a show

name: Facile
head: Rewards a board you have barely used
a: Raises the multiplier to a power if the scoring cards have been scored few times this run
b: Raises the multiplier to a power if none of the scoring cards has ever scored before
c: Raises the multiplier to a power scaling inversely with how often the scoring cards have been used

name: Flash
head: The first time this card would score each show it scores triple; every later score that show is zero
a: The first time this card scores each show it scores triple; every later score that show is zero
b: The first time this card scores each show it scores triple; every later score that show is halved
c: The first line this card completes each show scores triple for every card in it, and this card cannot score again that show

name: Green Seal
head: Pays for the card that did not score
a: Creates a bonus card whenever a placed card fails to score
b: Creates a bonus card whenever a placed card fails to score, capped once per Entrance refill
c: Creates a bonus card for each card in a completed line that contributed nothing to the hand

name: Lot Lice
head: Town rule: the show's first placement scores 0 fame
a: Town rule: the show's first placement scores nothing
b: Town rule: the first line completed in each grid scores nothing
c: Town rule: the show's first placement scores nothing and the second scores double

name: Non-scoring bonus card
head: Paid for not being used
a: If this card is not part of any scoring hand, it gives 10 points
b: If this card is not part of any scoring hand, it gives points equal to its rank
c: If this card is not part of any scoring hand this Entrance refill, it gives 10 points and gains +1 rank

name: Obelisk
head: Paid for not repeating yourself
a: Gains a permanent multiplier for each consecutive placement played without scoring your most-played hand, resetting when you do
b: Gains a permanent multiplier per Entrance refill played without repeating any hand you have already scored this show
c: Gains a permanent multiplier per consecutive placement without your most-played hand, and keeps half of it through the reset

name: Supernova
head: Paid by how often you have played it
a: Adds to the multiplier the number of times the scoring hand type has been played this run
b: Adds the number of times the scoring hand type has been played this show only
c: Adds the number of times the hand has been played this run, and doubles if it is your most-played

name: The Chromatic
head: Negative on alternate placements
a: Applies a negative multiplier on every odd-numbered placement and a positive one on every even
b: Applies a negative multiplier on every odd placement, and nothing on the even ones
c: Applies a negative multiplier on alternating placements, and you choose which placement it starts on

name: The Deficit Rank
head: A number below zero
a: This rank subtracts its value from the line it is in, and adds one to the combo for every card it drags down
b: This rank subtracts its value from the line, and doubles the line if the line still scores above target
c: This rank subtracts its value, and is the only rank that may be stacked on anything

name: The Eyesore
head: A card you must place that hurts what surrounds it
a: This card must be placed like any other and subtracts from every neighbour, but is worth a great deal itself
b: This card subtracts from every neighbour, and pays out fully only if it ends the show with no neighbours at all
c: This card subtracts from neighbours, and converts everything it subtracted into its own score when its line completes

name: The Negative
head: Props under it subtract score and add combo. (line 821)
a: A card at negative rank spawns props that subtract score instead of adding it, and each one still raises the show's combo
b: A card at negative rank spawns props that subtract score, and they raise the combo by double
c: A card at negative rank subtracts score itself and raises the combo, but its props behave normally

name: Grock's Instrument
head: Each placement this card would score, it instead hops one column away and banks the points; when it has no legal hop left, it scores everything banked at once
a: Each placement it would score, it hops one column instead and banks the points; when it cannot hop, it pays out the whole bank
b: Each placement it would score, it banks the points instead; cue at any time to pay the bank out
c: Each placement it would score, it hops one column and banks double; if another effect ever moves it, the bank is lost

name: Mid-show instant tips
head: Tips paid on the spot
a: A meld that scores over a threshold also pays gold on the spot
b: A meld over a threshold pays gold on the spot instead of its points, at a worse exchange rate
c: A meld over a threshold offers gold on the spot, and you choose per meld whether to take the gold or keep the points

name: Style flourish (Mie)
head: Holds the pose for the applause
a: A scored meld holds on screen a beat longer and pays extra tips
b: A scored meld holds a beat longer and pays extra tips, and holding two in a row pays more
c: You may choose to hold a meld, delaying the next placement by a turn in exchange for extra tips

name: Suspended Overhead
head: Paid for now, delivered later
a: Consumable: name any effect and a number of Entrance refills; it fires for free that many placements from now, at a strength that grows with the wait
b: Consumable: name any effect; it fires three scoring passes from now at triple strength, and cannot be cancelled
c: Consumable: name any effect and a number of Entrance refills; it fires then, and every placement of waiting also adds one to the combo

name: The Hunger Artist
head: Gains bonus points for every consecutive show it stays in the deck unplayed; when finally played and scored, pays it all at once and resets to zero
a: Gains bonus points for each consecutive show it stays in the deck unplayed, pays it all when scored, then resets to zero
b: Gains bonus points for each consecutive show unplayed, pays out when scored, and keeps half the total through the reset
c: Gains bonus points per show unplayed with no cap, but is destroyed if it goes ten shows unplayed

name: The Instrument
head: Keeps missing until it does not
a: Moves away rather than scoring each time it would score; when finally played it scores everything it dodged
b: Moves away rather than scoring, banking each dodge; cue at any time to cash the bank
c: Moves away rather than scoring, and each dodge raises what it eventually pays by more than the last

name: Clears Feed A Resource
head: A completed line pays fuel, not points
a: A completed line pays a resource rather than score, and the resource is what powers your effects
b: A completed line pays both score and a resource, at a reduced rate for each
c: A completed line pays a resource whose kind is set by the line's dominant suit

name: The Cloakroom
head: Points become charges
a: Cue when a placement finishes resolving: convert this placement payout into charges at a fixed rate, spendable on any cued effect
b: Cue when a placement finishes resolving: convert half this placement payout into charges, keeping the other half as score
c: Every placement, the score above target is converted into charges automatically rather than banked

name: The Hat Line
head: At show end, cue to convert the placement's unused combo above the payout into Gold tokens instead of losing it
a: At show end, cue to turn the placement's unused combo into gold tokens rather than lose it
b: At show end, unused combo automatically becomes gold tokens
c: At show end, cue to turn unused combo into gold, or into a rank increase on one card, your choice

name: The Lecture
head: Turns flavour into fame
a: Converts a card's flavour text into fame, once per card
b: Converts a card's flavour text into fame each time that card scores
c: Converts flavour text into fame, paying more for cards you have never scored before

name: Lemon Trophy
head: The multiplier cannot outgrow the points
a: The multiplier can never exceed the flat points it is multiplying
b: The multiplier can never exceed the flat points, and any excess converts to flat points instead
c: The multiplier and the flat points are both clamped to whichever is lower, then both doubled

name: The Round Number
head: Every line comes out tidy
a: Every line score is rounded to the nearest ten, up or down as the arithmetic falls
b: Every line score is rounded up to the next ten
c: Every line score is rounded down to the previous ten, and the remainder is banked and paid at show end

name: The Softcap
head: Growth slows rather than stopping
a: Past a threshold, additional score is added at a reducing rate rather than being capped outright
b: Past a threshold, additional score is added at a reducing rate, and a second threshold caps it hard
c: Past a threshold, additional multiplier converts to flat points instead of being reduced

name: The Tax
head: A ceiling on each placement
a: Boss: each placement's score is capped at a fraction of the goal, so no single act can win it
b: Boss: each placement's score is capped at a fraction of the goal, and the cap rises each placement
c: Boss: each placement's score is capped, and anything above the cap is banked for the next placement

name: Diversity-based scoring instead of combo
head: Variety as its own axis
a: The placement's payout scales with how many distinct suits and types are on the board, alongside the combo
b: The placement's payout scales with distinct suits and types instead of the combo, replacing it
c: The placement's payout scales with distinct suits and types, and the combo scales with distinct effects, multiplying together

name: Flea Circus
head: When scored, counts as five rank-1 cards for combo-counting purposes (not points)
a: When scored, counts as five separate triggers for the combo without adding any points
b: When scored, counts as one extra trigger for each card in its line, without adding points
c: When scored, counts as five separate triggers, and each one can be amplified by retrigger effects

name: Grand Spec
head: If every column has scored a meld this show, doubles the show's combo multiplier
a: If every column has scored a meld this show, the show's combo doubles
b: If every row and every column has scored a meld this show, the show's combo triples
c: The placement's combo is multiplied by the number of columns that scored a meld

name: Presentation
head: While spotlit, each time a placed card's rank is higher than the last card placed, gain +1 combo for the placement
a: While spotlit, each placed card of higher rank than the last placed card adds +1 combo for the placement
b: While spotlit, an unbroken ascending sequence of placements adds +1 combo per placement, and any drop resets it
c: While spotlit, each placed card of higher rank than the last adds +1 combo, and each lower one removes 1

name: Spangle
head: The first time this card is part of any scored meld each placement, it adds +1 to the show's combo
a: The first time this card is part of a scored meld each placement, it adds +1 to the show's combo
b: Every time this card is part of a scored meld, it adds +1 to the show's combo
c: The first time this card is part of a scored meld each placement, it adds +1 combo for each distinct suit in that meld

name: The Calliope
head: Gains +1 combo for every different class that scored this placement
a: Gains +1 combo for every different class that scored this placement
b: Gains +1 combo for every different class on the grid, whether or not it scored
c: Gains +1 combo per class that scored, and double that if every class on the grid scored

name: The Dramaturg
head: Rewrites one card's combo identity so each of its triggers registers a fresh combo key every time this placement, instead of only on first activation
a: Rewrites one card's combo identity so each of its triggers registers a fresh combo key this placement, instead of only the first
b: Rewrites every card's combo identity so each trigger registers a fresh combo key this placement
c: Rewrites one card's combo identity permanently, so its triggers always register fresh combo keys

name: The Exchange Rate
head: When a placement finishes resolving, cue to convert unused combo above 3 into flat points at a fixed rate, or spend points to pre-register +1 combo for the next placement
a: When a placement finishes resolving, cue to turn unused combo above 3 into flat points at a fixed rate, or spend points to pre-register +1 combo for the next placement
b: When a placement finishes resolving, unused combo above 3 automatically becomes flat points at a fixed rate
c: When a placement finishes resolving, cue to bank unused combo, carrying it into the next placement instead of converting it

name: The Forty-Two
head: When a row's score plus its column's score totals exactly 42, the show's combo gains +3
a: When a row's score plus its column's score totals exactly 42, the show's combo gains +3
b: When a row's score plus its column's score totals a specific number reseeded each run, the show's combo gains +3
c: When a row's score and its column's score are exactly equal, the show's combo gains +3

name: The System
head: Paid by the combo, and shy of inspection
a: After each placement, gains bonus points scaled to that placement's combo; any inspection effect halves the bonus permanently
b: After each placement, gains bonus points scaled to that placement's combo, with no downside
c: After each placement, gains bonus points scaled to the combo; being inspected halves it, and it recovers one step per show uninspected

name: The Menagerie
head: After the Cryptid mod's Zooble: paid for rank variety, unless it is a run
a: Gains a multiplier per distinct rank in the scoring line, unless that line is a straight
b: Gains a multiplier per distinct rank in the scoring line, always
c: Gains a multiplier per distinct rank and per distinct suit in the scoring line, unless it is a straight or a flush

name: Drumroll
head: The last meld scored each placement gets a bonus multiplier
a: The last line scored in each placement pays double
b: The highest-scoring line of each placement pays double
c: The lowest-scoring line of each placement is re-scored as though it were the highest

name: The First Juggler
head: The oldest trick there is
a: Scores a bonus for completing the simplest possible meld
b: Scores a bonus for completing the simplest meld, growing each time you do it again
c: Scores a bonus for completing the lowest-scoring meld of the placement, so the worst hand pays

name: The Odd Couple
head: The extremes of the row pay each other
a: The lowest- and highest-ranked cards in this card's row pay each other bonus points when the row scores
b: The lowest- and highest-ranked cards in this card's row pay each other bonus points scaling with the gap between them
c: In every line this card belongs to, the highest and lowest cards pay each other bonus points

name: The Scoop
head: Taking every line pays more than the sum
a: Scoring every line of a grid pays a large bonus on top of the individual lines
b: Scoring every line of every grid pays a large bonus
c: Scoring every line pays a bonus scaling with how many lines the grid has

name: Positional Royalties
head: The same hand is worth more where it is harder
a: A hand pays more in lines where the ordering rule makes it harder to achieve, so a flush in the middle beats a flush at the back
b: A hand pays more the closer its line is to the centre of the grid, whatever the ordering rule
c: Each line carries a printed multiplier fixed at show start, so which line you build a hand in is a decision

name: The Comeback
head: Stronger the further behind you are
a: Scores a multiplier scaling with how far below the goal you currently are
b: Scores a multiplier scaling with how far behind you are, and nothing once you are ahead
c: Scores a multiplier scaling with how far behind you are at the START of each placement, so catching up early costs you

name: The Front-Runner
head: Stronger once you are already winning
a: Scores a multiplier once you are past the goal, scaling with the overshoot
b: Scores a multiplier once you are past halfway to the goal, fixed
c: Scores a multiplier past the goal, and the overshoot it earns is banked as fame rather than points

name: The Handicapper
head: The board reads the scoreboard
a: Every effect that scales reads the gap to the goal as its scaling input
b: Every effect that scales reads the gap to the goal, but only in the last placement before you press End
c: Falling far enough behind switches the whole board to a stronger set of defaults for that show

name: The Photo Finish
head: Pays for landing exactly
a: Pays an enormous bonus for finishing a show within a hair of the goal, and nothing for overshooting
b: Pays a bonus scaling inversely with how far past the goal you finish
c: Pays an enormous bonus for finishing exactly on the goal, to the point

name: Adjacency-required marriage melds
head: Melds that need true adjacency
a: Marriage melds require the cards to be exactly adjacent, not merely in the same line
b: Marriage melds require exact adjacency, and diagonal adjacency counts double
c: Marriage melds require exact adjacency, and any two adjacent cards that pair score as a meld of their own

name: Badugi
head: A hand made entirely of differences
a: A new hand: four cards with no two sharing a rank and no two sharing a suit
b: A new hand: a full line with no two cards sharing a rank and no two sharing a suit
c: A new hand: four cards sharing neither rank nor suit, ranked by how low its highest card is

name: Beehive four-of-a-kind removal
head: Take four of a kind off the board
a: Any four of a kind on the grid may be removed together for a bonus
b: Any four of a kind on the grid may be removed together, scoring as a meld and freeing the cells
c: Any four of a kind may be removed, and doing so pulls four new cards into the Entrance

name: Blackjack bust rule
head: Twenty-one exactly
a: A line whose ranks total exactly 21 scores as its own meld; going over scores nothing
b: A line whose ranks total exactly 21 scores as its own meld, alongside its poker hand
c: A line totalling exactly 21 scores as a meld, and the closest line to 21 without going over scores as well

name: Bulwark
head: A hand made of rankless cards
a: A new hand: five rankless, suitless cards score as a large flat meld
b: A new hand: five rankless cards score as a large meld, and each blank card in your deck raises it
c: A new hand: any five cards that share no rank and no suit at all score as a meld

name: Clusterfuck/Cluster
head: A hand made of nothing matching
a: A new hand: eight or more cards containing no pair, no flush and no straight score as a large meld
b: A new hand: a full line containing no pair, flush or straight scores as a large meld
c: A new hand: a line where no two cards share a rank or a suit scores as a large meld

name: Cribbage phase-1 stack-to-31
head: Build to thirty-one
a: A running total builds across placements up to 31, scoring at exact totals along the way
b: A running total builds across placements up to 31; hitting exactly 31 scores, and overshooting resets it
c: A running total builds per line rather than per show, scoring at exact totals along the way

name: Cribbage-style scoring
head: Cribbage counting
a: Face cards count as 10; score 2 per 15-sum, 2 per 31-sum, 2 per pair, 6 per triple, 12 per quad, and 3 to 7 for runs
b: Face cards count as 10, and only the 15-sums score, at 2 each
c: Face cards count as 10; the cribbage counts score alongside poker hands rather than replacing them

name: Flower Pot
head: One of every suit
a: A line containing one card of every suit scores as its own meld
b: A line containing one card of every suit scores as its own meld, ranked above a flush
c: A line containing one card of every suit scores as a meld, and the more suits the game has the more it pays

name: Mahjong hand check across ring
head: Mahjong hands across a grid
a: A grid holding four triplets and a pair across its rows or its columns scores as a mahjong hand
b: A grid holding four triplets and a pair scores as a mahjong hand, replacing its poker scoring
c: Any grid satisfying one of a set of named mahjong hands scores that hand as a bonus meld

name: The Whole Company
head: After the Cryptid mod's Many Have Lost Their Minds Comprehending This Joker: a hand made of the entire deck
a: A hand consisting of every card in the deck at once scores an absurd amount
b: A hand consisting of every card on the board at once scores an absurd amount
c: A hand consisting of every card in the deck scores absurdly, and is the only way to win that show

name: None
head: A hand of no cards at all
a: At show end, each empty line counts as its own meld, worth nothing but registering as a hand
b: At show end, an empty line scores as its own meld, and pays out if it is the only line of its grid left empty
c: At show end, every empty line counts as a hand, and every empty line on the board raises the show's combo

name: Pyramid entrance-match removal
head: Match the Entrance card to clear
a: A grid card may be removed if it matches the current Entrance card by one rank up or down
b: A grid card may be removed if it matches the current Entrance card in rank or in suit
c: A grid card may be removed if it matches the Entrance card by rank; doing so scores both

name: Pyramid pair-removal rule
head: Pairs that add to thirteen
a: Two cards whose ranks sum to 13 may be removed together for a bonus
b: Two cards whose ranks sum to 13, or which match, may be removed together for a bonus
c: Two cards summing to 13 may be removed and score as a meld, freeing their cells

name: Rummy meld types
head: Runs and sets, rummy style
a: Three or more same-suit consecutive cards, or three to four of the same rank, score as melds
b: Three or more same-suit consecutive cards score as melds, but same-rank sets do not
c: Rummy melds score alongside poker hands rather than replacing them

name: Sets-of-3 rank boost
head: After the board game Risk: sets of three do something
a: Any three matching cards on the grid trigger an effect, such as raising their ranks
b: Any three matching cards on the grid may be cashed in for an effect you choose from three
c: Any three matching cards trigger an effect, and the effect improves the more sets you have cashed

name: The Fifteen
head: This card also melds with any adjacent neighbors whose ranks sum to 15 with it
a: Also melds with any adjacent neighbours whose ranks sum to 15 with it
b: Also melds with any set of cards in its line whose ranks sum to 15 with it
c: Also melds with any adjacent neighbours whose ranks sum to a target that changes each show

name: The Pure Hand
head: A whole grid in one suit
a: A new hand: an entire grid of one suit scores enormously
b: A new hand: an entire grid of one suit, or of one suit plus one named exception, scores enormously
c: A new hand: an entire grid using only two suits scores enormously, and one suit scores more again

name: The Triple
head: A short run pays out
a: If this card completes a run of exactly three cards assembled that turn, that run scores triple
b: If this card completes a run of exactly three cards, that run scores triple; runs of four or more score nothing
c: Any run of exactly three cards scores as a full meld in its own right, whoever completes it

name: Ultimate Pair
head: Two pairs, each in its own suit
a: A new hand: two two-pairs, each one entirely within a single suit, across two suits
b: A new hand: two two-pairs each within a single suit, and it outranks a full house
c: A new hand: any two melds each confined to one suit, across two different suits

name: Four Fingers
head: Four is enough
a: Flushes and straights may be completed with four cards instead of five
b: Flushes may be completed with four cards; straights still need five
c: Any meld may be completed one card short, at three quarters of its value

name: Paved Joker
head: Blanks plug the gaps
a: Rankless cards may fill single-rank gaps in straights and flushes
b: Rankless cards may fill any number of gaps in straights and flushes
c: Rankless cards may fill gaps, and each one used raises the line's score

name: Shortcut
head: Straights can skip
a: Straights may be completed with gaps of one rank
b: Straights may be completed with gaps of one rank, at three quarters value
c: Straights may be completed with gaps of one rank, and gaps of two if the line is otherwise a flush

name: The Red Wagon
head: Money counts as anything
a: While spotlit, every Gold token in the deck counts as a wildcard toward any column run
b: While spotlit, every Gold token on the grid counts as a wildcard toward any line at all
c: While spotlit, every token card of any kind counts as a wildcard toward any line

name: The Spider Rule
head: Build loosely, but only clear strictly
a: Stacks build one rank down regardless of suit, but a run is only removed and scored when it is entirely one suit
b: Stacks build one rank down regardless of suit, and a run of any suits may be removed and scored at a lower rate
c: Stacks build loosely, and a same-suit run scores double what a mixed one does

name: Fouling
head: Lines must be ordered by strength, or nothing scores
a: Each line must score at least as high as the line above it; break the order and the whole grid scores nothing
b: Each line must beat the line above it; break the order and only the offending line scores nothing
c: Each line must beat the line above it; break the order and the grid scores, but pays a penalty larger than the best line was worth

name: The Blacklisted Hand
head: The hand you leaned on stops paying
a: The hand type you scored most in one placement scores nothing in the next
b: The hand type you scored most in one placement scores half in the next, and full again the placement after
c: Each hand type may be scored only twice per show; the third time it pays nothing

name: The Eye
head: Boss: no hand type twice
a: Boss: no hand type may be scored more than once in a show
b: Boss: no hand type may be scored more than once per Entrance refill
c: Boss: no hand type may be scored twice in a row, but may return later

name: The Mouth
head: Boss: only one hand type all show
a: Boss: only one hand type may be scored for the whole show, fixed by the first line you complete
b: Boss: only one hand type may be scored, named by the boss before the show starts
c: Boss: only one hand type may be scored, and you choose it before seeing your Entrance

name: Calculation Solitaire looping stacks
head: Piles that count by their own number
a: Foundation stacks build in increments of their own base number, wrapping past King
b: Foundation stacks build in increments of their base number without wrapping, ending at King
c: Each column builds in increments of its own index, so column 3 stacks in threes

name: Fan Tan foundation-build rule
head: Sevens are the foundation
a: Sevens are foundations, extended only by a same-suit card one rank higher or lower
b: Sevens are foundations extended by any suit, one rank higher or lower
c: The first time this card is spotlit, name a rank; it becomes the foundation for the rest of the run, extended by same-suit neighbours in rank

name: Foundations From Both Ends
head: Two foundations growing toward each other
a: A line may be built from its low end upward or its high end downward, and it scores when the two meet
b: A line is built from both ends toward the middle, and the card that closes the gap scores double
c: Two foundations run in opposite directions and a card may join either; completing both pays enormously

name: Spite and Malice communal foundations
head: Communal foundations, kings wild
a: Up to four shared foundations build from 1 to Queen regardless of suit, with kings wild; a completed foundation is set aside and replaced
b: Up to four shared foundations build from 1 to Queen regardless of suit, and completing one scores it as a meld
c: One shared foundation builds 1 to Queen with kings wild, and completing it scores the whole run at once

name: The Forged Ace
head: This card has an enormous rank that counts as two Aces in melds; if any inspection effect examines it, it is destroyed and the show's fame payout is voided
a: An enormous rank counting as two Aces in melds; any inspection effect that examines it destroys it and voids the show's payout
b: An enormous rank counting as two Aces in melds; being inspected destroys it but the payout survives
c: An enormous rank counting as two Aces; each show it survives without being inspected, its rank grows

name: Canasta rank-based wildcards
head: One rank is wild. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Marks of the wild rank count as matched by any card placed on them
a: The first time this card is spotlit, name a rank; it acts as a wildcard in every meld for the rest of the run
b: One rank acts as a wildcard, and which rank it is changes each show
c: One rank acts as a wildcard, and using it in a meld consumes it permanently

name: Crazy Eights wild-suit rule
head: One rank changes the suit
a: One rank is wild and names a suit; the next card placed that is not that suit scores nothing in the lines it completes — **level 2:** An eight on a mark it matches names the suit, and the constraint never applies to cards placed on marks they match
b: One rank is wild and names a suit; until another is played, a card placed that is not that suit scores nothing in the lines it completes — **level 2:** An eight on a mark it matches names the suit, and the constraint never applies to cards placed on marks they match
c: One rank is wild and names the suit for its whole line, retroactively — **level 2:** An eight placed on a mark it matches names the suit for every line through it

name: The Smudge
head: After Balatro's Smeared Joker: two suits count as one. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The paired suits also count as one suit when matching suit marks
a: Two named pairs of suits each count as a single suit for melds
b: Two named pairs of suits count as one for melds but stay distinct for stacking
c: All suits count as one suit for flushes only, making flushes trivial and everything else unchanged

name: The Salt
head: Matches its own kind, or anything, and matches any rank mark. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On its mark the choice is made per line, so it can be its own kind in its row and a wild in its column
a: This card melds either with another of its own kind or with any card at all, your choice at scoring
b: This card melds with any card at all, but never with another of its own kind
c: This card melds with anything, and every one used in a meld makes the next one in the deck stricter

name: Burnt Joker
head: Levels up a hand type. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may raise the hand type of your choice instead ⚑ *pair review: (a) keyed on a discarded hand type, and a discard here is a card, not a hand*
a: Permanently raises the level of the first hand type scored through its cell each show
b: Permanently raises the level of the first hand type scored each show
c: Raises the level of the hand type you scored least this show, at show end

name: The Arm
head: Boss: your hands get worse
a: Boss: permanently lowers the level of whichever hand type you score
b: Boss: lowers the level of the hand type you score for this show only
c: Boss: permanently lowers the level of your most-played hand type, once

name: The Practised Hand
head: Hands you play often get better, and hands you neglect rot. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Hands scored through its cell never rot ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0048, which you wrote: hands you play more pay more*
a: Each hand type levels up one step each time it is scored, and loses a level each show it is never scored
b: Each hand type levels up one step each time it is scored, and levels never decay
c: Each hand type levels one step per show in which it was scored at all, however many times

name: Universum
head: Levelling up is worth more. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each level-up also adds +1 to the combo ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q1545 (Rising Tide): every hand gains when one levels*
a: When a hand type levels up, it gains multiplier and flat points rather than flat points alone
b: When a hand type levels up, it gains double what it normally would
c: A level-up through its cell also raises the hand type of every other line that scored that placement

name: Lowball
head: The worst hand pays the most. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell pay on both ladders
a: Lines through its cell pay on the inverted ladder: a high card pays as a straight flush, a pair as five of a kind, and so on, down to a straight flush paying as a high card
b: Every line on its grid pays on the inverted ladder
c: One line per grid, named at show start, pays on the inverted ladder; the rest score normally

name: Splash
head: The cards a hand leaves out are a hand of their own. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The leftover hand through its cell pays into the special bucket
a: In a line through its cell, the cards the hand does not use score as a second hand, added to the first
b: In every line on its grid, the leftover cards score as a second hand
c: The leftover cards score as a second hand, and when it is the same type as the first the two count as copies of one hand

name: Dead Man's Hand
head: Scoring two pair, Aces over Eights, in one row pays a jackpot and triggers a map event. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell that are one card short of the hidden meld light up
a: A hidden meld: two pair, aces over eights, in one line pays a large bonus the first time it is found each run
b: A hidden meld reseeded each run; every line that scores tells you how many of its cards belong to the hidden meld, so you can work it out
c: A hidden meld: two pair, aces over eights, pays a large bonus every time and permanently unlocks a card the first time it is found

name: Sword Swallower
head: A column that is one perfect descending run from top to floor pays a large bonus and mints a Knife-suit card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A fourth perfect column in one show pays all four again ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q1493 (a descending stack headed by a king); it absorbs Q0141*
a: A column that is one perfect descending run from top to floor pays a large bonus and mints a Knives card
b: Any line that is one perfect run in either direction pays a large bonus and mints a card of that line's dominant suit
c: A column that is a perfect descending run pays a large bonus, and finding it once reveals what it does permanently

name: The Secret
head: A condition nobody announced. **Level 2, on its own mark:** When it flips, it fires once more for each card in its lines that sits on its own matching mark
a: Place this card face down naming a condition; when the condition is met the card flips and its effect fires unprompted
b: Place this card face down; the condition is drawn at random from a known list, and it flips when met
c: Place this card face down naming a condition; if the show ends without the condition being met, the card is destroyed and pays nothing

name: The Three Rings
head: Three full lines in one placement
a: Scoring three separate full five-card hands in one placement permanently unlocks a new skill for the rest of the run — **level 2:** Lines that score through its cell count twice toward the three
b: Scoring three separate full five-card hands in one placement pays a large bonus, every time — **level 2:** Lines that score through its cell count twice toward the three
c: Completing a row, a column and a diagonal with one placement permanently unlocks a new skill for the rest of the run — **level 2:** A height line through its cell counts as one of the three

name: The Episode Rules
head: This run is played under a different rulebook. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may rename one of its hands at the start of each show
a: The first time this card is spotlit, name three hand types as the only ones that score; every other completed line pays nothing, for the rest of the run
b: The first time this card is spotlit, name three hand types that score double, for the rest of the run; everything else scores normally
c: The first time this card is spotlit, name three hand types that score double and one that scores nothing, for the rest of the run

name: The Private Objective
head: A scoring goal only this run has. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It draws two objectives and keeps both ⚑ *pair review: (c) depends on a rival, which is its own unanswered question*
a: The first time this card is spotlit, draw a hidden scoring objective, revealed immediately, that pays alongside normal scoring for the rest of the run
b: The first time this card is spotlit, draw a scoring objective that stays hidden until the run ends
c: The first time this card is spotlit, draw three objectives and choose one; the others stay live for a rival

name: This Season's Trend
head: Certain abilities, not hands, pay extra this run. (line 835). **Level 2, on its own mark:** Abilities fired by cards sitting on marks they match count as trending
a: The first time this card is spotlit, name a few abilities as trending; they score extra whenever they fire, for the rest of the run
b: The first time this card is spotlit, name a few abilities as trending; the trend rotates every town
c: A few abilities trend at a time, and using a trending ability enough times makes it trend permanently for the rest of the run

name: Half Joker
head: Paid for playing short. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match do not count toward the grid's total
a: Scores a large multiplier if its line completes while the grid holds ten cards or fewer
b: Scores a large multiplier scaling with how few cards the grid holds when its line completes
c: Scores a large multiplier if the whole grid holds five cards or fewer when its line completes

name: Rank-merging meld rule
head: Longer lines pay disproportionately. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards stacked beneath a line's cards count toward its length ⚑ *pair review: does nothing unless another effect makes a line longer*
a: A line's points are multiplied by its length, doubling at five cards and rising with every card beyond five, where another effect makes a line longer
b: A line's points are multiplied by its length linearly, with no cap
c: A line's points are multiplied by its length, and lines longer than the grid pay a further bonus

name: The Six-Card Line
head: Lines are longer than the grid was built for. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A six-card line through its cell scores both of its five-card windows ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0030, which you wrote: a card past the edge makes six-card lines*
a: Lines are six cells long, so each grid row runs one cell into the grid beside it
b: Lines are six cells long, drawn only on grids that have been widened to six by an unlock
c: Lines may be five or six cells, and a six-card line scores as the best five plus a length bonus

name: Line Ledger
head: Turns line types on and off. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell always score, whichever line types are switched off
a: At show start choose one line kind; it pays double this show, and one other kind you name pays nothing
b: At show start, one line type is disabled at random and everything else scores double
c: Each Entrance refill, name one line kind; it pays double until the next refill

name: The Clearance Threshold
head: A line whose ranks add past a threshold scores and empties. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cells it empties are dealt fresh marks ⚑ *pair review: a running total is undefined; adding ranks is easy to do in your head (your Q0075)*
a: A line whose rank total passes a threshold scores and empties, freeing its cells
b: A line whose rank total passes a threshold scores and empties, and the threshold rises each time
c: A line whose rank total passes the threshold scores, and only the card that pushed it over is discarded

name: The Short Ring
head: Grants the short diagonals as lines, paying into the special bucket
a: The four four-card diagonals of a grid also score as lines — **level 2:** Short diagonals through its cell score an extra step
b: The four four-card diagonals score at half value — **level 2:** Short diagonals through its cell pay full value
c: One short diagonal per grid, chosen at show start, scores as a full line — **level 2:** It may choose a second short diagonal

name: The Border Line
head: The edge of the grid is a track of its own, paying into the special bucket. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A border line through its cell scores an extra step for each corner card sitting on a mark it matches
a: Any five consecutive cells along the grid border that turn a corner score as a line
b: The sixteen border cells score as one line when all are filled, paying at the best five within it
c: Any five consecutive border cells score as a line, and a line that turns a corner scores an extra step

name: The Knight Line
head: Five cells a knight apart, paying into the special bucket. **Level 2, on its own mark:** After a knight line through it scores, it may jump one knight move to an empty cell whose mark it matches
a: While this card is on the grid, any five cells connected by knight moves score as a line
b: While this card is on the grid, five cells connected by knight moves score as a line, and this card must be one of them
c: Cue once per Entrance refill: nominate five cells connected by knight moves; if all are filled they score as a line

name: The Puszta Five
head: In every column at once. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its cue recharges at every Entrance refill
a: Cue, once per show: for one scoring pass this card stands in for the single empty cell of every column that has exactly one, and each column that completes scores
b: Cue, once per show: for one scoring pass this card stands in for the single empty cell of every line that has exactly one, rows and diagonals included
c: Cue, once per show: for one scoring pass this card counts as a member of the same column in every grid

name: Stage Fright
head: Disturbance costs instead of pays ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) only cost you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Disturbing a completed line re-scores it, but the re-score subtracts rather than adds — **level 2:** Lines through its cell are exempt
b: Disturbing a completed line scores nothing at all, so lines are final once made — **level 2:** Lines through its cell are exempt
c: Disturbing a completed line re-scores it at half, and the half withheld is paid into the special bucket — **level 2:** Lines through its cell pay both halves

name: The Cascade
head: A clear collapses the board and can clear again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A chain that starts through its cell adds +1 to the multiplier for each link
a: A completed line through its cell clears; the cards above fall in, and every line the fall completes or re-forms scores again, at a multiplier that rises one per link
b: A completed line through its cell clears; the cards above fall in, and every line the fall completes or re-forms scores again at flat value
c: A completed line through its cell clears; the cards above fall in, and every line the fall re-forms scores again; chains stop after three links

name: The Reprise
head: Re-fires a line by disturbing it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Re-scoring a line through its cell also re-fires the lifted card's level 2, if it sits on a mark it matches ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0029, which you wrote: tap to rescore as if placed again*
a: Cue: lift and replace one card in a completed line to score that line again
b: Cue: lift and replace one card to re-score its line, at half value each subsequent time
c: Any card removed and replaced re-scores its line, with no cue needed and no limit, which is already the default - this option keeps it

name: The Understudy Call
head: Swaps a card without breaking the line. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card swapped in counts as matching the mark it lands on
a: Cue: swap one card in a completed line for one in the Entrance; the lifted card takes the Entrance slot, and the line re-scores with the new card
b: Cue: swap one card in a completed line for one in the Entrance; the lifted card takes the Entrance slot, and the line does not re-score
c: Cue: swap any two cards between two completed lines; both re-score

name: Element boards (ice/water)
head: Rows that do not hold still. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card sliding through its lines stops on the first mark it matches
a: Ice rows slide any card placed on them to the end of the column; water rows let cards drift
b: One row per grid is ice, sliding any card placed on it to the end of its column
c: Ice and water rows appear at random per show, and which rows they are is telegraphed before you place

name: Free Cell reserve slots
head: A reserve you can reach any time. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card returning from reserve may land on any empty cell whose mark it matches, ignoring the committed grid
a: A card may go from the Entrance to a reserve cell instead of the grid, and return to any empty cell as a later placement
b: A card may go from the Entrance to a reserve cell, and cards in reserve still count for class and set bonuses
c: A card may go from the Entrance to a reserve cell, and a card returning keeps whatever it gained in reserve

name: Sawdust
head: When this card is discarded from the grid, its slot keeps a marker that gives the next card placed there bonus points on its first score
a: When this card leaves a cell, the cell keeps a marker giving the next card placed there bonus points on its first score
b: When this card leaves a cell, every empty cell in its row keeps a marker giving the next card placed there bonus points
c: When this card leaves a cell, the cell is marked permanently and every card ever placed there scores bonus points

name: Tetromino shape-matching bonus tiles
head: After the game Tetris: cells that want a shape. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A shape covering its cell forgives one wrong card
a: Certain cells want a preset tetromino shape placed over them, rotatable, matched by suit or rank, for a bonus
b: Certain cells want a preset shape placed over them, matched by suit only
c: Certain cells want a shape that changes each show, and matching it scores the whole shape as a meld

name: The Butoh Walker
head: Moves one slot automatically every other turn; every slot it leaves permanently grants bonus points to the next card scored there. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It walks only onto cells whose mark it matches, and skips the rest
a: Every other turn it steps to an adjacent empty cell of your choice; the lines it leaves and joins re-score, and every cell it leaves permanently pays bonus points to the next card scored there
b: Every turn it steps to an adjacent empty cell of your choice; the cells it leaves pay for this show only
c: Every other turn it steps to a cell of your choice; the cells it has left form a trail that pays all at once when the trail closes a loop

name: Trap card
head: A space that is not really there. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The extra cell is dealt a mark
a: Creates an extra empty cell; the next card placed there goes beneath this card instead, and the cell vanishes
b: Creates an extra empty cell that any card may use normally, until this card leaves
c: Creates an extra empty cell that swallows the next card placed there entirely, removing it from the show

name: Hidden-mine bomb-prefilled grid
head: After Microsoft's Minesweeper: bombs under the grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card placed on a mark it matches defuses every bomb beside it
a: Grids start with hidden bombs; numbered cells show how many are adjacent, and placing on a bomb lowers that card's value
b: Grids start with hidden bombs; numbered cells show how many are adjacent, and placing on a bomb destroys the card
c: Grids start with hidden bombs you may defuse by completing a line through them

name: Null
head: Junk material inserted by hazards: occupies a slot, scores nothing, and melds nothing
a: Junk inserted by hazards: it fills a cell, scores nothing and melds nothing
b: Junk inserted by hazards: it fills a cell and melds nothing, and can only be cleared by a line completing around it
c: Junk inserted by hazards: it fills a cell, melds nothing, and drags its whole line's score to zero

name: Mobile pageant zone
head: The ring turns. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The column or row it sits in may stay put while the rest cycle
a: Cue, once per Entrance refill: cycle the grid's columns one step, the last becoming the first, cards and marks travelling with them; rows keep their hands, and every diagonal re-forms and scores if complete
b: Cue, once per Entrance refill: cycle the grid's rows one step instead, cards and marks travelling with them
c: Cue, once per Entrance refill: cycle either the columns or the rows, your choice each time

name: Non-5x5 ring layouts with hazards
head: Grids that are not five by five. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose the next venue's layout from two
a: Alternative grid layouts that are not 5x5, some pre-filled with cards or hazards
b: Alternative grid layouts that are not 5x5, with line length adjusting to the layout
c: Alternative grid layouts chosen per town, so the shape of the board is part of the venue

name: Sliced Reality (summary)
head: Splits a column, or welds two together. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may split or merge rows too
a: Splits one column into two, or merges two columns into one
b: Splits one column into two, or merges two into one, once per show
c: Splits one column into two or merges two into one, and the affected cards redistribute rather than being discarded

name: The Floors
head: The grid is stacked into levels that resolve in order. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack's floor resolves twice ⚑ *pair review: nothing on this board is a threat that climbs floors*
a: A grid's stack heights act as floors that resolve bottom to top, and a threat that survives one floor rises to the next
b: A grid's stack heights act as floors that resolve bottom to top, and a threat stopped on a floor is destroyed there
c: A grid's stack heights act as floors, and you choose the order they resolve in each show

name: Uneven Rows
head: The lines are not the same length. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Short lines through its cell score on the full hand table
a: A grid's lines have different lengths - three, five, five - and a short line is scored on its own smaller hand table
b: A grid's lines have different lengths, and a short line pays proportionally more per card
c: A grid's lines have different lengths, and you choose the shape before the show starts

name: Cross-grid row expansion setting
head: Grids grow together, or apart
a: Setting: when one grid's rows spread apart to make room for height, every other grid spreads too
b: Setting: only the grid that grew spreads, and the others stay compact
c: Setting: grids spread together, and a line can then run across grids at the same height

name: Rows spanning multiple grids
head: Lines that run across grids. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its row may run on into the next grid even where that grid's row is not full ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Rows may run across multiple grids at the same y, scoring as one long line
b: Rows may run across grids at the same y, scoring as one line but only if every grid contributes
c: Rows may run across grids, and such a line scores separately from each grid's own row

name: The Aligned Column
head: Columns line up across grids as well. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its column across grids scores even if one grid's column is a card short ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: The same column index across every grid forms one long line, scored as the best five within it
b: The same column index across grids forms a line only when every grid has that column full
c: The same column index across grids forms a line, and cards in it also still score in their own grid column

name: Strike the Set
head: Closes a grid down. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Closing a grid pays each of its matched marks once more ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Cue: close one grid; its cards are discarded and the show's goal drops proportionally
b: Cue: close one grid; its cards return to the deck and the goal is unchanged
c: Cue: close one grid and its cards are dealt into the remaining grids' empty cells

name: The Fourth Ring
head: Opens another grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The grid it opens copies this grid's matched marks, so what you have already aimed at counts there too
a: Unlocks one additional grid for this show only
b: Unlocks one additional grid permanently for the rest of the run
c: Unlocks one additional grid, and the show's goal rises by the fraction it adds

name: The Merger
head: Welds two grids into one. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A merged cell keeps both marks, and a card matching either counts as matched ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Cue: merge two adjacent grids into one wider grid, so its rows are ten cards long
b: Cue: merge two adjacent grids, and lines in the merged grid need seven cards rather than five
c: Cue: merge two adjacent grids, overlaying them so cards land on top of each other as height

name: The Touring Rig
head: Grids arrive when you earn them, not when the deck grows
a: A new grid unlocks each time a show is cleared above target, rather than per fifty-two cards of deck — **level 2:** A show cleared while it sits on its own mark counts as cleared above target
b: Grids unlock per fifty-two cards as usual, and one more unlocks the first show you clear with every mark in a line matched — **level 2:** A show cleared while it sits on its own mark counts as a line of matched marks
c: Grids unlock per fifty-two cards, and one is taken away each time a show is cleared below target — **level 2:** A show cleared below target while it sits on its own mark takes no grid away

name: Per-ring independent entrances
head: Every grid has its own Entrance ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Each grid holds its own five-card Entrance, playable in any order between grids — **level 2:** Swaps between Entrances are free
b: Each grid holds its own Entrance, but only one may be played from per turn — **level 2:** Swaps between Entrances are free
c: Each grid holds its own Entrance, and cards may be swapped between them at a cost — **level 2:** Swaps between Entrances are free

name: The Booked Stage
head: One grid holds the whole placement. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines it completes score two extra steps ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: While this card is on a grid, the Entrance stays committed to that grid for the whole show rather than lifting, and every line it completes scores an extra step
b: While this card is on a grid, the Entrance stays committed to that grid for the whole show, and every grid it locks out pays at show end for staying untouched
c: While this card is on a grid, the entrance alternates strictly between grids, one refresh each

name: The Free Hand
head: You may change your mind about which grid you are feeding. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Switching grids is free after a card lands on a mark it matches ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Once the first card of a refresh is placed you may still switch grids, but switching costs an Entrance card, discarded
b: You may switch grids mid-refresh once per Entrance refill at no cost
c: You may switch grids mid-refresh freely, but a refresh split across grids scores no line bonuses

name: Trigger cross-ring effects while placing
head: Trigger elsewhere while you place here. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Effects of cards on matched marks in the other grids fire too ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Effects in other grids may be triggered while placing into the committed grid
b: Effects in other grids may be triggered while placing, but only once per refresh
c: Effects in other grids fire automatically when a line completes in the committed grid

name: Fairy Floss
head: When scored, gives +1 rank to all orthogonally adjacent cards for the rest of the show. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each neighbour may take -1 instead of +1, your choice, so it can steer them onto their rank marks
a: When this card scores, every orthogonally adjacent card gains +1 rank for the rest of the show
b: When this card is placed, every orthogonally and diagonally adjacent card gains +1 rank permanently
c: When this card scores, every card in the 3x3 around it gains +1 rank for the rest of the show

name: Misdirection
head: While spotlit, the topmost covered card in each adjacent column is also treated as spotlit. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Every covered card in its row counts as spotlit too
a: While spotlit, the topmost covered card in each adjacent column also counts as spotlit
b: While spotlit, every covered card in this card's own column also counts as spotlit
c: While spotlit, the card directly beneath this one also counts as spotlit

name: Mr. Punch
head: Each placement, gains points for every orthogonally adjacent card debuffed or destroyed. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts diagonal neighbours too
a: Each placement, gains points for every orthogonally adjacent card that is debuffed or destroyed
b: Each placement, gains points for every debuffed or destroyed card anywhere in its grid
c: Gains +1 permanent rank each time an orthogonally adjacent card is destroyed

name: Neighbor-type value bonus (3-Ring Circus)
head: Cares who is beside it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Neighbours sitting on marks they match count twice
a: Gains value based on the types of the cards to its left and right
b: Gains value based on the types of all four orthogonal neighbours
c: Gains value based on how many distinct types surround it, in all eight directions

name: Punch
head: Hits what is next to it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It beats neighbours of equal rank too
a: Scores points for each adjacent card it beats in rank
b: Scores points for each adjacent card it beats in rank, and knocks the lowest one into the discard pile; its cell keeps its mark
c: Scores points for each adjacent card it beats, doubled if it beats all four

name: Spiderweb
head: When scored, gains +1 point per card diagonally adjacent to it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays for every card on the diagonal lines through it, stacked cards included
a: On scoring, gains +1 point per diagonally adjacent card
b: On scoring, gains +1 point per card on every diagonal run through its cell, of any length, climbs included
c: On scoring, gains +1 point per diagonally adjacent card, doubled if all four diagonals are occupied

name: Terrain Combinations
head: Two placed hazards make a third thing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose which of the two hazards the combination keeps ⚑ *pair review: hazards are level modifiers, not cards you place beside each other*
a: Two specific hazard cards placed adjacent transform into a stronger single hazard with a larger reward
b: Two specific hazards placed adjacent cancel each other out
c: Two hazards placed adjacent combine, and the combination is different for each pair

name: The Courier
head: While spotlit, it stands in for one empty cell of a line beside it
a: While spotlit, this card also stands in for one empty cell of the column beside it, the side chosen when it is placed, so that column can complete one card short — **level 2:** It stands in for the row beside it too
b: While spotlit, this card stands in for one empty cell of any line that passes within one cell of it — **level 2:** It may stand in for two cells of the same line
c: While spotlit, this card stands in for one empty cell of both its own row and its own column at once, as if it sat in each — **level 2:** It stands in for the row beside it too

name: The Puppet (Bunraku)
head: Needs hands to work it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Supporters sitting on marks they match count as two
a: While two or more orthogonal neighbours are placed, every line through its cell also pays into the special bucket
b: With two supporters its lines pay into the special bucket too; with three, its row pays there as well; with four, every line through it pays double
c: While two or more neighbours support it, every line through it pays into the special bucket, and when a line through it scores, each supporter's level 2 fires as if it sat on a matched mark

name: The Wiring Diagram
head: Names exactly which neighbours it checks. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One named cell may be empty, and it reads the mark there
a: This card names which of its neighbouring cells it reads, and ignores the rest
b: This card names which neighbouring cells it reads, and you may re-point them once per show
c: This card reads only the neighbours that are diagonal to it, never the orthogonal ones

name: The Zoning Board
head: Adds to some neighbours and subtracts from others. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Neighbours sitting on marks they match are never subtracted from
a: This card adds points to the cells on one side of it and subtracts from the cells on the other
b: This card adds points to orthogonal neighbours and subtracts from diagonal ones
c: This card adds to neighbours of its own suit and subtracts from all others

name: The Awkward Shape
head: Occupies more than one cell, and can be turned
a: This card occupies an L-shaped footprint of three cells and may be rotated when placed
b: This card occupies a two-cell footprint and may be rotated when placed
c: This card occupies an L of three cells, may be rotated, and counts in every line any of its cells touches

name: The Corridor
head: Connected regions score, not lines; a region pays into the special bucket. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Groups through its cell may connect diagonally
a: The largest connected group of each suit scores, alongside the normal lines
b: The largest connected group of each suit scores INSTEAD of the normal lines
c: Every connected group of three or more of one suit scores, and the largest scores double

name: The Ring Of Five
head: A shape that is not a line, paying into the special bucket. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An uncovered mark in the ring stands in for its cell
a: This card scores for every card in the ring of eight cells around it, counting suits and ranks as a hand
b: This card scores for the ring of eight around it only when all eight are filled, paying as a made hand
c: This card scores for the ring of eight around it, and the ring may cross into a neighbouring grid

name: Hunting Season
head: Kills the middle one. The emptied cell keeps its mark, and the next card placed there re-scores the line. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which card of the line is destroyed
a: If a line scores a three of a kind, the centre card of that line is destroyed afterwards
b: If a line scores a three of a kind, the centre card is destroyed and this card takes its rank
c: The centre cell of any scoring line is destroyed afterwards, whatever the line's length

name: Performance Rings
head: Depth is worth more. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack's multiplier steps every four levels instead of five
a: Every stack line through its cell pays into the row bucket as well as the special one
b: Score zones by stack height, with the multiplier applying only to the column score, not the row
c: Score zones by height rather than row: every five levels of stack height multiplies that stack's score by one more

name: Ring Column
head: One per column: adds one grid column at game creation; its rank equals which column it is
a: One per column: adds a grid column at game creation, its rank equal to which column it is
b: One per column: adds a grid column at game creation, and can be destroyed mid-run to remove that column
c: One per column: adds a grid column whose cells all carry a bonus matching the column's rank

name: Sliced Bread
head: On submission, if a same-suit card sits lower in this card's stack, gain a point per card between them. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards between that sit on marks they match count twice
a: On scoring, gain a point for each card lying between this card and the nearest same-suit card lower in its stack
b: On scoring, gain a point for each card between this one and the nearest same-suit card anywhere in its line
c: On scoring, gain a point for each card between this one and every same-suit card in its line, counting each pair

name: Escaramuza
head: When the grid's column heights read the same left-to-right as right-to-left at scoring, gain bonus multiplier on the placement. A column's height is the number of cards it holds, stacked cards included. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A palindrome through its cell that is one card off still pays
a: If the grid's column heights read the same left to right as right to left when a line scores, the placement gains a large multiplier
b: While the grid's column heights read the same in both directions, every line scored pays double
c: Any line whose ranks read the same forwards as backwards pays double

name: Front And Back
head: The row a card sits in decides what it does. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose where the boundary between front and back rows lies ⚑ *pair review: no hazard picks a front row to hit first*
