a: Cards in the grid's front rows take hazards first and cards in the back rows score more, so placement is a risk trade
b: Cards in the front rows take hazards first; back rows are otherwise identical
c: Front rows take hazards first and score less; the boundary between front and back moves each placement

name: Latin-square grid bonus
head: After the puzzle Sudoku: sudoku on the grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each line through its cell may repeat one rank ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0104, which you wrote: a grid with no matching suit and rank*
a: If the ranks on a grid satisfy sudoku constraints, the grid scores a bonus
b: If any row, column or block satisfies sudoku constraints, that line scores a bonus
c: If no rank repeats in any row or column of a grid, that grid scores a bonus scaling with how full it is

name: The Button
head: Three connected of a kind pays a token. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A token from a group through its cell is worth double ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0102, which you approved: three matching cards cashed in*
a: Three connected cards sharing a suit may be cashed for a token that scores at show end
b: Three connected cards sharing a suit or a rank may be cashed for a token
c: Three connected cards of a kind pay a token, and the token's value rises with each one already banked

name: The Hammer
head: Half the ranks are dead
a: Boss: every odd-ranked card is debuffed
b: Boss: every card of one parity is debuffed, and which parity flips each placement
c: Boss: every odd-ranked card is debuffed, and every even-ranked card scores double

name: The Junk Orchestra
head: Scores by position, not by rank. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Skill-less cards sitting on marks they match score by their pattern and by their rank ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a positional pattern pays*
a: Skill-less cards score by their positional pattern rather than their ranks
b: Skill-less cards score by positional pattern, paying more the more regular the pattern is
c: Skill-less cards score by positional pattern, and matching a pattern named at show start pays double

name: The Kickline
head: The tallest card in each column. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An empty column lends the mark of its tallest cell
a: When the highest-stacked cards of the five columns, one per column, all share a suit, the row those five sit in scores again
b: When the highest-stacked cards of the five columns all share a suit, every line through any of them scores again
c: When the highest-stacked cards of the five columns form a poker hand, that hand scores as a line into the special bucket

name: The Pyramid
head: A staircase of stacks, paying into the special bucket. A column's height is the number of cards it holds, stacked cards included. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack counts as one card taller for formations
a: Formation: three adjacent columns holding stacks of exactly 3, 2 and 1 score a bonus meld
b: Formation: any three adjacent columns whose heights descend by one score a bonus meld, scaling with the height they start from
c: Formation: any run of columns whose heights ascend or descend by one scores a bonus meld per column involved

name: The Repulsor
head: Only the ends of the row fire
a: Boss: only the first and last card of each line trigger; everything between does nothing
b: Boss: only the first and last card of each line trigger, and they trigger twice
c: Boss: only the centre card of each line triggers

name: Callback
head: Reaches back a fixed number of turns. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The re-triggered card fires its level 2, as if it sat on a matched mark
a: Cue: re-trigger whatever card you placed three turns ago, wherever it is now
b: Cue: re-trigger whatever card you placed on the previous turn
c: Cue: name a turn number; re-trigger the card you placed on that turn this show

name: The Opener
head: Remembers what went first
a: Scores a bonus equal to the rank of the first card you placed this show — **level 2:** It counts the first card of every Entrance refill too
b: Scores a bonus equal to the rank of the first card placed in its own line — **level 2:** It counts the first card placed in every line through its cell
c: The first card placed after each Entrance refill is spotlit until the next refill, wherever it sits — **level 2:** The first card of each refill stays spotlit for the rest of the show

name: The Running Order
head: Reads the sequence, not the position. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A placement onto a matched mark may break the order without spoiling it
a: Scores a bonus if the cards in its line were placed in ascending rank order
b: Scores a bonus if the cards in its line were placed in any strictly ordered sequence, ascending or descending
c: Scores a bonus per card in its line that was placed in order, so a partly ordered line still pays

name: The Diagonal Company
head: Only diagonals count as adjacent. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards next to it count both diagonal and orthogonal neighbours
a: Adjacency is diagonal only; orthogonal neighbours do not count as adjacent
b: Adjacency is diagonal only for effects, but lines still score orthogonally
c: Adjacency is diagonal only, and which it is flips each placement

name: The Joined Tents
head: Grids touch at their edges. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line crossing the seam through its cell pays double ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: The rightmost column of each grid is adjacent to the leftmost column of the next
b: Grids are adjacent at their edges, and a line may cross that seam
c: Grids are adjacent at their edges only while both are more than half full

name: The Long Reach
head: Counts distant cells as adjacent. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Every cell on its grid counts as adjacent to it
a: This card treats every cell in its own row and column as adjacent to it
b: This card treats every cell within two steps as adjacent to it
c: This card treats the mirrored cell across the grid's centre as adjacent to it

name: The Round Ring
head: The grid wraps
a: The grid's left and right edges are adjacent, so rows wrap around — **level 2:** Lines through its cell may wrap on both axes
b: All four edges wrap, so the grid is a torus and every cell has four neighbours — **level 2:** Diagonals through its cell wrap too
c: The edges wrap, and a line that uses the wrap scores double — **level 2:** A wrapped line through its cell may wrap twice

name: Accordion pile-combining rule
head: Piles that combine at a distance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A stack in which any card matches its cell's mark may combine from any distance along any line
a: Stacks whose top cards match may combine if they are adjacent or exactly three apart
b: Stacks whose top cards match may combine if they are adjacent, two apart, or at opposite ends of the line
c: Stacks whose top cards match may combine at any distance, but only along a row

name: Any card placeable on this card
head: Anything can go on top of it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On its mark, this card may itself be placed on top of any card, whatever the stacking rules say
a: Any card may be placed on top of this one, whatever the stacking rules say
b: Any card may be placed on top of this one, and doing so scores this card immediately
c: Any card may be placed on top of this one, and this card takes the suit of whatever lands there

name: Devil's Grip +3 rank stacking
head: Stack by threes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack may also build by one rank
a: Stacking requires a rank exactly three higher, with the starting row deciding the sequence
b: Stacking requires a rank exactly three higher or three lower
c: The first time this card is spotlit, name a fixed rank gap; stacking requires that gap for the rest of the run

name: Hanoi Solitaire
head: Only smaller on larger, ever
a: A card may only be stacked on a card of strictly higher rank — **level 2:** A descending stack of five on its cell scores as a straight
b: A card may only be stacked on a card of strictly higher rank, and a descending stack of five scores as its own meld — **level 2:** A descending stack of five on its cell scores its meld twice
c: A card may only be stacked on a higher rank, and moving a stack moves only its top card — **level 2:** A descending stack of five on its cell scores as a straight

name: Jumbo
head: Heavy: no cards may be placed on this card, but it can be placed on anything; scores bonus points per card beneath it when scored
a: Nothing may be placed on this card, though it may be placed on anything; scores bonus points per card beneath it — **level 2:** It scores its bonus twice for each card beneath it that also matches the cell's mark
b: Nothing may be placed on this card and it may only go on an empty cell; it scores triple — **level 2:** Its triple also pays for each card beside it sitting on a mark it matches
c: Nothing may be placed on this card; it scores bonus points per card in its whole column — **level 2:** It scores its bonus twice for each card beneath it that also matches the cell's mark

name: Klondike empty-space king rule
head: Only a king opens an empty cell. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Any stack headed by a card that matches the empty cell's mark may fill it
a: An empty cell can only be filled by a stack headed by the highest rank
b: An empty cell can only be filled by a stack headed by the highest rank, or by a single card of any rank
c: A stack headed by the highest rank moved into an empty cell scores that cell's lines twice

name: Rosin
head: Cards placed onto this card cannot be picked up again, but score +1 bonus per level deeper than they stand
a: Cards placed on this one can never be lifted again, but score +1 for each level they sit above it
b: Cards placed on this one can never be lifted again, and score double
c: Cards placed on this one can be lifted only by paying a charge, and score +1 per level above it

name: The Grip
head: The bottom card legalises the pile. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It legalises the stacks in the cells beside it too
a: At the bottom of a stack, this card makes everything above it legal, whatever the stacking rules say
b: At the bottom of a stack, this card makes the card directly above it legal, one card only
c: At the bottom of a stack, this card legalises the whole stack, and the stack cannot be broken up afterwards

name: The Mighty Atom
head: Small, and holds up anything. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each card it holds adds +1 to its score
a: A rank-3 card that can legally hold any stack above it, whatever the stacking rules
b: A rank-3 card that can hold any stack above it, and scores per card it is holding
c: A low-ranked card that can hold any stack, and the lower its rank the more it scores for doing so

name: The Packer
head: Packs a row into one stack. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The stack it builds scores its height line at once, whatever its height
a: Cue: gather the cards of this card's row that could legally stack, left to right, into one stack on this cell, stopping at the first illegal card
b: Cue: gather every card of this card's row that could legally stack into one stack on this cell, skipping the illegal ones
c: Cue: gather the legal cards of this card's row, left to right, into one stack on this cell, and the emptied cells have their marks re-dealt

name: Ringmaster's Grip
head: This card and the stack it heads can always be picked up, regardless of stack legality
a: This card and the stack it heads can always be picked up, whatever the stacking rules say — **level 2:** A stack it heads may be put down on any cell whose mark this card matches, whatever the stacking rules say
b: This card and the stack it heads can always be picked up, and can always be put down anywhere — **level 2:** The stack it heads may be set down on a covered cell, stacking whatever the rules say
c: Any stack containing this card can always be picked up, even from underneath it — **level 2:** A stack it heads may be put down on any cell whose mark this card matches, whatever the stacking rules say

name: The Acrobat
head: This card can be grabbed even while covered; the cards above cascade down one slot. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Once grabbed, it may be put down on any cell whose mark it matches, even a covered one
a: This card can be grabbed while covered; the cards above it cascade down one slot
b: This card can be grabbed while covered, taking the cards above it along as a stack
c: Any card can be grabbed while covered while this one is on the grid; the cards above cascade down

name: The Recall
head: Cards may come back off the foundation
a: A card that has already scored may be taken back off its line and replayed elsewhere — **level 2:** A recalled card scores its rank as it leaves the line
b: A card that has already scored may be taken back once per show — **level 2:** A recalled card scores its rank as it leaves the line
c: A scored card may be taken back, but its line then scores nothing for the rest of the show — **level 2:** A recalled card put down on a mark it matches leaves its old line's score intact

name: Carrier-stacking bonus points
head: Tricks on top of other performers. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card stacked on it fires its skill twice
a: A skill card stacked on another skill card scores bonus points for both
b: A skill card stacked on another skill card scores bonus points scaling with the stack's height
c: A skill card stacked on another scores bonus points, and the carrier also fires its own skill again

name: Chair stack
head: Paid by the tallest stack
a: Gains a multiplier per card in the tallest stack on its grid — **level 2:** It adds its own stack to the count
b: Gains a multiplier per card in its own stack — **level 2:** It counts its own stack and the tallest beside it
c: Gains a multiplier per card in the two tallest stacks on its grid — **level 2:** It adds its own stack to the count

name: Mallakhamb Pole
head: While spotlit, every card in this card's column gains bonus points per row of column height when the column scores. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A height line completed in its stack also re-scores its row
a: While spotlit, every card in this card's column gains bonus points per level of column height when that column scores
b: While spotlit, this card scores its rank once for every level of height beneath it
c: While spotlit, a height line completed in this card's stack scores twice

name: Poker Crown
head: When scored, this card and the 4 cards directly above it in its column stack are also evaluated as a poker hand, once. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The crown hand is read twice: the five above it and the five below it, as two hands
a: When this card scores, any five consecutive cards of its stack that include it are read as a poker hand at heights 6 to 9, where the stack itself pays nothing
b: As (a), read again every time the stack changes
c: When this card scores, the five cards nearest it, in a line or not, are read once as a poker hand

name: The Backlift
head: Paid by what is piled on it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards stacked on top that match the cell's mark count double
a: Scores extra per card currently stacked on top of this one
b: Scores extra per card stacked on top, doubled if it is the bottom of its stack
c: Scores extra per card stacked on top, and the whole stack scores with it

name: The Forge
head: Two placements, both onto the same cell. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The cell it builds pays the mark match for both cards
a: Cue: place two Entrance cards this turn onto the SAME cell, building height two at once
b: Cue: place two Entrance cards onto the same cell, and the pair scores as a single card of their summed rank
c: Cue: place any number of Entrance cards onto one cell this turn; each after the second discards one Entrance card

name: Collapse
head: Brings a whole column down ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) depend on Q0256 or Q0320 entering: stacks never have gaps otherwise*
a: Consumable: every stack on one grid compacts to the floor at once, scoring each card that falls
b: Consumable: every stack on one grid compacts to the floor, scoring nothing
c: Consumable: one stack collapses entirely, and its cards spread into the nearest empty cells

name: Dead Weight
head: What happens to the pile above
a: Removing a card drops everything above it, and the card that lands on the mark pays its match again — **level 2:** Each card that falls scores twice
b: Removing a card leaves a gap in the stack that only another card can fill — **level 2:** The gap may be filled by a card from the Entrance without spending the placement
c: Removing a card drops everything above it, and each card that falls scores its rank — **level 2:** Each card that falls scores twice

name: The Scaffold
head: Holds the stack up
a: While this card is anywhere in a stack, removing a card from that stack leaves the rest suspended — **level 2:** It holds up the stacks in the cells beside it too
b: While this card is at the bottom of a stack, that stack never compacts — **level 2:** It holds up the stacks in the cells beside it too
c: While this card is in a stack, cards above a removal fall two levels instead of one — **level 2:** Each card that falls two levels scores its rank as it lands

name: The Tire Trick
head: Hidden in the stack, gone when it is taken apart. (line 975)
a: While buried, this card is safe from everything; dismantling the stack removes it from play, and rebuilding the stack brings it back — **level 2:** When it returns, its cell's mark is rerolled to one it matches
b: While buried, this card is safe from everything; dismantling the stack destroys it permanently — **level 2:** Dismantling the stack discards it instead of destroying it
c: While buried it is safe and scores nothing; dismantling the stack removes it, and it returns with a bonus when the stack is rebuilt to the same height — **level 2:** When it returns, its cell's mark is rerolled to one it matches

name: Air
head: Whenever this card's stack changes, it automatically moves to the top of that stack
a: Whenever its stack changes, this card rises to the top of that stack
b: This card can never be covered: a card placed on it goes underneath it instead
c: At each Entrance refresh this card rises one position in its stack, reaching the top over time rather than at once

name: Earth
head: Whenever this card's stack changes, it automatically sinks to the bottom of that stack, carrying its stamp with it
a: Whenever its stack changes, this card sinks to the bottom of that stack
b: This card can never be placed on another card; anything played to its cell goes on top of it
c: At each Entrance refresh this card sinks one position in its stack

name: Gold type
head: Sinks, but not all the way
a: Sinks toward the bottom of its stack, stopping at other heavy cards
b: Sinks straight to the bottom of its stack regardless of what is there
c: Sinks one level per turn until it reaches the bottom or meets another heavy card

name: The Surveyor
head: Everything you drop sinks. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card its drop displaces from the bottom is compared against the mark of any empty cell beside it, and moves there if it matches
a: While spotlit, cards you drop resolve to the bottom of the target column instead of the top
b: While spotlit, cards you drop resolve to whichever end of the target column you choose
c: While spotlit, cards you drop resolve to the bottom of the target column, and the card displaced scores as it rises

name: Tunneler card
head: Everything sinks past it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card sinking past it scores its rank as it passes
a: A single card placed on this one drops to the bottom of the stack instead
b: A single card placed on this one drops to the bottom of the stack, and this card scores its rank
c: Every card placed on this one drops to the bottom, so the stack builds downward

name: Distancing card
head: Hovers without covering
a: Hovers above its stack without blocking the card beneath, and cannot be clicked — **level 2:** It may be clicked again, and put down on any cell whose mark it matches
b: Hovers above its stack without blocking the card beneath, and counts as occupying an extra row for line purposes — **level 2:** Its extra row counts for the lines through both of its heights
c: Hovers above its stack without blocking anything, and any card may be placed beneath it freely — **level 2:** A card placed beneath it counts as newly placed on the mark

name: Ghost Light
head: This card does not block the Spotlight of cards beneath it; they stay active as if uncovered
a: Does not block the spotlight of cards beneath it — **level 2:** Nor does anything else in its stack
b: Does not block the spotlight of cards beneath it, and nor does anything else in its column — **level 2:** Nor does anything in its row
c: Does not block the spotlight of cards beneath it, and the card directly beneath also scores when this one does — **level 2:** The whole stack scores when it does

name: Kuroko
head: This card does not block Spotlight beneath it and cannot be targeted by boss or town effects. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A boss or town effect aimed at it fizzles, and the fizzle counts as a trigger for the combo
a: Does not block spotlight beneath it, and cannot be targeted by boss or town effects
b: Does not block spotlight beneath it, and cannot be targeted by any effect at all, including your own
c: Does not block spotlight beneath it, and the cards beneath it cannot be targeted either

name: Glass type
head: Transparent, and brittle
a: Cards behind this one stay spotlit through it, but it breaks if a Heavy card passes through
b: Cards behind this one stay spotlit through it, and it breaks the third time anything passes through
c: Cards behind this one stay spotlit, and it never breaks, but it cannot score itself

name: Global
head: This card's modifiers are active from anywhere: grid, Entrance, deck, or discard. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its modifiers also fire once at each Entrance refill
a: This card's modifiers are active from anywhere: grid, Entrance, deck or discard
b: This card's modifiers are active from the Entrance and the deck, but not from the discard
c: This card's modifiers are active from anywhere, at half effect when it is not on the grid

name: Hidden bearers (costaleros)
head: The ones underneath are carrying it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Covered cards that match the cell's mark add double
a: Covered cards beneath a scoring card add their ranks to it
b: Covered cards beneath a scoring card add half their ranks to it, rounded down
c: Covered cards beneath a scoring card add their ranks to it, and each also counts as a trigger for the combo

name: Humbug
head: While covered, counts as a copy of the most valuable card in its row; when uncovered, is revealed as junk (rank 2, base score only)
a: While covered, counts as a copy of the highest-value card in its row; uncovered it is junk at rank 2 — **level 2:** Uncovered, it is revealed as the card whose mark it sits on, not as junk
b: While covered, counts as a copy of the highest-value card in its row; uncovering it destroys it — **level 2:** Uncovered, it becomes the card whose mark it sits on instead of being destroyed
c: While covered, counts as a copy of the card covering it; uncovered it is junk at rank 2 — **level 2:** Uncovered, it is revealed as the card whose mark it sits on, not as junk

name: Lithograph
head: While this card sits in the Entrance its skill is active globally; on the grid it has no effect
a: This card's skill is active globally while it is in the Entrance, and does nothing on the grid
b: This card's skill is active globally from the Entrance, and at half strength on the grid
c: This card's skill is active from the Entrance or the deck, and does nothing on the grid

name: Revealing
head: This card's modifiers stay active while covered. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It fires once more at the moment it is uncovered
a: This card's modifiers stay active while it is covered
b: This card's modifiers stay active while covered, and it stays visible by pushing the rows below it down
c: This card's modifiers stay active while covered, and fire again when it is uncovered

name: The Free Edge
head: Playable only if something is open beside it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts as an empty cell for its neighbours' free-edge test, so the cards beside it are never walled in ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) only restrict you; it reads as a hazard*
a: A card may only be picked up if at least one of its horizontal neighbours is empty
b: A card may only be picked up if it is uncovered AND has a free edge, so a card walled in on both sides is stuck
c: A card with a free edge counts as spotlit whether or not it is covered

name: The Prompter
head: Keeps one card in the light
a: While spotlit, choose one card in this card's column; that card's modifiers stay active however it is covered — **level 2:** It keeps two cards in the light instead of one
b: While spotlit, choose one card anywhere on the grid; its modifiers stay active however it is covered — **level 2:** It keeps two cards in the light instead of one
c: While spotlit, choose one card per row; each keeps its modifiers active — **level 2:** You may move one row's light to another row each placement

name: The Seed
head: Grows while it is buried. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its growth spreads: the card covering it gains +1 rank too
a: Gains +1 rank every turn it stays covered
b: Gains +1 rank every turn it stays covered, and loses it all the moment it is uncovered
c: Gains +1 rank every turn covered, keeping the gain permanently once it finally scores

name: The Shadow
head: Tall cards suppress what stands behind them. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack casts no shadow ⚑ *pair review: it only takes score away; it reads as a hazard*
a: A card casts a shadow across cells behind it proportional to its height, and shadowed cards score nothing
b: A card casts a shadow proportional to its height, and shadowed cards score half
c: A card casts a shadow proportional to its height, and the direction the shadow falls rotates each placement

name: The Spirit Cabinet
head: Works best buried. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Every line through its cell scores twice while it is buried
a: While fully covered, every card in this card's column triggers as though spotlit
b: While fully covered, every card in this card's grid triggers as though spotlit
c: While fully covered, this card's own column triggers as though spotlit, and the effect grows with how deeply it is buried

name: The Stilt-Walker
head: Tall enough to be seen over one card
a: Spotlit even when covered by one card, but not by two — **level 2:** Spotlit through two covering cards
b: Spotlit even when covered by one card, and the card covering it is spotlit too — **level 2:** Spotlit through two covering cards
c: Spotlit through any number of covering cards, but its effects work at half strength per card above it — **level 2:** Its effects work at full strength however deep it stands

name: Champion card
head: Clears its own rank above and below. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also discards neighbours of its mark's rank, and of the rank above when that is its own
a: Cards of the same rank directly above or below this one are discarded
b: Cards of the same rank anywhere in this card's column are discarded, and this card gains a rank for each
c: Cards of the same rank adjacent in any direction are discarded, and this card scores their summed rank

name: Consume
head: Eat what is underneath and grow. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which of the eaten card's properties it keeps as well
a: When this card is placed onto another, it destroys the card beneath and adds that rank to its own permanently
b: When placed onto another, it destroys the card beneath and adds half that rank to its own, permanently
c: When placed onto another, it destroys the card beneath and takes its suit, rank and skill outright

name: Edith's Bayonet
head: Cue: permanently destroy one Knives-suit card and add its rank to this card's own, forever
a: Cue: destroy one card of this card's own suit anywhere on the grid and add its rank to this card's, permanently — **level 2:** It may destroy a card of any suit, not only its own
b: Cue: destroy the card directly above this one and add its rank to this card's, permanently — **level 2:** It may destroy the card directly above or directly below
c: Automatically destroys any card of its own suit placed orthogonally adjacent to it, gaining half that card's rank — **level 2:** It may destroy a card of any suit, not only its own

name: Gentling
head: Tame it instead of eating it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Tamed cards gain the full rank
a: Animal cards may be tamed rather than consumed, gaining half the rank the eater would have taken, without being destroyed
b: Animal cards may be tamed rather than consumed, gaining half the rank; a tamed card cannot be eaten by anything afterwards
c: Any card may be tamed rather than eaten, gaining half the rank the eater would have taken

name: The Gobbler
head: After the game Hungry Hungry Hippos: consumes cards dropped onto it, adding their rank to its own up to a cap of 13, and returns everything eaten at show end
a: Eats cards placed on it, adding their rank to its own up to 13, and gives everything back at show end — **level 2:** What it gives back at show end returns with +1 rank each
b: Eats cards placed on it, adding their rank to its own up to 13; what it eats is destroyed — **level 2:** Each card it destroys also pays its rank as points
c: Eats cards placed on it, adding half their rank rounded up with no cap, and gives them back at show end — **level 2:** What it gives back at show end returns with +1 rank each

name: Parasite card
head: Replaces its host. **Level 2, on its own mark:** When it replaces its host, it keeps the host's skill as well
a: Attaches to the next card placed on it; when a line scores, it replaces that card
b: Attaches to the next card placed on it; when a line scores it replaces that card and keeps its rank
c: Attaches to the next card placed on it and slowly drains its rank each turn, replacing it at rank 0

name: Snake card
head: Eats downward through the stack
a: Consumes every lower-ranked card beneath it, leaving a temporary body card of the same rank behind each — **level 2:** The body cards it leaves count as matching the cell's mark
b: Consumes every lower-ranked card beneath it outright, leaving nothing behind — **level 2:** Each card it consumes scores its rank as it goes
c: Consumes one lower-ranked card beneath it per turn, leaving a body card each time — **level 2:** The body cards it leaves count as matching the cell's mark

name: The Digesting Duck
head: Consumes cards dropped on it like a Glutton, but secretly stores them; cue to return any one stored card to the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may return a stored card straight onto any cell whose mark that card matches
a: Consumes cards dropped on it but stores them instead of destroying them; cue to return any one stored card to the Entrance
b: Consumes cards dropped on it and stores them; all stored cards return to the deck at show end
c: Consumes cards dropped on it and stores them; cue to return one, and it scores bonus points per card still stored

name: Vampire
head: Eats the enhancements off cards
a: Gains a permanent multiplier per stamped card that scores, and strips that card's stamp — **level 2:** Stamps it strips from cards on matched marks count double
b: Gains a permanent multiplier per stamped card that scores, leaving the stamp intact — **level 2:** A stamped card scoring on a matched mark counts double
c: Gains a permanent multiplier per stamped card that scores and strips the stamp, keeping it for itself — **level 2:** Stamps it strips from cards on matched marks count double

name: Conjoined cards
head: Two cards, one body. **Level 2, on its own mark:** When either half completes a line, the other half's lines score again
a: Cue: fuse this card with an adjacent card; they move as one unit and score as two
b: Cue: fuse this card with an adjacent card; they move as one unit and score as one card of summed rank
c: Cue: fuse this card with an adjacent card until either scores, then they separate

name: Frankenstein
head: When a line scores, merges with the cards directly above and below it into one 3-card stack of summed rank that stays in the zone after scoring. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The merged card counts every property any of its parts matched
a: When a line scores, merges with the cards directly above and below into one card of their summed rank
b: Cue: merges with the card directly above into one card carrying both suits and their summed rank
c: When a line scores, merges with its whole stack into one card of summed rank, capped at 30

name: The Double Act
head: Two cards that become one performer. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The fused card may be fused once more
a: Cue: fuse this card with the card directly above it into a single card carrying both skills and the higher rank
b: Cue: fuse this card with any adjacent card of the same class into one carrying both skills and the summed rank
c: Cue: fuse this card with the card above it into one carrying both skills; the fused card cannot be moved or unfused

name: The Merge
head: Two equal cards become the next one up
a: Two cards of equal rank pushed together merge into one of the next rank up — **level 2:** A merge on a matched mark climbs two ranks instead of one
b: Two cards of equal rank pushed together merge into one of double the rank — **level 2:** The doubled card keeps both suits
c: Two cards of equal rank merge into the next rank up, and a merge that creates the highest rank scores enormously — **level 2:** A merge on a matched mark climbs two ranks instead of one

name: The Castell
head: Formation: a stack of 6+ cards topped by the lowest-ranked card pays a large bonus at scoring; if the stack is broken by a hazard first, lose double the bonus instead
a: A stack of six or more topped by its own lowest-ranked card pays a large bonus at scoring; if a hazard breaks it first, lose double that bonus — **level 2:** Five cards are enough
b: A stack of six or more topped by its own lowest-ranked card pays a large bonus, with no penalty for breaking — **level 2:** Five cards are enough
c: Any stack topped by its own lowest-ranked card pays a bonus scaling with the stack's height — **level 2:** A stack broken by a hazard keeps the bonus it had earned

name: The Contortionist
head: May share one grid slot with another card; both cards count in melds
a: May share one cell with another card; both count in melds, and a line through the cell is read as six cards — **level 2:** It may share its cell with two cards
b: May share one cell with another card; both count in melds, and the pair scores as a single card of their summed rank, and a line through the cell is read as six cards — **level 2:** It may share its cell with two cards
c: May share a cell with any number of cards, but only the top two count in melds — **level 2:** The top three cards count in melds

name: The Foot Juggler
head: Holds one card spinning above itself. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The suspended card counts as sitting on this card's mark
a: Holds one card suspended in a sub-slot above itself, playable from there at any time
b: Holds one card suspended above itself; that card scores in every line this card belongs to
c: Holds up to two cards suspended above itself, played one at a time

name: The Half Card
head: This card has half rank (rounded down) and half size: two copies occupy one grid slot together and meld as one combined card
a: Half rank rounded down and half size: two copies share one cell and meld as a single combined card — **level 2:** Two Half Cards sharing a matched mark each pay the rank-match bonus
b: Half rank rounded down and half size: two copies share one cell and meld as two separate cards — **level 2:** Two Half Cards sharing a matched mark each pay the rank-match bonus
c: Half rank and half size: it shares a cell with any card, and the pair melds as whichever of the two is more useful — **level 2:** Its cell-mate counts as matching the mark on rank too

name: The Seven Pyramid
head: One stack, seven high. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Six cards are enough
a: Formation: a single stack of exactly seven legally-run cards scores a large bonus; broken by a hazard, rebuilding it once scores double
b: Formation: a single stack of exactly seven legally-run cards scores a large bonus, once per show
c: Formation: a stack of exactly seven legally-run cards pays the bonus, and an eighth card placed on it pays it again

name: The Singa Barong
head: Carries the whole stack as one
a: Everything above this card counts as a single card for movement — **level 2:** The carried stack also scores as one card
b: Everything above this card counts as a single card for movement and for scoring — **level 2:** The carried stack may be set down on top of another stack
c: Everything above this card counts as one card for movement, and this card scores their summed rank — **level 2:** The carried stack may be set down on top of another stack

name: Low Ceiling
head: A venue that will not take a tall act
a: Boss: stack height is capped for this show, where it is normally unbounded
b: Boss: stack height is capped, and the cap falls by one each placement
c: Boss: stack height is capped and any stack already taller is cut down to it

name: The Cherry Picker
head: Raises the ceiling
a: While on the board, this card exempts its own stack from any height cap a level imposes — **level 2:** It exempts the cells beside it from the cap too
b: Raises any imposed height cap by one for each level this card sits above the floor — **level 2:** It exempts the cells beside it from the cap too
c: Removes any imposed height cap, and scores a bonus per level of the tallest stack — **level 2:** Its own stack's height counts twice for its bonus

name: The Dome
head: Seals a cell against any further height. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A sealed cell whose card matches its mark scores its lines when sealed
a: Cue: seal a cell at its current height so nothing may ever be stacked on it again
b: Cue: seal a cell at its current height for the rest of the show only
c: Cue: seal a cell, and every sealed cell on the grid raises this card's score

name: The Rigging Loft
head: Sets how high a stack may go
a: Stacks may not exceed a fixed height, and a card that would exceed it cannot be placed — **level 2:** Its own stack may exceed the cap by one
b: Stacks may not exceed a fixed height; a card that would exceed it pushes the bottom card out to the top of the stock you choose — **level 2:** The card pushed out of its stack scores as it leaves
c: There is no height cap, but placing above the fifth level discards one Entrance card — **level 2:** Levels above the fifth on its own stack cost nothing

name: Hopak Burst
head: Cue, 1 charge per show: jumps this card's entire stack one row upward in its column, sliding everything beneath up. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its charge refills whenever its stack lands on a cell whose mark this card matches
a: Cue, one charge per show: this card's whole stack jumps one row up its column, sliding everything beneath it up
b: Cue, one charge per show: this card alone jumps one row up its column, swapping with whatever is there
c: Cue, one charge per show: this card's whole stack jumps to the top row of its column

name: Rabbit card
head: Bolts when you reach for it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It bolts to an empty cell whose mark it matches, if there is one
a: If clicked or grabbed, this card moves to the furthest orthogonal cell instead
b: If clicked or grabbed, this card moves one cell away at random
c: If clicked or grabbed, this card moves to the furthest orthogonal cell and scores a bonus for escaping

name: Selection sort card
head: Sorts itself upward. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also moves up past cards of equal rank
a: Moves up one position whenever the card above it is of lower rank
b: Moves up one position per turn until the card above it is of higher rank
c: Moves up one position whenever the card above is lower, and scores a bonus each time it moves

name: The Crowd Surf
head: Cue: pass this card across the tops of all columns to the far edge, scoring bonus points per column crossed; if any crossed column is empty, this card is discarded instead. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An empty column no longer stops it or discards it
a: Cue: pass this card across the tops of every column to the far edge, scoring per column crossed; an empty column discards it
b: Cue: pass this card across the tops of every column, scoring per column crossed; an empty column simply stops it there
c: Cue: pass this card across the tops of every column, scoring per column crossed; if it reaches the far edge it surfs back once, scoring again

name: The Leotard
head: Carries its stack anywhere. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may move any card and the stack above it, not only its own
a: Cue: move this card and everything above it to the top of any column, ignoring legality
b: Cue: move this card and everything above it to any cell in any grid, ignoring legality
c: Cue: move this card and everything above it onto any cell whose mark this card matches

name: The Messenger
head: Unlimited movement, so long as height never changes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A move that ends on a mark the moved card matches refunds the cue
a: Cue, once per Entrance refill: move this card any distance across cells of the same height
b: Cue, once per Entrance refill: move up to five cards any distance, so long as none changes height
c: Cue, once per Entrance refill: move this card any distance at the same height, scoring per cell crossed

name: The Second Step
head: Moves twice, but never back. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each step that lands on a mark it matches earns one more step
a: Cue: move this card twice in one action, and it may not return to the cell it started in
b: Cue: move this card twice in one action with no restriction on where it ends
c: Cue: move this card any number of times in one action, so long as each cell is one it has not occupied this placement

name: The Traceur
head: Never enters a stack. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may drop into a stack when that cell's mark matches it
a: Moves only across the tops of columns, never into a stack; cue to move any distance sideways along topmost cells
b: Moves only across the tops of columns; cue to move one column per turn, and it may stop on a covered cell's top
c: Moves only across the tops of columns; cue to move any distance sideways, and it may stop on top of a stack whatever the stacking rules say

name: Tumbler's Poise
head: One hop, spend it or lose it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An unused charge pays a step instead of spending itself
a: One charge per turn: cue to hop this card one column sideways, and an unused charge spends itself on the next refresh
b: One charge per turn: cue to hop one column sideways; unused charges accumulate up to three
c: One charge per turn: cue to hop one cell in any direction, and an unused charge spends itself on the next refresh

name: Walking Through the Wall
head: Steps through what is in the way. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may chain through walls, turning once along the way
a: Cue: move this card through an occupied cell into the empty cell beyond it
b: Cue: move this card through any number of occupied cells in a straight line to the first empty one
c: Cue: move this card through an occupied cell into the cell beyond, and the card passed through is spotlit for the placement

name: Carries a chosen card
head: Takes a passenger. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Carried cards land on marks they match if any lie beside where it stops
a: Carries one chosen card wherever it moves, so the two relocate together
b: Carries one chosen card wherever it moves, and that card cannot be targeted while carried
c: Carries every card adjacent to it when it moves, so a cluster relocates as a unit

name: Colleano's Somersault
head: Cue: swaps positions with the single card covering it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card it swaps beneath it stays spotlit
a: Cue: swap places with the card directly covering this one
b: Cue: swap places with any card in the same stack
c: Swaps with the card covering it the first time each line it belongs to completes, once per Entrance refill

name: Foot of God
head: Cue: this card switches locations with any card on screen (grid, Entrance, or decks). **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card it swaps with has its new cell's mark rerolled to one it matches
a: Cue: swap places with any card on screen, including the Entrance and the decks
b: Cue: swap places with any card on the grid, in any grid
c: Cue: swap places with any card on screen, and the card swapped with keeps this card's stamp

name: Human Cannonball
head: Cue: fire the bottom card of any column to the top of any other column
a: Cue: fire the bottom card of any column to the top of any other column — **level 2:** The fired card may land on any empty cell whose mark it matches instead
b: Cue: fire the bottom card of any column into the same cell of an adjacent grid — **level 2:** The fired card may land on any empty cell whose mark it matches instead
c: Cue: fire this card to any empty cell in any grid, scoring every card it passes over — **level 2:** Fired onto a mark it matches, it fires again next placement

name: Block Pull card
head: After the game Jenga: pull one out and the pile shifts. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A buried card it moves fires its own effect as it lands
a: Clicking a buried card moves it to the top of the next-smallest stack, leaving a gap; too many gaps and this card is discarded
b: Clicking a buried card moves it to the top of the smallest stack on the grid, leaving a gap
c: Clicking a buried card moves it to the top of any stack you choose, leaving a gap that closes when a placement finishes resolving

name: The Bull
head: Pushes rather than swaps. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A pushed card may be pushed onto a stack
a: Placing this card onto an occupied cell pushes that card one further in the same direction; it is destroyed if there is no room
b: Placing this card onto an occupied cell pushes that card one further; if there is no room the placement is illegal
c: Placing this card pushes the whole line of cards beyond it along by one, like a shove

name: The Displacer
head: Swaps with what it would have pushed out. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The displaced card may be sent to any empty cell whose mark it matches
a: Placing this card onto an occupied cell swaps the two rather than stacking
b: Placing this card onto an occupied cell swaps the two, and the displaced card keeps this one's stamp
c: Placing this card onto an occupied cell swaps them, and both count as newly placed for line-completion purposes

name: The Dragon Meld
head: When a run of 4+ scores while this card is in it, that run can be relocated as a unit anywhere on the grid once, next turn. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Relocated as one unit, the run's lines re-score at their destination, and the run may land on top of occupied cells
a: When a run of four or more scores with this card in it, that run may be relocated as one unit anywhere on the grid next turn
b: When a run of four or more scores with this card in it, that run may be relocated as one unit next turn, and it may land on top of occupied cells
c: When any run of four or more scores, it may be relocated as one unit once, and this card is spent for the show

name: Blondin's Crossing
head: Once per show: shift an entire row one column left or right, wrapping around the grid edge
a: Once per show, shift a whole row one cell left or right, wrapping at the grid edge — **level 2:** It may shift a column as well as a row
b: Cue with three charges: shift a whole row or column one cell, wrapping at the edge — **level 2:** A shift that lands any card on a mark it matches refunds the charge
c: Once per show, shift a whole row one cell; the card pushed off the edge is discarded rather than wrapping — **level 2:** It may shift a column as well as a row

name: Earthquake card
head: Shakes the board apart
a: Scrambles the positions of every card on one grid
b: Scrambles the positions of every card on one grid, and any line the scramble happens to complete scores
c: Scrambles every card on one grid except those sitting on marks they match

name: Poker shuffle: pre-commit reshuffle
head: Rearrange before the square is full
a: Each Entrance refill, one placed card may be shifted to an empty cell, and a line the shift completes scores — **level 2:** Two shifts per refill
b: Placed cards may be shifted around freely until the first line completes — **level 2:** Shifting stays allowed until the second line completes
c: Placed cards may be shifted freely, but each shift discards one card from the Entrance — **level 2:** A shift onto a mark the card matches costs nothing

name: The Hanged Man
head: Consumable: flips the order of one entire stack, bottom becomes top
a: Consumable: flip one whole stack over, bottom becomes top
b: Consumable: flip one whole stack over, and every card in it re-triggers as it lands
c: Consumable: flip one whole column of the grid, so the top row becomes the bottom

name: Three-box shuffle
head: Shuffles three of them. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The three may be non-adjacent if all three sit on marks they match
a: Cue: rearrange the order of any three adjacent cards
b: Cue: rearrange the order of any three cards in one line
c: Cue: rearrange any three adjacent cards, and if the new order completes a meld it scores at once

name: Turntable card
head: Turns the board upside down
a: Flips the whole grid vertically, so the top row becomes the bottom
b: Flips the whole grid vertically, and every line re-scores in its new position
c: Flips the whole grid horizontally instead, so the left column becomes the right

name: Windy Day card
head: The wind takes the board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match do not blow away
a: At each Entrance refill, every card shifts one row or column at random
b: At each Entrance refill, every card shifts one cell in the same random direction
c: At each Entrance refill, every card shifts one cell in the same direction, and the direction is telegraphed one turn ahead

name: The Advancing Line
head: A gap in the line closes toward one end
a: When a card leaves a line, everything behind it shifts one step to close the gap — **level 2:** Cards that shift onto marks they match trigger twice
b: When a card leaves a line, everything behind it shifts to close the gap, and each card that moves triggers — **level 2:** Cards that shift onto marks they match trigger twice
c: When a card leaves a line, the gap stays open and can only be filled from the Entrance — **level 2:** A card placed into the gap onto a mark it matches scores the line twice

name: The High Dive
head: Cue: drop this card from the top of its column to the bottom, scoring bonus points per row fallen. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may dive to the bottom of any stack whose mark it matches, in any column
a: Cue: drop this card from the top of its stack to the bottom, scoring per row fallen
b: Cue: drop this card from the top of its stack to the bottom, scoring per row fallen and applying a status to each card it passes
c: Cue: drop this card through its column and on into the same column of the neighbouring grid, scoring per row fallen

name: The Slide
head: Everything moves at once, in one direction. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each sliding card stops at the first mark it matches
a: An action slides every card on the grid in one direction until it hits something, and merges happen where equals meet
b: An action slides every card in one direction, with no merging
c: An action slides one line in one direction rather than the whole grid

name: Water
head: Always seeks the lowest level
a: On each refresh, if an adjacent stack is lower, this card flows sideways onto it
b: On each refresh, this card flows toward the lowest stack on its grid, one step at a time
c: On each refresh, this card flows onto the lowest adjacent stack, and every card it passes catches a Wet status

name: Brass Ring
head: A token rotates one column per turn; if that column scores while the token is on it, the meld pays double and a Ticket Stub is banked. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The token moves where you choose instead of rotating
a: A token sits on one column and rotates one column per Entrance refresh; a line scored through that column pays double
b: A token sits on one cell and walks one cell per placement; the card placed on that cell scores twice
c: A token sits on one cell, and a line scored through it in every direction at once pays a large bonus

name: Checkers hop-capture card
head: Hops over what is in the way. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A hop that lands it on a mark it matches may hop again
a: May hop over an adjacent card into the cell beyond it
b: May hop over an adjacent card into the cell beyond, and may chain hops while empty cells follow
c: May hop over an adjacent card into the cell beyond, capturing what it jumped

name: Conveyor Deck
head: The board conveys. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose the direction the belt moves
a: Each refill every stock shifts one slot right; the card leaving the right edge is duplicated into the left stock
b: Each refill every stock shifts one slot right, and the left stock's top card is destroyed
c: Each refill every stock shifts one slot right, and you may pay points to freeze the belt once

name: Diabolo
head: Every Entrance refresh, alternates between two adjacent columns, granting bonus points to the top card of the column it leaves. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Returning to its mark pays the match again, and leaving it gives the bonus to every card in the column
a: On each Entrance refresh this card moves between two adjacent columns, giving bonus points to the top card of the column it leaves
b: On each Entrance refresh this card moves one cell along its row, wrapping, and gives +1 rank to the card it passes
c: On each line completion this card jumps to the mirrored cell across the grid's centre

name: The Bishop
head: May be placed onto any card along an open diagonal, capturing it; blocked by occupied slots between. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may also capture along its open row and column, like a queen
a: May be placed on any card along an open diagonal, capturing it; occupied cells in between block the path
b: May be placed on any card along an open diagonal, capturing it, and may pass through one blocking card, which is discarded too
c: May be placed on any card along an open diagonal, capturing it, and a capture raises this card's rank by 1

name: The King
head: Moves like a king, and is worth taking. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may step onto any mark it matches along a line, at any distance
a: Moves one cell in any direction by swapping only, never capturing; steps out of check on its own whenever you act; a chess card that captures it gains a large bonus and +1 rank
b: Moves one cell in any direction by swapping; if it is ever captured, the show ends immediately
c: Moves one cell in any direction by swapping, and every card orthogonally adjacent to it cannot be targeted by hazards

name: The Knight
head: Jumps in an L and takes what it lands on. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A capture that lands it on a mark it matches lets it jump again
a: May be placed on any card two cells and one cell away, discarding it and taking its place, ignoring stacking legality
b: May be placed on any card an L away, and the card it lands on is returned to the Entrance rather than discarded
c: May be placed on any card an L away in any grid, discarding it and taking its place

name: The Line of Sight
head: Clears what is directly beyond
a: Moving this card into a cell destroys whatever sits in the next cell along the same direction — **level 2:** It clears the next two cells along, not one
b: Moving this card into a cell destroys whatever sits in the next cell along, and this card gains its rank — **level 2:** It clears the next two cells along, not one
c: Moving this card into a cell pushes everything in that direction one cell, and what falls off the grid returns to the Entrance — **level 2:** What falls off the grid goes to the top of the stock you choose

name: The Pawn
head: Advances and takes on the diagonal. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Reaching the top of a stack whose mark it matches, it captures diagonally at once
a: Stacked under a card, it swaps upward with it on each refresh, two slots if it is bottommost; placed diagonally onto a card, it captures and replaces it
b: Stacked under a card, it swaps upward on each refresh; it captures diagonally, and reaching the top of its stack it becomes any other chess card you own
c: Stacked under a card, it swaps upward on each refresh; it captures diagonally, and each capture raises its rank by 1

name: The Procession
head: A meld that walks. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It collects twice from a column where any of its cards lands on a mark it matches
a: A scored meld walks one column toward the nearer edge each refill, its five cards swapping with whatever they meet, collecting a bonus from each column crossed
b: As (a), and it wraps once to the far edge
c: As (a), and each column it enters is re-scored as the line it now forms

name: The Rook
head: Takes along its row or column. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may also capture along open diagonals, like a queen
a: May be placed on any card along its open row or column, capturing it
b: May be placed on any card along its open row or column, capturing it, and may continue into the next grid at the same row
c: May be placed on any card along its open row or column, capturing it, but only toward the grid's edge

name: Cards bounce/swap between grids
head: Bounces a card to another grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card it sends lands on a mark it matches there, if one is free ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Cue: send a card to the same cell in another grid, or swap two cards between grids
b: Cue: send a card to any cell in an adjacent grid
c: Cue: swap two whole columns between two grids

name: The Long Step
head: Five to the left is the next grid over. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may move any distance up to five ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Cue: move this card five cells in any direction; five left or right lands in the same cell of the neighbouring grid
b: Cue: move any card five cells in any direction, crossing into the neighbouring grid if it runs off the edge
c: Cue: move this card five cells, and it may cross as many grid boundaries as the distance allows

name: The Tour Bus
head: A card that never stays in one town ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: At the end of each placement, this card moves to the same coordinate one grid to the right, wrapping at the last grid — **level 2:** It may skip a grid
b: At the end of each placement, this card moves one grid to the right and one cell down, wrapping at both edges — **level 2:** It may skip a grid
c: At the end of each placement this card moves one grid right, and scores a step for every grid it has visited this show — **level 2:** It scores a step for every mark it has matched on its tour

name: Centrifugal column (Wall of Death)
head: Nothing falls while it spins. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The spin also keeps its column's marks from being rerolled or swapped
a: Cards in this column cannot fall or be discarded while it spins, for a limited number of turns
b: Cards in this column cannot fall or be discarded while it spins, and the spin lasts until the column scores
c: Cards in this column cannot fall or be discarded, and the column also cannot be added to, for three turns

name: Quartz Stake
head: Some cards get pinned in place
a: Difficulty: a proportion of cards arrive pinned to their Entrance slot and cannot be placed until every other slot is empty
b: Difficulty: a proportion arrive pinned and, once placed, cannot be grabbed or moved by any effect
c: Difficulty: a proportion arrive pinned to their slot, and a pinned card that completes a line when finally placed pays double

name: Stone
head: Once placed on the grid this card cannot be grabbed again, and it scores a bonus for remaining unmoved ⚑ *pair review: overlaps your Q0015: a card locked in place that scores more*
a: Once placed, this card can never be grabbed again, and scores a bonus for staying unmoved
b: Once placed, this card can never be grabbed again, and its bonus grows each show it stays put
c: Once placed, this card can be moved once per show, and its bonus resets when it is

name: Straitjacket
head: Starts each show unable to be moved; frees itself and scores bonus points the first time its column scores
a: Starts each show unable to be moved; frees itself and scores bonus points the first time its column scores — **level 2:** Placed on its mark it starts free and pays its bonus at once
b: Starts each show unable to be moved; frees itself the first time any line it belongs to scores, and the bonus scales with how long it stayed bound — **level 2:** Its bound count keeps growing while it sits on its mark after freeing
c: Starts each show bound and never frees itself, but while it is bound the cards beside it cannot be moved, discarded or hit by a hazard — **level 2:** Its protection reaches its whole row

name: The Handicap
head: Locks another card in place, and that card scores double. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may re-lock a different card at each Entrance refill
a: Cue: lock any one other card on the grid against being grabbed for the show; it scores double
b: Cue: lock any one other card on the grid for the show; it scores double, and the lock also protects it from every hazard
c: Cue: lock any one other card on the grid for the show; it scores double while this card is uncovered

name: The Light and Heavy Chest
head: Yours to move, nobody else's. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its protection covers the cards beside it too
a: You may always grab this card, and no board effect or hazard can move or discard it
b: You may always grab this card, and no effect at all can move it, including your own others
c: You may always grab this card and everything above it, and hazards cannot touch its whole stack

name: Boss: adjacency-only placement
head: Boss: cards must touch
a: Boss: cards may only be placed adjacent to a card already on the grid
b: Boss: cards may only be placed adjacent to a card already placed, diagonals not counting
c: Boss: cards must be placed adjacent to the card placed immediately before, forming a path

name: Column-locked entrance placement
head: One card per column, per refresh. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own column accepts two cards per refresh ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) only restrict you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Each column accepts only one Entrance card per refresh, from whichever of the five you choose
b: Each column accepts only one Entrance card per refresh, and the column is chosen for you at random
c: Each column accepts one Entrance card per refresh, and filling all five in one refresh pays a bonus

name: Cross-path entrance bonus
head: Rewards cards crossing paths. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card that crosses others and lands on a mark it matches counts each crossing twice
a: A card crosses another when it comes from a slot further left and lands in a column further right, or the reverse. Scores a bonus when Entrance cards cross each other's paths on the way to the cells they are placed in
b: Scores a bonus per crossing, so an entirely reversed Entrance pays most
c: Scores a bonus when Entrance cards cross, and a larger one if every card crosses at least one other

name: Leader elemental fears
head: Afraid of the sharp ones. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On its mark it stops fearing, and each feared-suit card beside it pays it a step ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) only restrict you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Some leaders fear fire or knives and cannot be placed on cards of those suits
b: Some leaders fear one suit, chosen at run start, and cannot be placed adjacent to it either
c: Some leaders fear one suit and cannot be placed on it, but score double when they end a show next to it

name: The Diva
head: Will not go on second. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its skill stays enabled when it is placed second ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what its skill is*
a: The strongest card of its class, but its skill is disabled unless it is placed first each show
b: The strongest card of its class, but its skill is disabled unless it is the first card placed in its grid
c: The strongest card of its class; placing it first each show also buffs everything placed after it

name: The Invisible Wall
head: Seals a column against everything. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The seal lasts two turns
a: Cue: seal one empty column for a turn so nothing may enter or leave it, hazards included
b: Cue: seal one column for a turn, cards and all, so nothing in it can be moved, scored or hit
c: Cue: seal one column for a turn, and the cards in it pay their matches again when the seal lifts

name: Sleight of Hand
head: The card does not land where you put it. (line 937). **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards placed onto marks they match always land where you chose ⚑ *pair review: it only makes placing harder; it reads as a hazard*
a: Cards you place have a chance to land in a different cell than the one you chose, and you are shown where after the fact
b: Cards you place always land one cell off in a direction this card names, so the offset is learnable
c: Cards you place land where you chose, but this card silently swaps two already-placed cards each placement

name: The Catcher
head: Takes a card out of somebody else's move
a: Cue: the next card moved by any effect is intercepted and lands on a cell you choose instead — **level 2:** The intercepted card fires its own effect as it lands
b: Cue: the next card moved by any effect is intercepted and lands adjacent to this card instead — **level 2:** The intercepted card may land on any empty cell whose mark it matches
c: Every card moved by any effect while this card is spotlit is intercepted and lands adjacent to this card, once per Entrance refill — **level 2:** The intercepted card may land on any empty cell whose mark it matches

name: The Crosswind
head: Things do not land where they were aimed
a: Any card moved more than two cells is deflected one cell perpendicular to its travel — **level 2:** A deflected card that lands on a mark it matches scores its line double
b: Any card moved more than two cells is deflected one cell, in a direction that flips each placement — **level 2:** A deflected card that lands on a mark it matches scores its line double
c: Any card moved more than two cells is deflected one cell, and a deflected card that still completes a line scores double — **level 2:** You choose the direction of the deflection

name: The Dzhigit's Pickup
head: During an Entrance refresh, once armed by cue, intercepts one falling card as it drops and redirects it to any column. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may also intercept a card an effect is moving, not only a refresh drop
a: Armed by cue: intercepts one card as the Entrance refreshes and redirects it to any column
b: Armed by cue: intercepts one card as the Entrance refreshes and redirects it to any cell in any grid
c: Armed by cue: intercepts one card as the Entrance refreshes and sends it to the bottom of the deck instead

name: Deja Vu card
head: Remembers where it was. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It returns to any empty cell whose mark it matches, not only the cell it left
a: Remembers its cell; the next time that cell is empty, it returns there from anywhere
b: Remembers its cell; the next time that cell is empty it returns there, and scores a bonus for coming home
c: Remembers every cell it has occupied, and returns to whichever of them opens first

name: Stowaway card
head: Slides into the gap once it has scored
a: After it scores, this card moves itself into any empty cell you choose — **level 2:** It may move twice
b: After it scores, this card moves itself into the nearest empty cell in its grid — **level 2:** It prefers an empty cell whose mark it matches
c: After it scores, this card moves into an empty cell that would complete a line, if one exists — **level 2:** It prefers an empty cell whose mark it matches

name: Bottom Deal
head: Cue: this turn, the Entrance refills from the bottom of the deck instead of the top. **Level 2, on its own mark:** At each refresh you choose, stock by stock, whether it draws from the top or the bottom
a: Cue: the next Entrance refresh draws from the bottom of the deck instead of the top
b: While this card is on the grid, every Entrance refresh draws from the bottom of the deck
c: Cue: look at the bottom five cards of the deck and move one of them to the top

name: Heavy
head: After any shuffle or return to deck, this card sinks to the deck bottom
a: After any shuffle or return to the deck, this card sinks to the bottom
b: After any shuffle this card sinks to the bottom, and once placed it cannot be moved
c: This card sinks to the bottom of the deck and drags the card above it down with it

name: Helium
head: After any shuffle or return to deck, this card rises to the top and is always the first card drawn on refresh
a: After any shuffle or return to the deck, this card rises to the top and is drawn first
b: After any shuffle this card rises to the top, and on the grid it floats to the top of its stack
c: This card rises to the top of the deck and cannot be placed below the third row of any grid

name: The Ambitious Card
head: Always rises to the top of the deck after any shuffle or discard, and scores bonus points if drawn the same show it was discarded. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Discarded from its mark, it rises to the top of whichever stock you choose
a: Always rises to the top of the deck after any shuffle or discard, and scores a bonus if drawn in the same show it was discarded
b: Always rises to the top of the deck after any shuffle or discard
c: Always rises to the top after any shuffle or discard, and each trip through the discard raises its rank by 1

name: The Wedding Band
head: Two cards that travel together
a: Applied to two cards: the pair always shuffles adjacent and is always drawn together — **level 2:** When the partner is drawn it goes straight onto an empty cell whose mark it matches, if there is one
b: Applied to two cards: the pair always shuffles adjacent, and if one is drawn the other joins the same Entrance — **level 2:** When the partner is drawn it goes straight onto an empty cell whose mark it matches, if there is one
c: Applied to two cards: the pair always shuffles adjacent, and separating them on the board destroys the stamp — **level 2:** Separated on the board, the stamp survives while either sits on a mark it matches

name: Metamorphosis
head: Cue: swap this card with any card in the deck (seen or unseen), taking its board position. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may swap with a card in the discard as well as the deck
a: Cue: swap this card with any card in the deck, seen or unseen, taking its position
b: Cue: swap this card with any card in the deck you have already seen this run
c: Cue: swap any card on the grid with any card in the deck

name: The Call Sheet
head: Fetches whatever the line is missing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may pull a card that would also match the mark of the cell it completes
a: Cue while spotlit: pull from the deck the card that would complete this card's row, if one exists
b: Cue while spotlit: pull from the deck a card that would complete any line on this grid, and place it yourself
c: Once per Entrance refill, automatically pulls into the entrance the card that would complete whichever line is closest to done

name: The Card Index
head: Cue, once per show: search the deck for any card and put it into the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its search may reach into the discard
a: Cue, once per show: search the deck for any card and put it into the Entrance
b: Cue, once per show: search the deck for any card and put it on top of the deck
c: Cue, once per show: name a card; if it is in the top ten of the deck it goes to the Entrance, otherwise nothing happens

name: The Tutor
head: Reach into the deck and take exactly what you need
a: Consumable: name any card in your deck and put it into the entrance
b: Consumable: name any card in your deck and put it directly onto any empty cell
c: Consumable: name any card property - a suit, a rank, a class - and pull the first matching card from the deck into the entrance

name: Madame Zora's Eye
head: The next card to be drawn is always visible above the deck slot while this card is anywhere in play. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It shows the next card of every stock
a: The next card to be drawn is always shown above the deck
b: The next three cards to be drawn are always shown above the deck
c: The next card to be drawn is shown, and once per show you may send it to the bottom instead

name: The Programme
head: The running order, printed in advance
a: While this card is on the grid, the next two entrance refreshes are shown before they arrive — **level 2:** It shows one refresh further ahead
b: While this card is on the grid, the whole remaining deck order is visible — **level 2:** Once per refill you may swap two cards in it
c: While this card is on the grid, the next refresh is shown, and one card in it may be swapped for the card after it — **level 2:** It shows one refresh further ahead

name: The Scry
head: Look ahead, and put the bad ones on the bottom
a: On each entrance refresh, look at the top three cards of the deck and send any number of them to the bottom — **level 2:** It looks at five instead of three
b: On each entrance refresh, look at the top three and reorder them freely, but none may be binned — **level 2:** It looks at five instead of three
c: Once per Entrance refill, look at the top five and send any number to the bottom — **level 2:** One of them may go on top of the stock you choose

name: The Cooler
head: Consumable, once per run: replaces the remaining deck with a copy in a chosen order
a: Consumable, once per run: replace the rest of the deck with the same cards in an order you choose
b: Consumable, once per run: reorder the next ten cards of the deck
c: Consumable, once per run: reorder the rest of the deck, but the show's goal rises 20%

name: The Reshuffle Clause
head: Order restored, on your terms
a: On each entrance refresh you may move one undrawn card to the top of the deck — **level 2:** It may move two cards
b: On each entrance refresh you may move one undrawn card to the top or the bottom of the deck — **level 2:** It may move two cards
c: Once per Entrance refill you may sort the undrawn deck by suit, by rank, or by class — **level 2:** You may sort one stock or the whole deck

name: The Suit Call
head: Stacks the deck around one property. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may name a rank alongside the suit
a: Cue: name a suit; every card of that suit in the deck rises above every card that is not
b: Cue: name a suit or a rank; every matching card in the deck rises to the top, in the order they were shuffled
c: Cue: name a suit; matching cards rise to the top, and the cards they displace are binned rather than sinking

name: The Tarot Reading
head: Rearranges what is coming. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Once per Entrance refill instead of once per show
a: Cue, once per show: look at the top five cards of the deck and reorder them freely
b: Cue, once per show: look at the top five cards, reorder them, and send one to the bottom
c: Cue, once per show: look at the top five, reorder them, and put one on top of the stock you choose

name: Blowdown
head: At show start and each Entrance refresh, a random seeded card is discarded from the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which incoming card is discarded ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you cards unless something you hold pays for discards*
a: At each Entrance refresh one random incoming card is discarded before you see the rest
b: At each Entrance refresh one random incoming card is discarded and replaced from the deck
c: At show start only, the first Entrance is dealt one card short

name: The Grand Entry
head: After the Cryptid mod's Effarcire: deals the whole deck at once. **Level 2, on its own mark:** After it deals, you may place two cards per turn
a: When a show begins, the entire deck is dealt into the Entrance at once
b: When a show begins, the entire deck is dealt out, but only five may be placed per turn
c: Cue once per show to deal the whole remaining deck into the Entrance

name: Flash Mob
head: Cue, once per show: deploy the entire Entrance onto the grid in one action, columns assigned left-to-right automatically. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards it places onto marks they match score their lines twice
a: Cue, once per show: place the whole Entrance onto the grid at once, filling left to right
b: Cue, once per show: place the whole Entrance onto the grid at once into cells you pick, resolving every line completion together
c: Cue, once per show: place the whole Entrance into a single row or column at once

name: Popcorn Cascade
head: Whenever a stack of five or more cards scores, refill 1 card into the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The refilled card comes from the stock you choose
a: Whenever a stack of five or more cards scores, refill one card into the Entrance
b: Whenever any line scores, refill one card into the Entrance
c: Whenever a line scores, refill one Entrance card for every card in that line above four

name: The Grease Joint
head: At show start, discards the bottom card of the deck, then refills 1 card into the Entrance
a: At show start, discard the bottom card of the deck and refill one Entrance card — **level 2:** You choose which of the bottom three cards is discarded
b: At show start, discard the bottom three cards of the deck and refill one Entrance card — **level 2:** Look at the three first, and keep one on top instead
c: At every Entrance refresh, discard the bottom card of the deck and refill one extra Entrance card — **level 2:** You choose which of the bottom three cards is discarded

name: The Pineapple
head: Draw more than you can keep
a: The Entrance deals more cards than you may place, and the remainder are discarded at the end of the turn — **level 2:** One card per turn that would be discarded may go back on top of its stock instead
b: The Entrance deals more cards than you may place, and the remainder carry into the next Entrance — **level 2:** The carried-over cards may be reordered
c: The Entrance deals more than you may place, and you choose which to discard before seeing where they would fit — **level 2:** One card per turn that would be discarded may go back on top of its stock instead

name: The Serpent
head: The Entrance always refills to a fixed size
