a: After every placement or discard, the Entrance refills to a fixed smaller size — **level 2:** You choose which stock each refilled slot draws from
b: After every placement or discard, the Entrance refills to its full size immediately — **level 2:** You choose which stock each refilled slot draws from
c: After every placement, the Entrance refills by one card rather than waiting to empty — **level 2:** You choose which stock the refilled slot draws from

name: The Stray Whistle
head: One card jumps the queue. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card drops onto an empty cell whose mark it matches, if there is one
a: A random Entrance card is placed early into the lowest empty cell of a random column
b: A random Entrance card is placed early into the lowest empty cell of a column you choose
c: A random Entrance card is placed early into the lowest empty cell of a random column, and scores double if it completes a line

name: Clown Car
head: On Entrance refresh, adds one extra card into this card's column, plus one more per Clown-class card scored last placement. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which stock the extra card comes from
a: Each Entrance refresh deals one extra card, drawn from the stock under this card's column
b: Each Entrance refresh deals one extra card from the stock under this card's column, plus one more for every Clown-class card on the grid
c: The Entrance holds six cards instead of five while this card is on the grid

name: The Narrow Gate
head: Fewer choices, better cards. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which three stocks feed it
a: The entrance holds three cards instead of five, and every card in it is drawn from the top third of the deck by rank
b: The entrance holds three cards, and each placement you may name one property the refresh must match
c: The entrance holds three cards, and a refill whose three cards all land in one line pays a step

name: The Second Door
head: A separate way onto the board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its two cards may be placed in one action
a: While this card is on the grid, a second entrance of two cards opens, feeding only this card's grid
b: While this card is on the grid, a second entrance of two cards opens and feeds any grid, but its cards must be placed adjacent to an existing card
c: While this card is on the grid, a second entrance of two cards opens and is refreshed from the discard rather than the deck

name: The Wide Doorway
head: More cards waiting to come on. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The two extra slots draw from stocks you choose
a: The entrance holds seven cards instead of five
b: The entrance holds seven cards, and refills when three are empty
c: The entrance holds seven cards, and the two extra slots are refilled only once per Entrance refill

name: Discard-to-deck on score
head: Puts two back in the deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The returned cards go on top of the stocks you choose
a: On score, two random cards return from the discard to the deck
b: On score, two cards of your choice return from the discard to the deck
c: On score, two random cards return from the discard; an exhausted version returns four and then never fires again

name: The Egg Bag
head: Cue while spotlit: stash the top discard inside this card; when this card scores, the stashed card returns to the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The stashed card returns straight onto an empty cell whose mark it matches
a: Cue while spotlit: stash the top card of the discard inside this one; it returns to the Entrance when this card scores
b: Cue while spotlit: stash any card from the discard inside this one; it returns to the Entrance when this card scores
c: Cue while spotlit: stash the top discard inside this one; it returns at the start of the next show instead

name: The Lost Property Office
head: The discard is a second deck
a: When the deck empties, the discard becomes the deck without shuffling, so the show replays in the order you discarded — **level 2:** It also takes effect when any single stock empties, not only the whole deck
b: When the deck empties, the discard is shuffled and becomes the deck, but each card that returns this way scores a step less — **level 2:** It also takes effect when any single stock empties, not only the whole deck
c: The discard is drawn from directly whenever the entrance would refill with fewer than five cards — **level 2:** You choose which discard card fills the slot

name: The Second Curtain Call
head: Call the last one back
a: Consumable: return the most recently discarded card to the entrance
b: Consumable: return any one card from the discard to the entrance
c: Consumable: return any three cards from the discard to the top of the deck

name: Crooked Deck Solitaire
head: After A Solitaire Mystery's Cheatdeck Solitaire: the deck is not honest ⚑ *pair review: it is a hazard in (a) and (c) and a hidden buff with a cost in (b)*
a: The deck quietly favours cards you do not need, and an effect can expose and correct it — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark the bias reverses: each refill deals at least one card that matches an uncovered mark
b: The deck quietly favours cards you DO need, and the show's goal rises to compensate — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, the goal does not rise
c: The deck is stacked against you in a way stated up front, so it is a constraint rather than a trick — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark the bias reverses: each refill deals at least one card that matches an uncovered mark

name: Lucky Streak
head: Once it scores, random outcomes stop repeating. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It is active from the start of the show
a: Once it scores, a random outcome that repeats the last one is rerolled, for the rest of the show
b: Once it scores, every random outcome for the rest of the show may be rerolled once
c: Once it scores, every random outcome for the rest of the show is rolled twice and the better result kept

name: The Redeal
head: Gather what is left and lay it out again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A redeal also rerolls the marks of every empty cell
a: When no legal move remains, you may gather the unplayed cards, shuffle and lay them out again, a limited number of times
b: When no legal move remains you may redeal without shuffling, preserving the order
c: Cue at any time: gather the Entrance and every stock, shuffle, and deal them out again; each redeal discards one Entrance card

name: Deck auto-slotter
head: Slots itself in from the deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Landing on a mark it matches, it returns to the deck after its lines score, to slot itself again
a: While in the deck, this card moves itself into any legal empty cell that becomes available
b: While in the deck, this card moves itself into a legal empty cell once per show
c: While in the deck, this card moves itself into an empty cell that would complete a line

name: Psycho
head: Every Entrance refresh, automatically plays the top card of the deck into this card's column
a: Every Entrance refresh, the top card of the deck is played automatically into the lowest empty cell of this card's column — **level 2:** The auto-played card goes to a cell in its column whose mark it matches, if there is one
b: Every Entrance refresh, the top card of the deck is played automatically into a random empty cell of this card's grid — **level 2:** The auto-played card goes to any cell whose mark it matches
c: Every Entrance refresh, the top card of the deck is played automatically into the lowest empty cell of this card's column, and this card scores for each one that completes a line — **level 2:** The auto-played card goes to a cell in its column whose mark it matches, if there is one

name: The Voice From The Wings
head: Working before it is ever drawn
a: While this card is still in the deck, every line that scores its suit scores an extra step — **level 2:** On its mark, the extra step also applies to lines through its own cell
b: While this card is still in the deck, every line that scores its suit scores an extra step, and the bonus is lost the moment it is drawn — **level 2:** On its mark the lost bonus returns for the lines through its cell
c: While this card is in the deck it fires its own effect once per Entrance refill at half strength, and at full strength once placed — **level 2:** On its mark its effect fires once more at each refill, at full strength

name: The Comedic Drop
head: Cue: discard this card mid-show for a bonus larger than scoring it would have paid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Discarded from its mark, it goes to the top of the stock you choose instead of the discard
a: Cue: discard this card mid-show for a bonus larger than scoring it would have paid
b: Cue: discard this card mid-show for a bonus scaling with how many cards are still in the deck
c: Cue: discard this card mid-show for a bonus, and it returns to the deck at the start of the next show

name: The Death Rattle
head: It goes off when it goes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its effect fires from the cell it left, so it reaches the lines through its mark
a: When this card is destroyed or discarded, its effect fires once from wherever it went
b: When this card is destroyed or discarded, its effect fires once, and again the next time it is drawn
c: When any card carrying this stamp leaves play by any route, its effect fires from the discard at the end of the placement

name: The Empty Chair
head: Still working from the pile. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, its discard effect also works from the board
a: While this card is in the discard, every line that scores its suit scores an extra step
b: While this card is in the discard, every line that scores its suit scores an extra step, and the bonus grows with the size of the discard
c: While this card is in the discard it keeps firing its own effect once per Entrance refill, at half strength

name: The Escape Map
head: When discarded, reveals part of the world map's fog of war. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which part of the map it reveals
a: When discarded, reveals part of the world map's fog
b: When discarded, reveals the next two map nodes and their contents
c: When discarded, reveals part of the map and may be recovered from the discard once per run to do it again

name: Blue Joker
head: Paid by what is left to draw. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts the cards in the discard as still in the deck
a: Scores bonus points per card remaining in the deck
b: Scores bonus points per card remaining in the deck, halving once the deck is under a quarter full
c: Scores bonus points per card remaining, or per card already drawn, whichever is higher

name: The Last Cards
head: Strongest when there is almost nothing left. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The step is paid again for each stock that empties while it sits there
a: Scores a step for each Entrance stock that has run empty
b: Scores a step for each Entrance stock that has run empty, doubled once every stock but one is empty
c: Scores nothing until a stock runs empty, then a step for every five cards the remaining stocks hold

name: The Trimmed Bill
head: A smaller deck is a stronger deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also counts the cards in the discard
a: Every card scores an extra step for each five cards by which the deck is under its starting size
b: Every card scores an extra step for each five cards removed from the run permanently, not merely drawn
c: Every card scores an extra step per five cards removed from the run, and the run target rises to match

name: The Census
head: Reads the deck's balance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also counts the suits of the marks matched this show
a: Scores a bonus scaling with how evenly your deck's suits are balanced
b: Scores a bonus scaling with how UNEVENLY your deck's suits are balanced
c: Scores a bonus per suit your deck holds at least five of

name: The Ledger
head: Deck shape sets the defaults. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may pick the suit instead
a: At show start, whichever suit your deck holds most of scores double all show
b: At show start, whichever suit your deck holds LEAST of scores double all show
c: At show start, the suit you hold most of scores double and the one you hold least scores nothing

name: The Purist
head: Paid for what your deck does not contain. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also pays for each class your deck lacks
a: Scores a large bonus while your deck contains no cards of a named suit
b: Scores a large bonus while your deck contains no cards of a named class
c: Scores a bonus for each suit your deck contains none of, so a narrow deck pays most

name: The Repertoire Check
head: Reads class spread rather than count. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Classes of cards sitting on marks they match count twice ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0072, which you approved: distinct classes, counted on the grid*
a: Scores a bonus per distinct class present in your deck
b: Scores a bonus per distinct class present in your deck, doubled if every class is
c: Scores a bonus per distinct class in your deck, and a penalty for each class you hold more than three of

name: Certificate
head: Deals in a card with a stamp on it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each Entrance refill while it sits on its mark adds one more such card
a: At the start of each show, adds a random card carrying a random stamp to the Entrance
b: At the start of each show, adds a random card carrying a stamp you choose
c: At the start of each show, adds a random card with a random stamp, and the stamp is kept even if the card is discarded

name: Hall of Mirrors
head: Boss: duplicates the grid's reflection with fake copies of your cards interleaved into rows; they score 0
a: Boss: fake copies of your cards are interleaved into every row; they score 0 and cannot be removed
b: Boss: fake copies of your cards fill every empty cell and score 0; a fake is dispelled when a card matching its rank or suit is placed beside it
c: Boss: each grid is mirrored by a fake grid, and lines completed in the fake grid subtract from your score

name: Pickpocket card
head: Adds a card if it never performs
a: If this card is never scored during a show, it adds an extra card to the deck — **level 2:** You choose the card it adds, from the discard pile
b: If this card is never scored, it adds an extra card to the deck and gains +1 rank — **level 2:** You choose the card it adds, from the discard pile
c: If this card is never scored, it steals a card from the town and adds it to your deck — **level 2:** You choose the card it steals from the town

name: Cookie Jar card
head: After Yu-Gi-Oh!'s Pot of Greed: alone, it doubles. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which Entrance stocks the two cards are drawn into
a: When this card sits alone in a cell with nothing adjacent, discard it and draw two cards from the deck
b: When this card sits alone in its row, discard it and draw two cards into the Entrance
c: When the first card is placed adjacent to it, it goes to the discard and two cards are drawn into the Entrance; its cell keeps its mark, and the next card to hit that mark pays the match twice

name: The Signed Card
head: Every card the game creates comes out as this one. (line 988). **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may re-name the card at each Entrance refill while it sits there
a: Name a card: the next card any effect creates is that card instead of what it would have made
b: Name a card: every card any effect creates is that card instead, for the rest of the show
c: Name a card: when it leaves the board, the next card created anywhere is it, returning

name: Loaned temporary cards
head: Borrowed, and due back
a: Creates a temporary card that lasts a few shows and then leaves — **level 2:** The loan lasts one show longer
b: Creates a temporary card that lasts a few shows; if it scores in every one of them, it stays — **level 2:** It may miss one show
c: Creates a temporary card on loan; keeping it past its term costs one card from your deck each show — **level 2:** The first overdue show costs nothing

name: Spirit Photo
head: Consumable: creates an intangible ghost copy of an owned card that plays for one show at half score, then disappears
a: Consumable: an intangible ghost copy of one owned card plays for one show at half score, then vanishes
b: Consumable: an intangible ghost copy of one owned card plays for three shows at half score, then vanishes
c: Consumable: an intangible ghost copy of one owned card plays at full score for one show, and cannot be targeted

name: The Guest Star
head: Consumable: a random Legendary card joins the deck for exactly 3 shows then departs, kept permanently if a hidden condition is met during its stay
a: Consumable: a random Legendary joins the deck for exactly three shows, kept permanently if a hidden condition is met while it is there
b: Consumable: a random Legendary joins the deck for exactly three shows, then leaves
c: Consumable: a random Legendary joins the deck permanently, but one card of the same rarity leaves

name: The Souvenir Stand
head: A card that only lasts the evening
a: Consumable: create a copy of any card on the grid; the copy exists for this show only
b: Consumable: create a copy of any card on the grid that lasts one placement
c: Consumable: create a copy of any card on the grid; it lasts the show, and if it is still on the board at show end it becomes permanent

name: Cat Tag
head: Two of the same merge upward
a: Two of these at the same level merge into one of the next level when combined
b: Two of these merge into the next level, and the top level converts into a permanent card
c: Any two identical consumables merge into a stronger single one

name: DNA
head: Copies your opening card
a: If the first card you place after this one each show completes no line, a permanent copy of it joins the deck and arrives in the Entrance — **level 2:** It copies the first card even when that card completes a line
b: If the first card you place after this one each show completes no line, a copy of it joins the deck for that show only — **level 2:** It copies the first card even when that card completes a line
c: The first card placed after this one each show is copied permanently, whatever else you place after it — **level 2:** The copy arrives in the next Entrance refill

name: Genie's Wish
head: Consumable: choose any card in your deck and create a full copy of it in the Entrance for this show, which becomes permanent in the deck afterward
a: Consumable: choose any card in your deck; a copy appears in the Entrance and joins the deck permanently after the show
b: Consumable: choose any card in your deck; a copy appears in the Entrance for this show only
c: Consumable: choose any card in your deck and duplicate it permanently, but the original is out for the rest of the show

name: Invisible Joker
head: Held long enough, it copies something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It needs only one show
a: After being held through two shows, cue to destroy it and duplicate another card you own at random
b: After being held through two shows, cue to destroy it and duplicate another card you choose
c: After being held through two shows it duplicates a random card of yours automatically, then leaves

name: Pepper's Ghost
head: While spotlit, an intangible duplicate of this card appears in the opposite zone; it scores in melds but cannot be touched, moved, or targeted
a: While spotlit, an intangible duplicate appears in the mirrored cell of its grid; it melds but cannot be touched, moved or targeted — **level 2:** You choose the duplicate's cell
b: While spotlit, an intangible duplicate appears in the mirrored cell of its own grid, or in the same cell of the grid to its left if there is one; it melds but cannot be touched — **level 2:** You choose the duplicate's cell
c: While spotlit, an intangible duplicate appears in any empty cell you choose, and vanishes when this card is covered — **level 2:** The duplicate stays when this card is covered

name: Perkeo
head: Copies a consumable, for free
a: At the start of each show, creates a slot-free copy of one random consumable you hold — **level 2:** The copy is made at the first Entrance refill after it lands on its mark, and again at each refill while it stays
b: At the start of each show, creates a copy of one consumable you choose — **level 2:** The copy is made at the first Entrance refill after it lands on its mark, and again at each refill while it stays
c: Every consumable you use leaves a slot-free copy of itself behind, once per show — **level 2:** Its copy is not limited to once per show

name: SUS
head: Copies one card and destroys the rest. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It destroys only the Entrance cards you choose
a: At each show's end, copies one card from the Entrance and destroys all the others
b: At each show's end, copies one card of your choice from the Entrance and destroys the rest
c: At each show's end, copies the Entrance card that scored most and destroys the rest

name: The Avatar
head: This card copies another deck card's name, class, and identity for all checks until it has scored 3 times, at which point it is unmasked
a: Copies another deck card's name, class and identity for every check until it has scored three times, then is unmasked — **level 2:** Scores while it sits there do not count toward the three
b: Copies another deck card's identity permanently, and can never be unmasked — **level 2:** You may unmask it by cue and re-mask it as another card at the next refill
c: Copies another deck card's identity until it is covered; being covered unmasks it — **level 2:** Being covered does not unmask it

name: The Costume Fitting
head: On show start, copies the stamp of one adjacent card for the duration of the show
a: When placed, copies the stamp of one adjacent card for the whole show — **level 2:** It may copy the stamp of any card in its lines
b: When placed, copies the stamp of any card on the grid for the whole show — **level 2:** It copies two stamps
c: Copies the stamp of the most recently placed adjacent card, updating whenever a new neighbour is placed — **level 2:** It keeps the copied stamp when the neighbour leaves

name: The Imitator
head: Choose a deck card at acquisition: this card scores 150% of that card's base points, but only while the original is not on the board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also copies the original's skill
a: Choose a deck card when this is acquired: this card scores 150% of that card's base points, but only while the original is off the board
b: Choose a deck card when this is acquired: this card scores 150% of its base points whenever the original is also on the board
c: This card copies whichever card scored highest last show, at 150% of its base points

name: Three Of A Kind Merges
head: Copies combine into something stronger. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Two copies are enough when one of them sits on a mark it matches
a: Three copies of the same card merge automatically into one stronger version, and three of those merge again
b: Three copies merge into one stronger version, once only, with no second tier
c: Three copies merge into one stronger version, and you choose when rather than it happening automatically

name: Tintype
head: Prints a copy of what made it
a: On acquisition, permanently copies the rank and suit of the card it was created from
b: On acquisition, permanently copies the rank, suit and stamp of the card it was created from
c: On acquisition, copies the rank and suit of the card it was created from, and re-copies whenever that card changes

name: Arsonist
head: Burns the board down after a big hand: the hand you name when placing it
a: If a named hand scores, every card on the grid is destroyed after scoring resolves — **level 2:** Cards sitting on marks they match are spared the fire
b: If a named hand scores, every card in that line is destroyed after scoring resolves — **level 2:** Cards sitting on marks they match are spared the fire
c: If the named hand scores, every card on the grid burns, and each pays its rank into the bucket of the line that burned it; a card in no complete line pays into special — **level 2:** You choose which cards burn

name: Milk Can
head: Cue: place one grid card inside the can, safe and out of play; cue again on a later turn to retrieve it to the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A retrieved card may go onto an empty cell you choose instead of the Entrance
a: Cue: put one grid card safely out of play; cue again later to bring it back to the Entrance
b: Cue: put one grid card out of play; it returns on its own at the start of the next show
c: Cue: put up to three grid cards out of play, retrieving them one at a time

name: Corner the Market card
head: After the board game Monopoly: corners the market on a card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Four of the card are enough
a: Scoring five identical cards in one line removes that card from future generation
b: Scoring five identical cards in one line removes it from generation and pays you every time it would have appeared
c: Scoring five identical cards in one line removes it from generation for the rest of the run, and you may reverse it once

name: Queen's Gambit
head: Sacrifices a card out of the best hand. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The rare card it creates arrives in the Entrance
a: If a line scores as the highest hand, one named card in it is destroyed and a rare card is created
b: If a line scores as the highest hand, one card of your choice in it is destroyed and a rare card created
c: Any line that scores above a threshold destroys its highest card and creates a rare one

name: The Called Shot
head: Takes the top off a stack
a: Destroys the top card of any stack, leaving the rest intact — **level 2:** It takes the top card off two stacks
b: Destroys the top card of any stack and this card takes its place — **level 2:** You choose whether it takes the top card's place or stays
c: Destroys the top card of any stack, and the card beneath is spotlit for the placement — **level 2:** It takes the top card off two stacks

name: The Kite
head: Sends a card away and brings it back better. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card lands on any empty cell whose mark matches its new rank, your choice; if there is none, it lands where it left
a: Cue: send a card out of play and name the Entrance refill it returns; it lands with +1 rank per Entrance refill aloft, up to +3
b: Cue: send a card out of play; it returns on its own after three Entrance refills with +3 rank
c: Cue: send a card out of play indefinitely; it gains +1 rank per Entrance refill aloft with no cap, but a hazard may lose it

name: The Tower
head: Levels a column for points
a: Consumable: destroy an entire column; half the summed rank of its cards is paid as flat points into the special bucket and the cards go to the discard
b: Consumable: destroy an entire column; the full summed rank is paid into the column bucket
c: Consumable: destroy any line; half its summed rank is paid into the special bucket, the cards go to the discard, and every cell keeps its mark

name: The Wishbone
head: After the Cryptid mod's Astral in a Bottle: destroyed, it upgrades something at random
a: When destroyed, applies a random upgrade to a random card you own — **level 2:** You choose the card
b: When destroyed, applies a random upgrade to a card you choose — **level 2:** You choose the upgrade too
c: When destroyed, applies an upgrade and a drawback to two different random cards — **level 2:** You choose which card takes the drawback

name: Bian Lian
head: Cue: instantly swap this card's rank and suit with an adjacent card's. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may swap only the property you choose, rank or suit
a: Cue: exchange this card's rank and suit with an orthogonally adjacent card's
b: Cue: exchange this card's suit with any card's in its grid, leaving both ranks alone
c: Every time a line it belongs to completes, it swaps rank and suit with a random adjacent card, free and automatic

name: Brittle Candy
head: Stamps whatever scores, for a while. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The stamp goes to the card of your choice in the line
a: For the next several placements, adds a random stamp to the last scoring card of each line
b: For the next several placements, adds a stamp of your choice to the last scoring card of each line
c: For the rest of the show, adds a random stamp to one scoring card per Entrance refill

name: Cotton Candy
head: Destroyed, it upgrades its neighbours. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also upgrades the cards two cells away
a: When destroyed, the cards adjacent to it become slot-free
b: When destroyed, the cards adjacent to it each gain a random stamp
c: When destroyed, the cards adjacent to it become slot-free, and every other card loses a stamp

name: Custard Pie
head: Cue: target card's suit becomes Balls; if that completes a flush row, gain bonus multiplier immediately. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The changed card may take the suit printed on its own mark instead of this card's
a: Cue: change one card's suit to match this card's
b: Cue: change every card in one row to match this card's suit
c: Cue: change one card's suit to match this card's, and if that completes a flush the line scores at once

name: High Five
head: Everything becomes one rank. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Only the cards you choose change rank
a: If the highest scoring rank in a line is a named rank, every scoring card becomes that rank for that scoring only
b: Every scoring card in a line becomes the rank of its highest card for that scoring only
c: Every scoring card in a line becomes the rank of its highest card, permanently

name: Hikinuki
head: On scoring, swaps this card's stamp with any stamp held in reserve
a: On scoring, swap this card's stamp with any stamp held in reserve — **level 2:** It may swap stamps with two cards
b: Cue: swap this card's stamp with the stamp of any card on the grid — **level 2:** It may swap stamps with two cards
c: On scoring, this card takes the stamp of the card directly above it, destroying that stamp — **level 2:** The stamp is taken without being destroyed

name: Midas Mask
head: Turns face cards to gold. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Any card sitting on a rank mark it matches turns gold too
a: Face cards become Gold cards when they score
b: Face cards become Gold cards when they score, and stay gold permanently
c: One card per Entrance refill becomes a Gold card when it scores, chosen by you

name: Paintbrush card
head: Paints what lands on it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** For each card placed on it, you choose whether that card takes this card's suit, its rank, or both
a: Cards placed on top of this one take its suit
b: Cards placed on top of this one take its suit permanently, even after they leave
c: Cards placed on top of this one take its suit, and so do their orthogonal neighbours

name: Rewrite card
head: Rewrites what is underneath. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which remembered cards it replaces
a: On entering the grid it remembers the cards below it in its column; when a line scores it rewrites that many of them into the cards printed on their own marks, so they now match fully
b: On entering it remembers the cards below; when a line scores it replaces them with copies of itself
c: On entering it remembers the cards below; when a line scores it swaps their positions rather than replacing them

name: Slapstick
head: Cue: swap the ranks of this card and one adjacent card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Once per turn, free: it may swap the ranks of any two adjacent cards
a: Cue: swap the ranks of this card and one adjacent card
b: Cue: swap the ranks of any two cards in this card's line
c: Cue: give this card's rank to an adjacent card and take that card's rank, keeping whichever is higher for itself

name: Sniper card
head: Takes a rank off whatever you touched last. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may raise the rank instead of lowering it
a: On the next refresh, lowers the rank of the last card you interacted with by one, discarding it at rank 1
b: Cue: name an uncovered mark; at each refresh its printed rank falls by one until a card in the Entrance matches it
c: Lowers the rank of the last card you interacted with by one every refresh, until it is discarded

name: The Ghost Writer
head: Each show start, writes a temporary skill (a copy of an effect that fired last show) onto one blank/prop card; it fades at show end. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its mark, the written skill is also written onto the next blank card to arrive in the Entrance
a: At show start, writes a copy of an effect that fired last show onto one blank card; it fades at show end
b: At show start, writes a copy of an effect that fired last show onto one blank card; it stays until that card is destroyed
c: At show start, writes a copy of any effect in your deck onto one blank card; it fades at show end

name: The Steelpan
head: Teaches a plain card a trick
a: Cue, once per show: permanently give one skill-less card the ability to score bonus points when its row melds — **level 2:** Twice per show
b: Cue, once per show: permanently give one skill-less card a copy of any skill already on the grid — **level 2:** Twice per show
c: Cue: give one skill-less card a bonus-scoring ability for this show only, with unlimited uses — **level 2:** The ability lasts into the next show

name: The Wardrobe Trunk
head: Keeps a stamp in the wings
a: Holds one stamp in reserve; cue to apply it permanently to any spotlit card, and it refills at the start of the next show — **level 2:** It refills at the next Entrance refill rather than next show
b: Holds one stamp in reserve; cue to apply it permanently to any card at all, and it refills at the start of the next show — **level 2:** It refills at the next Entrance refill rather than next show
c: Holds up to three stamps in reserve; cue to apply one per show — **level 2:** It may apply two per show

name: Cutting Up Jackpots
head: Rerolls a card into its own class. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may reroll within the same suit instead of the same class
a: Cue: reroll any card in the deck into another card of the same class
b: Cue: reroll any card in the deck into another card of the same rarity
c: Cue: reroll any card in the deck into another of the same class, once per show, keeping whichever you prefer

name: Mystery Box
head: On game start, this card becomes a random skill for the rest of the run, deterministic per seed. **Level 2, on its own mark:** When it lands on its mark it re-rolls, and you choose between two results
a: At run start this card becomes a random skill for the whole run, fixed by the seed
b: At the start of every show this card becomes a random skill for that show
c: At run start this card becomes a random skill, and re-rolls each time it is destroyed and recovered

name: Utter Chaos
head: A new trick every refresh. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It becomes a skill of your choice from those it has held this show
a: Becomes a random skill on every Entrance refresh
b: Becomes a random skill on every Entrance refresh, drawn only from skills already in your deck
c: Becomes a random skill on every line completion, so the pace is set by how fast you score

name: Randomizer
head: Cards evolve into other cards
a: Cards that upgrade become a randomly chosen other card rather than their designated upgrade — **level 2:** An upgrade rolls twice and you pick
b: Cards that upgrade become a random card of the next rarity up — **level 2:** An upgrade rolls twice and you pick
c: Cards that upgrade become a random card, and you may reroll the result once — **level 2:** The reroll is free and you keep either result

name: Tappable Clown
head: 3 charges per show: cue to deterministically re-roll the ranks of all adjacent cards. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One rerolled card may be set to the rank printed on its mark instead of rolled
a: Cue, 3 charges per show: re-roll the ranks of every adjacent card
b: Cue, 3 charges per show: re-roll the ranks of every card in one line
c: Cue, 3 charges per show: re-roll the rank of one card of your choice, anywhere

name: The Face Change
head: Reroll what a card is
a: Consumable: reroll one slot of a chosen card - its suit, rank, type, stamp or skill - keeping the rest
b: Consumable: reroll every slot of a chosen card at once
c: Consumable: reroll one slot of a chosen card, and each further reroll discards one Entrance card

name: The Six Faces
head: A card that keeps changing which card it is. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It holds its face without spending a cue
a: This card cycles through six fixed identities, advancing one each time a line it is in scores
b: This card cycles through six fixed identities, advancing one per Entrance refill, and you may hold it on the current one by cue
c: This card cycles through six fixed identities at random on each entrance refresh

name: The Wheel
head: Spins the ranks of a row
a: Consumable: re-roll the ranks of every card in one row
b: Consumable: re-roll the ranks of every card in one row, and keep whichever result scores higher
c: Consumable: re-roll the ranks of every card in one line, chosen after you see the result of the first roll

name: The Shapeshifter
head: After the Cryptid mod's Vermillion Virus: one card is replaced every placement
a: Boss: one random card you own is replaced by another every placement
b: Boss: one random card you own is replaced every placement, and you see what it becomes before the placement resolves
c: Boss: one random card is replaced every placement, and any card that scored that placement is safe

name: Pizza
head: Breaks into pieces on a timer. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose each piece's suit
a: After several shows, this card breaks itself into six smaller cards
b: After several shows, this card becomes six smaller cards, and you keep it too
c: You choose when it breaks; the longer you wait, the more pieces it makes

name: Sawing in Half
head: Cue: split a target card into two same-suit cards of half rank (one rounded up, one down); this card exhausts for the show. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Both halves are placed at once, on empty cells you choose
a: Cue: split a card into two same-suit cards of half its rank, one rounded up and one down; this card is spent for the show
b: Cue: split a card into two cards of half rank that must be placed in different lines; this card is spent for the show
c: Cue: split a card into two of half rank; if both later score in the same line, they merge back at double rank

name: The Half Card talent
head: Splits down the diagonal
a: On placement, splits into two halves along the diagonal: one keeps the rank and stamp, the other only the suit; stacking the halves back together scores them as their own meld — **level 2:** The halves may reunite anywhere, not only stacked
b: On placement, splits into two cards each holding half the original rank — **level 2:** Halves scoring in the same line score as their own meld
c: On placement it splits, and the halves may be placed anywhere; reuniting them in one line scores a large bonus — **level 2:** Reuniting re-scores the line they reunite in

name: The Lion Dance
head: Splits rather than dies, and feeds on what it lands on. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each half keeps its full skill
a: When destroyed it splits into two cards of half rank instead of dying; placed onto a card, it takes bonus points from the one beneath
b: When destroyed it splits into two cards of half rank; the halves cannot split again
c: When destroyed it splits into two cards of half rank, and each half can split again down to rank 1

name: Buried Alive
head: Cue: remove a card from the game for 2 shows; it returns upgraded one rarity, with a seeded chance it does not return. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The buried card scores at half while buried
a: Cue: bury one card under this one; it returns with +5 rank when uncovered
b: Cue: bury one card under this one; it returns with +5 rank and one rarity higher when uncovered
c: Cue: bury one card under this one; it returns with +5 rank when uncovered, and you may uncover it by cue

name: Upgrade quests
head: After the game Teamfight Tactics: upgrades itself when something odd happens
a: Carries a rare random condition that, when met, permanently upgrades it into a stronger version — **level 2:** You may re-roll the condition once per show
b: Carries a rare random condition, revealed only once met, that permanently upgrades it — **level 2:** Its condition is shown from the start
c: Carries a rare condition that upgrades it, and a second hidden condition beyond that — **level 2:** Its condition is shown from the start

name: Rotation re-trigger naming / fail-to-unlock
head: Has to fail before it can succeed. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each failure counts twice
a: Must publicly fail a set number of times before unlocking its true form
b: Must publicly fail a set number of times to unlock its true form; each failure also pays a small consolation
c: Must fail a set number of times to unlock; the number is hidden and only revealed as you approach it

name: Sapling
head: Grows into something better. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Stamped cards scoring through its cell count double
a: After enough stamped cards have scored, this card leaves and becomes a much rarer one
b: After enough stamped cards have scored, this card becomes a much rarer one and stays
c: After enough cards of any kind have scored, this card becomes rarer, and can do so repeatedly

name: The Whetstone
head: A card that sharpens itself. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The cards scoring beside it in the line gain the step too
a: Each time this card scores, it permanently gains a step, for the rest of the run
b: Each time this card scores, it permanently gains a step, and loses one each show it does not score
c: Each time this card scores it gains a step for the show; at End the steps become permanent only if it sits on a mark it matches

name: Wax and Gold
head: Says one thing, means another. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its hidden effect unlocks at once ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what either effect is*
a: Has a visible effect, and a hidden second effect that unlocks after the visible one has fired five times
b: Has a visible effect and a hidden second effect that unlocks after the visible one fires five times, then replaces it
c: Has a visible effect and a hidden one that unlocks on a condition you are never told

name: Double-Sided
head: There is another card on the back
a: This card can be flipped to reveal a different card on its reverse, and either face may be played
b: This card can be flipped to reveal a different card, and flipping costs an Entrance card, discarded
c: This card can be flipped, and the two faces merge into one combined card if it ever scores on both

name: Egg card
head: Hatches into something better. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose between two hatchlings
a: When a line scores, becomes a completely random other card of higher rank
b: When a line scores, becomes a random other card of higher rarity
c: When a line scores, becomes a random card of higher rank, and the longer it went unplayed the higher

name: The Repertoire
head: Three skills, one slot
a: Holds three skills in one slot; the active one rotates each placement, and a cue rotates it early — **level 2:** You may rotate it by hand at any time, not only each placement
b: Holds three skills in one slot; you choose which is active at the start of each show — **level 2:** You may re-choose once mid-show
c: Holds three skills in one slot, all active at once, each at one-third strength — **level 2:** One of its three runs at full strength, your choice

name: The Ripening
head: Turns into something else over time
a: After three Entrance refills in place, this card becomes the card printed on its own mark and counts as matching it fully — **level 2:** The cards beside it ripen with it
b: After three Entrance refills in place, this card becomes a copy of the adjacent card you choose — **level 2:** Two refills are enough
c: After three Entrance refills, this card becomes the card printed on any uncovered mark in its lines, your choice, and moves to that cell — **level 2:** Two refills are enough

name: The Two Masks
head: Two faces, and it turns. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Both sides are up at once
a: Comedy side buffs its neighbours, tragedy side buffs itself, and it flips every time it scores
b: Comedy side buffs its neighbours, tragedy side buffs itself, and you choose which side is up when placing it
c: It flips every time it scores, and each flip makes the active side slightly stronger

name: The Two-Sided Bill
head: One card, two shows
a: This card has two faces with different effects; playing one face returns the card to the deck with the other face up — **level 2:** It stays on the board after playing, the other face up
b: This card has two faces; it flips to the other face each time its line scores — **level 2:** You choose whether it flips
c: This card has two faces; you choose the face when you place it, and the unchosen face is lost for the rest of the show — **level 2:** The unchosen face is not lost

name: Dedi's Mercy
head: Once per show, when one of your cards is destroyed, restore it to the discard pile instead
a: Once per show, the first of your cards destroyed goes to the discard pile instead of leaving the run — **level 2:** Twice per show
b: Once per show, the first of your cards destroyed returns to the deck instead — **level 2:** Twice per show
c: Once per run, every card destroyed so far returns to the deck at once — **level 2:** The returned cards arrive in the Entrance

name: Marotte
head: When this card is destroyed, a rank-1 copy of it (same skill, no stamp) survives in its place
a: When destroyed, a rank-1 copy with the same skill and no stamp survives in its place — **level 2:** The copy keeps its rank
b: When destroyed, a full copy survives in its place, once per run — **level 2:** The copy keeps this card's stamp
c: When destroyed, it returns to the deck at rank 1 rather than leaving the run — **level 2:** The copy keeps its rank

name: The Basket
head: Destroyed into a box, not into nothing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It reappears this show, not next
a: Destroys a card into this one; it reappears in the Entrance next show unharmed, and pays fame for the trick
b: Destroys a card into this one; it reappears next show at +1 rank
c: Destroys a card into this one; it reappears next show, and each trip through the discard raises the fame the trick pays

name: The Dead List
head: Destroyed cards get a zone of their own. (lines 905, 995). **Level 2, on its own mark:** Once per show while it sits on its own mark, return one card from the dead list to the Entrance slot you choose
a: Destroyed cards go to a dead list rather than vanishing, and effects may reach into it
b: Destroyed cards go to a dead list you can see but never reach into
c: Destroyed cards go to a dead list, and one card may be recovered from it per tour by skipping that show's reward

name: The Hologram Tour
head: Brings back the dead, faintly
a: Consumable: one destroyed card returns for one show as an intangible duplicate that scores but cannot be touched
b: Consumable: one destroyed card returns permanently at half rank
c: Consumable: one destroyed card returns for one show intangible, and stays if it scores in every placement

name: The Ofrenda Show
head: The dead perform one more night
a: Show: destroyed and discarded cards return for a single show, then rest again
b: Show: destroyed cards return for a single show, and one of them may be kept
c: Show: destroyed cards return for one show at rank 1, and any that score are restored permanently

name: The Ox
head: Death is worth something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It returns in the next Entrance refill this show, not next show
a: When destroyed, grants bonus fame and returns to the deck next show
b: When destroyed, grants bonus fame scaling with its rank and returns to the deck next show at rank 1
c: When destroyed, grants bonus fame and returns to the deck next show; each death raises the fame it pays

name: Brass Check
head: Whenever this card's effects trigger, mint a Gold token card onto the top of the deck. Its tokens are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends ⚑ *pair review: a Gold token's only use was trade at a shop, and there is no shop*
a: Each time this card's effects trigger, one Gold token card is put on top of the deck — **level 2:** Its tokens go into the Entrance instead of the deck
b: Each time this card scores, one Gold token card is put straight into the Entrance — **level 2:** It mints one per line scored through its cell
c: The first time this card triggers each show, three Gold token cards are put on top of the deck — **level 2:** Its tokens go into the Entrance instead of the deck

name: Candy Basket
head: Fills a basket over the tour. The basket keeps its tokens between shows; a released token is a ghost
a: Accumulates tokens as shows are beaten, more for bosses; cue to release them all — **level 2:** You may release them one at a time
b: Accumulates tokens as shows are beaten and releases one per show automatically — **level 2:** Two per show
c: Accumulates tokens as shows are beaten, and the basket's contents upgrade the longer they sit — **level 2:** They upgrade twice as fast

name: Chick production (gali-gali)
head: Something under the cup. Its tokens are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It produces a token under any scored card sitting on a mark it matches, face down or not
a: Produces a rank-1 token beneath any scored card that missed its mark on every property
b: Produces a rank-1 token beneath any scored card that missed its mark on every property, one per miss in the meld
c: Produces a rank-1 token beneath any scored card that missed its mark on every property, and the token is the card the mark wanted

name: Dove production
head: Doves out of the meld. A flier lands on the lowest empty cell of its column; if the column is full it is stacked on the column's top card. Its fliers are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends
a: Scored melds release rank-1 token fliers that land on random columns as free cards — **level 2:** They land on columns you choose
b: Scored melds release rank-1 token fliers that land on columns you choose — **level 2:** They land on the cells you choose
c: Scored melds release one rank-1 flier per distinct suit in the meld, landing on random columns — **level 2:** You choose each flier's column, and a flier landing on a mark of its suit counts as matching it

name: Klyaksa
head: Comes with a free rank-1 token card that shuffles into the deck and follows this card's column when drawn. The token it comes with stays in the deck; tokens it mints are ghosts
a: Comes with a free rank-1 token that shuffles into the deck and follows this card's column when drawn — **level 2:** When the token is drawn it may land on any cell adjacent to this card
b: Comes with a free rank-1 token that is placed adjacent to this card automatically whenever this card is placed — **level 2:** The token lands on the adjacent cell you choose
c: Mints a new rank-1 token into the Entrance every time this card scores — **level 2:** It mints two per score

name: Reverse Card
head: Fills every empty slot, then goes. Its tokens are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends
a: On a condition, fills every empty skill slot with token cards, then destroys itself — **level 2:** It survives the first time it fires
b: On a condition, fills every empty skill slot with token cards and survives — **level 2:** It may also fire by cue
c: On a condition, fills every empty cell on the grid with token cards, then destroys itself — **level 2:** It survives the first time it fires

name: The Butterfly Trick
head: Cue: create two rank-1 paper-token cards of any suit that drift down one chosen column, one row per Entrance refresh. Its tokens are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends
a: Cue: create two rank-1 token cards of any suit that drift one row down a chosen column per Entrance refresh — **level 2:** The tokens take the suit of each mark they drift over
b: Cue: create two rank-1 token cards of any suit placed directly into cells you choose — **level 2:** The tokens take the rank and suit printed on the marks of the cells they are placed in
c: Cue: create two rank-1 token cards that drift down a column and raise the rank of every card they pass — **level 2:** The tokens take the suit of each mark they drift over

name: The Candy Butcher
head: Whenever a full 5-card row meld scores, mints one Ticket Stub to the deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line through its cell mints two stubs ⚑ *pair review: it mints Ticket Stubs, whose only value was trade at a shop*
a: Whenever a full five-card row meld scores, mint one Ticket Stub into the deck
b: Whenever any five-card line scores, mint one Ticket Stub into the deck
c: Whenever a five-card line scores, mint one Ticket Stub per distinct suit in that line

name: The Conjuror
head: Once per turn, produce a rank-1 token card of any suit into the Entrance. Its tokens are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends
a: Once per Entrance refill, produce a rank-1 token card of any suit into the Entrance — **level 2:** The token carries the rank and suit of any uncovered mark you name
b: Once per Entrance refill, produce a rank-1 token of any suit directly into an empty cell you choose — **level 2:** The token takes the rank and suit printed on the mark of the cell it goes onto
c: Once per Entrance refill, produce a token whose suit and rank you choose, up to a total rank budget of 5 per show — **level 2:** The token takes the rank and suit printed on the mark of the cell it goes onto

name: The Witch's Gold
head: Tokens that pay out by detonating. A token that never explodes is a ghost. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An exploding token also pays for each uncovered mark adjacent to it
a: Spawns gold tokens that explode at the end of the placement, paying its rank into the special bucket and destroying whatever cell they sat in
b: Spawns gold tokens that explode at the end of the placement, paying its rank into the special bucket and damaging their neighbours
c: Spawns gold tokens that explode when a placement finishes resolving unless you have placed them first, so holding them in the Entrance is the gamble

name: 72 Transformations
head: Cue: copy any spotlit card's skill; track total copies across the run, and at 72 total copies this card permanently upgrades to Legendary stats. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The copied skill fires in its level-2 form
a: Cue: copies the skill of any spotlit card for the rest of the show; after 30 copies across the run it keeps one copied skill permanently
b: Copies the skill of whichever card scored most recently, free and automatic, re-copying every time a line completes
c: Cue: copies the skill of any spotlit card and destroys that card; keeps every skill taken this way, up to three at once

name: The Apprentice
head: Blank skill; each show it permanently learns the first effect it observes firing, up to three learned effects
a: Starts blank; each show it permanently learns the first effect it sees fire, up to three learned effects — **level 2:** It learns two effects each show
b: Starts blank; each show it learns the first effect it sees fire, replacing whatever it learned before — **level 2:** It learns two effects each show
c: Starts blank; it learns every effect that fires in a line it belongs to, but forgets them all at show end — **level 2:** It keeps what it learned into the next show

name: The Dubplate
head: Event-forged unique card created for this save file, assembled from the two effects scored most this run. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its mark it also carries the effect that has scored most this show
a: A unique card forged for this save file out of the two effects that scored most this run
b: A unique card forged for this save file out of two effects you choose from those that scored this run
c: A unique card forged for this save file that re-forges itself out of the run's two top effects at the start of every run

name: The Impersonation
head: Wears a dead card's skill
a: Copies the skill of a card destroyed earlier this run — **level 2:** It wears two dead cards' skills at once
b: Copies the skill of the most recently destroyed card, changing as more are lost — **level 2:** It wears two dead cards' skills at once
c: Copies the skill of a destroyed card, and can hold one skill per card you have lost, up to three — **level 2:** A card destroyed while it sits there is added even past three

name: The Synthetic Idol
head: Assembled out of other cards' skills ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a fragment of a skill is*
a: Its skill is assembled from fragments of other cards' skills in your deck — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose which fragments it keeps
b: Its skill is assembled from fragments of the skills that scored most last show — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose which fragments it keeps
c: Its skill is assembled from fragments you choose, one fragment added per show — **level 2:** It gains a second fragment this show

name: Understudy
head: Learns from what dies above it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It keeps its own skill as well as the copied one
a: If the card in the cell directly above it, in the row above, is destroyed or discarded, this card permanently copies its skill
b: If any card stacked on this one is destroyed, it permanently copies that card's skill, overwriting what it had
c: If the card in the cell directly above it is destroyed, this card copies its skill for the rest of the show only

name: Call-and-response
head: Answers what its neighbour does. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It answers any card in its lines, not only an adjacent one
a: When an adjacent card triggers, this card may answer by mirroring that trigger at half power
b: When an adjacent card triggers, this card mirrors it at half power automatically
c: When an adjacent card triggers, this card mirrors it at full power, but only once per Entrance refill

name: Canvas
head: Retriggers what is behind it, per what is ahead
a: Retriggers every card to its left in its row once for each card to its right that sits on a mark it matches — **level 2:** It counts every card to its right
b: Retriggers every card to its left in its row once, whatever is on the right — **level 2:** It retriggers both sides
c: Retriggers every card in its row once for each card in its column sitting on a mark it matches — **level 2:** It counts every card in its column

name: Double Tag
head: Copies the next reward you take
a: Consumable: the next reward you take is duplicated
b: Consumable: the next reward you take is duplicated, and this card is consumed by the duplication
c: Consumable: the next two rewards you take are each duplicated once

name: The Cue Card
head: Cue: manually fire one adjacent card's trigger hook exactly as if the game had triggered it, including combo credit and stamps
a: Cue: fire one adjacent card's trigger by hand exactly as the game would, combo credit and stamps included — **level 2:** It may fire any card in its lines, not only an adjacent one
b: Cue: fire any card's trigger by hand, combo credit and stamps included — **level 2:** It may fire two
c: Cue: fire one adjacent card's trigger by hand; it counts for points but grants no combo — **level 2:** It may fire any card in its lines, not only an adjacent one

name: The Monkey
head: A token that cues what it climbs. **Level 2, on its own mark:** At each refresh you choose whether the token climbs one row or steps one cell sideways
a: Spawns a token that climbs its column one row per Entrance refresh, freely cueing whatever card it sits on
b: Spawns a token that climbs one row per refresh and cues what it sits on; reaching the top, it starts again at the bottom
c: Spawns a token that climbs one row per refresh, cueing what it sits on and gaining +1 to the strength of each cue as it rises

name: The Kindling
head: After Hearthstone's Spellburst: fires once off another effect
a: The first time any other effect fires while this card is spotlit, this card's effect fires too, and the stamp is spent for the placement — **level 2:** It fires off the first two other effects, not one
b: The first time any other effect fires while this card is spotlit, this card's effect fires too, and the stamp recharges each placement — **level 2:** It fires off the first two other effects, not one
c: Every time another effect fires while this card is spotlit, this card's effect fires at a fraction of strength — **level 2:** It fires at full strength

name: Caeruleum
head: Promotes its neighbours' operators
a: Adjacent scoring cards use the next operator up: a flat bonus is paid as mult, and a mult bonus makes its line pay into the special bucket as well as its own — **level 2:** It promotes every card in its lines
b: As (a), for one adjacent card per Entrance refill — **level 2:** It promotes every card in its lines
c: Every card in this card's line goes from flat to mult only — **level 2:** Mult bonuses in its line also pay into the special bucket

name: Fun-house-mirror effect modifiers
head: Bends the effects around it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose, per neighbour, whether it amplifies or distorts
a: Amplifies: adjacent cards' effects fire with their numbers doubled
b: Distorts: adjacent cards' effects fire from the cell mirrored across the grid's centre, so they reach the far side
c: Which of the two each neighbour gets is rerolled each show

name: Gemini
head: Doubles what is beside it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It doubles two adjacent cards
a: At the end of each show, doubles every value on an adjacent card
b: At the end of each show, doubles every value on an adjacent card, then that card is spent
c: At the end of each show, doubles every value on the adjacent card that scored least

name: Twin Harmony
head: Doubles what is next to it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An adjacent card sitting on a mark it matches has its effect tripled instead
a: Doubles any combo or multiplier effect on cards adjacent to it
b: Doubles any combo or multiplier effect on cards in its row and column
c: Doubles any combo or multiplier effect on adjacent cards, and triples it if the adjacent card shares its class

name: The Calm Voice
head: Once per run, negate a disaster event or boss effect and gain fame equal to its severity instead. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It negates two
a: Once per run, negate a disaster or boss effect and gain fame equal to its severity instead
b: Once per show, negate a disaster or boss effect, gaining nothing for it
c: Once per run, negate a disaster or boss effect, and the next boss effect of the same kind is negated too

name: The Loophole
head: Turns the hazard around. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may invert two hazards
a: Choose one active town or boss hazard: its effect inverts to help you for this show
b: Choose one active town or boss hazard: it is simply switched off for this show
c: Choose one active hazard: it inverts to help you, and the boss gains a second hazard in exchange

name: The Patch
head: Cancels a rule before it lands
a: Consumable: cancel one town penalty or hazard rule card before the show begins
b: Consumable: cancel one town penalty or hazard rule card at any point during the show
c: Consumable: swap one town hazard for a different one drawn at random

name: The Vigil
head: Your last move dictates what others may do ⚑ *pair review: a two-player rule: in a solitaire it only restricts your own cards*
a: If this card rose in height last turn, no other card may rise in height this turn — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, its restriction binds only hazards, not your cards
b: If this card rose in height last turn, no OPPOSING effect may raise a card this turn — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, its restriction binds only hazards, not your cards
c: Whatever this card did last turn, no other card may do this turn — **level 2:** Whatever it did last turn, a card that does the same from its lines this turn pays double

name: Ghost
head: Possesses another card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It possesses two cards
a: At each show's end, a chance to possess a random card of yours, taking over its effects
b: At each show's end, a chance to possess a random card, and a smaller chance to destroy itself
c: Cue to possess a card of your choice for the show, returning its effects when the show ends

name: The Boot Code
head: Passes a buff down its row card-to-card without triggering, invisible to effects that count or punish triggers ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what the buff is*
a: Passes a buff along its row card to card without triggering, invisible to anything counting or punishing triggers — **level 2:** The buff runs along its column too
b: Passes a buff along its row card to card without triggering, and the buff doubles at the far end — **level 2:** The buff runs along its column too
c: Passes a buff to any one card in any grid without triggering, invisible to trigger counters — **level 2:** It buffs two cards

name: The Double
head: Assign a 'star' card at show start; the first destruction or debuff aimed at the star hits this card instead. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Once per show it survives a hit it takes
a: Name one card at show start; the first destruction or debuff aimed at it hits this card instead
b: Name one card at show start; every destruction or debuff aimed at it hits this card instead, until this card is destroyed
c: The first destruction or debuff aimed at any of your cards each placement hits this card instead

name: The Rigger
head: Crosses the wires. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may rewire three cards in a ring
a: Cue: swap the wiring of two cards so each one's skill now answers the other's events
b: Cue: swap the wiring of two cards for one placement only
c: Cue: redirect one card's skill so it answers this card's events instead of its own

name: The Throw (ventriloquism)
head: Throws its voice. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The effect lands in two places
a: Cues a card's ability as though the card were in a different column
b: Cues a card's ability as though it were in any cell you name, in any grid
c: Cues a card's ability from its real position, but its effect lands where you name

name: Automaton
head: On every Entrance refresh, automatically performs this card's cue for free; it can never be triggered manually
a: This card's cue fires automatically on every Entrance refresh and can never be triggered by hand
b: This card's cue fires automatically whenever a line it belongs to completes, and can never be triggered by hand
c: This card's cue fires automatically at show start and again at show end, and can never be triggered by hand

name: Configurable rhythm-buff (calliope organ)
head: A programmable rhythm. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you may reorder its answers at each Entrance refill ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what answering a trigger does*
a: A punched-card organ you configure: choose which triggers it answers and in what order
b: A punched-card organ that answers a fixed rhythm of triggers you set once at run start
c: A punched-card organ you reconfigure each show, choosing which triggers it answers

name: Instead Of That
head: If something would happen, something else happens. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It holds two substitutions ⚑ *pair review: it does not say which events it may name*
a: This card names one event and one substitute; whenever the named event would happen anywhere, the substitute happens instead
b: This card names one event and one substitute, and the substitution applies only on its own grid
c: This card names one event and one substitute; the substitution applies once per Entrance refill and then waits

name: Lazzi trigger-macros
head: A rehearsed combo you can equip. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, a macro may fire without being rehearsed first ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a macro does or what it costs*
a: Equippable trigger macros: small scripted sequences a card can rehearse and then fire as one
b: Equippable trigger macros that a card rehearses once and can fire once per show
c: Equippable trigger macros you write yourself from effects already in your deck

name: The Cannon King
head: Fireworks-suit cards may score directly from the Entrance without entering the grid
a: Fireworks-suit cards may score straight from the Entrance without ever being placed — **level 2:** The Entrance card scores as part of the lines through this card's cell
b: Any card of one suit you name at show start may score straight from the Entrance without being placed — **level 2:** The Entrance card scores as part of the lines through this card's cell
c: Cue, once per refresh: fire one Entrance card at an uncovered mark it matches; it pays that mark's match bonus into the special bucket without occupying the cell, then is discarded, and the mark stays — **level 2:** Two per refresh instead of one

name: The Conductor
head: All on-refresh effects are held each turn and fire together when the placement scores instead, in a chosen order
a: All on-refresh effects are held each turn and fire together when the placement scores, in an order you choose — **level 2:** You may release one held effect early, at a moment you choose
b: All on-refresh effects are held and fire together when the placement scores, in the order they were held — **level 2:** You may release one held effect early, at a moment you choose
c: You may hold any one effect's trigger and release it at a moment of your choosing later in the show — **level 2:** It may hold two triggers

name: The Dragoman
head: Choose a card: its on-score effects also fire when it is discarded
a: Choose a card: its on-score effects also fire when it is discarded — **level 2:** Choose two cards
b: Choose a card: its on-score effects also fire when it is discarded or when it is covered — **level 2:** Choose two cards
c: Every card's on-score effects also fire when it is discarded, at half strength — **level 2:** It works at full strength

name: The Rewritten Cue
head: Turns one hook into another. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its modifiers fire on both hooks at full strength
a: The other modifiers on this card fire on placement instead of on scoring
b: The other modifiers on this card fire on placement as well as on scoring, at half strength each
c: The other modifiers on this card fire when it lands on a mark it matches, instead of when it scores

name: Duende
head: When a placement scores 5 or more distinct combo classes and every meld that placement raised the combo, triples the placement's payout
a: If a placement raises the combo with five or more distinct effect classes, its payout triples — **level 2:** Four distinct classes are enough
b: A placement's payout is multiplied by the number of distinct effect classes that fired in it — **level 2:** The multiplier is the count plus one
c: If every line scored in a placement raised the combo, the placement's payout triples — **level 2:** It triples even if one line failed to raise the combo

name: The Combo Chain
head: The chain, not the hit, is the score ⚑ *pair review: the show's combo already pays per distinct effect class*
a: Each distinct effect that fires within one placement extends a chain; the placement payout is multiplied by the chain length rather than by a fixed combo — **level 2:** Effects through its cell count twice
b: Each distinct effect within one placement extends a chain, and the chain carries into the next placement if the placement scored above target — **level 2:** The chain carries whether or not the placement scored above target
c: Each distinct effect extends a chain, and a repeated effect breaks it back to one — **level 2:** A repeat through its cell does not break the chain

name: The Critic
head: After each placement, the effect that triggered most is silenced for the next placement; any effect that triggered exactly once scores a bonus
a: After each placement, the effect that triggered most is silenced for the next placement, and every effect that triggered exactly once pays a bonus — **level 2:** Effects that fired exactly once pay double
b: After each placement, the effect that triggered most is silenced for the next placement — **level 2:** Effects that fired exactly once pay a bonus
c: After each placement, every effect that triggered more than three times is silenced for the next placement, and those that triggered once pay a bonus — **level 2:** Effects that fired exactly once pay double

name: The Uniqueness Bonus
head: Paid for variety, not volume. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Effects fired from matched cells count twice ⚑ *pair review: the show's combo already pays per distinct effect class; overlaps Q0562*
a: When a placement finishes resolving, score a step for every distinct effect that fired this placement, and nothing for repeats
b: When a placement finishes resolving, score a step for every distinct effect that fired, and a larger step for every effect that fired exactly once
c: When a placement finishes resolving, score for every distinct effect that fired this show rather than this placement, counting each only the first time

name: The Jumbled Bill
head: After Balatro's Amber Acorn: shuffles the running order. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You pick the new order instead of shuffling it
a: Shuffles the resolution order of every effect on the board
b: Shuffles the resolution order of every effect, and you may look at the new order before committing
c: Reverses the resolution order of every effect on the board

name: Cascade Scorer
head: When a line scores, scores all rows first, then all columns simultaneously per row band
a: When two lines complete at once, the special bucket's lines resolve first and rows before columns after them, so what diagonals and stacks trigger applies to rows and columns — **level 2:** Lines through its cell always resolve last, so they gain from everything the others triggered
b: When two lines complete at once, the line containing the card you just placed resolves last, so what the others trigger applies to it — **level 2:** Lines through its cell always resolve last, so they gain from everything the others triggered
c: When two lines complete at once, the line containing the card you just placed resolves first and its result feeds the others — **level 2:** The line that resolves first pays a step more

name: Resolution By Rank
head: Effects fire in rank order, not board order. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may swap two adjacent effects in the order each placement
a: When several effects trigger at once, they resolve in descending rank order rather than by position
b: When several effects trigger at once they resolve in descending rank order, ties broken by which was placed first
c: When several effects trigger at once, they resolve in ascending rank order, so the smallest card acts first

name: The Approach
head: A line resolves from one end, in order. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line through its cell resolves from both ends toward the middle
a: A completed line resolves card by card from the edge inward rather than all at once, and an effect may stop the resolution partway
b: A completed line resolves from the edge inward, and you choose which edge each time
c: A completed line resolves from the edge inward, and each card it passes raises the value of the next

name: The Reading Order
head: Where a card sits decides when it fires. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match jump to the front of the order
a: Effects resolve in reading order across the grid, so moving a card changes when it fires
b: Effects resolve in the order the cards were placed, not by position
c: Effects resolve in reading order, and a card may pay a charge to jump to the front

name: The Showdown Order
head: Lines resolve strongest first. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The strongest line pays once more at the end
a: Completed lines resolve in order of the strength of the hand they made, strongest first
b: Completed lines resolve weakest first, so the strongest benefits from everything the others triggered
c: Completed lines resolve strongest first, and each weaker line inherits the multiplier of the one before it

name: Top Billing
head: First on the bill. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It scores both first and last within its meld
a: Always scores first within its meld, ahead of normal dispatch order
b: Always scores last within its meld, so everything else has already resolved when it fires
c: You choose whether it scores first or last within its meld, per Entrance refill

name: The Costumier
head: All your cards may hold 2 stamps. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match may hold three stamps
a: All your cards may hold two stamps
b: All your cards may hold two stamps, but every stamp works at half strength
c: Cards in this card's lines may hold two stamps

name: The Illustrated
head: This card may hold unlimited stamps, but can never hold a skill
a: May hold unlimited stamps, but can never hold a skill — **level 2:** It may carry a skill while it sits there
b: May hold up to three stamps, and its skill works at half strength — **level 2:** Its skill works at full strength
c: May hold unlimited stamps and no skill, and scores a bonus per stamp it carries — **level 2:** It may carry a skill while it sits there

name: The Double Billing
head: A card that holds two skills
a: This card may hold two skills at once, both fully active — **level 2:** A talent match by either skill unlocks both skills' level 2
b: This card may hold two skills, each firing at half strength — **level 2:** Both skills fire at full strength
c: This card may hold two skills, and only the one matching the line's dominant suit fires — **level 2:** Both skills fire whatever the dominant suit

name: The Fitted Slot
head: A slot that only takes certain cards
a: This card has a second stamp slot that accepts only stamps whose effect fires on placement — **level 2:** The second slot takes any stamp
b: This card has a second stamp slot that accepts any stamp, but both fire at half strength — **level 2:** Both stamps fire at full strength
c: This card has a second stamp slot that accepts only stamps already carried by another card on the grid — **level 2:** The second slot takes any stamp

name: The Quick Change
head: Moves a modifier between slots. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may move a modifier onto another card
a: Cue: move a card's skill into its stamp slot, or the reverse
b: Cue: move any modifier on a card into any other slot on that card, if the slot is empty
c: Cue: swap the contents of two slots on the same card, whatever they are

name: The Rank Requirement
head: Equipment that wants a number
a: This card holds a skill from another card, but only fires it while this card sits at rank seven or higher — **level 2:** It fires the held skill at full strength whatever its rank
b: This card holds a skill from another card and fires it at a strength set by this card's rank — **level 2:** It fires the held skill at full strength whatever its rank
