c: This card holds two skills from other cards and fires whichever matches its current rank band — **level 2:** Both held skills fire

name: The Stripped Act
head: Removes a slot entirely. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may remove two slots
a: Cue: permanently remove a card's type slot; the card scores more for having less
b: Cue: permanently remove any one slot from a card, and it scores more for each slot it lacks
c: Cue: permanently remove a slot from a card and graft that slot onto another card

name: No-conditions cue
head: A cue with no strings. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its cue also fires the cue of one card in its lines ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what its cue does*
a: This card's cue works from anywhere, with no conditions at all
b: This card's cue works from anywhere, but only once per show
c: This card's cue works from anywhere and from any zone, including the deck and the discard

name: Peanut Pitch
head: Cue, 3 charges per show: gives bonus points to any one card on the grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A charge spent on a card sitting on a mark it matches is refunded
a: Cue, 3 charges per show: give bonus points to any one card on the grid
b: Cue, 3 charges per show: give bonus points to every card in one line
c: Cue, 3 charges per show: give bonus points to one card, and the charge is refunded if that card scores this turn

name: Tap Solitaire
head: Tapping is the only verb
a: A show where cards are only cued from the Entrance, except that a card may be placed where the cell's mark matches it — **level 2:** A cued card whose mark it matches is placed there after its cue resolves
b: A show where placement is free but every card must also be cued once before it can score — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you may place one card each refill without cueing it
c: A show where you may either place or cue each turn, never both — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark you may both place and cue in one turn

name: The Charge Bank
head: Charges are a pool, not a per-card allowance
a: Charges are held in one shared pool rather than per card; any cued effect may draw from it — **level 2:** The pool gains a charge per line scored through its cell
b: Charges are held per card as usual, but a card may lend a charge to any adjacent card — **level 2:** A card may lend to any card in its lines
c: Charges are held in one shared pool that refills by one each placement, and any effect may draw from it — **level 2:** The pool refills by two

name: Bonus Joker
head: Sometimes it makes room. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The chance doubles for cards scoring through its cell ⚑ *pair review: the brief names no limit on how many skills or consumables you carry, so there is no slot to grow*
a: A scoring card has a small chance to permanently grant one extra slot, up to twice per show
b: A scoring card has a small chance to grant one extra slot for the current show only
c: Every completed line has a small chance to grant one extra slot, with no per-show cap

name: Negative
head: Takes no room at all. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card placed beside the wearer while it sits on its mark takes no slot either ⚑ *pair review: (c) could not be sold, and there is no shop*
a: This card occupies no slot, so it is carried in addition to your normal capacity
b: This card occupies no slot, and grants one extra slot besides
c: This card occupies no slot, but it cannot be moved or destroyed once acquired

name: Nostalgic Deck
head: One pool of slots for everything. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you may move one card between the pools ⚑ *pair review: the brief names no limit on how many skills or consumables you carry, so there is no slot to grow*
a: Skill slots and consumable slots are one shared pool
b: Skill slots and consumable slots are one shared pool, and the pool is smaller than the two were
c: Every slot on every card is one shared pool, so a card may trade a stamp for a skill

name: The Metronome
head: More charges, everywhere. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A cue fired from a card sitting on a mark it matches spends no charge
a: Every charge-based effect on your cards gains +1 maximum charge
b: Every charge-based effect gains +1 maximum charge, and one spent charge is refunded per show
c: Every charge-based effect gains +1 maximum charge, and unspent charges carry into the next show

name: The Unlocked Cell
head: Capacity is a reward, not a starting stat. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A three of a kind through its cell is enough
a: Scoring a four of a kind widens the Entrance by one slot for the rest of the run; the new slot deals from its own stock
b: Scoring a four of a kind widens the Entrance by one slot for the rest of the show, the new slot filled from the deepest stock
c: Every four of a kind widens the Entrance by one slot, and every card of yours destroyed narrows it by one

name: Clockwork Joker
head: Four clocks, and they can align
a: Runs four staggered timers with different periods, each firing its own effect; when all four coincide it copies itself — **level 2:** Three of the four timers aligning is enough
b: Runs four staggered timers, each firing its own effect, with no bonus for alignment — **level 2:** Each timer fires twice on its tick
c: Runs four staggered timers whose periods you set once, and aligning all four copies the card — **level 2:** Three of the four timers aligning is enough

name: Happy House
head: A very long fuse. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A placement onto a matched cell counts twice toward its fuse
a: Does nothing until a large number of placements have been made, then raises the multiplier to a power
b: Does nothing until a large number of placements have passed, then pays a single enormous lump sum
c: Its threshold is hidden and revealed only as you approach it, then it raises the multiplier to a power

name: Loyalty Card
head: Fires hard, but rarely. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also fires on any placement that lands a card on a mark it matches
a: Every sixth placement, this card scores a large multiplier; the rest do nothing
b: Every sixth placement it scores a large multiplier, and the counter carries across shows
c: Every Nth placement it scores a large multiplier, and you set N when you acquire it

name: All-Out Effort
head: After Deadpool's catchphrase Maximum Effort: doubles this card's points on score; afterward it is Exhausted (scores nothing) until a show passes in which it was never played
a: Doubles this card's points, then Exhausts it until a show passes in which it was never played — **level 2:** It triples instead of doubling
b: Doubles this card's points, then Exhausts it until it next lands on a mark it matches — **level 2:** It triples instead of doubling
c: Triples this card's points, then Exhausts it for two shows — **level 2:** It Exhausts for one show, not two

name: The Countdown Equipment
head: Powerful, and then unavailable for a while
a: This card fires a large effect, then goes dark for three scoring passes before it can fire again — **level 2:** Its dark time halves
b: This card fires a large effect, then goes dark for three placements before it can fire again — **level 2:** Its dark time halves
c: This card fires a large effect, then goes dark until a line containing it scores — **level 2:** It wakes when any line through a matched cell scores

name: Campfire
head: Grows on what you discard, resets on bosses. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts destroyed cards as well as discarded ones
a: Gains a permanent multiplier for each card discarded from the board, reset whenever a boss is beaten
b: Gains a permanent multiplier for each card discarded from the board, never reset
c: Gains a multiplier for each card discarded from the board, and beating a boss banks the current value rather than resetting it

name: Cheat Day
head: If the show is won with cards still in the deck, every remaining deck card gains +1 rank permanently
a: If a show is won with one Entrance stock never drawn from, every card in that stock gains +1 rank permanently — **level 2:** You may give the whole gain to one card of that stock
b: If a show is won with a stock never drawn from, this card gains +1 rank per card left in it, permanently — **level 2:** +2 per card
c: At the end of every show, the cards left in the deepest stock gain +1 rank permanently — **level 2:** The two deepest stocks

name: Constellation
head: Grows every time you spend a consumable. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A consumable used on a card sitting on a mark it matches counts twice
a: Gains a permanent multiplier every time a consumable is used
b: Gains a permanent multiplier every time a consumable is used, doubled for rarer ones
c: Gains a permanent multiplier per consumable used, and a further one per distinct consumable used

name: Corrupted
head: Improves once, and the improvement sticks
a: The first time a line containing this card scores above a threshold, this card is permanently upgraded — **level 2:** It upgrades at half the threshold
b: Each time a line containing this card scores above a threshold, the threshold rises and the card upgrades again — **level 2:** It upgrades at half the threshold
c: The first time this card scores at all it is permanently upgraded; the second time it upgrades again and the stamp is spent — **level 2:** The stamp is not spent at the second upgrade

name: Double Scale
head: Growth that curves upward. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match grow cubically
a: Every card that grows with use grows quadratically rather than linearly
b: Every card that grows with use grows quadratically, but resets at the end of each show
c: Every card that grows with use grows quadratically, and the curve steepens once past a threshold

name: Energia
head: Copies rewards, more each time. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each line scored through its cell counts as a reward taken
a: Whenever you take a reward, it is copied; the number of copies rises by one each time
b: Whenever you take a reward it is copied once, always
c: Whenever you take a reward it is copied, the count rising each time, and resetting when you skip one

name: First of May
head: A random Common card that permanently upgrades to its Rare version after scoring 10 times across the run
a: After scoring 10 times in a run, this card permanently becomes its Rare version — **level 2:** It needs five scores
b: After scoring 10 times in a run, this card permanently gains one rarity tier, and can keep doing so — **level 2:** It needs five scores
c: Gains +1 rank each time it scores, and at rank 20 permanently becomes its Rare version — **level 2:** +2 rank per score while it sits there

name: Garden Solitaire
head: Cards grow where you plant them. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A growing card whose rank reaches the rank printed on its mark counts as matching it on rank from then on
a: A card in no complete line gains +1 rank at each Entrance refill; when a line through it completes it is harvested: the ranks it gained are paid as flat points into that line's bucket and its rank returns to printed
b: As (a), but a harvested card keeps its grown rank, and a grown card that is moved or covered loses all of it
c: As (a), and a card orthogonally adjacent to two growing cards gains +2 per refill

name: Glass Joker
head: Feeds on a particular kind of death
a: Gains a permanent multiplier every time a card of a named type is destroyed — **level 2:** It names two types
b: Gains a permanent multiplier every time any card is destroyed, at half the rate — **level 2:** It works at the full rate
c: Gains a permanent multiplier per card of a named type destroyed, and it names the type when acquired — **level 2:** It names two types

name: Hiker
head: Every card it sees gets permanently better. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards scoring through its cell gain double
a: Every card that scores permanently gains a small flat bonus
b: Every card that scores permanently gains a small flat bonus, capped per card
c: Every card that scores permanently gains a bonus, and this card gains one too for each

name: Hologram
head: Grows with the deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards added straight into the Entrance count twice
a: Gains a permanent multiplier every time a card is added to your deck
b: Gains a permanent multiplier per card added, and loses one per card removed
c: Gains a permanent multiplier per card added, doubled if the card was created by an effect

name: The One-Trick Pony
head: After the Cryptid mod's Jimball: rewards playing the same hand over and over ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0040 and Q0048, which you ruled on: repeats of a hand grow it*
a: Gains a multiplier per consecutive placement in which you score your most-played hand type — **level 2:** Switching hands halves it instead of emptying it
b: Gains a multiplier per Entrance refill in which you score your most-played hand, consecutive or not — **level 2:** A refill scoring the hand through its cell counts double
c: Gains a multiplier per consecutive placement scoring the same hand, and loses it all when you switch — **level 2:** Switching hands halves it instead of emptying it

name: Light Card
head: Grows, and asks for more. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its requirement rises every second time it grows
a: Gains a multiplier each time it scores in a full line, and raises by one the number of cards in that line that must sit on marks they match before it pays again: first any full line, then one hit, then two, up to five
b: As (a), but the hits are counted anywhere on the grid, not in the line
c: As (a), and the requirement resets each show

name: The Fixer-Upper
head: After the Cryptid mod's Pot of Jokes: starts as a penalty and grows out of it
a: Begins by shrinking the Entrance, and gives one slot back every show until it is a net gain — **level 2:** It gives back two slots a show
b: Begins by shrinking the Entrance, recovering one slot per show until it is neutral, and no further — **level 2:** It gives back two slots a show
c: Begins by shrinking the Entrance, and recovers one slot every time a line scores — **level 2:** Two per line

name: Ride the Bus
head: A streak that a face card breaks
a: Gains a multiplier per consecutive placement with no face card scoring, resetting the moment one does — **level 2:** A face card sitting on a mark it matches does not break the streak
b: Gains a multiplier per consecutive placement with no face card, and keeps half through the reset — **level 2:** A face card sitting on a mark it matches does not break the streak
c: Gains a multiplier per consecutive placement without any card of a rank you name — **level 2:** A card of the named rank sitting on a mark it matches does not break the streak

name: Runner
head: Permanent growth from one hand type. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It grows twice for hand types scored through its cell ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0040 and Q0048, which you ruled on: hand types grow with play*
a: Gains a permanent flat bonus each time a line scores as a named hand type
b: Gains a permanent flat bonus each time a line scores as any hand type it has not scored before
c: Gains a permanent bonus per named hand type scored, and the named type changes each show

name: Self-Granted Title
head: This card counts as one rarity higher for all effects and bonuses, but not for rarity-based rewards. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts as two tiers higher
a: Counts as one rarity higher for every effect and bonus, but not for rarity-based rewards
b: Counts as one rarity higher for everything, rarity-based rewards included
c: Counts as one rarity higher for every effect, and gains a further tier each time it wins a show single-handedly

name: The Fadista
head: Scores bonus points per card destroyed or lost this run. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts discarded cards too
a: Scores bonus points for every card destroyed or lost this run
b: Scores bonus points for every card destroyed or lost this show
c: Gains +1 permanent rank for every third card destroyed or lost this run

name: The Gentled Beast
head: Cards dropped on this card are not consumed but returned to the column below it; each one permanently adds +1 to this card's score bonus. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose where in the column each passing card lands
a: Cards dropped on this one are not consumed but pass to the nearest empty cell below it in its column, stacking on it if there is none, and each permanently adds +1 to this card's bonus
b: Cards dropped on this one pass to the nearest empty cell below it in its column, stacking on it if there is none and each adds +1 to this card's bonus for the show only
c: Cards dropped on this one pass to the nearest empty cell below it in its column, stacking on it if there is none, and each adds +1 rank to this card permanently

name: The Murga
head: Paid by the run's history. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also counts every mark matched this run
a: Scores per boss beaten, per card lost and per event survived this run
b: Scores per boss beaten this run only
c: Scores per boss beaten, card lost and event survived, and remembers across runs on the same profile

name: The Streak
head: Scoring in a row and going scoreless in a row both pay. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A streak survives one break
a: Each consecutive placement that completes a line adds a rising bonus to that line's bucket; a scoreless placement resets it
b: Each consecutive scoreless placement adds one to a slump; the next line to score pays the slump squared as flat points into its bucket and resets it, so filling the board without completing lines is a line of play
c: Both counters run at once, and whichever breaks pays

name: Weary Willie
head: Feeds on your losses. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also grows when your cards are discarded
a: Gains +1 rank permanently per card of yours destroyed or discarded, and per Entrance refill that completes no line
b: Gains +1 rank permanently per card destroyed, and +5 per Entrance refill that completes no line
c: Gains +1 rank per card destroyed, and loses it all the moment a show ends with none of your cards destroyed

name: The Lollipop
head: After the Cryptid mod's Clicked Cookie: wears out as you use it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cueing it costs it nothing
a: A large flat bonus that shrinks by one every time this card is cued
b: A large flat bonus that shrinks every time it is cued, and is destroyed at zero
c: A large flat bonus that shrinks with use and recovers one step per show it goes uncued

name: The Corn Dog
head: After the Cryptid mod's Fast Food M: on a timer you can extend. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each line scored through its cell adds a show to its life
a: A large bonus that self-destructs after a few shows; a specific action adds a show to its life
b: A large bonus that self-destructs after a few shows, with no way to extend it
c: A large bonus on a timer you may extend by destroying a card from your deck, one more each time

name: Glass
head: Scores double points, and is destroyed permanently after its third score ⚑ *pair review: a second Glass type: Q0268 is also Glass, transparent and brittle*
a: Scores double, and is destroyed for good after its third score
b: Scores double, with a 1-in-4 chance of shattering each time it scores
c: Scores double, and is destroyed at the end of any show in which it was covered

name: Ice Cream
head: Melts as the show runs. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It melts only on placements that match no mark
a: Starts with a large flat bonus that shrinks with every placement played, ending at nothing
b: Starts with a large flat bonus that shrinks each placement, and is destroyed when it reaches nothing
c: Starts with a large bonus that shrinks each placement, and cue at any time to cash out what remains

name: Persistent spin-buff (Sangmo)
head: Keeps spinning while the combo holds ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what the buff is*
a: A buff that lasts as long as the combo keeps rising, and ends the moment it does not — **level 2:** A combo that stalls while it sits on its own mark does not end the buff
b: A buff that decays one step per Entrance refill unless re-triggered — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark the buff does not decay
c: A buff that lasts while the combo rises and, when it ends, pays out everything it accumulated — **level 2:** A combo that stalls while it sits on its own mark does not end the buff; it pays out at show end at the latest

name: Starfruit
head: A huge exponent that decays away. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A placement that lands a card on a mark it matches does not decay it
a: Raises the multiplier to a power, losing part of the exponent every show
b: Raises the multiplier to a power, losing part of the exponent every placement
c: Raises the multiplier to a power that decays each placement, and recovers a step each placement that scores nothing

name: The Top
head: Spins until it topples
a: Cue to set it spinning: it scores a little every turn until it topples after a random duration — **level 2:** Its topple chance rises half as fast
b: Cue to set it spinning: it scores a little every turn and topples after exactly five turns — **level 2:** You may stop it early and keep what it scored
c: Cue to set it spinning; it scores more each turn it stays up, and topples on a rising chance — **level 2:** Its topple chance rises half as fast

name: Wax
head: Melts near fire
a: At each show end, loses 1 rank per Flames card that shared its column that show, and is destroyed at rank 0
b: At each show end, loses 1 rank per Flames card anywhere on its grid, and is destroyed at rank 0
c: Loses 1 rank the moment any Flames card is placed in its column, and is destroyed at rank 0

name: Burn After Reading
head: Spent the moment it is read ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what its effect is*
a: Cue: apply this card's effect to any target, then destroy this card — **level 2:** Cued from its own mark, it is not destroyed
b: Cue: apply this card's effect to any target; the card survives but can never be cued again — **level 2:** Cued from its own mark, it may be cued once more
c: Cue: apply this card's effect, then destroy it; it returns to the deck at the end of the run — **level 2:** Cued from its own mark, it returns next show, not next run

name: The Exhausted Card
head: Fires once, hugely, and is gone from the show
a: This card fires its effect at triple strength and is removed from the show, returning for the next one — **level 2:** It returns at the next Entrance refill instead of next show
b: This card fires at triple strength and is removed from the run entirely — **level 2:** It returns next show instead of leaving the run
c: This card fires at triple strength and is removed from the show; if it was in the placement that met the goal, it returns permanently upgraded — **level 2:** It returns upgraded if any line through its cell scored while it sat there

name: Flagpole Sitter
head: Gains bonus points for each consecutive show it ends as the top card of the same column; any move resets the streak to zero
a: Gains bonus points for each consecutive show it ends as the top card of the same column; any move resets it — **level 2:** Ending in an adjacent column keeps the streak
b: Gains +1 rank for each consecutive show it is never moved; being moved returns it to its printed rank — **level 2:** +2 rank per show
c: Gains a stacking multiplier for each consecutive show it ends in the exact same cell; being moved or covered resets it — **level 2:** Being covered no longer resets its streak

name: The Holdout
head: Stores one card outside the game across shows; cue once per run to insert it into any stack at any moment, but a town search loses it
a: Stores one card outside the game across shows; cue once per run to insert it into any stack at any moment, and a town search loses it — **level 2:** Twice per run
b: Stores one card outside the game across shows; cue once per show to insert it into any stack — **level 2:** The stored card may be swapped for another at any Entrance refill
c: Stores one card outside the game; it returns automatically at the moment its line would complete — **level 2:** Twice per run

name: The Running Gag
head: A counter that survives the curtain. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its counter survives this card being destroyed and returning
a: Any counter this card accumulates is kept across the show boundary rather than reset
b: Any counter this card accumulates is kept across shows, and halved at each boundary
c: Any counter on any card is kept across shows while this one is in the deck

name: The Standing Set
head: The board is not struck between shows
a: Cards left on the grid at show end stay there for the next show, and the entrance fills around them — **level 2:** Cards left standing keep the marks they sat on
b: The cards in one line of your choice are left standing between shows and the rest are struck — **level 2:** Cards left standing keep the marks they sat on
c: Cards left on the grid stay for the next show, but each one that stays scores a step less each time — **level 2:** Cards left standing on matched cells score no step less

name: Season Ticket
head: The run leaves something behind
a: The highest-scoring card of each run is added to the next run's starting deck
b: The highest-scoring card of each run is added to the pool, not the deck
c: One card of your choice from each finished run joins the next run's deck, upgraded

name: The Trunk
head: Packs something for next time. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It packs two cards
a: One card of your choice keeps everything it gained into the next run
b: One card of your choice keeps half of what it gained into the next run
c: One card keeps what it gained, and the card chosen is locked into the next run's starting deck

name: Ascended
head: A threshold that, once crossed, is never uncrossed
a: Once ten cards on this grid sit on marks they match at one moment, every card on it scores an extra step for the rest of the run — **level 2:** Eight are enough
b: Once ten cards on this grid sit on marks they match at one moment, every card on it scores an extra step for the rest of the show — **level 2:** Eight are enough
c: Once any three lines have scored the same hand type in one show, that hand type scores an extra step for the rest of the run — **level 2:** Two lines are enough

name: Permanent-toggle effect archetype
head: Once on, never off ⚑ *pair review: an archetype, not an effect: it does not say what stays on*
a: Once activated, this effect stays active for the rest of the show and can never be switched off — **level 2:** Switched on from its own mark, it stays on into the next show
b: Once activated, this effect stays active for the rest of the run and can never be switched off — **level 2:** Switched on from its own mark, it may be switched off once
c: Once activated it stays active permanently, and its strength grows the longer it has been on — **level 2:** Switched on from its own mark, it starts as if it had been on a whole show

name: The Sworn Oath
head: A promise you cannot take back
a: At show start, name a hand type; it scores double all show, and no other hand type may ever be named again this run — **level 2:** You may re-name the hand once, the moment it lands on its mark
b: At show start, name a hand type; it scores double this show, and the choice locks for the next show as well — **level 2:** The lock does not carry into the next show
c: Name a hand type at show start; it scores double, and each show you re-name the same one raises the bonus a step — **level 2:** Re-naming keeps the steps already earned

name: The Trance
head: Goes into a trance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It comes out of the trance without being Exhausted
a: Enters a trance for several turns: it acts on its own and is immune to everything, then is hard Exhausted
b: Enters a trance for several turns, immune and autonomous, and cannot be brought out early
c: Enters a trance you can end at any time; the longer it lasts the greater the payout and the harder the Exhaust

name: The Alchemist
head: Cue: transmute all statuses of one class on a target card into another class, count preserved. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It converts two kinds at once
a: Cue: turn every status of one kind on a target card into another kind, keeping the count
b: Cue: turn every status of one kind anywhere on the grid into another kind, keeping the count
c: Cue: turn every negative status on a target card into the positive status of your choice

name: The Fire Breather
head: Cue: apply Burning to every card in this card's entire row; this card becomes Exhausted. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It is not Exhausted
a: Cue: apply Burning to every card in this card's row, then Exhaust this card
b: Cue: apply Burning to every card in this card's row and column, then Exhaust this card
c: Cue: apply Burning to any five cells you choose in its grid, then Exhaust this card

name: Wet
head: A status that changes what may sit on what
a: A wet card may have any card stacked on it regardless of suit or rank, and dries at the end of the placement
b: A wet card may have anything stacked on it and spreads wet to whatever is stacked on it
c: A wet card may have anything stacked on it, scores a step less while wet, and dries only when a Flame prop crosses it

name: Eruption card
head: An eruption that snakes outward. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You steer the snake one step each turn
a: Cards catch Burning in an expanding snake pattern, with no way to stop it
b: Cards catch Burning in an expanding snake, which can be stopped by completing a line in its path
c: Cards catch Burning in an expanding snake whose direction is telegraphed one turn ahead

name: Fire spreading card
head: Fire that roads can stop. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Burning never spreads onto cards sitting on marks they match
a: Burning spreads to paper-type cards and is blocked by iron-type cards
b: Burning spreads to any card and is blocked only by a card that has already burned
c: Burning spreads along a suit and is blocked by any card of the opposing suit

name: The Contagion
head: Each Entrance refresh, every status on this card's neighbors copies one card further outward, with merge-by-class capping the counts. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which statuses spread
a: At each Entrance refresh, every status on this card's neighbours copies one cell further outward
b: At each Entrance refresh, every status on this card copies to all its orthogonal neighbours
c: At each Entrance refresh, statuses spread one cell outward from every card that carries one, anywhere on the grid

name: The Frostline
head: A status that walks along the line
a: At the end of each placement, this status moves from the card it is on to the next card along its row toward the edge it is nearer, turning down its column at the edge
b: At the end of each placement, this status copies itself onto the next card along its row toward the edge it is nearer, turning down its column at the edge rather than moving
c: At the end of each placement, this status moves one card along its row toward the edge it is nearer, turning down its column at the edge and grows a step stronger each time it moves

name: Tinder
head: Catches whatever lands on it

b: Whenever a card is placed on this one, the covering card catches Burning, and so does everything above it
c: Whenever a card is placed on this one, the covering card catches Burning; if it is already Burning, this card is destroyed and the whole column catches

name: Ascetic
head: This card is immune to hazard effects that target rows or the floor
a: Ignores any hazard or debuff that targets a whole row or column — **level 2:** It ignores every hazard
b: Ignores any hazard or debuff aimed at its row, its column or its stack as a whole, and passes it to the card above — **level 2:** It ignores every hazard
c: Ignores every hazard while it is the lowest card in its stack — **level 2:** Whatever its height

name: Canvas
head: The first debuff or status applied to this card each show is discarded
a: The first status or debuff applied to this card each show is discarded
b: This card can never carry a status at all, good or bad
c: Statuses applied to this card are passed to the card directly above it instead

name: Digital
head: This card cannot be discarded from the grid by any effect
a: This card cannot be removed from the grid by any effect
b: This card cannot be removed from the grid or the deck by any effect, including your own
c: This card cannot be removed from the grid; an effect that tries removes the card above it instead

name: Iron Body
head: Immune to the first destruction or debuff that targets this card each show. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A hit it prevents mints two rank-1 token cards, which are ghosts
a: Immune to the first destruction or debuff that targets it each show
b: Immune to all destruction, but not to debuffs
c: Immune to the first destruction each show, which is redirected to the card above it

name: Meal Call
head: Cue, once per show: every card on the grid removes one debuff or status
a: Cue, once per show: every card on the grid sheds one debuff or status — **level 2:** Twice per show
b: Cue, once per show: every card on the grid sheds all debuffs and statuses — **level 2:** Twice per show
c: Cue with unlimited uses: one card sheds all its debuffs and statuses — **level 2:** Every card in the target's lines sheds them too

name: Sacred juggling (Daikagura)

b: Each Balls meld scored removes one debuff from every card in that meld
c: Each meld of the suit this card carries removes one debuff from the grid

name: The Cleansing Pass

a: Consumable: remove every status from every card on one grid
b: Consumable: remove every status from every card on one grid, and score a step per status removed
c: Consumable: remove one status from every card on the board, choosing which status

name: The Incubator
head: Repairs whatever it covers
a: Each placement a card sits covered by this one, that card sheds one debuff and recovers 1 lost rank — **level 2:** It also cleans the card above it
b: Each placement a card sits covered by this one, that card sheds all debuffs; lost rank is not restored — **level 2:** It also cleans the card above it

name: The Purifier
head: A card nothing sticks to

b: This card cannot receive statuses, and strips one status from each adjacent card each placement — **level 2:** Each status it strips scores a step
c: This card can receive statuses but discards them at the end of each placement, scoring a step for each one it shed — **level 2:** It scores two steps per status shed

name: Mud Show

b: Town rule: every stack pickup after the first each placement discards the top card of the deck

name: The Tooth

b: Lose points for every card placed after the first five of each show
c: Lose points for every card placed, and gain double that for every line completed

name: Cards cannot retire until scored
head: Nothing leaves until it has performed

b: A card cannot be removed until it has scored at least once; abilities firing do not count — **level 2:** A card sitting on a mark it matches may be removed by cue once it has scored, freeing its cell
c: A card cannot be removed until it has scored, and removing it pays more the more it has scored — **level 2:** Removing a card that sits on a mark it matches pays double

name: Diet Cola
head: Destroy it to get something else
a: Cue: destroy this card to create a free bonus of a named kind — **level 2:** The bonus it creates is doubled
b: Cue: destroy this card to create a free bonus you choose from three — **level 2:** You keep two of the three
c: Cue: destroy this card to create a free bonus scaling with how long you held it — **level 2:** The bonus it creates is doubled

name: The Egress

a: Cue: send any grid card to the discard
b: Cue: send any grid card to the discard, and this card gains +1 rank
c: Cue: send any grid card to the discard, or destroy it outright and gain its rank

name: Common

a: While in the deck, doubles the chance of Rare cards appearing among rewards — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, the next reward offered contains a Rare
b: While in the deck, doubles the chance of the rarity one step above this card's own appearing among rewards — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, the next reward offered contains a Rare

name: The Applause Meter

b: Completed lines pay applause, spent during the show, and whatever is unspent converts to points at show end — **level 2:** Lines through its cell pay double applause

name: The Cheap Pop
head: When scored, grants a small bonus fame in every town. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The fame it grants is also granted to the next town on the map
a: When scored, grants a small amount of bonus fame in every town
b: When scored, grants bonus fame scaling with how many shows you have already played in this town
c: When scored, grants bonus fame, doubled in any town you have never performed in before

name: Luxury Tax
head: Wealth costs you room ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: The Entrance shrinks by one card for every fixed amount of points you have scored — **level 2:** Each card the Entrance has lost adds +1 to the multiplier of lines through its cell
b: The Entrance shrinks by one for every fixed amount of points scored, down to a floor of two — **level 2:** Each card the Entrance has lost adds +1 to the multiplier of lines through its cell
c: The grid loses one usable cell for every fixed amount of points scored — **level 2:** A lost cell in its lines counts as filled, so a line through it completes with four cards

name: The Advance
head: Spend what you have not earned. **Level 2, on its own mark:** An advanced line that completes through its cell pays the advance again
a: Cue once per show: name an incomplete line; it scores now as if complete, uncovered marks standing in for its empty cells; if it has not truly completed by show end, the next show's reward is skipped
b: As (a), and the line also scores normally when it completes
c: As (a), and each further show it stays incomplete skips one more reward

name: The Claque
head: Consumable: raises this show's fame floor to 60% of goal, but every later show's reward drops
a: Consumable: this show's floor rises to 60% of goal, and every later show's reward drops by 2%, forever
b: Consumable: this show's floor rises to 60% of goal, and the next three shows' rewards drop by 5%
c: Consumable: this show's floor rises to 60% of goal, and every later show's reward drops by 5%

name: The Overload
head: Borrowing against the next placement ⚑ *pair review: assumes cued effects have a cost; nothing prices them*
a: An effect may be fired before it is paid for; the cost comes out of the next placement's resources — **level 2:** The unpaid cost comes out of the placement after next
b: An effect may be fired before it is paid for, at a surcharge; the cost comes out of the next placement — **level 2:** It charges no surcharge
c: Any cued effect may be fired unpaid once per show, and the debt is settled at show end from your score — **level 2:** The debt settled at show end is halved

name: Banner
head: Paid for the discards that never happened
a: Scores bonus points at show end for every card on the board, but only if no card was discarded from the board this show — **level 2:** Cards discarded from matched cells do not count against it
b: Scores bonus points at show end, one step fewer for every card discarded from the board this show — **level 2:** Cards discarded from matched cells do not count against it
c: Scores bonus points for every card in the discard pile — **level 2:** A card discarded from a matched cell counts twice in the pile

name: Crazy Tan escalating draw penalty

a: Each consecutive Entrance refill in which no card lands on a mark it matches sends one more card than the last from the top of a stock you choose to the discard; a hit resets it — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, the penalty does not grow

name: Green Joker

b: Gains a multiplier per Entrance refill this show, and discards cost it nothing — **level 2:** A discard from a matched cell gains it a multiplier instead of costing nothing

name: The Loose Card
head: Discard whatever the plan has no use for. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The freed cell's mark is re-dealt from the top card of a stock you choose
a: A card sitting on a mark it matches on nothing may be discarded freely, and its cell is empty again
b: As (a), and the top of a stock you choose is flipped into the Entrance
c: As (a), and the discarded card goes to the bottom of its stock instead of the discard pile

name: Fame banks at Continue
head: A win is not banked until you say so ⚑ *pair review: an engine rule about when a win is committed, and undo already covers the show; (c) is the only new effect*

c: Fame is committed when you press Continue, and you may replay the show once instead of banking it — **level 2:** The replay keeps the better of the two scores

name: Live undo during resolution
head: Undo mid-resolution ⚑ *pair review: an engine rule about undo during resolution, not a card effect*
a: Pressing Undo during a resolving placement cancels it: resolution fast-forwards and the board before it returns, costing no placement — **level 2:** You may undo two placements back
b: Pressing Undo during a resolving placement cancels it, but the placement is still spent — **level 2:** The placement is refunded
c: Pressing Undo during a resolving placement pauses it, letting you resume or cancel after seeing what has resolved so far — **level 2:** You may resume from any step you choose

name: The Rewinder
head: Spends your safety net for points
a: Cue: destroy your oldest undo snapshots for bonus points each, up to five per Entrance refill — **level 2:** You choose which snapshots it destroys
b: Cue: destroy every undo snapshot you hold for bonus points each, once per show — **level 2:** The newest snapshot survives the cue
c: Cue: destroy your oldest undo snapshot for bonus points scaling with how many turns ago it was taken — **level 2:** You choose which snapshots it destroys

name: The Second Roll
head: Take the offer again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The discarded cards go to the bottom of their stocks instead of the discard pile
a: Cue once per show: discard the whole entrance and refill it
b: Cue once per show: discard any number of entrance cards and refill only those slots
c: Cue: discard the whole entrance and refill it; each use this show discards one more card from the new Entrance than the last

name: Burglar
head: More cards, no discards. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each Entrance refill puts one more discard-pile card on top of a stock you choose
a: When a show begins, three cards of your choice from the discard pile are dealt to the tops of stocks you choose, but no effect may discard a card from the board this show
b: When a show begins, three random discard-pile cards join the stocks, and every card discarded this show is destroyed instead of going to the pile
c: You choose at show start how many discard-pile cards to take; each one makes the next card discarded this show be destroyed instead of kept

name: John Robinson
head: Elite hazard: the show is cut short, with the goal unchanged
a: Elite hazard: the show ends after a fixed number of placements, well short of the deck, with the goal unchanged
b: Elite hazard: the show ends after a fixed number of placements, and the goal drops 20%
c: Elite hazard: the show ends the moment any grid is completely filled

name: The All-Nighter
head: Three times the show
a: Show: triple the placements, triple the goal, triple the reward
b: Show: triple the placements and goal, with the reward scaling to how far past the goal you get
c: Show: triple the placements and goal, and the deck is not reshuffled between them

name: The Needle
head: Boss: one placement only
a: Boss: the show has a single Entrance refill, at a proportionally lower goal
b: Boss: the show has a single Entrance refill at the full goal
c: Boss: the show has a single Entrance refill at a proportionally lower goal, and the one line it can complete pays into all three buckets

name: The Taxi Meter
head: After the Cryptid mod's Lavender Loop: the goal grows while you think. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each line through its cell takes the goal back one step ⚑ *pair review: fame is not spendable*
a: The show's goal rises steadily with real time spent in it
b: The show's goal rises with the number of actions taken, not with real time
c: The show's goal rises with real time, and pausing stops the clock at the cost of the show's reward

name: The Interval
head: Buy the room back ⚑ *pair review: patience exists only under your Q0059 boss rule*
a: Consumable: restore the patience total to full, once per show
b: Consumable: restore half the patience total, usable any number of times, each use discarding a stock's top card
c: Consumable: restore the patience total to full, and the next placement does not spend any

name: Roman Numerals rank
head: A rank that keeps time. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on a rank mark it matches, its clock stops
a: Ranks run 1 to 12 and wrap; the rank advances by 1 with every player action
b: Ranks run 1 to 12 and wrap; the rank advances by 1 with every line completed
c: Ranks run 1 to 12 and wrap; the rank advances by 1 per action, and you may cue to stop the clock for one placement

name: The Charivari
head: If 4 or more cards are placed onto the grid on the first turn of a show, gain bonus multiplier on the show's first placement's payout ⚑ *pair review: it counts turns, and the board has no turn; an Entrance refill is the nearest unit*
a: If four or more cards are placed on the first turn of a show, the show's first placement's payout gains a multiplier — **level 2:** Its multiplier also applies to lines through its cell
b: If the whole Entrance is placed within one turn, that placement's payout gains a multiplier — **level 2:** Its multiplier also applies to lines through its cell
c: Each placement gains a multiplier scaling with how few turns it took to fill the lines that scored in it — **level 2:** Lines through its cell count as filled one turn faster

name: The House Clock
head: Everything on the board is on a timer
a: Every card on the grid carries a counter that drops on each placement; a card whose counter reaches zero fires its effect unprompted — **level 2:** Cards sitting on marks they match count down twice as fast
b: Every card carries a counter that drops on each placement, and a card at zero is removed rather than firing — **level 2:** A card sitting on a mark it matches resets to full at zero instead of being removed
c: Every card carries a counter that drops each Entrance refill rather than each placement, and fires at zero — **level 2:** Cards sitting on marks they match count down twice as fast

name: The Saga
head: A card that tells its story one beat per placement. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It advances two chapters when a line through its cell scores
a: This card advances one chapter each time you place a card anywhere, firing a larger effect at each of three chapters, then is destroyed
b: This card advances one chapter per Entrance refill rather than per placement, and holds on the board once its last chapter fires
c: This card advances one chapter per Entrance refill, and you may spend a placement to hold it on its current chapter

name: The Ticking Card
head: Its own clock, running on your actions. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A placement onto a matched cell counts it down twice
a: This card carries a counter that drops by one on every placement anywhere; at zero it fires its effect and resets
b: This card carries a counter that drops on every placement; at zero it fires and the counter resets one higher
c: This card carries a counter that drops on every placement; at zero it fires and the card is spent

name: The Vanishing Act
head: A countdown that runs whatever you do. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Scoring it adds two counters back
a: This card loses one counter each placement and is destroyed at zero; its effect scales with the counters remaining
b: This card loses one counter each Entrance refill and is destroyed at zero; its effect scales with the counters remaining
c: This card loses one counter each placement and is destroyed at zero, but scoring it adds a counter back

name: La Belle Lucie merci rule
head: One mercy move. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The mercy move may carry the moved card's mark with it, swapping marks with the cell it enters, so a hit stays a hit
a: When no card in the Entrance matches any uncovered mark, one grid card may be moved one cell into an empty neighbour; landing on a mark it matches pays the match
b: When no card in the Entrance matches any uncovered mark, one grid card may be moved to any empty cell, once per show
c: One mercy move per show, stuck or not, lost if unused

name: Limited Move Solitaire
head: A budget of moves for the whole show
a: The show allows a fixed number of moves in total, and running out ends it — **level 2:** A line through its cell refunds a move
b: The show allows a fixed number of moves, and unused moves convert to score at the end — **level 2:** Unused moves convert at double while it sits on its own mark
c: The show allows a fixed number of moves; each line completed refunds one — **level 2:** A line through its cell refunds two moves

name: Soundcheck
head: At show start, grants one free move (grab and place one stack) before the first Entrance refresh, without spending a placement. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The free move may also take a card from the discard pile
a: Once per show, while this card is on the grid, one free grab-and-place costing no placement
b: At the start of every placement, one free grab-and-place costing no placement
c: At show start, one free grab-and-place, and another every time a grid is completely filled

name: Stuntman
head: Huge, and it costs you room
a: A very large flat bonus, at the cost of two Entrance slots — **level 2:** While it sits on its mark the Entrance has all its slots back and the bonus stays
b: A very large flat bonus, at the cost of one placement per show — **level 2:** It costs no placement in a show in which it lands on its mark
c: A very large flat bonus, at the cost of two Entrance slots, refundable by destroying it — **level 2:** While it sits on its mark the Entrance has all its slots back and the bonus stays

name: The Automation
head: Something you used to do by hand starts doing itself. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, each action counts twice toward becoming automatic ⚑ *pair review: it does not say which actions it automates or what automatic means*
a: An action you have performed enough times becomes automatic for the rest of the run
b: An action performed enough times becomes automatic for the rest of the run, and you may switch it off
c: An action performed enough times becomes automatic permanently for the rest of the run, even if this card is later removed from play

name: The Double Harvest
head: Two placements, never the same cell. **Level 2, on its own mark:** If both cards land on marks they match, a third card may be placed
a: Cue: place two Entrance cards this turn instead of one, into different cells
b: Cue: place two Entrance cards this turn into different cells, and only the second may complete a line
c: Cue: place two Entrance cards into different cells; a line that both of them complete scores twice

name: The Sanctioned Cheat
head: You may break placement legality, carefully. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A cheat onto a cell whose mark the card matches is free
a: You may place a card anywhere regardless of legality a limited number of times per show
b: You may place a card anywhere regardless of legality at any time, but each cheat permanently raises the show's goal
c: You may cheat once per show, and the cheated card is marked and scores nothing

name: Time-travel card
head: After the game 5D Chess With Multiverse Time Travel: sends a card into the past. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The rewound board keeps the cards sitting on marks they match
a: Cue: send a card into a past board state, play that board out, and keep only what differs from the present
b: Cue: send a card into the previous placement's board state and replay that turn with it there
c: Cue: rewind the grid to its state three placements ago, keeping every card you have gained since

name: Labyrinth
head: Every placement is the show's first placement. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also counts every Entrance refill as the show's first
a: Every placement counts as the show's first placement for every effect that cares
b: Every placement counts as the show's first placement, and every discard as the first discard
c: Every placement counts as the first, and every placement also counts as the last

name: The Crowd Takes Over
head: The audience plays your turn. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The audience places onto matched cells whenever it can
a: For one placement, a seeded random audience makes your moves for you
b: For one placement the audience makes your moves, and anything it scores pays double
c: For one placement the audience proposes each move and you may veto one of them

name: The Forethought
head: Acts on both sides of its own move
a: Cue: this card acts once before it moves and once after, at the cost of never being able to gain height that turn — **level 2:** It pays no height cost
b: Cue: this card acts before and after it moves, with no cost — **level 2:** It acts a third time if it lands on another mark it matches
c: Cue: choose per placement whether this card acts before moving, after, or both at the cost of its height — **level 2:** It pays no height cost

name: The Fourth Wall
head: Once per Entrance refill, during scoring resolution, pauses the show to allow one grab/place before resolution continues. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The paused line scores once before the grab and place and once after it
a: Once per Entrance refill, pause scoring mid-resolution to make one grab and place before resolution continues
b: Once per show, pause scoring mid-resolution to make one grab and place
c: Once per Entrance refill, pause scoring mid-resolution to make one grab and place, but the paused line scores at half

name: The Stance
head: A mode you are in until you leave it
a: Cue: enter Rows or Columns; lines of that kind add +1 to the combo and lines of the other kind add nothing; switch once per Entrance refill — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you may switch stance any number of times
b: Cue: enter Rows or Columns; the chosen kind pays double and the other pays half; switching sends an Entrance card to the discard — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, switching costs nothing
c: Cue at show start: enter Rows, Columns or Special; that bucket pays double for the show and cannot be changed — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you may change stance once

name: The Time Signature
head: Splits the placement in two. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell resolve in both halves
a: Rows score when the placement scores as normal; columns score at the start of the next placement against the board as it then stands, and the combo carries across
b: Rows score when the placement scores; columns score at the start of the next placement at half value
c: You choose per Entrance refill whether rows or columns resolve first, and the second one resolves against the board the first one left

name: The Judge's Buzzer
head: After the Got Talent shows' Golden Buzzer: consumable, once per run: skips one town's requirement entirely for an instant win with full rewards
a: Consumable, once per run: one show is skipped and counts as won with full rewards
b: Consumable, once per run: one show is skipped and counts as won, with no rewards
c: Consumable, once per run: one show is won immediately at whatever score is already on the grid

name: The Early Curtain
head: Stop while you are ahead. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts every card left in the stocks, not whole refills
a: Cue: End the show now, if the goal is met; the fame it banks is multiplied by the Entrance refills still left in the stocks
b: Cue: End the show now, if the goal is met; the fame it banks is multiplied by the refills left, but the next show's target rises
c: Cue: end the show now and keep the board standing into the next show as well as the payout

name: The Gong
head: Town hazard: any placement scoring under 25% of goal ends the show immediately
a: Town hazard: any placement scoring under 25% of goal ends the show at once
b: Town hazard: any placement scoring under 25% of goal costs you an Entrance card, discarded
c: Town hazard: any placement scoring less than the one before it ends the show at once

name: The Big Top
head: Priced in board space; its row and column can never complete, so only a diagonal scores it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It blocks only the neighbours you choose
a: This card blocks the four cells beside it for the show, and every diagonal through it pays triple
b: This card blocks the four cells beside it, and each diagonal through it pays a step per cell still blocked
c: This card blocks its neighbours until a diagonal through it scores, then releases them and its row and column open

name: The Clearance
head: Room is the resource. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Effects fired from its lines cost one empty cell less ⚑ *pair review: assumes cued effects have a cost; nothing prices them*
a: Effects are paid for with empty cells at a fixed rate
b: Effects may be paid for with empty cells or points, your choice, at a fixed rate
c: Effects are paid for with empty cells, and a full grid means nothing can fire

name: The Deposit
head: Pay a cell to fire ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what its effect is; the per-card form of Q0764, effects paid for with empty cells*
a: Cue: permanently destroy one empty cell on the grid to fire this card's effect — **level 2:** The destroyed cell returns at show end
b: Cue: block one empty cell for the rest of the show to fire this card's effect — **level 2:** The blocked cell unblocks when this card leaves
c: Cue: block one empty cell per use, so repeated use costs more and more room — **level 2:** The cost does not grow

name: The Ground Rent
head: One card each Entrance refill buys nothing but space. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A resource card placed on a mark it matches still scores ⚑ *pair review: assumes cued effects have a cost; nothing prices them*
a: One card per Entrance refill must be placed as a resource rather than scored; it never scores, but it pays for cued effects all show
b: One card per Entrance refill may be placed as a resource rather than scored; you choose whether to spend the placement that way
c: One card per Entrance refill is placed as a resource, and resource cards form their own line that scores at show end

name: The Augment Offer
head: Three permanent choices at fixed points in the run
a: At three fixed points in the run you are offered three run-permanent effects and must take one
b: At three fixed points you are offered three run-permanent effects and must take one, with one reroll per offer
c: At three fixed points you are offered three, must take one, and the two refused are removed from the pool for the rest of the run

name: The Casting Call
head: Lets you choose the target every time. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may split its effect between two targets ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what its effect is*
a: Each time this card triggers, you choose which card its effect lands on
b: Each time this card triggers, you choose the target from three the card offers
c: Each time this card triggers you choose the target, and choosing the same one twice running doubles it

name: The Director's Note
head: Fires, then asks
a: When a line scores, choose which of its cards keeps the bonus for the rest of the show — **level 2:** You choose two cards instead of one
b: When a line scores, choose one of its cards to score again immediately — **level 2:** You choose two cards instead of one
c: When a line scores, choose between a large bonus now and a smaller permanent one — **level 2:** The permanent bonus is also printed on the mark under the chosen card, and the next card to match that mark inherits it

name: The Discovery
head: Three doors, pick one
a: Consumable: three cards are drawn from the deck and shown; take one and bin the other two
b: Consumable: three cards are shown from anywhere in the deck; take one, and the other two return to the top
c: Consumable: three cards are shown; take one now and one more later in the show, and bin the third

name: The Fork
head: Two roads, pick one
a: Consumable: offers two effects drawn at random; you take one and the other is lost
b: Consumable: offers two effects; you take one now and the other becomes available next show
c: Consumable: offers three effects and you take one, with the rejected two raising the odds of better offers later

name: Bus Driver
head: Usually great, sometimes awful. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It shows whether the next payout is the bad one before it fires, and you may hold it back once a show
a: A large multiplier three times in four, and an equally large penalty the fourth
b: A large multiplier three times in four, and nothing the fourth
c: A large multiplier three times in four and a penalty the fourth, with the odds improving each time it pays out

name: Chocolate Die
head: A die decides what happens next
a: Beating a boss rolls a die to start a random event
b: Beating a boss rolls a die to start a random event, and you may reroll once
c: Beating a boss rolls a die whose faces you have collected over the run

name: Glitched
head: Every number on it is a lie
a: Every value on this card is randomised within a wide band, rerolled each show — **level 2:** You choose which of its values is rerolled
b: Every value on this card is randomised once, when acquired, and fixed thereafter — **level 2:** Landing on its mark, you may reroll one of its values once, permanently
c: Every value is randomised each placement, so the same card is different every time it fires — **level 2:** You choose which of its values is rerolled

name: Misprint
head: A wildly variable bonus. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The roll is made after the line is known, and you choose which line through its cell takes it
a: Scores a random multiplier between nothing and a large amount, rerolled every placement
b: Scores a random multiplier between nothing and a large amount, fixed for the whole show once rolled
c: Scores a random multiplier, and you may reroll it once per Entrance refill

name: Snake Oil
head: Consumable: gives +3 rank to one card this show, with a seeded 1-in-4 chance of doing nothing
a: Consumable: +3 rank to one card this show, with a 1-in-4 chance of doing nothing at all
b: Consumable: +3 rank to one card permanently, with a 1-in-2 chance of doing nothing at all
c: Consumable: +3 rank to one card this show; on the 1-in-4 failure it instead loses 3 rank

name: Trick-or-Treat
head: Destroyed, it is a treat or a trick. What it creates stays in the deck, curse included. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It creates three tokens instead of two
a: When destroyed, usually creates two useful tokens, and occasionally a cursed card instead
b: When destroyed, creates two useful tokens or a cursed card at even odds
c: When destroyed, creates tokens or a curse, and you may destroy a second card to improve the odds

name: Wheel of Death roulette
head: A wheel that lands where the knife did. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may re-spin once for free
a: A bonus wheel spins and pays out on the cell where the last Knives card scored
b: A bonus wheel spins and pays out on a random cell, with the payout scaling with that cell's rank
c: A bonus wheel spins where the last Knives card scored, and you may re-spin once at the cost of half the payout

name: Fragile
head: Its odds cannot be improved. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The first roll that would destroy it on its mark erases the mark instead
a: A large multiplier with a small chance of destruction each trigger, and no effect may alter those odds
b: A large multiplier with a small chance of destruction, and odds-improving effects work on it normally
c: A large multiplier whose destruction odds cannot be altered, and which grows each time it survives

name: Non Verisimile
head: Long odds pay proportionally. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Checks made by cards sitting on marks they match count twice
a: Whenever a probability check succeeds, gains a multiplier equal to how unlikely it was
b: Whenever a probability check succeeds, gains a fixed multiplier regardless of the odds
c: Whenever a probability check succeeds, gains a multiplier equal to its odds, and loses one when a check fails

name: The Horseshoe
head: After Balatro's Oops! All 6s: doubles every chance in the game
a: Every stated probability in the game is doubled — **level 2:** Probabilities against you are no longer doubled
b: Every stated probability affecting your own cards is doubled — **level 2:** Probabilities for cards sitting on marks they match are tripled
c: Every stated probability is doubled, including the ones that work against you — **level 2:** Probabilities against you are no longer doubled

name: The Balanced Pool
head: Every roll pulled toward the middle
a: Every probability roll this show is rolled twice and the results averaged — **level 2:** You may keep either roll instead of the average
b: Every probability roll this show is rolled twice and the worse result taken, but each success pays double — **level 2:** Rolls from cards sitting on marks they match take the better result instead
c: Every probability roll draws from a pool that empties as it is used, so results even out over the show — **level 2:** You may look at the next result in the pool before it is drawn

name: Wheel of Hope
head: Paid for its failures
a: Gains a permanent multiplier every time one of your probability checks fails — **level 2:** A failed check made on a matched cell counts twice
b: Gains a permanent multiplier every time a probability check fails, and loses it when one succeeds — **level 2:** A success no longer takes its multiplier away
c: Gains a permanent multiplier per failed check, scaling with how likely that check was to succeed — **level 2:** A failed check made on a matched cell counts twice

name: Injury stacking status
head: Injuries stack, and they end careers. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line through its cell sheds every injury stack on it ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Each placement a card performs may add an injury stack, and each stack raises the chance it retires permanently; a card that sits out a placement sheds one
b: Each placement may add an injury stack raising the retirement chance; stacks never clear
c: Each placement may add an injury stack; a card sits out to shed one, and a protective card lowers the chance

name: Net card lowers retirement, raises injury
head: A net changes the odds. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It lowers the retirement chance of the cards beside it too ⚑ *pair review: injury and retirement exist only if Q0787 enters, and it does not say whose odds it changes*
a: Raises the chance of injury but lowers the chance of retirement
b: Lowers the chance of retirement without affecting injury at all
c: Raises injury chance and lowers retirement chance, and converts each prevented retirement into fame

name: The Bruise
head: Damage that does not heal on its own
a: A bruised card scores a step less; bruises stack, and a card at three bruises is destroyed
b: A bruised card scores a step less; bruises stack and clear one per show
c: A bruised card scores a step less and cannot be moved; bruises never clear, and a card at three is removed from the run

name: The Corruption Meter
head: Failure accumulates where you can see it ⚑ *pair review: a placement has no target of its own*
a: Each placement that completes no line adds one corruption; at five, a random card leaves the deck for the run — **level 2:** Placements onto a mark the card matches add none
b: As (a), and each corruption raises the show's goal a step; corruption never clears — **level 2:** Placements onto a mark the card matches add none
c: Each placement that completes no line adds one corruption and each placement that completes one removes one — **level 2:** A line through its cell removes two

name: Contract Ink
head: Scores +X points per show it is played; if benched two shows in a row, it is permanently removed from the deck
a: Scores bonus points each show it is played; two consecutive shows unplaced and it is removed from the deck for good — **level 2:** A show in which it lands on its mark counts as two shows played
b: Scores bonus points each show it is played; one show unplaced and it drops a rarity tier — **level 2:** A show in which it lands on its mark counts as two shows played
c: Scores double points each show it is played, and is removed from the deck for good after five shows regardless — **level 2:** A show in which it lands on its mark does not count toward its five

name: Railroad Jump
head: Map-edge hazard: traveling this route costs one card, permanently removed from the deck
a: Map hazard: taking this route costs one card, removed from the deck for good
b: Map hazard: taking this route costs one card of your choice, removed from the deck for good
c: Map hazard: taking this route costs one random card, which returns two towns later

name: The Last Season
head: A card that has a last night. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each show it lands on its mark adds a show to its life
a: This card scores double, and is permanently removed from the deck after three shows
b: This card scores double, and is removed after three shows unless it scored in each of them
c: This card scores double and is removed after three shows, leaving behind a permanent upgrade for whichever card was next to it most often

name: The Void
head: Take a card out of the run for good
a: Consumable: remove any card from the run permanently; every remaining card of its suit is upgraded a step
b: Consumable: remove any card from the run permanently and gain its rank as a permanent bonus to one other card
c: Consumable: remove any card from the run permanently; the deck pays out a step per card removed this way, compounding

name: Bull-leap vault
head: Dodges the attack and takes a bow. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It dodges for its whole row as well
a: When a boss attacks this card's column, it dodges and scores instead
b: When a boss attacks anywhere on its grid, this card dodges the hit for the whole column and scores
c: When a boss attacks this card's column, it dodges and scores; each successful dodge raises the score it takes

name: Deus ex Machina
head: Consumable, once per run: when a show is lost, it is instead won at exactly the goal
a: Consumable, once per run: a lost show is instead won at exactly its goal
b: Consumable: a lost show is replayed from the start with the same deck and a fresh seed
c: Consumable, once per run: a lost show is won, and the next show's goal doubles

name: The Elimination Save
head: Two would die, so they duel
a: When two cards would be destroyed at once, they duel and the winner survives — **level 2:** The loser goes to the top of a stock you choose instead of the discard
b: When two cards would be destroyed at once, you choose which survives — **level 2:** Both survive when one of them sits on a mark it matches
c: When two cards would be destroyed at once they duel, and the survivor takes the loser's rank — **level 2:** The survivor also takes the loser's skill

name: The Mime
head: Takes the hit for the stack
a: Attaches to a stack and absorbs the first hostile effect aimed at any card in it — **level 2:** It absorbs the first two hostile effects
b: Attaches to a stack and absorbs every hostile effect aimed at it, breaking after three — **level 2:** It does not break
c: Attaches to a stack and absorbs the first hostile effect each show, refreshing between shows — **level 2:** It absorbs the first two hostile effects

name: All In card
head: Double now, double the goal. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The goal rises by half the multiplier instead of all of it ⚑ *pair review: it raises the next goal, which the overscore ruling tells effects not to do*
a: On the next score, the total doubles, and so does the score needed next round
b: On the next score the total doubles, and the next show's goal rises by half
c: You choose the multiplier; the goal rises by the same multiplier

name: The Colossus
head: After the Cryptid mod's Flesh Panopticon: an enormous boss that pays enormously
a: Boss: the goal is many times larger than normal, and beating it grants an outsized reward
b: Boss: the goal is many times larger, and you may decline it for a lesser reward
c: Boss: you set the multiplier on the goal yourself, and the reward scales with it

name: Overpurified
head: Past the goal is not free. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell pay triple past the goal ⚑ *pair review: the show ends the moment its goal is met, so nothing scores after it*
a: Cue: once the show's goal is met, every line you score pays double, but if the show ends short of double the goal those lines score nothing
b: Cue: once the show's goal is met, every line you score pays double
c: Cue: once the show's goal is met, every line you score pays double, but a line holding no card that sits on a mark it matches pays nothing

name: Risk/reward doubled-points tricks
head: Bigger tricks fail more often. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Tricks attempted from its lines fail at the lower tier's rate ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a trick is*
a: Higher-tier tricks pay more and fail more often, with risk-lowering cards to manage it
b: Higher-tier tricks pay more and fail more often, and you opt in per trick
c: Every trick may be attempted at doubled points for doubled failure chance, chosen per attempt

name: The Bullet Catch
head: When scored, scores 10x rank, but has a seeded 1-in-13 chance of being destroyed instead. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its destruction chance halves
a: When scored, scores ten times its rank, with a 1-in-13 chance of being destroyed instead
b: When scored, scores ten times its rank, with a 1-in-13 chance of being destroyed; each survival shortens the odds by one
c: When scored, you choose the multiplier up to ten times rank, and the destruction chance scales with it

name: The Committee
head: Test a ghost: a hit makes it real. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The ghost may copy any card on the grid, stamps and skill included
a: Cue: create a ghost copy of any card in your deck in the Entrance; if it lands on a mark it matches, it becomes real and stays in the deck
b: As (a), and it pays a large reward the moment it becomes real
c: Cue: create a ghost copy of any card in your deck; it becomes real only if a line through it completes as a made hand

name: The Mask Wager
head: Stake your identity ⚑ *pair review: a duel needs an opponent, and a solitaire has none*
a: Duel: stake a card's stamp and identity; losing unmasks it permanently across the save file
b: Duel: stake a card's stamp; losing removes the stamp but leaves the card
c: Duel: stake a card's identity, and the prize is the opponent's, so a win doubles your stamps

name: Entrance-set betting proposal
head: Bet on this Entrance against the next. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A winning wager on a refill whose cards landed on matched cells pays double ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what is staked; (c) sold the Entrance, and there is no currency*
a: Before placing, wager on whether the current Entrance will out-score the next one
b: Before placing, wager on whether the current Entrance will out-score the next; winning lets you keep both
c: Before placing, you may discard the current Entrance unseen and take the next instead

name: Mock the Booking
head: Talks the contract down ⚑ *pair review: depends on Q0811 (The Booking) entering*
a: Once per tour, reduce the declared Booking target — **level 2:** Twice per tour
b: Once per tour, reduce the declared Booking target by half — **level 2:** Twice per tour
c: Once per show, reduce the declared Booking target, but the reward falls by the same fraction — **level 2:** The reward does not fall

name: The Booking
head: Declares a goal/term for the show (e.g. score X with no Knife melds); fulfilling it grants bonus fame, missing it triggers a worse penalty. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A missed term costs nothing if a line through its cell scored
a: Declare a term for the show before it starts - a score with a named restriction; meeting it pays a bonus, missing it costs more than the bonus was worth
b: Declare a term before the show; meeting it pays a bonus, missing it simply pays nothing
c: Declare a term before the show, and declare how much you are staking on it; both the bonus and the penalty scale with the stake

name: The Rider
head: Carries a clause you have to honour. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its instruction is shown to you
a: Carries one hidden instruction; obeying it all show scores this card double, and breaking it scores it zero without telling you
b: Carries one hidden instruction; obeying it scores this card double, and breaking it is announced when it happens
c: Carries one hidden instruction that you may read before the show by discarding a card from the Entrance

name: The Critical Peg
head: One card whose triggers can land harder, rather than the whole board
a: Every trigger from this card has a small chance to fire at triple strength — **level 2:** Triggers from every card in its lines may crit too
b: Every trigger from this card has a small chance to fire at triple strength, and the chance rises each time it fails to — **level 2:** Triggers from every card in its lines may crit too
c: Every trigger anywhere has a small chance to fire at triple strength while this card is spotlit — **level 2:** The chance is doubled for cards in its lines

name: The Long Odds
head: Trades reliability for a tail. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Triggers from cards sitting on marks they match never fizzle
a: Cue: for the rest of this placement every trigger has a chance to land at five times strength and a chance to fizzle entirely
b: Cue: for the rest of this show every trigger has a chance at five times strength and a chance to fizzle
c: Every trigger from cards in this row has a chance at five times strength and a chance to fizzle, permanently

name: The Lucky Cell
head: One cell on the grid pays out big. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose where the lucky cell goes each placement
a: One cell per grid is chosen at show start; any trigger that fires from it lands at triple strength
b: One cell per grid is chosen and moves each placement; triggers from it land at triple strength
c: The lucky cell is always the uncovered mark of the highest rank on the grid; triggers fired from it land at triple strength, and it moves as marks are covered

name: Brodie's Leap
head: Banks fame each show for an unearned stunt; if a card is ever stacked on it, loses everything banked. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may cash the bank out once, whenever you choose ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0037 and Q0074, which you wrote: bank score now, pay it later*
