a: Banks points each show instead of scoring them; a card ever stacked on it forfeits the whole bank
b: Banks points each show and pays out at the end of the run, but the bank is lost entirely if this card is ever covered
c: Banks double points each show, with a 1-in-4 chance at the end of each show that the bank is lost

name: Cavendish
head: Enormous, and it might not survive. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A show it ends on its mark rolls no destruction
a: Triples score, with a 1-in-1000 chance of being destroyed at the end of each show
b: Triples score, with a 1-in-100 chance of being destroyed at the end of each show
c: Triples score, and the destruction chance rises each show it survives

name: Devil Parade
head: Play the show with damaged goods
a: Show variant: play the debuffed cards; each one scored turns its debuff into fame
b: Show variant: play the debuffed cards; each one scored clears its debuff permanently
c: Show variant: every card you play is debuffed on arrival, and scoring turns each debuff into fame

name: The Corrupted Face
head: A material that pays and takes
a: Cards of this material score double, and each time one scores, a random card in the deck loses a rank
b: Cards of this material score double, and each time one scores, another card of this material is destroyed
c: Cards of this material score double, and at show end each one still on the board costs you a card from the deck

name: The Dirty Opening
head: Everything starts damaged
a: Show: every card starts debuffed, and any card that scores anyway pays double
b: Show: every card starts debuffed, and scoring one clears its debuff
c: Show: every card starts debuffed and pays double; the debuffs deepen each placement

name: The Kneeling Devil
head: A liability that pays off at the very end. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It debuffs only the cards you choose in its column
a: Debuffs its own column every show; kept in the deck for the whole tour, it becomes a Legendary at the final city
b: Debuffs its own column every show; kept for the whole tour it becomes Legendary, and destroying it early pays nothing
c: Debuffs its own column every show, and each show survived raises what it becomes at the final city by one tier

name: The Scottish Play curse
head: Do not say its name. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, naming it brings no bad luck ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what the bad luck is or what naming it means*
a: Cueing this card by its true name brings bad luck; a discoverable ritual cleanses it
b: Cueing this card by its true name brings bad luck permanently, with no cure
c: Cueing it by name brings bad luck, and the ritual that cleanses it is different each run

name: Till Eulenspiegel deal
head: Does exactly what it says. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Accepted from its own mark, both readings are shown and you pick one ⚑ *pair review: fame is not spendable*
a: Grants exactly what its text says rather than what you meant by it
b: Grants exactly what its text says, and the text is written to be misread
c: Grants exactly what its text says; you may skip a reward to have the text clarified before accepting

name: White Elephant
head: Enormous, and it eats. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays no upkeep for a show it spent on its mark
a: Scores hugely, but takes 1 rank from your highest card every show it stays in the deck
b: Scores hugely, but destroys one card of your choice every show, and is destroyed if you have none to give
c: Scores hugely, and its upkeep rises by one rank for every show it has been in the deck

name: Effigy build-to-burn
head: After the Burning Man festival: build it up to burn it down. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A burned venue that includes its cell pays the ranks of matched cards twice ⚑ *pair review: it does not say how a venue is built from cards*
a: Build a temporary venue out of your own cards and burn it for a payout; ending the show with an empty board pays a further bonus
b: Build a temporary venue out of your own cards and burn it for a payout scaling with the ranks committed
c: Build a temporary venue and burn it; the payout scales with the ranks committed, and an empty board at show end doubles it

name: Ceremonial Dagger
head: Eats the card beside it for good. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may take a card two cells away
a: When placed, destroys an adjacent card and permanently gains twice that card's value as a multiplier
b: When placed, destroys an adjacent card and permanently gains that card's value
c: Cue to destroy an adjacent card at any time, gaining twice its value permanently

name: Madness
head: Grows by eating your own
a: When placed, gains a multiplier and destroys one of your other cards at random — **level 2:** It never destroys a card sitting on a mark it matches
b: When placed, gains a multiplier and destroys one of your other cards, chosen by you — **level 2:** A card you take from a matched cell pays it double
c: Gains a multiplier each placement and destroys one of your cards at random each placement — **level 2:** It never destroys a card sitting on a mark it matches

name: The Ninot
head: An investment that only pays if it burns. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Points banked from lines through its cell count double ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0037 and Q0074, which you wrote: bank score now, pay it later*
a: Cue: bank any part of the placement's score into this card each show; burning it at the final city pays triple everything invested, and a seeded vote may instead pardon it into the next run
b: Cue: bank any part of the placement's score into this card; burning it at the final city pays triple, with no chance of a pardon
c: Cue: bank any part of the placement's score into this card; you may burn it at any city for double, or hold for triple at the last

name: The Sacrifice
head: Cards are the currency for playing cards. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Placing a card on a mark it matches costs nothing
a: Placing a card costs you another card already on the grid, destroyed to pay for it
b: Placing a card of high rank costs another card on the grid; low ranks are free
c: Placing a card costs another card, and the cost may be paid from the Entrance instead of the grid

name: The Prepared Deck
head: Makes an outcome stop being random. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The fixed result also applies to the check after it
a: Cue: the next probability check this show succeeds automatically
b: Cue: the next probability check this show fails automatically, and the two after it succeed
c: Cue: fix the next probability check's result now, before you know what it will be used for

name: The Rehearsal
head: See the roll before you commit
a: Cue: see the result of the next probability check before deciding whether to take it — **level 2:** It sees the next two checks
b: Cue: see the result of the next check, and you may re-roll it once at a cost — **level 2:** It sees the next two checks
c: Cue once per show: see the results of every probability check that show, in advance — **level 2:** You may re-roll one of them

name: Chorus cards
head: Two in a row see it coming. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One of these on its own mark counts as a pair on its own ⚑ *pair review: a turn is not a unit the board has*
a: While any two of these share a row, the boss's next intent is revealed one placement early
b: While any two of these share a line, the boss's next two intents are revealed
c: While any two of these are on the board at all, the boss's next intent is revealed one placement early

name: Effect-order deck viewer
head: Shows the order effects will fire in ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) are interface; you rejected a UI-only effect at Q0038*
a: Shows the trigger order of every skill in the deck, even while the deck is shuffled — **level 2:** You may swap two of them once per show
b: Shows the trigger order of the next five skills that will fire — **level 2:** It shows the next ten
c: Shows the trigger order of every skill, and lets you swap two of them once per show — **level 2:** The swap may be made once per Entrance refill

name: Everything Face Up
head: Nothing is hidden; the difficulty is the puzzle
a: The whole deck is visible from the start, so the show is pure planning with no unknowns — **level 2:** You may swap the top card of any stock with the one beneath it
b: The next card of every stock is visible, so you always know the five cards after these five — **level 2:** You may swap the top card of any stock with the one beneath it
c: The whole deck is visible for the show's first placement only, then hidden again — **level 2:** The deck stays visible while it sits on its own mark

name: The audience warns you
head: The crowd shouts a warning. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A warned card sitting on a mark it matches dodges the hit
a: The crowd warns one step before a hazard hits a card
b: The crowd warns one step before a hazard hits, and names which card it will hit
c: The crowd warns one step ahead, and two steps ahead for a card sitting on a mark it matches

name: The Disaster March
head: Learn the tell. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, the cue plays two turns ahead ⚑ *pair review: a turn is not a unit the board has*
a: A hidden audio cue plays one placement before a surprise boss effect
b: A hidden audio cue plays one placement before a surprise effect, and a visual tell appears once you have heard it enough times
c: A hidden cue plays one placement before a surprise effect, differing per boss so each has to be learned

name: The Discoverie
head: Consumable, 3 uses: reveals every fake card in play (yours and the town's); banned (a crime event) in pious towns ⚑ *pair review: you defined a fake as a ghost card, one that does not stay in the deck when the game ends; this effect's premise, a hidden fake to find, is not that*
a: Consumable with three uses: reveals every fake card in play, yours and the town's; using it in a pious town is a crime
b: Consumable with three uses: reveals every fake card in play
c: Consumable with three uses: reveals every fake card, and each fake revealed scores a step

name: The Learned Pig
head: Reads anything face-down
a: Once per Entrance refill, reveal the identity of any face-down, hidden or unknown card — **level 2:** It reveals two cards per Entrance refill
b: Once per Entrance refill, reveal the identity of any hidden card, and it stays revealed for the rest of the show — **level 2:** It reveals two cards per Entrance refill
c: Every hidden card adjacent to this one is permanently revealed — **level 2:** Every hidden card in its lines is revealed, not only adjacent ones

name: The Talking Board
head: After the Ouija board: asks the deck a question
a: Consumable with three charges: ask one true-or-false question about the deck per show, answered honestly
b: Consumable with three charges: ask one true-or-false question about the deck or the map per show
c: Consumable with three charges: ask one question per show; the answer is honest, but a wrong guess costs an Entrance card, discarded

name: The Séance Buster
head: Calls out every fake on the board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its cue also turns an exposed town fake into a card of your deck ⚑ *pair review: you defined a fake as a ghost card, one that does not stay in the deck when the game ends; this effect's premise, a hidden fake to find, is not that*
a: Cue: reveal every fake card on the board, yours and the town's, scoring bonus points per fake exposed
b: Cue: reveal every fake on the board and destroy the town's, scoring per fake exposed
c: Cue: reveal one fake per Entrance refill automatically, scoring bonus points each time

name: X-Ray Eyes
head: Sees more the deeper it is buried. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It sees one card further into every stock
a: While covered, reveals every face-down board card and the top three of the deck
b: While covered, reveals every face-down board card and the top of the deck, seeing one card further per card covering it
c: While covered, reveals every face-down board card; while uncovered it reveals nothing at all

name: Bauta
head: This card's rarity and identity are hidden from inspection effects until it scores. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Placed on a mark, its hidden rank and suit become the mark's own ⚑ *pair review: assumes inspection effects; you rejected inspection-by-looking at Q0076*
a: This card's rank, suit and skill are hidden from inspection until it first scores
b: This card's rank and suit are hidden from you as well as from effects until it is placed
c: This card shows itself as a copy of another random card on the grid until it scores

name: Blackout turn
head: One refill in the dark. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card placed blind on a mark it matches scores its line triple
a: One Entrance refill per show is played with the marks face down
b: One Entrance refill per show is played with the marks face down; any line completed during it scores double
c: As (b), and you choose which refill

name: Concealed Versus Exposed
head: A hand built in the open is worth less. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A face-down card placed on a mark it matches turns up and still pays the concealed bonus
a: You may place any card face down; a line built entirely from face-down cards pays more than the same line built face up
b: You may place any card face down; a line built entirely face down pays double, and revealing any card of it forfeits the bonus
c: A line built face down pays more, and you choose per card whether to place it face up or down

name: Grand Vanish
head: Cue, once per show: hide an entire column so it cannot be seen, targeted, scored, or touched for one turn; it then returns with bonus points on every card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may vanish a row as well as a column
a: Cue, once per show: one column vanishes until the next Entrance refill, unseeable, untargetable and unscoreable, then returns and every line through it re-scores
b: Cue: one column vanishes until the end of the show and its cards return to the Entrance
c: Cue, once per show: one column vanishes until the next Entrance refill and returns in a different column's position

name: The Fish
head: Boss: cards arrive face down
a: Boss: cards are dealt face down after each placement
b: Boss: cards are dealt face down after each placement, and turn face up once placed
c: Boss: cards are dealt face down and stay face down until they score

name: The Mask Maker
head: Puts a card behind a mask. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may mask two cards ⚑ *pair review: (a) hides a card from inspection, which you rejected at Q0076*
a: Cue, once per show: mask any card, hiding its identity and rarity from inspections and towns until it scores twice
b: Cue, once per show: mask any card until it scores twice; while masked it cannot be targeted by town hazards
c: Cue: mask any card permanently; it never unmasks, but it also never counts toward set or class bonuses

name: Klondike reveal-on-move rule
head: Moving one reveals the next. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card turned up onto a mark it matches pays its match at once ⚑ *pair review: cards on the board are not face down, so there is nothing beneath to turn up*
a: Moving a face-up card off a stack turns the card beneath face up
b: Moving a face-up card off a stack turns the card beneath face up and spotlights it for the placement
c: Moving any card reveals the card beneath, and revealing pays a small bonus

name: The Envelope Act
head: A card placed face down and turned up only when its line resolves
a: Cue on placement: place this card face down; it turns face up and takes effect only when its line completes — **level 2:** Placed on a mark it matches, it turns up at once and pays double
b: Cue on placement: place this card face down; it turns up when its line completes, and pays double for having been hidden — **level 2:** It pays double again when its line re-scores
c: Cue on placement: place any card face down; it turns up when its line completes, and until then counts as a blank for meld purposes — **level 2:** A card placed face down on a mark it matches counts as itself for melds, not a blank

name: The Reveal Fee
head: A face-down card costs something to turn over. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Flipping a card in its lines is free ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what the fee is paid in*
a: A face-down card does not turn up on its own; you pay to flip it, and it does nothing until you do
b: A face-down card flips free the first time each placement and costs thereafter
c: A face-down card flips only when paid for, and the price is its rank

name: The Sucker Trap
head: A face-down card that punishes whatever disturbs it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Fired on its mark, it stays face down and can fire again
a: While face down, any effect that reads or moves this card is cancelled and the reader takes a penalty
b: While face down, any effect that reads or moves this card flips it and fires its effect on the reader instead
c: While face down, any effect that reads this card is cancelled; any effect that moves it is redirected onto the mover

name: The Trick
head: Everything flips over
a: Boss: after each placement, every face-up card in the Entrance flips face down
b: Boss: after each placement, every face-up card on the grid flips face down
c: Boss: after each placement, every card flips - face-up becomes face-down and back again

name: Murder Mystery Solitaire
head: Deduce the fact the board is hiding. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It gives one free clue each show
a: One hidden fact about the deck is deducible from what you have seen; naming it correctly pays enormously and naming it wrongly costs the show
b: One hidden fact is deducible; naming it correctly pays, and a wrong guess costs only a placement
c: One hidden fact is deducible, and each placement reveals one further clue whether you want it or not

name: Second Sight
head: Predicts the line, not the hand. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may name two lines
a: At each Entrance refill, name an incomplete line; if it completes before the next refill, +1 combo
b: As (a); if it completes, +2 combo, and if a different line completes first, -1
c: At each Entrance refill, name an incomplete line and its hand; the line completing pays +1 combo, the hand being right pays +3

name: The Mentalist
head: Calls it before it happens. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its mark you may change the named hand type once
a: At show start, name a hand type; scoring it pays a large bonus, and failing to costs nothing
b: At show start, name a hand type; scoring it pays a large bonus, and failing to costs fame
c: At show start, name a hand type and a placement; scoring it in exactly that placement pays an enormous bonus

name: The Sealed Envelope
head: A prediction opened later
a: Consumable: write down a prediction now, opened at show end; a correct one pays several times over
b: Consumable: write down a prediction now, opened at show end, and you may change it once
c: Consumable: write a prediction that is opened three shows later, paying more the longer it waited

name: Chalk On The Case
head: Tagged cards become addressable by every effect
a: A tagged card can be named as the target by any effect whose text says a random card — **level 2:** A tag placed on a card sitting on a mark it matches lasts into the next show
b: A tagged card can be named by any targeting effect, and a card may carry only one tag at a time — **level 2:** A tag placed on a card sitting on a mark it matches lasts into the next show
c: Tags are placed by the player, one per Entrance refill, and every targeting effect prefers tags over random choice — **level 2:** Two tags per Entrance refill

name: Marked
head: Always shows this card's position in the deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may also name any one card each show; its position is shown too
a: This card's position in the deck is always visible
b: This card's position in the deck is always visible, and once per show you may move it up one place
c: Every card sharing this card's suit shows its position in the deck

name: The Tail
head: A tag that draws everything toward it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may tag two cards
a: Cue: tag one card on the grid; every prop and hazard this placement targets the tagged card first
b: Cue: tag one card; every prop this placement targets it first, and every hazard avoids it
c: The last card placed is always tagged, and props target the tagged card before any other

name: Turncoat card
head: After the game Among Us: one of your cards is lying. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, the fake in its lines is revealed ⚑ *pair review: you defined a fake as a ghost card, one that does not stay in the deck when the game ends; this effect's premise, a hidden fake to find, is not that*
a: A card is secretly fake: playing it loses score, and it ignores the rules on certain turns until you find and remove it
b: A card is secretly fake and loses score when played; it is revealed after it has cost you three times
c: A card is secretly fake, and each placement you may accuse one card, at a cost if you are wrong

name: Kayfabe
head: While it is in play, ghost cards stay
a: While this card is in play, every ghost card counts as real and stays in the deck when the show ends — **level 2:** Ghosts in its lines stay even if this card leaves play before the show ends
b: While this card is in play, one ghost card of your choice stays in the deck at each show end — **level 2:** Two ghosts stay
c: While this card is in play, ghost cards stay in the deck, but real cards you never scored this show become ghosts — **level 2:** Unscored cards in its lines stay real

name: Marketed monster
head: Advertised as a monster. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Landing on its own mark exposes it: its debuff on its neighbours becomes a buff ⚑ *pair review: assumes inspection effects; you rejected inspection-by-looking at Q0076*
a: Debuffs adjacent cards while secretly being harmless, and is exposed if inspected
b: Debuffs adjacent cards while secretly being harmless; being exposed turns the debuff into a buff
c: Appears to debuff adjacent cards but actually buffs them, and inspection reveals the truth to the town, not to you

name: The Charm
head: The card text is not the trigger. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On its mark, its real trigger is shown to you
a: The printed trigger is not the real one; the real trigger is something else entirely
b: The printed trigger is not the real one, and the real one is revealed after it first fires
c: The printed trigger is not the real one; you may learn the truth early by discarding an Entrance card

name: The Gaff
head: Shows one value, holds another; it matches a rank mark by the rank it displays. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its true value is revealed the moment it lands, and any line through its cell that completes with the truth scores then
a: Wild pip: displays a fixed rank and suit until scored, then reveals its true randomly determined value
b: Wild pip: displays a fixed rank and suit until scored, then becomes whatever would have scored highest
c: Wild pip: displays a fixed value that is a lie, and discarding an Entrance card reveals the truth before it scores

name: The Radio Dummy
head: Its gimmick does not work, and it scores anyway ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what its gimmick is*
a: Its stated gimmick is nullified by the board context, and it scores regardless — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, its gimmick works as well
b: Its stated gimmick is nullified, and it scores more the more thoroughly it is nullified — **level 2:** It counts as fully nullified
c: Its stated gimmick never works, and the card scores a flat amount that no effect can change — **level 2:** Its flat amount is paid to every line through its cell

name: The Skipping Tape
head: Exposed after the fact. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, no fake in its lines is exposed ⚑ *pair review: you defined a fake as a ghost card, one that does not stay in the deck when the game ends; this effect's premise, a hidden fake to find, is not that*
a: A fake that already scored is exposed retroactively, and you pay back the fame it earned
b: A fake that already scored is exposed retroactively, and you pay back double
c: A fake that already scored may be exposed retroactively, and you may pay points to bury the story instead

name: The Unicorn
head: Worth a fortune until somebody checks. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, inspection does not reduce it ⚑ *pair review: assumes inspection effects; you rejected inspection-by-looking at Q0076*
a: Scores as a Legendary at five times base until an inspection effect examines it, after which it scores half, forever
b: Scores as a Legendary until inspected, after which it scores half for the rest of that show only
c: Scores as a Legendary until inspected; being inspected destroys it outright

name: Exposure cost
head: Looking behind the curtain costs something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Revealing a card in its lines is free ⚑ *pair review: you defined a fake as a ghost card, one that does not stay in the deck when the game ends; this effect's premise, a hidden fake to find, is not that*
a: Revealing a fake's true nature, yours or the boss's, costs the show's reward
b: Revealing a fake's true nature costs an Entrance card, discarded
c: Revealing a fake costs the show's reward, and revealing your own costs the next show's as well

name: The Blind Spot
head: The inspector can only watch one side. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose which grid is watched ⚑ *pair review: a turn is not a unit the board has*
a: While the inspector watches one grid, outlawed cards may act freely in the others
b: While the inspector watches one grid, outlawed cards act freely elsewhere, and you are shown where they are watching
c: The inspector watches one grid, chosen fresh each placement without warning

name: The Escalating Look
head: Each glance costs more than the last ⚑ *pair review: assumes inspection effects; you rejected inspection-by-looking at Q0076*
a: The first inspection each show is free, the second costs one patience, and each after that costs one more — **level 2:** Inspecting a card in its lines is free
b: Every inspection this show costs one more than the last, but each one shows one card further — **level 2:** Inspecting a card in its lines is free
c: Inspections are free, but each one permanently raises the show's score requirement by a small step — **level 2:** An inspection from its lines does not raise the requirement

name: The Ticket Booth
head: Looking behind the curtain has a standing price. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The card paid for a look is one you choose, and goes to the bottom of its stock instead of the discard ⚑ *pair review: it only puts a price on information; it reads as a hazard*
a: Reading any hidden information - deck order, rules deck, a face-down card - costs one Entrance card, discarded
b: Reading hidden information is free once per Entrance refill and costs an Entrance card thereafter
c: Reading hidden information costs an Entrance card, and every look also reveals one thing to the show's hazards

name: The Blind
head: Hides your board from the opposition. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Nor the cells beside its lines ⚑ *pair review: on one grid, one grid of your choice was the whole board*
a: The boss cannot see the lines through this card, so its targeting never lands there
b: The boss cannot see the lines through this card, and targets the others twice as often
c: The boss cannot see any card that has not yet scored

name: The Critic In The Stalls
head: What the show can see of your board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match are invisible to hazards too ⚑ *pair review: near Q0856 (b), where a masked card cannot be targeted by town hazards*
a: Hazards and boss rules read only the cards that are currently spotlit; anything covered is invisible to them
b: Hazards read only spotlit cards, and a covered card may be revealed deliberately to bait them
c: Hazards read the whole board, but one card per Entrance refill may be hidden from them by cue

name: The Decoy
head: Shows the opposition something false. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose the card the false picture points at ⚑ *pair review: no hazard chooses its target by reading your play*
a: Presents a false picture of your board so the boss targets a card that is not there
b: Presents a false picture so the boss targets this card instead of what it wanted
c: Presents a false picture; the boss targets at random instead of choosing

name: The Tell
head: The opposition reads you back. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The boss targets it; each hit it survives adds +1 to the multiplier of its lines ⚑ *pair review: no hazard chooses its target by reading your play; it only costs you*
a: The boss targets whichever card scored most last placement
b: The boss targets whichever card scored most last placement, and you are told before it lands
c: The boss targets whichever card you have moved most this show

name: Contradiction
head: Two stacking rules at once
a: Two stacking rules apply at once, and a build is legal if it satisfies either — **level 2:** Its own stack may break both rules
b: Two stacking rules apply at once, and a build is legal only if it satisfies both — **level 2:** Its own stack may build by either rule
c: Two stacking rules apply, alternating by column, so neighbouring columns build differently — **level 2:** Its own stack may build by either rule

name: House Rules: Building
head: Rewrites what a legal build is
a: Replaces the default stacking rule with same-suit ascending instead of different-suit adjacent — **level 2:** Its own stack is exempt from the stacking rule
b: Replaces the default stacking rule with anything-on-anything, removing legality entirely — **level 2:** Its own stack pays at four cards, not five
c: The stacking rule is drawn at random each show from a fixed set, and announced before play — **level 2:** Its own stack is exempt from the stacking rule

name: The Amendment Clause
head: Lets you edit the stacking rule. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cued from its mark, the relaxed clause stays relaxed into the next show
a: Cue once per show: relax one clause of the stacking rule for the rest of the show
b: Cue once per show: relax one clause of the stacking rule for one placement only
c: Cue once per show: swap the stacking rule for any other you have seen this run

name: Double Billing
head: Two scoring rules, both paid
a: Every line scores under two rules at once, and both payouts are banked — **level 2:** Lines through its cell score under a third rule as well
b: Every line scores under two rules, and you keep whichever paid more — **level 2:** Lines through its cell take both payouts
c: Rows score under one rule and columns under another — **level 2:** Lines through its cell take both payouts

name: House Rules: Scoring
head: Rewrites how a line resolves. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell pay both the poker hand and the rank sum
a: A line's score is the sum of its ranks rather than its poker hand
b: A line's score is its poker hand multiplied by the number of distinct suits in it
c: A line scores as its poker hand, or its rank sum, whichever is higher

name: The Best Hand Only
head: One hand per placement, not twelve. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell always pay, best or not
a: Only the single highest-scoring line each placement pays; the others complete without scoring
b: Only the highest-scoring line each placement pays, at five times its normal rate
c: Only the highest-scoring line pays, and every other completed line adds one to the combo instead

name: The Deferred Line
head: Lines wait for the curtain. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A held line through its cell gains a step for every card placed on a matched cell while it waits
a: A completed line does not score immediately; it holds and pays at the next Entrance refill, so effects can still change it
b: A completed line holds and pays at the next Entrance refill, and pays an extra step for every placement it was left standing
c: A completed line holds until you press End, and every held line pays at once

name: The Revised Bill
head: Swaps the scoring rule mid-show
a: Cue: swap the scoring rule for the rest of the show from a slate of three — **level 2:** The new rule also re-scores lines through its cell
b: Cue: swap the scoring rule for one placement only, from a slate of three — **level 2:** The new rule also re-scores lines through its cell
c: Cue: swap the scoring rule, and every line already scored this show re-scores under the new one — **level 2:** You may pick the new rule from any rule, not only the slate

name: The Simultaneous Resolution
head: Lines that complete together are one hand. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A merged hand through its cell counts every one of its cards, not only the best five
a: Lines completed by the same placement resolve as a single hand made of all their cards, scored as the best five, into the special bucket
b: Lines completed by the same placement resolve as one hand and pay it once into each bucket the merged lines belonged to
c: Lines completed by the same placement resolve separately, and each one after the first pays an extra step

name: 15 Minute City
head: A deck with holes in it
a: Deck: two copies of every face card and no aces, twos or threes
b: Deck: two copies of every face card and no low ranks, with two locked cards you can never remove
c: Deck: a named set of ranks is missing entirely, and which ranks differ per challenge

name: Antimatter Deck
head: Every deck's upside at once
a: Deck: carries the upside of every deck you have already won with
b: Deck: carries the upside of every deck in the game at once
c: Deck: carries the upside of every deck you have won with, and one downside for each

name: Dual-Purpose Deck
head: After the Cryptid mod's CCD Deck: every card is also a consumable. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, a card placed in its lines may still be spent as its consumable without leaving the board
a: Every card is also a random consumable, spendable instead of placed
b: Every card is also a consumable, and spending it removes the card from the deck
c: Every card is also a consumable, and which consumable it grants rerolls each show

name: Edition Deck
head: Every card is the same edition
a: Every card on this grid carries this card's chosen stamp, and no card may ever change it — **level 2:** You may change the stamp once per show
b: Every card on this grid carries this card's chosen stamp, and you may change it once per show — **level 2:** You may change the stamp at any time
c: Every card on this grid carries a stamp chosen at random each show — **level 2:** You choose the stamp instead of a random one

name: Gauntlet Deck
head: After the Cryptid mod's Enter the Gungeon deck: every show is a boss
a: Deck: every show is a boss show and none may be skipped
b: Deck: every show is a boss show, and beating one lets you skip the next
c: Deck: every show is a boss show, and the bosses are drawn without repeating

name: Glowing Deck
head: Beating a boss buffs everything
a: Beating a boss multiplies the values of every card you own — **level 2:** A boss beaten while it sits on its own mark multiplies the cards in its lines again
b: Beating a boss multiplies the values of one card you choose — **level 2:** You choose two cards
c: Beating a boss multiplies every card's values, and losing one divides them — **level 2:** A loss while it sits on its own mark does not divide

name: Hundred Entertainments deck
head: A hundred commons
a: Deck: 100 cards, all Common, built for combo scoring
b: Deck: 100 cards, all Common, and the combo multiplier counts double
c: Deck: 100 cards, all Common, and every tenth card scored upgrades permanently

name: Legendary Deck
head: Starts legendary, and might get more
a: Deck: starts with a Legendary card, with a chance of gaining another whenever a boss is beaten
b: Deck: starts with a Legendary card and nothing else out of the ordinary
c: Deck: starts with a Legendary, and every Legendary gained costs you two Commons

name: Magic deck
head: Suits as elements, melds as spells ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a spell does*
a: Each suit acts as an element, and completing certain suit combinations casts a spell effect — **level 2:** You choose the spell for lines through its cell
b: Each suit acts as an element, and any line with three or more elements casts a random spell — **level 2:** You choose the spell for lines through its cell
c: Each suit acts as an element, and this card lets you choose which spell each combination casts — **level 2:** A line through its cell casts its spell twice

name: Punk / Minimal unlockable decks
head: Two decks with a philosophy
a: Decks: a rule-breaking commons deck with no Producer class, and a pips-only deck with no skills at all
b: Decks: a rule-breaking commons deck, and a pips-only deck where pip effects are twice as strong
c: Decks: a commons-only deck that upgrades cards through play, and a pips-only deck that gains one skill per tour

name: Small-tent starting deck (Carpas)
head: Start small, end famous
a: Deck: a weak starting deck built around an underdog-to-star arc, gaining strength as fame rises
b: Deck: a weak starting deck whose cards each upgrade once at a fame threshold
c: Deck: a weak starting deck that gains one card of the highest rarity you have ever scored, each tour

name: Suit Deck
head: One suit, all the way down. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may change its suit once per show
a: While spotlit, every card on this card's grid counts as this card's suit, and no card may ever change suit
b: While spotlit, every card on this card's grid counts as this card's suit for props and for suit marks, but keeps its own suit for melds
c: While spotlit, every card on this card's grid counts as one suit, and the suit changes each show

name: Survivor deck
head: Suits as supplies
a: Deck: suits represent survival resources - food, water, blade and so on - each with its own upkeep
b: Deck: suits represent survival resources, and running out of one imposes a debuff until it is replenished
c: Deck: suits are resources consumed when scored and replenished by specific melds

name: The Collective deck
head: No stars, just the ensemble. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match keep their own power if it is higher ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a card's power is*
a: While spotlit, every card shares the average power of all cards, and a deck with no rares scores a bonus multiplier
b: While spotlit, every card shares the average power of all cards, so buffing one buffs all
c: While spotlit, every card shares the average power of the cards on the board, recalculated as cards are placed

name: The Doubled Next
head: One refill, two deals. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The deal you do not keep returns to the bottom of its stocks instead of the discard
a: While this card is on the grid, each Entrance refill deals twice, discarding the first deal
b: While this card is on the grid, each Entrance refill deals twice and you keep whichever five you choose
c: While this card is on the grid, each Entrance refill deals twice and both sets are available at once

name: The Third Button
head: A control the game did not have. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its button may be used once more per Entrance refill
a: A third button is added beside End and Undo that swaps the contents of two grid cells, usable once per Entrance refill
b: A third button is added beside End and Undo that slides one row one cell along, wrapping, usable once per Entrance refill
c: A third button is added beside End and Undo that swaps one grid card with one Entrance card, usable once per Entrance refill

name: The Side Tent
head: A rule that only applies to one grid. **Level 2:** none beyond the flat mult a match pays ⚑ *pair review: its only reach is other grids, and a normal run plays one*
a: This card's talent affects only its own grid, never another
b: This card's talent affects only its own grid, and may be moved to another grid once per show
c: This card's talent affects only its own grid, and every other grid gets the opposite effect

name: The Town Ordinance
head: Where you play sets a standing restriction
a: Each town imposes one restriction for every show played there, announced before you arrive
b: Each town imposes one restriction announced only after the show's first placement
c: Each town offers a choice of two restrictions, the harder one paying more

name: Rehearsal Hall
head: Class counts unlock tiers. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own class reaches each tier one card sooner
a: Two, four and six cards of one class on the board each unlock a stronger bonus for that class
b: Every second card of one class on the board raises that class's bonus by one step, with no cap
c: Two, four and six of one class unlock tiers, and the tiers differ per class

name: The Census Taker
head: Counts one named thing, anywhere. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards of the named class sitting on marks they match count twice
a: Scores a bonus per card of one named class anywhere on the board, however far away
b: Scores a bonus per card of one named class in its lines
c: Scores a bonus per card of the class it has seen least this run, so it chases variety

name: Thin Bill
head: Pays for having almost none
a: Scores a large bonus if exactly one card of its class is on the board — **level 2:** It counts only cards of its class that are not sitting on marks they match
b: Scores a large bonus if it is the only card of its class in the whole deck — **level 2:** Cards of its class sitting on marks they match do not count as in the deck
c: Scores a bonus scaling inversely with how many of its class are on the board — **level 2:** It counts only cards of its class that are not sitting on marks they match

name: Cross-class Clown leader
head: A leader whose joke lands everywhere
a: Leader: its buff reaches every class rather than one — **level 2:** Its buff reaches cards in its lines twice
b: Leader: its buff reaches every class, at half the strength a single-class leader would give — **level 2:** Its buff reaches every class at full strength in its own lines
c: Leader: its buff reaches every class, growing with the number of distinct classes on the board — **level 2:** Its buff reaches every class at full strength in its own lines

name: Magician leader (Tenkatsu)
head: A leader who prints cards. The cards it prints stay in the deck. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The token goes on top of a stock you choose
a: Leader: produces one token card per show
b: Leader: produces one token card per Entrance refill, whose suit you choose
c: Leader: produces a token card whenever a line scores with no token in it

name: Satirical Animal Trainer leader
head: Fame up, relations down ⚑ *pair review: assumes town relations the game does not track*
a: Leader: satire raises fame and lowers town relations — **level 2:** Satire from its own mark raises fame without lowering relations
b: Leader: satire raises fame and lowers town relations, and low relations raise the payout further — **level 2:** Relations lowered while it sits on its own mark count double toward the payout
c: Leader: satire raises fame and lowers relations; at zero relations the town bars you and pays a lump sum — **level 2:** Satire from its own mark raises fame without lowering relations

name: The Front Rank
head: Where a card stands changes what its class does. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own class bonus applies in every ring
a: A class bonus applies only to cards of that class in the outermost ring of the grid
b: A class bonus applies at full strength in the outer ring and half strength in the centre
c: Each class names the ring it wants, and its bonus applies only there

name: The Juggler King
head: Leader that keeps one suit scoring. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards of its suit sitting on suit marks they match re-score twice
a: Leader: Balls cards may re-score each placement for as long as at least one Balls card scores every placement
b: Leader: cards of one suit you name at run start may re-score each placement while that suit scores every placement
c: Leader: cards of the suit that scored most last placement may re-score this placement

name: The Ringmaster
head: The leader who never leaves. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The cell it ends the show on keeps its mark into the next show
a: Leader with no suit or rank: starts in the Entrance, is always grabbable, may be placed anywhere uncovered, and stays on the board from one show to the next, starting each show already placed
b: Leader with no suit or rank that stays on the board from one show to the next, but may only occupy the centre cell of a grid
c: Leader with no suit or rank that stays on the board from one show to the next and counts as a member of every line it touches

name: The Satirist
head: More fame, worse weather. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Shows earn 50% more fame instead of 25%
a: Leader: shows earn 25% more fame, and every town's hazard is one tier harsher
b: Leader: shows earn 25% more fame, and every town gets one extra hazard
c: Leader: shows earn 25% more fame per hazard active in the town, and hazards are one tier harsher

name: The Sharpshooter
head: Calls the rank of the night. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards of the named rank sitting on rank marks they match score triple
a: Leader: name a rank at each show start; cards of that rank score double all show
b: Leader: name a rank at each show start; cards of that rank score double, and cards one either side score 50% more
c: Leader: the rank printed on the most uncovered marks scores double, re-read after every placement

name: The Sweet Tooth
head: Makes the buffs stick. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Rank buffs on cards sitting on marks they match are doubled
a: Leader: every rank buff your effects grant becomes permanent instead of lasting the show
b: Leader: every rank buff your effects grant lasts an extra show, stacking if reapplied
c: Leader: rank buffs become permanent, but every debuff your cards take is permanent too

name: The Tiger Queen
head: Takes the lid off eating. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Eating on a matched cell gains double
a: Leader: every consumption effect loses its cap, so rank gains from eating are unbounded
b: Leader: every consumption effect loses its cap, and eaten cards are never returned
c: Leader: consumption caps double rather than vanish, and eating a card of the same class as the eater ignores the cap entirely

name: The Widow's Succession
head: The partner inherits ⚑ *pair review: leaders are planned (DESIGN_DOC.md section 11), but nothing yet says what happens when one is destroyed*
a: When a leader is destroyed, its partner card inherits the leader slot and one signature power — **level 2:** A partner sitting on a mark it matches inherits every power
b: When a leader is destroyed, its partner inherits the leader slot with all its powers — **level 2:** The partner keeps its own powers as well
c: When a leader is destroyed, any card of its class may be promoted, keeping one power of your choice — **level 2:** The promoted card keeps two powers of your choice

name: Pink Lemonade
head: When a Flames card and a Concessions card score in the same row, gain bonus points and refill 1 card into the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which stock the refill draws from
a: When a Flames card and a Concessions card score in the same line, gain bonus points and refill one Entrance card
b: When any two named classes score in the same line, gain bonus points and refill one Entrance card
c: When two cards of different classes score adjacent to each other, gain bonus points; refill one Entrance card if three or more classes were involved

name: The Engineer
head: Gamble-tagged cards have their destruction odds halved. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Gamble-tagged cards sitting on marks they match cannot be destroyed
a: Gamble-tagged cards have their destruction odds halved
b: Gamble-tagged cards that survive a destruction roll gain +1 rank
c: Each gamble-tagged card on the grid raises every other one's payout

name: The Lion's Bride
head: Survives the animal act. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It cannot be eaten at all
a: Scores bonus points each placement it shares a column with a consuming Animal card and is not eaten
b: Scores bonus points each placement it is adjacent to any card that consumes, and cannot be eaten by it
c: Scores bonus points scaling with how many consuming cards are on its grid, and is always eaten last

name: Macabre Joker
head: Purges everything but one class. The tokens it creates stay in the deck, in place of what it destroyed. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Placed on its own mark, each card it destroys leaves a token in the Entrance ⚑ *pair review: it clears your own board when placed; (b) only costs you*
a: When placed, destroys every other card on the board not of a named class, creating a token for each destroyed
b: When placed, destroys every other card on the board not of a named class, with no compensation
c: When placed, destroys every other card on the board not of the class you own most of, creating a token for each

name: The Closed Shop
head: Its lines admit one union only
a: Its row and column accept only cards of this card's class — **level 2:** Its own lines accept any class
b: Cards of other classes may be placed in its row and column but score nothing there — **level 2:** Cards of other classes in its lines score normally
c: Its row and column accept only two classes named when it is placed, and a line there of a single class scores double — **level 2:** The two classes are named when it lands on its mark

name: The Rival Acts
head: Two classes that will not share a stage
a: Two named classes may never be placed on the same grid; the entrance will not release one onto a grid holding the other — **level 2:** A rival sitting on a mark it matches may share the grid
b: Two named classes may share a grid, but while they do neither scores — **level 2:** A rival sitting on a mark it matches still scores
c: Two named classes may share a grid; while they do, both score double and both are destroyed when a placement finishes resolving — **level 2:** Rivals sitting on marks they match score triple instead of double

name: The Struck Name
head: Take a class off the bill
a: Consumable: name a class; no card of that class may be placed for the rest of the show, and every other class scores an extra step
b: Consumable: name a class; no card of that class may be drawn for the rest of the show
c: Consumable: name a class; cards of that class are removed from the deck for the rest of the run, and each one removed scores its rank now

name: Clown set bonus raises patience
head: Clowns buy you patience. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A meld through its cell refills two patience ⚑ *pair review: patience exists only under your Q0059 boss rule*
a: Each distinct Clown card on the board raises patience by 1, and holding a full set gives a chance not to spend patience at all
b: Each distinct Clown card on the board raises patience by 1
c: Each distinct Clown card raises patience by 1, and a full set stops patience being spent entirely

name: Congress deck
head: One of everything
a: Deck: starts with one card from every regional tradition, with cross-tradition synergy tags
b: Deck: starts with one card from every class, and class bonuses count double
c: Deck: starts with one card from every tradition, and holding a full set of any tradition pays a standing bonus

name: Houses
head: Cards belong to houses. **Level 2, on its own mark:** House members sitting on marks they match count twice toward the house's size
a: Cards belong to named houses led by a Mother card, and each house member scores extra when its Mother card is on the board
b: Cards belong to named houses led by a Mother card; a full house on the board pays a standing bonus
c: Cards belong to houses, and a house's Mother card buffs every member on the board by the house's size

name: Named court card identities
head: The face cards have names
a: Face cards carry hidden historical identities discovered through play; finding all twelve grants a meta reward
b: Face cards carry hidden identities; each one discovered permanently buffs that card
c: Face cards carry hidden identities discovered through play, and each discovery reveals a hint toward the next

name: The Dragon Collapse
head: Collect a set, and it seals a slot. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Three of the group are enough when one of them sits on a mark it matches
a: When all four cards of a named group are uncovered at once, they collapse into one cell which is then permanently sealed
b: When all four of a named group are uncovered, they collapse and are removed from the run entirely, paying their summed rank
c: When all four of a named group are uncovered, they collapse into one card carrying all four of their skills

name: The Erdnase Cipher
head: A signature that turns up across runs
a: A hidden signature appears on random cards across many runs; collecting them all unlocks an unexplained reward
b: A hidden signature appears on random cards; scoring a signed card pays a small bonus and marks progress
c: A hidden signature appears across runs, and each one found makes the next slightly more likely

name: The Major Arcana
head: A set worth completing across runs
a: A series of 22 unique one-shot consumables; collecting all 22 across runs grants a permanent profile reward
b: A series of 22 unique one-shot consumables; each one you have already used this run makes the next cheaper
c: A series of 22 unique consumables; holding any three at once lets you spend them together for a combined effect

name: Animal-puppet tokens
head: An animal that is legally a puppet. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts for both Animal and Puppet class bonuses ⚑ *pair review: assumes towns ban classes, which the game does not do*
a: Animal effects that register as Puppet-type, immune to animal bans
b: Animal effects that register as Puppet-type, immune to animal bans but excluded from Animal class bonuses
c: Any card may be re-registered as Puppet-type once per run, dodging bans on its real class

name: Bahurupiya
head: At the start of each show, this card is assigned a random different class (seeded), and counts for that class's synergy effects for the show
a: At show start this card is assigned a random class and counts as that class all show
b: Counts as every class at once for class-count effects, but never as its own
c: Counts as whichever class is most represented on its grid, updating as cards are placed

name: Face/heel alignment
head: Villain or hero, and towns care
a: Cards carry a face or heel alignment with different bonuses, and towns prefer one or the other
b: Cards carry a face or heel alignment you may flip once per show, with towns preferring one
c: Cards carry an alignment, and a card scoring with a town's preference earns double while one scoring against it earns nothing

name: Greasepaint
head: This card counts as a Clown-class card in addition to its own class. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts as every class present in its lines
a: Counts as a Clown-class card in addition to its own class
b: Counts as one additional class of your choice, fixed when the stamp is applied
c: Counts as the class printed on the mark it sits on, as well as its own

name: The Bonded Troupe
head: Cards trained together take a shared tag. (DESIGN_REFERENCES.md F6, the Academy family)
a: Between runs, several Common cards may be trained together; they gain a shared group tag and score a bonus whenever two of them are on the board
b: Between runs, several Commons may be trained together into one merged card of their summed rank
c: Between runs, several Commons gain a shared tag, and the bonus scales with how many of the troupe are on the board at once

name: The Capoeirista
head: Registered as a Dancer but functions as an Escape Artist; town bans on Escape Artist-type acts still let it perform. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts for both classes' bonuses ⚑ *pair review: assumes towns ban classes, which the game does not do*
a: Registered as a Dancer but works as an Escape Artist, so town bans on Escape Artists never catch it
b: Registered as one class and works as another, both chosen when acquired, so bans on the working class never catch it
c: Whenever a town bans a class, this card registers as a different one for that show

name: The Heel Turn
head: Turn heel, and stay turned
a: Flip the leader to heel mid-tour for new powers and changed town reactions, with no way back this run
b: Flip the leader to heel mid-tour, and flip back once at the cost of the next show's reward
c: Flip the leader to heel mid-tour; every town's reaction changes, and heel shows pay double in towns that prefer a villain

name: The Impresario
head: Kings are renamed and count as Producer-class cards. The tokens Kings mint are ghosts
a: Kings count as Producer-class cards — **level 2:** A King on a King mark makes every face card in its lines a Producer
b: Kings count as Producer-class cards and mint a rank-1 token card whenever they score — **level 2:** A King on a King mark makes every face card in its lines a Producer
c: Every face card counts as a Producer-class card — **level 2:** Every card in its lines counts as a Producer, not only face cards

name: The Little Umbrella
head: A prop that lends its class. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its holder may perform the moves of two classes
a: While held, lets its holder perform Acrobat moves regardless of the holder's class
b: While held, lets its holder perform the moves of any one class you name
c: While held, lets its holder perform the moves of whichever class is adjacent to it

name: The One-Man Band
head: Three jobs, badly. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts as every class present on its grid, at full effect
a: Counts as three classes chosen when acquired, each at one-third effect
b: Counts as three classes chosen when acquired, each at full effect, but it can never be the target of a class bonus itself
c: Counts as three classes chosen fresh at the start of each show, each at one-third effect

name: The Renaming
head: A class renames itself
a: After a vote event, one class's tag upgrades to a better-received label with better town reactions
b: After a vote event, one class's tag changes, and cards of that class gain a new synergy
c: After a vote event you choose which class renames, and towns react to the new label from then on

name: The Shift
head: Change what a card counts as. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may change a card's suit instead of its class
a: Cue: change one card on the grid to any class for the rest of the show
b: Cue: change one card to any class permanently, once per run
c: Cue: change every card in one line to the class of the card you point at, for the rest of the show

name: Troupe adoption
head: Everyone takes the leader's colours
a: Any card without a class takes the current leader's class tag — **level 2:** Cards in its lines that have a class take the leader's class too
b: Any card without a class takes the current leader's class, and loses it if the leader is destroyed — **level 2:** Cards in its lines keep the class if the leader is destroyed
c: Every card takes the leader's class tag in addition to its own — **level 2:** Cards in its lines count the leader's class twice

name: Baseball Card
head: Paid by rarity. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match count one rarity higher ⚑ *pair review: the same effect as Q0942, counting rarity instead of class*
a: Every card of a named rarity on the board gives a multiplier
b: Every card of a named rarity on the board gives a multiplier, and the rarity rises each show
c: The multiplier scales with how many distinct rarities are represented on the board

name: Beige Deck
head: Commons hit far harder. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It also quadruples the rarity you own least of
a: Common cards have their values quadrupled
b: Common cards have their values quadrupled, and rarer cards halved
c: Whichever rarity you own most of has its values quadrupled

name: Driver's License
head: Paid once your deck is stamped enough. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Stamps on cards sitting on hat marks they match count twice
a: Triples score once your deck holds at least a threshold number of stamped cards
b: Triples score once the deck holds a threshold of stamped cards, and the threshold rises each time it triggers
c: Scales smoothly with how many stamped cards the deck holds, rather than snapping at a threshold

name: Stone Joker
head: Paid by a type you have collected. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts two types ⚑ *pair review: the same effect as Q0942, counting type instead of class*
a: Gains a flat bonus for each card of a named type in your whole deck
b: Gains a flat bonus for each card of a named type in your deck, and names the type when acquired
c: Gains a flat bonus for each card of whichever type you own most of

name: The Cloverleaf
head: Four of a kind together upgrade each other. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A block that includes this card needs only three of the class
a: Four cards of the same class placed in a two-by-two block all upgrade permanently
b: Four cards of the same class placed adjacent in any shape all upgrade for the show
c: Four of the same class in a two-by-two block upgrade permanently, and the block then counts as one card

name: One Ring at a Time
head: Class bonuses count per grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Class counts in its lines count double ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Class counts are counted per grid rather than across the whole board
b: Class counts are per grid, and a class present in every grid pays a further bonus
c: Class counts are per grid, and a grid holding only one class pays double for it

name: Rival Companies
head: Two grids, two classes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its grid's class is named when it lands on its own mark ⚑ *pair review: it assigned at show start, when the card is still in the deck*
a: Each grid is assigned a class when this card is placed; cards of that class score double there and half elsewhere
b: Each grid is assigned a class; cards of other classes cannot be placed there at all
c: Each grid is assigned a class, and you choose the assignment before the show

name: The Company Split
head: Rewards spreading a class thin. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards of its class sitting on marks they match count twice ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Scores a bonus for each grid containing at least one card of its class
b: Scores a bonus for each grid containing at least two cards of its class
c: Scores a bonus for each grid containing its class, doubled if every grid does

name: Reserved Seating
head: Some cells only take one class. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Reserved cells in its lines accept any class ⚑ *pair review: overlaps the board plan: a cell that asks for one class is a talent mark*
a: Certain cells accept only cards of a named class, shown before you place
b: Certain cells accept only a named class, and a card of that class placed there scores double
c: Certain cells accept only a named class, and which class is rerolled each placement

name: The Dressing Room
head: A cell that belongs to whoever used it last ⚑ *pair review: overlaps the board plan: a cell that asks for one class is a talent mark*
a: This cell accepts only cards of the class that last scored in it; the first card placed there sets the class for the show
b: This cell accepts only cards of the class that last scored in it, and the class resets each Entrance refill
c: This cell accepts any class, but a card whose class differs from the last one to score there scores nothing

name: The Star Trap
head: Claims a cell for its own class. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may claim two cells ⚑ *pair review: overlaps the board plan: a cell that asks for one class is a talent mark*
a: Cue: claim one empty cell so only cards of this card's class may be placed there; that card scores double
b: Cue: claim one empty cell so only this card's class may go there, permanently
c: Cue: claim one empty cell so only this card's class may go there, and every such cell raises the class's bonus

name: Union Rules
head: A class must be represented ⚑ *pair review: only a restriction; it reads as a hazard*
a: At least one card of each class already on the board must be placed each Entrance refill, or the next refill's placements score nothing — **level 2:** Lines through its cell are exempt
b: Each row must contain at least two distinct classes to score — **level 2:** A line through its cell holding three classes scores double
c: Each line must contain at least one card of the class named at show start to score at all — **level 2:** Lines through its cell are exempt

name: Club passing
head: Passing clubs between columns
a: Two of these in different columns trade a buff back and forth on every refresh — **level 2:** The buff trades on every placement, not every refresh
b: Two of these in different columns trade a buff back and forth, and the buff grows each pass — **level 2:** The buff grows twice as fast while either of them sits on its mark
c: Two of these trade a buff every refresh, and the buff grows with the distance between them — **level 2:** The buff grows twice as fast while either of them sits on its mark

name: Flyer & catcher system
head: Thrown to wherever the catcher is. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While either sits on its mark, the Flyer may be thrown onto any cell in any line through the Catcher whose mark it matches
a: Cue: move the Flyer from its cell to any empty cell in the Catcher's column
b: Cue: move the Flyer from its cell to any empty cell adjacent to the Catcher
c: Cue: move the Flyer to any empty cell in the Catcher's column, and both score if it completes a line through the Catcher

name: Karagöz & Hacivat
head: Bound pair: each gains bonus multiplier while they are in opposite zones (one in the Entrance, one on the grid). **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each gains double while one of them sits on its mark
a: A bound pair: each gains a multiplier while they sit in opposite zones, one in the Entrance and one on the grid
b: A bound pair: each gains a multiplier while they share a line, and neither scores at all if the other is absent
c: A bound pair: each gains a multiplier that scales with the distance between them on the grid

name: Pizza Slice
head: Grows when its siblings die. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It gains double for a sibling destroyed on a matched cell
a: Gains a multiplier whenever another card of the same kind is destroyed
b: Gains a multiplier whenever another card of the same kind is destroyed or discarded
c: Gains a multiplier per sibling destroyed, and the last surviving one keeps the whole total

name: The Grudge
head: Two cards that remember each other. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Their pairing grows two steps a show
a: Two named cards are rivals; while both are on the same grid, both score nothing
b: Two named cards are rivals; while both are on the same grid both score double, and if either is destroyed the other is too
c: Two named cards are rivals; each show they share a grid, the pairing scores a step more than it did last time

name: The Old Favour
head: A card that pays back what another one did for it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts both of its neighbours in its row
a: This card scores a step for every placement in which the card next to it scored, counted across the whole run
b: This card scores a step for every placement in which the card next to it scored, counted this show only
c: This card names one other card at run start and scores a step for every show they both appeared in

name: The Tango Pair
head: Two that dance, one that leads. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Both skills fire at full while the leader sits on its mark
a: A pair that must stay adjacent, the free one sliding to rejoin each refresh; they alternate lead each turn and only the leader's skill fires, at +50%
b: A pair that must stay adjacent; both skills fire, each at +25%
c: A pair that must stay adjacent; they alternate lead, and the follower's skill fires on the leader's target

name: The Triple Somersault
head: A partner has to catch what goes blind. (line 1092). **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its middle stage is shown to you ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what the three stages are*
a: A three-stage effect where the middle stage resolves hidden from you, and a partner card must be on the board to complete it or the whole thing fails
b: A three-stage effect whose middle stage is hidden; without a partner card it completes anyway at a third of its value
c: A three-stage effect where the middle stage is hidden and the partner must be in the same line, paying enormously if it lands

name: Whiteface & Auguste
head: One gives the order, the other misreads it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The second fires it twice
a: Cue the first to name an adjacent card's trigger; the second fires it on a different valid target instead, at 150%
b: Cue the first to name any card's trigger; the second fires it on a target of your choosing, at 150%
c: Cue the first to name an adjacent card's trigger; the second fires it on a random valid target at 200%

name: The Crowded Sky
head: A ceiling on how many props can be in the air
a: No more than four props may be travelling at once anywhere on the board; further props wait their turn — **level 2:** Each prop beyond the third adds one to the combo
b: No more than four props may travel at once per grid, and a fifth spawn destroys the oldest — **level 2:** Each prop beyond the third adds one to the combo
c: There is no ceiling, and every prop in the air beyond the fourth adds one to the combo — **level 2:** Each prop beyond the fourth also adds one to the next volley's size

name: The Emit Order
head: The last prop out is the heaviest. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: In a volley from this suit, each prop is a step stronger than the one before it
b: In a volley from this suit, the first prop is the strongest and each after it is weaker
c: In a volley from this suit every prop is equal, but the volley is one larger for each earlier volley this placement

name: The Multiball
head: One score, many props at once. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: This suit spawns three props at once rather than one, each on its own path
b: This suit spawns three props at once, but each carries a third of the usual effect
c: This suit spawns one prop, and one more for every other card of this suit already on the grid

name: The Prop Master
head: More props from everything. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own suit's volleys get two extra props
a: Every prop-spawning suit effect produces one extra prop per volley
b: Every prop-spawning suit effect produces one extra prop per volley, and the extra prop travels the column instead of the row
c: Every prop-spawning suit effect produces props equal to the number of distinct suits that scored in the line

name: The Reload
head: Props are a magazine, not a faucet ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (c) only cap your props; it reads as a hazard*
a: Each suit has a fixed number of props per show; when they are spent that suit spawns nothing until the next show — **level 2:** On its mark, its suit's magazine refills at each Entrance refill
b: Each suit has a fixed number of props per show, and props are returned to the magazine when they finish their path without hitting anything — **level 2:** On its mark, its suit's magazine refills at each Entrance refill
c: Each suit has a fixed number of props per Entrance refill, refilled at the start of the next placement — **level 2:** On its mark, its suit's magazine holds two more

name: The Slow Volley
head: Fewer props, but each one lingers. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Props spawned in a line through its cell fire twice more on cards sitting on marks they match
a: Props this card spawns arrive one at a time rather than as a burst, and each travels at half speed
b: Props this card spawns arrive one at a time at half speed, and each fires twice on every card it crosses
c: Props this card spawns arrive as a burst but travel at half speed, so the whole volley overlaps the placement

name: The Staggered Train
head: A volley strung out over the placement
a: Props this card spawns emit one per tick, each from the cell the last one stopped in — **level 2:** Props spawned in any line through its cell emit this way too
b: Props this card spawns emit one per tick, and each one that is still travelling when the next emits adds one to the combo — **level 2:** Each overlapping prop adds two to the combo
c: Props this card spawns emit all at once, but each is held back a tick longer than the last before it starts moving — **level 2:** Props spawned in any line through its cell emit this way too

name: Electric
head: When this card scores, an arc prop hops card-to-card through orthogonally adjacent cards, adding points per link, until it reaches a gap. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: On score, an arc hops between orthogonally adjacent cards adding points per link, stopping at the first gap
b: On score, an arc hops between every card of the same suit in the grid regardless of adjacency, adding points per link
c: On score, an arc hops between orthogonally and diagonally adjacent cards, stopping at the first gap, and each link pays a step into the special bucket

name: Fireworks
head: When this card scores, its rocket prop rises up the column and banks the column's score directly. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: On score, a rocket rises up the column and banks the column's score directly, scaled by this card's rank
b: On score, a rocket rises up the column and banks the column's score; each firework trigger adds one more rocket to the next
c: On score, rockets rise up this column and both columns beside it, banking each column's score at half

name: The Aimed Shot
head: You point it, the board does the rest. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It aims every prop spawned in a line through its cell
a: Cue on spawn: choose the direction the next prop leaves in; it then travels on its own until it stops
b: Cue on spawn: choose the direction and the speed of the next prop
c: Cue on spawn: choose the target cell; the prop routes to it by the longest path that crosses the most cards

name: The Bounce
head: A prop that never travels straight. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: This suit spawns a prop that changes direction ninety degrees each time it crosses an occupied cell
b: This suit spawns a prop that changes direction ninety degrees at each occupied cell, and finishes when it reaches an edge
c: This suit spawns a prop that reflects off the grid edges and keeps travelling until its tick budget runs out

name: The Mancala Walk
head: A prop that seeds as it goes. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: This suit spawns a prop that walks cell by cell around the ring of the grid, dropping one step of row score in each cell it passes
b: This suit spawns a prop that walks the ring, dropping a step in each cell and two in an empty cell whose mark shares this card's suit
c: This suit spawns a prop that walks the ring for exactly as many cells as its spawner rank, dropping score in each

name: The Marionette
head: Take the controls
a: Take direct control of one prop for the placement: it moves one cell per tick in the direction you steer — **level 2:** You steer two props
b: Take direct control of one prop for the placement, and it may change direction once per tick — **level 2:** You steer two props
c: Take direct control of every prop your own cards spawn this placement, steering them one at a time — **level 2:** You steer every prop on the grid this placement, not only your own cards'

name: The Route Rewrite
head: Redraws where a prop is going, mid-flight
a: Cue: redraw the remaining path of any prop in flight to any cells you choose of the same length — **level 2:** You may redraw every prop in flight, not only one
b: Cue: redraw the remaining path of any prop in flight, and it may be any length up to twice the original — **level 2:** You may redraw every prop in flight, not only one
c: Every prop that enters this card has the rest of its path redrawn to cross as many occupied cells as possible — **level 2:** The redrawn path may revisit cells it has already crossed

name: The Scenic Route
head: The long way round pays better. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: Props from this suit take the longest path to their destination rather than the shortest, and score per cell crossed
b: Props from this suit take the longest path, and score per cell crossed only where the cell was occupied
c: Props from this suit take a path that visits every line on the grid once, at half strength per cell

name: The Transformer
head: Changes a prop in flight. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose the kind a prop becomes
a: A prop passing this card is converted into a different kind of prop and continues on
b: A prop passing this card is converted and its remaining path is recalculated from here
c: A prop passing this card is duplicated, one continuing as it was and one as a different kind

name: The Bomb Peg
head: A prop that goes off where it lands. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The blast reaches two cells
a: A prop that reaches this card detonates, firing its effect on every card orthogonally adjacent instead of on this one
b: A prop that reaches this card detonates on every adjacent card, and this card is destroyed
c: A prop that reaches this card detonates across the whole 3x3 around it, at reduced strength per card

name: The Branding Iron
head: A prop that leaves equipment behind. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: A prop from this suit leaves a stamp on the last card it reaches, chosen from the stamps already on the grid
b: A prop from this suit leaves a stamp on every card it crosses, spending itself after three
c: A prop from this suit leaves on the last card it reaches the hat printed on the mark beneath that card, so the card now matches its mark on hat

name: The Hoop Encore
head: A prop that makes talents fire again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The re-fire reaches the cards beside the prop's path ⚑ *pair review: Hoop props already re-score the skill cards they sweep*
a: A prop from this card re-fires the skill of every card it crosses
b: A prop from this card re-fires the skill of every card it crosses, at half strength
c: A prop from this card re-fires the skill of the single highest-ranked card it crosses, at double strength

name: The Juggling Ball
head: A prop that knocks a juggling card off its cell. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
