a: A prop from this suit knocks the first juggling card it crosses one cell along its path, if that cell is empty
b: A prop from this suit knocks every juggling card it crosses one cell along its path, if that cell is empty
c: A prop from this suit knocks the first juggling card it crosses onto the nearest empty cell whose mark it matches

name: The Muck
head: A prop that leaves the board worse
a: A prop carrying this status coats every card it crosses; a coated card scores nothing until another prop crosses it
b: A prop carrying this status coats every card it crosses; a coated card scores half until the end of the placement
c: A prop carrying this status coats the first card it crosses only, and that card must be cleared by a second prop before it scores again

name: The Payload
head: What the prop is worth is what it has been through. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: A prop from this suit adds nothing on the cards it crosses; it banks one step per card and pays the whole total into the last card
b: A prop from this suit banks one step per card crossed and pays the total into the last card, doubling if it crosses five
c: A prop from this suit banks one step per card crossed and pays the total into whichever card in its path scored highest

name: The Prop Tax
head: A prop that takes instead of giving. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card on a mark it matches pays its step without losing it
a: A prop from this card removes a step from every card it crosses and pays the whole total to this card
b: A prop from this card removes a step from every card it crosses and pays the total to the last card it reaches
c: A prop from this card removes a rank from every card it crosses permanently, and pays the total to this card

name: The Refresh Peg
head: Being hit puts the board back. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own row and column are restored too
a: A prop that crosses this card spotlights every card in its line until the placement ends, covered or not
b: A prop that crosses this card restores its own line to spotlit and re-arms every spent cue in that line
c: A prop that crosses this card re-arms every spent cue on the grid, once per Entrance refill

name: The Target Girl
head: Every miss is worth something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Misses in its lines pay double
a: In a row a knife prop crosses, every miss becomes points
b: In any line a prop crosses, every miss becomes points
c: In a row a knife crosses, every miss becomes points, and a hit on this card becomes double points

name: The Chain Reaction
head: Props set each other off
a: A prop finishing its path spawns a fresh prop from wherever it stopped, up to a chain of three — **level 2:** The chain runs to four
b: A prop finishing its path spawns a fresh prop from where it stopped, and the chain is unlimited but halves each link — **level 2:** The first link does not halve
c: A prop finishing its path spawns a fresh prop only if it crossed at least three cards — **level 2:** A prop spawns its successor after crossing two cards, not three

name: The Collision
head: Props that meet each other
a: Two props meeting on the same cell both fire at double strength and both stop there — **level 2:** Props meeting on a matched cell do not stop there; both continue
b: Two props meeting on the same cell destroy each other — **level 2:** Props meeting on a matched cell pass through each other instead
c: Two props meeting merge into a single prop carrying both effects — **level 2:** Props meeting on a matched cell fire at double

name: The Deflection
head: Bounces one prop off another. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose the new direction
a: Cue: the next prop to meet another is deflected ninety degrees and continues on its new path
b: Cue: the next prop to meet another reverses direction and travels back the way it came
c: Props always deflect off one another rather than passing through, with no cue needed

name: The Overtake
head: What happens when a fast prop catches a slow one
a: A prop that catches another absorbs it, taking both effects and the faster speed — **level 2:** The absorbed prop's effect doubles
b: A prop that catches another pushes it along, both firing on every card thereafter — **level 2:** The pushed prop fires at double
c: A prop that catches another stops behind it, forming a queue that fires as one when the leader finishes — **level 2:** The queue fires twice when the leader finishes

name: The Split
head: One prop becomes two, then four
a: A prop crossing this card splits into two, each continuing on a perpendicular path at half strength — **level 2:** The halves travel at full strength
b: A prop crossing this card splits into two at full strength, and neither may split again — **level 2:** The halves may split once more on another such card
c: A prop crossing this card splits into two at half strength, and each half may split again on another such card — **level 2:** The halves travel at full strength

name: Curtain Call
head: Props survive the line
a: A prop is not cleared when its line finishes scoring; it continues into the next placement — **level 2:** A surviving prop fires again on the first card it crosses in its next placement
b: A prop is not cleared when its line finishes, but it fires at half strength thereafter — **level 2:** Surviving props fire at full strength
c: Props are cleared at show end rather than line end, so they accumulate all show — **level 2:** A surviving prop fires again on the first card it crosses in its next placement

name: The Endless Round
head: A prop that does not stop. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each lap pays a step more than the last instead of less
a: Props this card spawns wrap at the grid edge and keep travelling until they have crossed as many cards as the spawner's rank
b: Props this card spawns wrap at the edge and keep travelling for a fixed number of laps
c: Props this card spawns wrap and keep travelling, weakening by one step per lap

name: The Hopper
head: A cell that banks the props fed to it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays out twice
a: Props that reach this card are stored rather than resolved; the store pays out when the card scores
b: Props that reach this card are stored and pay out at the end of each placement
c: Props stored here pay out when the card scores, and the payout grows with how many kinds it has collected

name: The Lit Peg
head: A cell that stays lit once a prop has been through it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A lit cell whose mark the placed card matches scores two extra steps
a: A cell a prop crosses stays lit for the rest of the placement; a second prop crossing a lit cell fires at double strength
b: A cell a prop crosses stays lit for the rest of the show, and lit cells score an extra step at show end
c: A cell a prop crosses stays lit until a card is placed there, and placing on a lit cell scores an extra step

name: The Orphaned Prop
head: A prop outlives the card that threw it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Orphaned props fire at double
a: A prop keeps travelling and firing after its spawning card leaves the board
b: A prop keeps travelling after its spawner leaves, but at half strength
c: A prop whose spawner leaves the board finishes its current path and then stops where it is, becoming a fixed hazard

name: The Standing Prop
head: A prop that stays where it lands. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A standing prop on a matched cell fires twice
a: Props this card spawns stop on their last cell and stay there, firing again each placement
b: Props this card spawns stop on their last cell and stay for one further placement only
c: Props this card spawns stop where they land, and a card placed on that cell inherits the prop

name: The Blockhead
head: Absorbs one Knife prop per show, banking it as flat points instead of being hit
a: Absorbs one Knife prop per show, banking it as flat points instead of taking the hit — **level 2:** It absorbs two per show
b: Absorbs one prop of any kind per show, banking it as flat points — **level 2:** It absorbs two per show
c: Absorbs every prop that would hit its row, banking each as flat points, and breaks after three — **level 2:** It does not break while it sits on its mark

name: The Bumper
head: Bounces a prop instead of absorbing it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose the bounce direction
a: A prop that hits this card is deflected ninety degrees and continues from here
b: A prop that hits this card is sent back the way it came at double strength
c: A prop that hits this card is deflected toward whichever line is closest to completing

name: The Dodge
head: A card the prop passes over without touching
a: This card negates the effect of the first prop to cross it each placement, and the prop continues on — **level 2:** It dodges two props per placement
b: This card negates the effect of every prop that crosses it, and scores a step for each one dodged — **level 2:** Each dodged prop continues on at double strength
c: This card negates the first prop each placement and steals its effect, firing it on a card of your choice — **level 2:** It dodges two props per placement

name: The Funnel
head: Every prop ends up in the same place. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose where props drift each tick
a: Props drift one cell toward the centre of the grid each tick, on top of their own movement
b: Props drift one cell toward the nearest incomplete line each tick
c: Props drift one cell toward the last card placed each tick

name: The Magnet
head: Props bend toward it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Props pulled through it fire twice there
a: Every prop on this grid alters its path to pass through this card at some point
b: Every prop on this grid alters its path to pass through this card, and finishes there rather than continuing
c: Every prop within two cells of this card is pulled one cell toward it each tick

name: The Net
head: Catches a prop and throws it back. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Twice per Entrance refill
a: Once per Entrance refill, catch a falling prop mid-flight and re-aim it at any card in the same column
b: Once per Entrance refill, catch any prop mid-flight and re-aim it at any card on the grid
c: Once per Entrance refill, catch a prop mid-flight and hold it; release it on a later placement at double strength

name: Unpierceable
head: Knives go straight through. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Props passing through it fire twice on the card behind
a: Knife props pass through this card harmlessly, but still count as a miss for miss-triggered bonuses
b: Every prop passes through this card harmlessly, and each pass counts as a miss for miss-triggered bonuses
c: Knife props pass through this card and continue to the next card behind it, hitting that instead

name: The Border Toll
head: Crossing between grids costs the prop something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its props cross without paying ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: A prop may cross into the neighbouring grid, losing one step of strength at the boundary
b: A prop may cross into the neighbouring grid by paying one cell of its remaining path
c: A prop may cross into the neighbouring grid freely, but may never cross back

name: The Ferry
head: A card that carries props over the gap. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: A prop that finishes on a card of this suit is relaunched from the same coordinate in the neighbouring grid
b: A prop that finishes on a card of this suit is relaunched from the neighbouring grid at full strength, once per Entrance refill
c: A prop that finishes on a card of this suit is relaunched from the grid holding the fewest cards

name: The Flying Trapeze
head: A prop that leaves its grid ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Props this card spawns cross into the next grid at the same row and continue — **level 2:** Its props may cross back
b: Props this card spawns cross into the next grid and continue at full strength through every grid — **level 2:** Its props may choose the grid they cross into
c: Props this card spawns cross into the next grid, halving in strength at each boundary — **level 2:** Its props keep full strength across the boundary

name: The Grand Tour
head: One prop, every grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its props visit the grids in the order you choose ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: Props this card spawns route through every unlocked grid in turn before finishing
b: Props this card spawns route through every unlocked grid, and score a step more in each grid than the last
c: Props this card spawns route through every grid, and finish in whichever grid holds the most cards

name: The Long Throw
head: A suit whose props span the board. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match ⚑ *pair review: needs a second grid, and a normal run plays one*
a: This suit's props travel across every grid at once rather than staying in one
b: This suit's props travel across every grid, but only fire on the grid they started in
c: This suit's props travel across every grid, and score for each grid boundary they cross

name: The Relay
head: A prop that snakes down the grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its props snake back up once they run off the bottom
a: A prop reaching the grid edge re-enters from the opposite edge one row lower and keeps going, snaking down the grid until it runs off the bottom
b: As (a), but it re-enters only if the last card it crossed shares its spawner's suit
c: As (a), and it is a step stronger on each row than the last

name: Sterile Field
head: Props arrive clean
a: Props spawned by this card carry no statuses at all, ignoring anything on the spawner — **level 2:** Props spawned in its lines carry no statuses
b: Props spawned by this card carry no statuses, and strip statuses from every card they pass — **level 2:** Props spawned in its lines carry no statuses
c: Props spawned anywhere on this grid carry no statuses — **level 2:** Its props also cleanse the cards in its row

name: The Costume Change
head: Props carry their spawner's statuses. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which statuses its props carry
a: A prop inherits every status its spawning card carries
b: A prop inherits one status from its spawner, chosen at random
c: A prop inherits its spawner's statuses, and applies them to every card it passes

name: The Handoff
head: Props pick statuses up as they go
a: A prop takes on any status of the first card it passes, and carries it for the rest of its path — **level 2:** A prop may carry two statuses
b: A prop takes on the status of every card it passes, accumulating them — **level 2:** It leaves everything it accumulated on the last card it passes
c: A prop takes on the status of the first card it passes and leaves that status on the last — **level 2:** A prop may carry two statuses

name: Blacklist
head: Names a rank and kills it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell ignore the ban
a: Names a rank: any line containing it scores nothing; this card destroys itself once that rank is gone from the deck
b: Names a rank: any line containing it scores nothing, permanently
c: Names a rank each show: lines containing it score nothing, and removing that rank from the deck pays a bounty

name: Firetown's Snub
head: Town rule: Flames-suit effects score nothing here, and Burning statuses do not multiply
a: Town rule: one suit chosen per town scores nothing, and its statuses do not multiply
b: Town rule: one suit chosen per town scores nothing, but every other suit scores double
c: Town rule: whichever suit you played most last show scores nothing this show

name: Temperance Town
head: Town rule: Concessions-class cards are disabled
a: Town rule: Concessions-class cards are disabled
b: Town rule: one class chosen per town is disabled
c: Town rule: one class chosen per town is disabled, and every card of that class scores double in the next town

name: The Loggione
head: A crowd with expensive taste
a: Town hazard: Common cards score nothing here and Legendary cards score triple
b: Town hazard: cards below a named rarity score nothing here, and the rarity rises each show
c: Town hazard: the rarity you own most of scores nothing here

name: The Pillar
head: Boss: nothing works twice
a: Boss: cards that scored in an earlier placement score nothing for the rest of the show
b: Boss: cards that scored in an earlier placement score half for the rest of the show
c: Boss: cards that scored in the previous placement score nothing this placement, but recover the placement after

name: The Prepared Town
head: A town that has done its homework ⚑ *pair review: you defined a fake as a ghost card, one that does not stay in the deck when the game ends; this effect's premise, a hidden fake to find, is not that*
a: Boss: everything is pre-inspected, revealing and disabling every fake, masked and disguised card for the show
b: Boss: everything is pre-inspected and disabled, but each disguised card disabled adds one to the combo
c: Boss: one card per Entrance refill is inspected and disabled, chosen by the boss, in descending order of value

name: The Offering
head: After Balatro's Verdant Leaf: everything is off until you give something up
a: Boss: every card is debuffed until one of your cards has left the board this show, by any effect
b: Boss: a button beside End discards the highest-ranked card on the grid; every card is debuffed until it has been pressed once
c: As (a), and the debuff returns at each Entrance refill

name: Place Your Own Threats
head: The hazards are cards you chose to put down
a: You place the hazard cards yourself; each one raises the show's difficulty and its reward together
b: You place hazard cards yourself, and may remove one per Entrance refill at a cost
c: You place hazard cards yourself, and adjacent hazards combine into worse ones that pay more

name: Robber card
head: Robbers between the turns ⚑ *pair review: 'turns', 'steal' and 'catching' were undefined*
a: Between Entrance refills, a robber discards the highest-ranked card on the grid — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, robbers skip cards sitting on marks they match
b: Between Entrance refills, a robber discards the highest-ranked card on the grid unless it scored that refill — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, robbers skip cards sitting on marks they match
c: As (b); completing a line through the robbed cell that refill catches him: the card returns to the top of the stock you choose and the thefts stop for the show — **level 2:** A robber caught in its lines drops what it stole into the Entrance

name: The Hook
head: Town hazard: after each placement, the lowest-ranked grid card is discarded unless it scored that placement
a: Town hazard: after each placement, the lowest-ranked card on the grid is discarded unless it scored that placement
b: Town hazard: after each placement, the lowest-ranked card in the row just placed into is discarded unless it scored
c: Town hazard: after each placement, the card that has been on the grid longest without scoring is discarded

name: Vampire swarm edge-eating
head: After the game Vampire Survivors: something is eating the edges ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Cards at the grid's edge are eaten over several turns; playing them all removes the threat — **level 2:** Cards in its lines count as played toward removing the threat
b: Cards at the grid's edge are eaten one per turn until the edge is empty — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, its row's edge is not eaten
c: Cards at the edge are eaten over several turns, and each one eaten makes the next come faster — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, its row's edge is not eaten

name: Boss fire-breathing fight
head: A boss that breathes on the score
a: Boss: appears and must be beaten with specific hands or raw points while it burns down your score each turn
b: Boss: each placement it burns a step off your smallest non-zero bucket, faster the longer the show runs
c: Boss: each placement it burns a step off your smallest non-zero bucket, and only a line of the hand type it names heals that step back

name: Circus Maximus race show
head: Beat the clock, not the crowd
a: Show variant: reach the goal within a fixed number of turns
b: Show variant: reach the goal within a fixed number of turns, with the turn count shrinking each placement
c: Show variant: reach the goal within a fixed number of turns; finishing early banks the turns you saved as fame

name: Eldritch Invasion
head: Something is arriving whether you are ready or not ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: An invading force adds one hostile card to the grid each turn, from a fixed edge — **level 2:** A line through its cell pushes the invasion back a turn
b: An invading force adds one hostile card each turn from an edge that changes — **level 2:** A line through its cell pushes the invasion back a turn
c: An invading force adds cards at an accelerating rate, and clearing a line pushes it back a turn — **level 2:** A line through its cell also discards one invader

name: The Marathon
head: Three shows that never reset
a: Boss gauntlet: three shows where the board does not reset between them, statuses and hazards persist, and goals stack
b: Boss gauntlet: three shows where the board does not reset, but statuses clear between them
c: Boss gauntlet: three shows where the board does not reset and each show adds one new hazard

name: The Magician's Force
head: After Balatro's Cerulean Bell: one card is always chosen for you. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A forced card that lands on a mark it matches pays the match twice ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: One card in the Entrance is always forced: it must be the next card you place
b: One card in the Entrance is always forced, and which one changes each refresh
c: One cell of the grid must be filled before any other may be, chosen at random each refresh

name: Sapphire Stamp
head: One extra, one taken away
a: Place one extra card each placement, then one already placed is removed at random before scoring — **level 2:** A card sitting on a mark it matches is never the one removed
b: Place one extra card each placement, then one already placed is removed by your choice before scoring — **level 2:** The card you remove goes to the Entrance, not the discard
c: Place one extra card each placement, and the removal only happens if the line would have scored — **level 2:** A card sitting on a mark it matches is never the one removed

name: The Bring-In
head: The first placement is forced ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: The first card of each show must be placed in a cell the show names, not one you choose — **level 2:** A first card that lands on a mark it matches pays that match twice
b: The first card of each Entrance refill must be placed in a named cell — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose the named cell
c: The first card of each show is placed for you, and you are shown where before you see the card — **level 2:** A first card that lands on a mark it matches pays that match twice

name: The Curse In The Deck
head: Something you did not choose, taking up a slot ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Some cards enter the deck unbidden and cannot be placed; they must be drawn and discarded, costing a refresh — **level 2:** A curse drawn while it sits on its own mark may be placed in its lines and scores normally
b: Some cards enter the deck unbidden and can be placed but score nothing, occupying a cell all show — **level 2:** A curse placed in its lines scores normally
c: Some cards enter the deck unbidden and score negatively unless a line containing them is a made hand — **level 2:** A curse placed in its lines scores normally

name: The Psychic
head: Boss: exactly five, every time
a: Boss: no line scores until all five cards of the current Entrance refill have been placed
b: Boss: each Entrance refill's five cards must all go into a single row or column
c: Boss: the five cards of each Entrance refill must each be placed in a different column

name: Escalating Demands
head: The bar rises each refill
a: Boss: each Entrance refill names a harder hand than the last, and failing one ends the show
b: Boss: each Entrance refill names a harder hand; failing one voids that refill's lines but not the show
c: Boss: each Entrance refill names a harder hand, and you may bank an easy hand early to spend on a hard one later

name: The Audition
head: Prove it before you may continue
a: Boss: a specific hand must be scored before the show's second Entrance refill arrives
b: Boss: a specific hand must be scored within each Entrance refill before the next one arrives
c: Boss: a specific hand must be scored at some point in the show, or the show is lost regardless of score

name: The Bond
head: Prove you can pay before you are allowed to continue. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Scores through its cell count double toward the sum ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: A fixed sum must be banked before the show's second Entrance refill arrives, or the show ends there
b: A fixed sum must be banked before the show's second Entrance refill; falling short discards that refill rather than ending the show
c: A fixed sum must be banked before each Entrance refill arrives

name: The Set List
head: You must play the named hand
a: Boss: a hand type is named each Entrance refill, and that refill's lines score nothing unless that hand is among what you complete
b: Boss: a hand type is named each Entrance refill; that refill's lines of any other type score half
c: Boss: a hand type is named each Entrance refill, and completing it doubles that refill's lines rather than gating them

name: Avalanche
head: After scoring, reduce the show's score goal by the number of cards currently placed on the grid
a: After each line scores, the show's goal drops by the number of cards on the grid — **level 2:** Cards sitting on marks they match count twice toward the drop
b: When a line scores, the show's goal drops by the number of empty cells on the grid — **level 2:** Each card sitting on a mark it matches also counts toward the drop
c: Each time a grid is filled completely, the show's goal drops by 25 — **level 2:** The drop is 25 plus the number of cards sitting on marks they match

name: Chindon'ya
head: Consumable: the next town's fame requirement drops 15%
a: Consumable: the next show's goal drops by 15%
b: Consumable: the next show's goal drops by 25% and the show after it rises by 10%
c: Consumable: the next show's goal drops by 5% for each Entrance card left unplaced when you spend it

name: Pre-show challenge dance
head: Open with a display instead of a card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On its mark the display costs nothing: it scores as well
a: Placed as the show's first card, it scores nothing that placement and the show's goal drops a step
b: Placed as the show's first card, it scores nothing that placement and the show's goal drops by the score it forfeited
c: Placed as the show's first card, it scores nothing that placement and the goal drops a step, or two if it is also the second placement's only card

name: The Cliffhanger
head: Cue at show end: the next town's goal drops 30%, but this card must score in that show or lose double the discount as fame. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cued from its mark, this card is dealt into the next show's first Entrance
a: Cue at show end: the next town's goal drops 30%, but this card must score there or you lose double the discount in fame
b: Cue at show end: the next town's goal drops 30% with no condition attached
c: Cue at show end: name a discount up to 50%; this card must score there or you lose double it in fame

name: The Designated Loser
head: A boss show with a trivial goal that is normally always won, but has a hidden seeded 1-in-1000 chance the goal silently triples mid-show
a: A boss show with a trivial goal that is normally always won, with a hidden 1-in-1000 chance the goal silently triples mid-show
b: A boss show with a trivial goal, with a hidden 1-in-100 chance the goal silently triples mid-show
c: A boss show with a trivial goal that triples at the show's second Entrance refill, announced at show start, so the trivial goal must be met in five placements

name: The Flint
head: Boss: everything scores half
a: Boss: the base points of every hand, and every bonus mult, are halved
b: Boss: base points are halved, but the combo counts double
c: Boss: base points are halved, and every effect trigger is worth twice as much combo

name: The Vidushaka
head: Talks the goal down. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The goal drops 30% instead of 20%
a: Once per tour: the current show's goal drops 20%
b: Once per tour: the current show's goal drops 20%, and again by 20% if you are already past halfway
c: Once per show: the goal drops 20%, but the next show's goal rises by the same amount

name: Hurricane card
head: A storm that walks the grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A soaked card in its lines pays double when it scores ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Cards in a ring shape are soaked; the storm starts at a random strength, walks the grid and weakens
b: Cards in a ring shape are soaked; the storm walks the grid at constant strength until the show ends
c: Cards in a ring are soaked; the storm walks the grid, weakening, and its next position is telegraphed

name: Lightning card
head: Strikes the tallest thing on the board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lightning that strikes its lines adds +1 to that line's multiplier ⚑ *pair review: (c) needed a second grid*
a: Lightning strikes the highest-value card on the board, applying a shock effect
b: Lightning strikes the highest-value card and arcs to everything orthogonally adjacent to it
c: Lightning strikes the highest-value card in each column at once

name: Negative weather effects
head: The show must go on. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Weather skips its lines ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard; it also does not say what weather does*
a: Weather events impose negative effects during a show
b: Weather events impose negative effects, and are announced one town in advance
c: Weather events impose negative effects that intensify the longer the show runs

name: The Falling Wall
head: Boss attack, telegraphed one turn ahead: destroys an entire column except one exact row slot
a: Telegraphed one turn ahead: destroys an entire column except one exact cell
b: Telegraphed one turn ahead: destroys an entire line except one exact cell, and you are told which cell before it lands
c: Telegraphed one turn ahead: destroys an entire column, and you choose one card to save

name: The Great Dome (Final Venue)
head: After the Las Vegas Sphere: the venue itself performs
a: Final venue: board-wide effects from the town alter play every turn
b: Final venue: board-wide effects alter play every turn, drawn from every hazard you faced this run
c: Final venue: board-wide effects alter play every turn, and you are shown the next one in advance

name: The Volcano
head: The floor is lava
a: Terrain boss: the bottom row is lava; any card ending a turn there catches Burning and loses 1 rank per turn
b: Terrain boss: the bottom row is lava and rises one row every three turns
c: Terrain boss: one row is lava, and which row it is moves every turn, telegraphed one turn ahead

name: Tornado card
head: A tornado of random size. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards the tornado lifts from its lines land on marks they match ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard; it also does not say what the tornado does*
a: Affects an area whose size is rolled between one cell and a whole grid
b: Affects a single cell, and the area grows by one each turn it stays on the board
c: Affects an area whose size is rolled, and its path is telegraphed one turn ahead

name: Tsunami card
head: A wave that lowers the ceiling. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Stacks in its lines score at four high while the wave is up ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Washes up from the bottom row, lowering the maximum stack height, then recedes
b: Washes up from the bottom row, lowering the maximum stack height permanently for the show
c: Washes up from the bottom, lowering the height cap as it rises and restoring it as it recedes, on a fixed cycle

name: Blossom Stake
head: Any boss, any time
a: Final-tier bosses may appear at any point in the tour
b: Final-tier bosses may appear at any point, and you are warned one town ahead
c: Bosses are drawn from the whole pool at every town, so difficulty is unordered

name: Boss Tag
head: Reroll the boss
a: Consumable: reroll the current town's boss
b: Consumable: reroll the current town's boss, seeing the replacement before committing
c: Consumable: reroll the boss, and you may keep whichever of the two you prefer

name: Hippodrome factions
head: The crowd has favourites
a: Each show an audience faction favours one suit; ignoring them too long summons a Riot boss
b: Each show an audience faction favours one suit, and playing to them pays a bonus
c: Each show two factions favour opposing suits; pleasing one angers the other, and neglecting both summons a Riot

name: The Rogues' Gallery
head: After the Cryptid mod's Obsidian Orb: every boss you have already beaten, at once
a: Boss: carries the abilities of every boss you have beaten this run
b: Boss: carries the abilities of the three bosses you beat fastest
c: Boss: carries every beaten boss's ability, and you may disable one by skipping that show's reward

name: The Rat Sheet
head: Raises the stakes for both sides ⚑ *pair review: fame is not spendable*
a: Consumable: raises the next rival show's difficulty for both players; if both would pass, you take a quarter of its payout
b: Consumable: raises the next rival show's difficulty for both; if you pass and the rival does not, you take all of its payout
c: Consumable: raises the next rival show's difficulty for the rival only, at the cost of skipping its reward

name: The Rival Show
head: Somebody played this town first
a: Recurring boss: a rival plays the town first and raises the goal by 30%; beating it steals a card from the rival's deck
b: Recurring boss: a rival plays the town first and raises the goal by whatever margin it beat its own goal by
c: Recurring boss: a rival plays the town first; you see the exact board it built, and beating its score steals a card

name: Candy Sticks
head: The boss starts late. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Placed on its mark during a boss show, the boss's ability switches off until the next line completes
a: The next boss's ability does not switch on until you have completed one line
b: The next boss's ability does not switch on until the show's second placement
c: Every boss's ability starts one placement late for the rest of the run

name: FEMA mode
head: Relief arrives after enough disasters. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Relief arrives one weather card sooner ⚑ *pair review: depends on Q1117, and does not say what damage or relief is*
a: After a number of weather cards, disaster relief becomes available as a free repair
b: After a number of weather cards, disaster relief becomes available and scales with how much damage was taken
c: After a number of weather cards, you choose between relief now or a larger payout if you survive the next one

name: Hey Rube!
head: Boss: each placement, every card in the rightmost column gets Exhausted unless an Escape Artist-class card stands in that column
a: Boss: each placement, every card in the rightmost column is Exhausted unless an Escape Artist stands in that column
b: Boss: each placement, every card in one random column is Exhausted unless a protective stamp stands in it
c: Boss: each placement, the column that scored least is Exhausted entirely

name: Matador
head: Paid for setting off the trap. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays double for triggers from lines through its cell
a: Scores bonus points whenever a line you score triggers the boss's ability
b: Scores bonus points and +1 combo whenever a line you score triggers the boss's ability
c: Scores bonus points whenever the boss's ability fires at all, whatever set it off

name: Fog of war on choices
head: You cannot see far ahead
a: Fog obscures map choices beyond the next step
b: Fog obscures map choices beyond the next two steps
c: Fog obscures choices beyond the next step, and lifts one step further each time you win a show

name: The Advance Man
head: Consumable: reveals all fog-of-war nodes within 2 edges of the player's position, including contents
a: Consumable: reveals every fogged map node within two steps, contents included
b: Consumable: reveals every fogged map node on the whole route, but only their types, not their contents
c: Consumable: reveals every fogged node within two steps and lets you swap two of them

name: The Mitt Camp Reading
head: Buys the truth about what is ahead
a: Consumable: one true fact about each of the next three map nodes
b: Consumable: one true fact about a node of your choice anywhere on the route
c: Consumable: one true fact each about three nodes you choose

name: Branching escalating-difficulty paths
head: Branching paths of rising difficulty
a: Map: branching paths of escalating difficulty, splitting roguelike routes from preset puzzle levels
b: Map: branching paths of escalating difficulty, where clearing one path unlocks a shortcut on another
c: Map: branching paths where each path has its own theme and its own escalating difficulty curve

name: Calendar shows (Inti Raymi)
head: Festivals on a fixed calendar
a: Bonus festivals appear at fixed intervals along the route, every Nth node
b: Bonus festivals appear at fixed intervals, and reaching one early carries the bonus forward
c: Bonus festivals appear at fixed intervals, and you may skip a reward to move one closer

name: One-way constellation map
head: After the game FTL: Faster Than Light: a constellation you cannot walk back
a: Map: a constellation of cities with no backtracking; touring builds fame, and hazards and weather occur between them
b: Map: a constellation with no backtracking, and each city visited raises the odds of hazards on the next leg
c: Map: a constellation with no backtracking, and you plan the whole route before the tour begins

name: Map alternative topologies
head: The route has no end, only a shape
a: Map: no final city; the route circles and towns become revisitable once enough time has passed
b: Map: no final city; you must return to where you started, and the return leg is harder
c: Map: the route circles, and each full circuit raises every town's goal

name: Map probability rings
head: Better cards toward the middle
a: The map is a square of probability rings, with higher-rank nodes likelier toward the centre
b: The map is a square of probability rings, and each step inward skips one more reward
c: The map is a square of probability rings, and the centre is only reachable once per run

name: Route-as-song bonus
head: Repeat the route, strengthen the placement
a: Repeating a route pattern you have walked before grants a strengthening bonus
b: Repeating a route pattern grants a bonus that grows with how long the repeated stretch is
c: Repeating a route pattern grants a bonus, and repeating it in reverse grants a different one

name: The International Final
head: The regions you toured vote
a: Suits favoured by regions you toured generously score extra in the final show
b: Suits favoured by regions you toured generously score extra, and regions you skipped penalise theirs
c: Each region you toured contributes one favoured suit to a final pool, and lines using them score extra

name: The Route Book
head: Plan the route, then stick to it
a: Plan an intended route before the run; deviating from it costs fame
b: Plan an intended route before the run; following it pays a bonus, and deviating costs nothing
c: Plan an intended route; deviating costs fame, but you may re-plan once per biome

name: Triangle map boss phase
head: Boss phases in the terrain
a: The map places a boss phase every few tiers, drawn as terrain
b: The map places a boss phase every few tiers, and fights happen only at those phases
c: The map places boss phases every few tiers, and you may skip a reward to skip one per run

name: Triangle map choice
head: A triangle you narrow as you climb
a: Choose from the next three options; moving left permanently loses the right lanes, and the middle loses both
b: Choose from the next three options; the lanes you lose become visible so you know what you gave up
c: Choose from the next three; lanes lost reopen once per run by skipping a reward

name: Location difficulty from card
head: The card on the node is the node
a: A map location's suit and rank set its difficulty and its type
b: A map location's rank sets its difficulty and its suit sets its type, and both are visible before travelling
c: A map location's card is the reward you win from it, so choosing the node chooses the prize

name: Pay-to-unlock squares
head: After the board game Monopoly: pay a card to open the square
a: Some map squares must be unlocked by sacrificing a card before they can be used
b: Some map squares must be unlocked by sacrificing a card of a named class
c: Some map squares must be unlocked with a card, and the card you spend determines the reward

name: Special map squares
head: Squares that mean something fixed
a: Map squares carry fixed effects by rank, with higher ranks more likely toward the centre
b: Map squares carry fixed effects by rank, and one rank is designated the rest rank each run
c: Map squares carry fixed effects by rank, and an effect can change a square's rank to change what it is

name: The Egress (event)
head: A sign that says This Way Out
a: Map event: following a mysterious sign skips the node entirely, with no reward and no risk
b: Map event: following the sign skips the node and pays a small fame bonus for the mystery
c: Map event: following the sign skips the node and reveals what you would have faced

name: The Ghost Train
head: A node you cannot preview
a: Map node: its contents cannot be previewed, and its average reward is better for it
b: Map node: its contents cannot be previewed, and it is always either the best or the worst node available
c: Map node: unpreviewable, with a better average reward, and previewing it at all skips a reward

name: The Locked Room
head: Needs the right keys
a: Map node: requires specific card types as keys to open its reward
b: Map node: requires specific card types as keys, and shows which before you commit to it
c: Map node: requires keys, and each key you lack can be had by skipping a reward instead

name: The Unsanctioned Show
head: Perform where you should not
a: Map node: performing at a forbidden node pays enormous fame, and failing loses the region's next reward
b: Map node: performing at a forbidden node pays enormous fame, and failing bars you from the region
c: Map node: a forbidden node pays enormous fame, and merely visiting it marks you for a later boss

name: Amusement city (Coney Island)
head: A town that is never the same twice
a: Town: its layout and offers differ every visit, and a map event may burn it down so it rebuilds changed
b: Town: its layout and offers differ every visit, and each visit makes the next one stranger
c: Town: its layout and offers are rerolled each visit, and you may skip a reward to reroll once more

name: Arena/naumachia town
head: Only the dangerous acts score ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a risk-tagged card is*
a: Town: only risk-tagged cards score here
b: Town: only risk-tagged cards score, and they score double
c: Town: only risk-tagged cards score, and a flood event fills the bottom rows so nothing may be placed there

name: Cabaret city
head: A town that stays up late
a: Town: night-show rules apply, favouring Dancer and Concessions cards
b: Town: night-show rules favour two classes drawn at random for that town
c: Town: night rules favour whichever class you have fewest of, and penalise your most common

name: Exposition City
head: One enormous show that takes all comers
a: Town: a single vast goal, once per map, where every suit is welcome and nothing is penalised
b: Town: a single vast goal where every suit is welcome, and the reward scales with the margin of the placement that meets it
c: Town: a single vast goal where every suit is welcome, but the show ends after a fixed, small number of placements

name: Friendly Acrobat town
head: A town that likes tumblers
a: Town: an Acrobat pack is guaranteed here
b: Town: a pack of one class is guaranteed here, the class differing per town
c: Town: a pack of the class you own most of is guaranteed here

name: Improving town (Chautauqua)
head: A town with standards ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a risk-tagged card is*
a: Town: no risk-tagged cards may score, and Concessions cards score double
b: Town: no risk-tagged cards may score, and one class you name at arrival scores double
c: Town: no risk-tagged cards may score, and every clean show raises the town's standing reward

name: Jaded city (Richiardi)
head: A town that has seen it all ⚑ *pair review: it does not say what a shock or risk-tagged act is*
a: Town: only shock and risk-tagged acts impress here; everything else scores half
b: Town: only shock and risk-tagged acts score at all
c: Town: only acts you have never played in this town before score at full value

name: Outlawed
head: In pious/lawful towns this card cannot score at all; everywhere else it scores double
a: In lawful towns this card cannot score at all; everywhere else it scores double
b: In lawful towns this card cannot be placed at all; everywhere else it scores double
c: The first town that outlaws this card makes it score double for the rest of the run

name: Pierrot
head: Gains bonus multiplier on odd-numbered shows of the tour; has no effect otherwise
a: Gains a multiplier on odd-numbered shows of the tour and does nothing on even ones — **level 2:** It gains the multiplier on even shows too
b: Gains a multiplier that grows by one step for each show of the tour it has been played in — **level 2:** It grows two steps per show
c: Gains a multiplier on any show where it is the only card of its class on the grid — **level 2:** Cards of its class that sit on marks they match do not count as sharing its grid, so it stays alone while its class fills the board

name: Resort towns
head: An easy stop
a: Town: lower goals, better card rewards, no boss
b: Town: lower goals, but no card rewards
c: Town: lower goals and better card rewards, and the next town's goal rises to compensate

name: The Rappings
head: A town that stays haunted
a: Town: answers come by knocks, and debunking the haunting does not lift it
b: Town: answers come by knocks; debunking it converts the town to a normal one permanently
c: Town: answers come by knocks, and the knocks are honest exactly as often as the town is

name: The Right to Perform
head: Comply, or fight for it
a: Town: comply with a ban for no fame, or resist and play a hazard show for double fame and permanent change
b: Town: comply for no fame, or resist for double fame at the risk of losing the town for the run
c: Town: comply, resist, or negotiate, each opening a different show type

name: The Scam Booking
head: There is no venue
a: Town: arrive to find no venue; improvise a show where only Commons score, or take the failure
b: Town: arrive to find no venue; improvise where only Commons score, or oversell beyond your deck for a larger prize
c: Town: arrive to find no venue, and choose which restriction the improvised show runs under

name: Town size score requirements
head: Small towns, big cities
a: Town size sets the score requirement, with small towns cheap and cities dear
b: Town size sets both the requirement and the reward, scaling together
c: Town size sets the requirement, and you choose the size you play when you arrive

name: Add all cards to map
head: Every card is somewhere on the map
a: Every card in the game appears somewhere on the map as a collectible node
b: Every card appears on the map, and cards you already own appear as upgrades instead
c: Every card appears on the map, but only those you have unlocked are visible

name: Booster Tag
head: The next pack is twice the pack
a: Consumable: the next pack holds double the cards and double the choices
b: Consumable: the next pack holds double the cards, but you still keep the same number
c: Consumable: the next three packs each hold one extra card and one extra choice

name: Disaster card packs
head: A pack of disasters to pick from
a: Disaster packs appear on the map as a choosable option
b: Disaster packs appear on the map; taking one pays fame up front and adds hazards later
c: Disaster packs appear as an option, and refusing one raises the next town's goal

name: Fame gates pack rarity
head: Fame raises the odds
a: Accumulated fame raises a run-wide luck value that gates stamp, skill and type rolls in rewards
b: Accumulated fame raises reward rarity odds directly, with no separate luck value
c: Accumulated fame raises the luck value, and meeting a goal with a placement whose margin is larger than the goal raises it further for one reward

name: Kitty Printer
head: All rewards become one kind. **Level 2, on its own mark:** If it ends the show on its mark, you choose the kind of the next reward
a: Every skip reward becomes the same named kind
b: Every skip reward becomes a kind you choose at run start
c: Every skip reward becomes the kind you have taken least this run

name: Red Card
head: Paid for what you turn down. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each line through its cell also pays its skip bonus into whichever of its grid's buckets is lowest
a: Gains a permanent bonus every time you skip a reward
b: Gains a permanent bonus every time you skip a reward or a map node
c: Gains a permanent bonus per skip, and skipping also reveals what you passed up

name: Ten-in-One pack
head: Ten cheap acts in one
a: Pack: ten Common cards
b: Pack: ten Common cards, of which you keep five
c: Pack: ten Common cards, and any duplicate among them upgrades instead

name: The Boss Trade
head: A large reward you have to give something up for
a: After each boss you are offered a large permanent effect that replaces one you already carry
b: After each boss you are offered a large permanent effect at the cost of a permanent restriction of your choice
c: After each boss you are offered three large permanent effects and must take one, drawbacks included

name: The Carousel
head: A shared draft you physically move through
a: At intervals a ring of cards turns one step per show; you take the card in front of you when you choose to stop it
b: At intervals a ring of cards is offered; the wider the margin of the placement that met your last goal, the more steps you may turn it before taking one
c: At intervals a ring of cards is offered, each carrying an attached stamp, and you take the pair together

name: The New Act
head: A preview of something not unlocked yet
a: A mechanic you have not unlocked appears for one show as a preview
b: A mechanic you have not unlocked appears for one show, and completing that show unlocks it early
c: An unlocked-elsewhere mechanic appears for one show, chosen from what you are closest to unlocking

name: The Showbag
head: A cheap bag with one thing you wanted
a: Consumable pack: four random Commons, one of them guaranteed to be a Concessions card
b: Consumable pack: four random Commons, one of them guaranteed to be a class you name
c: Consumable pack: four random Commons; you keep two and the rest are discarded

name: Antique poster / benefit show
head: A show played for one card
a: Map event: all of a show's proceeds go to one card of your choice, buffing it massively
b: Map event: all of a show's proceeds go to one card, buffing it by the margin of the placement that met the goal, as a fraction of the goal
c: Map event: all proceeds go to one card, and that card cannot be destroyed for the rest of the run

name: Fantasyland
head: A strong result changes how the next show is dealt
a: A strong enough hand in a named line means the next show deals ten cards into the Entrance instead of five — **level 2:** The strong hand may be in any line through its cell, not only the named one
b: A strong enough hand in a named line means the next show starts with one card of your choice already placed on the mark it matches best — **level 2:** The strong hand may be in any line through its cell, not only the named one
c: A strong enough hand means the next show deals ten cards into the Entrance, and staying in it requires repeating the feat — **level 2:** The hand needed is one hand-type lower while it sits on its mark

name: Gym node (Zurkhaneh)
head: A gym with a code of honour
a: Map node: permanently +1 rank to one card, but only if that card has never destroyed another
b: Map node: permanently +1 rank to one card, with no condition
c: Map node: permanently +1 rank to one card that has never destroyed another, or +2 if it has never been covered either

name: Head of state attends
head: Someone important is watching
a: Passing this show permanently raises the fame floor for the rest of the run
b: Passing this show permanently raises the fame floor; failing it lowers the ceiling
c: Passing this show raises the fame floor, and the raise is larger the wider the margin of the placement that meets the goal

name: Meal call (cookhouse flag)
head: A rest between regions
a: Once per region, a rest tick clears one debuff from every card
b: Once per region, a rest tick clears all debuffs from one card of your choice
c: Once per region, a rest tick clears one debuff per card, or two if you skip the region's next reward

name: Panem et circenses free show
head: Play for free, earn goodwill
a: Give a free show: no card reward, a large fame gain and increased town loyalty
b: Give a free show: no card reward, a large fame gain, and the town's next pack holds an extra card
c: Give a free show: no card reward and a large fame gain; loyalty earned this way can be spent to skip a later hazard

name: Reward fast/lean wins
head: Winning lean is worth something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Each card sitting on a mark it matches in a line through its cell counts as one card fewer for the lean count
a: Meeting the goal with Entrance refills to spare pays a step per unused refill
b: Meeting the goal with cards still in the stocks buffs one card of each stock that still holds five
c: Both, and doing both pays a further step

name: The Fire (venue loss)
head: The venue burns down
a: Map event: lose a venue mid-tour, choosing between an insurance payout and a rebuild
b: Map event: lose a venue mid-tour; the insurance payout is fame and the rebuild is a permanent bonus
c: Map event: lose a venue mid-tour, and whichever you choose defines the character of the next few towns

name: The friendly grapple (Glíma)
head: A bout with nothing on it
a: Map node: test a card against a boss's stats with nothing at stake
b: Map node: test a card against a boss with nothing at stake, and learn one of the boss's hidden rules
c: Map node: a no-stakes bout that, if won, lowers that boss's goal when you meet it for real

name: The Lantern Roast
head: The town laughs at your failures
a: Map event: the town satirises your run's failures; accept for fame or take offence for a fight
b: Map event: the town satirises your failures, and the fame paid scales with how badly the run has gone
c: Map event: the town satirises your failures; accepting pays fame and permanently marks one card as the butt of the joke

name: The Pie Car
head: Rest, or gamble
a: Rest node: heal one debuff, or gamble at a rigged game for a small chance at a large win
b: Rest node: heal one debuff, or gamble the heal itself for a chance at healing everything
c: Rest node: heal one debuff, or gamble at a rigged game you may cheat at if you hold the right card

name: The Rest Stop
head: Rest, or improve
a: Between shows you choose exactly one of two: restore the run resource you are short of, or permanently upgrade one card
b: Between shows you choose one of three: restore, upgrade one card, or remove one card
c: Between shows you choose one of two, and each show you choose the same one makes it cheaper and the other dearer

name: Biome tour structure
head: A tour with gates in it
a: The run is split into biomes that change map generation, with a fame gate roughly every ten shows
b: The run is split into biomes that change map generation, with a fame gate at each biome boundary
c: The run is split into biomes you pick the order of before the tour starts, each with its own fame gate

name: Endless bookings
head: The contracts get absurd
a: In endless mode, each repeat's booking terms become more extreme
b: In endless mode, each repeat adds one clause to the booking, stacking
c: In endless mode, each repeat's booking is drawn from progressively harsher pools, and you may reject one per lap

name: Endless lap reversal
head: The tour turns around and goes back
a: Finishing a lap reverses the tour end to start on the same map, with goals scaling per lap
b: Finishing a lap reverses the tour, and every town you already played is harder the second time
c: Finishing a lap reverses the tour, and the towns you skipped the first time are the only ones available

name: Residency mode
head: Stay in one city and let it change
a: Endless mode: stay in one city that evolves each show instead of circling the map
b: Endless mode: stay in one city that evolves, and every fifth show it changes character entirely
c: Endless mode: stay in one city, and each show you choose which of its aspects escalates

name: The Joke
head: Overshoot far enough and skip ahead
a: A placement that meets the goal by a margin larger than the goal itself jumps you forward several towns
b: A placement that meets the goal by a margin larger than the goal itself jumps you forward one town
c: A placement that meets the goal by a margin larger than the goal itself lets you choose between jumping ahead or taking the reward twice

name: Hype Poster
head: Consumable: doubles the next show's fame requirement, in exchange for its rewards scaling up two tiers
a: Consumable: the next show's goal doubles and its rewards scale up two tiers
b: Consumable: the next show's goal rises 50% and its rewards scale up one tier
c: Consumable: you set the next show's goal multiplier yourself, and the rewards scale with whatever you set

name: The Standing Wager
head: The stake carries between shows
a: A stake raised in one show carries into the next at the same level unless you skip that show's reward to lower it
b: A stake raised in one show carries into the next and rises again automatically each show you clear
c: A stake raised in one show resets at the next, but clearing it banks a permanent reward

name: The Understated Bill
head: Promise less, and be paid for the surprise
a: Consumable: lower the show's target; the lowered target is what counts as a win, but the show runs on until the original is met, and every line scored between the two pays a step extra
b: Consumable: lower the show target and the payout together, and bank the difference as a permanent reward
c: Consumable: lower this show's target, and the next show's target absorbs what you took off

name: The Banked Act
head: Set score aside instead of taking it
a: Consumable: bank one placement payout instead of scoring it; it pays out in the next show at one and a half times
b: Consumable: bank one placement's payout instead of scoring it; release it whenever you choose, into the bucket you name at that moment, and it grows a step for each show it waits
c: Consumable: bank one placement payout; it pays out at run end at triple, and is lost if the run ends badly

name: The Deficit
head: Falling short follows you
a: A show cleared by less than a tenth of its target starts the next show with that gap added to the target
b: A show cleared by a narrow margin raises the next target, and a show cleared by a wide one lowers it
c: A show cleared narrowly raises the next target, and clearing that one anyway pays a bonus

name: The Griot
head: Carries a fifth of this show's score into the next show. **Level 2, on its own mark:** If it ends the show on its mark, the carry may be split between two buckets
a: Carries a fifth of this show's final score into the next show, paid into the bucket you name when the next show's marks are dealt
b: Carries a fifth of this show's final score into the next show's row bucket
c: Carries a fifth into the bucket you name, and a bucket that receives the carry two shows running pays it double

name: The Open Ledger
head: One line that never resets. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The kept total pays when the line completes, made hand or not ⚑ *pair review: a line has no running total until it completes, and the grid is emptied at show end*
a: The line this card sits in keeps its running total between shows rather than resetting
b: The line this card sits in keeps its total between shows, and the total is paid out in full the first time the line completes as a made hand
c: The line this card sits in keeps its total between shows, halving at each boundary

name: Monster
head: Future copies start stronger. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A step gained on its mark also pays at once into the special bucket
a: Gains a step each time it scores; every future copy starts with the steps this one ended its run with
b: As (a), across runs on the same profile
c: As (a), and this card loses a step for each copy that has gained one

name: Per-card personal bests
head: The card remembers its own record. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A record beaten by a line through its cell pays the margin into the special bucket
a: Personal bests are recorded on the card itself for this run, and beating one scores a bonus
b: Personal bests are recorded on the card for this run, and beating one permanently raises that card's floor for the rest of the run
c: Personal bests are recorded per card for this run, and a card that beats its record three times is dealt its own mark every show thereafter

name: The Belt
head: Exactly one card in the save file holds this stamp at a time; it scores double, and a challenge boss can take it and it must be won back
a: Exactly one card in the save file carries this stamp; it scores double, and a challenge boss can take it and must be beaten to win it back — **level 2:** No challenge boss can take it while it sits on its mark
b: Exactly one card in the save file carries this stamp; it scores double and can be moved to another card between runs — **level 2:** Its double reaches every card in a line through its cell
c: Exactly one card in the save file carries this stamp; it scores double and its bonus grows with every run it survives — **level 2:** Its double reaches every card in a line through its cell

name: The Long Memory
head: A card that remembers what it did
a: This card records the highest-scoring line it was ever part of, and scores a fraction of that total every show thereafter — **level 2:** Its recorded fraction pays twice while it sits on its mark
b: This card records the highest-scoring line it was part of this run, and matching that line again scores it double — **level 2:** Any line through its cell may match the record, not only the same line
c: Each time it scores, it pays +1 step per distinct hand type it has ever been part of — **level 2:** A hand type new to it, scored through its cell, adds that step to the special bucket too

name: Biome/route meta-unlocks
head: More world, unlocked over time
a: Meta progress unlocks additional biomes and lengthens the possible route
b: Meta progress unlocks additional biomes; route length is fixed and you choose which biomes fill it
c: Meta progress unlocks additional biomes, and each biome unlocked adds one card to the global pool

name: Card unlock tracks
head: Two ways to unlock things
a: Specific in-game actions unlock specific cards, while a separate threshold track unlocks commons through generic progress
b: Every unlock runs off one generic progress track, with no action-specific unlocks
c: Specific actions unlock specific cards; the generic track unlocks commons, and rarer cards need archetype-specific play

name: Lore scraps unlock
head: Scraps of a story you unlock
a: Wins and specific actions unlock lore scraps
b: Wins and specific actions unlock lore scraps, and completing a set unlocks a card
c: Wins unlock lore scraps that each name a condition for the next one, forming a chain

name: Route-length achievements
head: Distance travelled counts for something
a: Achievements for total map distance walked across all runs
b: Achievements for total distance walked, each unlocking a card
c: Total distance walked feeds a permanent bonus rather than discrete achievements

name: Speedrun endless categories
head: Endless mode has categories
a: Endless rulesets ship as named speedrun categories with per-category personal bests
b: Endless rulesets ship as named categories, and each has its own unlock track
c: Endless rulesets ship as named categories you can combine, with records kept per combination

name: The Exile (daily challenge)
head: A fixed board, once a day
a: A hard fixed layout offered as a daily challenge
b: A hard fixed layout as a daily challenge, with a shared leaderboard seed
c: A hard fixed layout as a daily challenge, and beating it grants a card for the next normal run

name: The Standing Ovation
head: Doing something well adds it to the pool
a: The first time you score any hand type above a threshold, a card matching that hand type is added to the run pool permanently
b: The first time you score any hand type above a threshold, that hand type levels up permanently for the run
c: The first time you score a hand type above a threshold, a card matching it is added to the pool, and beating the threshold again raises it

name: The Academy
head: A school that upgrades a card
a: Meta building: permanently upgrades one Common card per season into its Rare version
b: Meta building: permanently upgrades one card per season by one rarity tier, whatever it starts at
c: Meta building: upgrades one card per season, and the card chosen is unavailable for that run

name: The Prestige Layer
head: Reset the run to make the next one faster
a: You may end a run early to convert its score into a permanent multiplier on every future run
b: You may end a run early for a permanent multiplier, and the multiplier scales with how far you got
c: You may end a run early for a permanent multiplier, and each reset makes the next reset worth more

name: The School (social circus)
head: Turns junk into trained cards
a: Between runs, converts discarded and junk cards into trained Commons
b: Between runs, converts junk cards into trained Commons, one per run
c: Between runs, converts junk into trained Commons, and the conversion rate improves the more junk you feed it

name: Diamond Stake
head: The tour is longer
a: Difficulty: the run must go further before it can be won
b: Difficulty: the run must go further, and the extra towns are all bosses
c: Difficulty: the run must go further, and you choose how much further for a proportional reward

name: Glass Stake
head: Cards shatter as they score
a: Difficulty: a small proportion of cards shatter when they score
b: Difficulty: a small proportion shatter when they score, and a shattered card pays its rank into the bucket of the line that shattered it
c: Difficulty: a small proportion shatter when they score, rising as the tour goes on

name: Horizon Stake
head: The deck keeps growing
a: Difficulty: a random card is added to the deck at each show's start
b: Difficulty: a random card is added at each show's start, and you may remove one by skipping a reward
c: Difficulty: a random card is added each show, chosen from cards you have already rejected

name: Platinum Stake
head: Fewer shows per tier
a: Difficulty: the small shows are removed, leaving fewer chances to earn per tier
b: Difficulty: the small shows are removed, and the remaining ones pay more
c: Difficulty: one show per tier is removed, and you choose which

name: Purple Stake
head: The goal climbs faster
a: The score needed scales up faster with each town
b: The score needed scales up faster, and the reward scales with it
c: The score needed scales faster, and you may skip a reward to flatten the curve for one town

name: Dynasty save bonus
head: A bonus for finishing again
a: A standing bonus for consecutive finished tours in one save file
b: A standing bonus for consecutive finished tours, reset by any failed run
c: A standing bonus per finished tour, which never resets but grows more slowly each time

name: Seasonal crown
head: A title held until someone takes it
a: A per-season champion title carried between runs until beaten
b: A per-season champion title that grants a standing bonus while held
c: A per-season title that grants a bonus while held, and the bonus grows the longer you hold it

name: The Ghost Show
head: Only findable at the right hour
a: A secret card findable only in the menu after real-world midnight
b: A secret card findable only at a specific real-world hour, differing per profile
c: A secret card findable only under a real-world condition the game never states

name: The One-Night-Only
head: Usable once, ever
a: Consumable: an effect of enormous size that can be used once per profile and is then gone from every future run
b: Consumable: an effect of enormous size usable once per profile, which returns after a run is won without it
c: Consumable: an effect of enormous size usable once per profile, which is replaced by a weaker permanent version afterward

name: The Rope Trick
head: Only real once the rumour is true
a: Exists only in rumour and can never be drawn until a hidden condition makes it real
b: Exists only in rumour until a hidden condition makes it real, at which point it is added to every future run
c: Exists only in rumour; each run raises the chance it becomes real, and it stays real once it does

name: The Signature Trick
head: A card each profile can only learn once
a: The first run in which this card scores above a threshold, it is added to the profile permanently and cannot be earned again
b: The first run in which this card scores above a threshold, it is added to the profile permanently, and each later run may swap it for a different one
c: This card may be placed in exactly one run per profile, and choosing it locks out the other cards of its class for that profile

name: Four-in-a-row mini-mode
head: After the game Connect 4: four in a row
a: A Connect-4 minigame mode played with placed cards
b: A Connect-4 side objective running alongside normal play, paying a bonus for four of a suit in a line
c: A Connect-4 minigame where the town places against you on the same grid

name: Cups and balls minigame
head: Find the ball
a: A three-card shuffle minigame available at events
b: A three-card shuffle minigame at events, where guessing right upgrades the card you find
c: A three-card shuffle minigame whose difficulty rises each time you win it, with the reward rising too

name: Fishing minigame card
head: Fish a card out of the deck
a: Cue: fish a card out of the deck with a fishing minigame — **level 2:** The catch goes into the Entrance slot you choose
b: Cue: fish a card out of the deck; the harder the fish, the better the card — **level 2:** The catch goes into the Entrance slot you choose
c: Cue: fish a card out of the deck, with one attempt per show and a chance of losing this card instead — **level 2:** On its mark this card is never lost

name: Forbidden-solitaire event mode
head: Click cards straight into hand
a: Event mode: clicking a card sends it to a side pile rather than the grid
b: Event mode: clicking a card sends it to a side pile, scored as a single poker hand at End
c: Event mode: clicking a card sends it to a side pile, and you may return one per placement to the board

name: Karuta duel
head: First to spot it
a: A speed-pick minigame where the first correct click takes the reward
b: A speed-pick minigame where each correct click is worth more than the last
c: A speed-pick minigame where a wrong click costs you the show

name: Metro map mode
head: After the game Mini Metro: straights become lines on a map
a: The ends of straights become stations joined by their straight, and must serve passengers over a number of Entrance refills
b: The ends of straights become stations; each new straight extends the network, and the network's size is the score
c: The ends of straights become stations that must be connected into a single network before the show ends

name: The Arcade
head: A node full of small games
a: Map node: play solitaire-variant minigames for rewards
b: Map node: play solitaire-variant minigames for rewards, with harder variants paying more
c: Map node: play a minigame chosen from three, each tied to a different reward type

name: The Box Theater
head: A show inside the card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its miniature line also pays into the special bucket
a: Cue: play a miniature five-cell line inside this card from the next Entrance cards, scoring it separately
b: Cue: play a miniature five-cell line inside this card; its result is added to whichever line scores next
c: Cue: play a miniature line inside this card using the whole Entrance at once; it scores into the bucket of the line this card sits in

name: Collect number cards to progress
head: Collect the numbers, then face the faces
a: Win by collecting every number card, which unlocks a final stage against the face cards
b: Win by collecting every number card of one suit, then facing that suit's face cards
c: Win by collecting every number card; face cards cannot be scored until you have

name: Dispute settled by performance
head: Settled by performance, not points
a: Show variant: a town dispute is settled by performance rather than by score
b: Show variant: a town dispute is settled by which side scores the more varied board, not the higher one
c: Show variant: a dispute is settled by matching a formation the town names, not by score at all

name: Fork Solitaire
head: The board branches and you play both. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may fork twice
a: At a chosen moment the board forks into two states; you play both and keep the higher score
b: At a chosen moment the board forks; you play both and keep the SUM of the two
c: The board forks and you play both, but any card destroyed in either branch is destroyed in both

name: Hard cap on flush win-con plays
head: Win by a flush, but only so often
a: Alternate win: a single flush wins the show, with a hard cap on how many flushes a run may ever play
b: Alternate win: a single flush wins, and the cap falls by one each time you use it
c: Alternate win: a flush wins the show; the second time it must be a straight flush, and the third a flush five

name: Judged-category scoring
head: Graded in categories, not totals
a: Show: row, column and special are each graded against their own goal instead of one product
b: Show: row, column and special are graded separately, and you must pass two of the three
c: Show: row, column and special are graded separately, and only your weakest bucket counts

name: The Balance
head: Final-tier boss: cannot be beaten by score; win by ending the show with row total and column total within 10% of each other
a: Final boss: score cannot beat it; win by ending the show with the row total and the column total within 10% of each other
b: Final boss: win by ending the show with the row and column totals within 10% of each other, while still meeting a reduced goal
c: Final boss: score alone cannot beat it; win by ending the show with the row, column and special totals all within 10% of each other, while still meeting a reduced goal

name: The Demolition Show
head: Score by destroying, not by playing
a: Show: discarding scores points per card discarded from the board, and normal play scores nothing
b: Show: discarding scores points per card discarded from the board, alongside normal scoring
c: Show: discarding scores per card discarded from the board, and the goal is a count of cards rather than a score

name: The Exploration Show
head: No goal, just things to find
a: Show: no score goal at all, only hidden bonuses to find in a pre-built board
b: Show: no score goal, only hidden bonuses, and a limited number of placements to find them
c: Show: no score goal; the reward is whatever you uncover, and leaving early keeps what you have

name: The Faire
head: The audience performs and you judge
a: Show: the town performs and your cards judge them, for easy fame
b: Show: the town performs and your cards judge them; judging harshly pays more but costs fame
c: Show: the town performs, and you score by predicting which of their acts will score highest

name: The Fall
head: Win by dropping, not by climbing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A drop that ends on a mark the card matches counts one level more
a: Alternate win: one removal drops a stack of three or more cards by a level
b: Alternate win: a card that reached height five ends the show on the floor
c: Alternate win: end a show having dropped more total height than you built

name: The Last Line
head: One cell must never be reached
a: Alternate loss: a named cell must stay empty; covering it ends the show at once
b: Alternate loss: a named cell must stay empty, and each Entrance refill it survives empty pays a step into the special bucket
c: Alternate loss: a named cell must stay empty, and after each refill it moves to the uncovered mark with the most lines through it

name: The Long Count
head: Win on the board's state, not on your own ⚑ *pair review: depends on Q0303 (The Dome) entering: sealed cells exist nowhere else*
a: Alternate win: the show is won the moment a set number of sealed cells exist anywhere, whoever made them
b: Alternate win: the show is won when a set number of sealed cells exist, and hazards that seal cells count toward it
c: Alternate win: the show is won when every row holds at least one sealed cell

name: The Cursed Ring card
head: After The Lord of the Rings' One Ring: destroy it and you win
a: You always know exactly where this card is, and permanently destroying it wins the show — **level 2:** While it sits on its mark you may destroy it with a cue
b: You always know where it is, and destroying it wins the show, but only in the final show — **level 2:** While it sits on its mark you may destroy it with a cue
c: You always know where it is; destroying it wins the show, and it can only be destroyed while it sits on a mark it matches — **level 2:** A cue destroys it

name: Festival mini-contest node
head: Win any one of three
a: Map node: win any one of three mini-contests - score, formation or speed - for the prize
b: Map node: win any one of three mini-contests; winning two takes a larger prize
c: Map node: three mini-contests, and you must declare which one you are attempting before seeing your deck

name: Mini-game score-free events
head: Some shows are not about score
a: Some encounters replace the score goal with a puzzle objective, such as triggering five times
