b: Some encounters offer both a score goal and a puzzle objective, and either wins
c: Some encounters replace the score goal with a puzzle objective drawn from a pool, revealed only on arrival

name: The Masked Audience / One-on-One
head: Fame hidden around the board
a: Show: fame sources are hidden around the board to be found rather than scored
b: Show: fame is hidden around the board, and a single audience token pays outsized fame if performed to alone
c: Show: fame is hidden around the board, and each one found reveals a hint to the next

name: The String Figure
head: Copy the pattern
a: Copy a displayed board pattern with your own cards for a bonus
b: Copy a displayed board pattern for a bonus, with a larger pattern shown each time you succeed
c: Copy a displayed board pattern, or invent one the town must copy back

name: The Water Torture Cell
head: Three locks, one escape. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One lock opens the moment it lands on its mark
a: Arrives locked under three conditions - covered, column unscored, unmoved - one opening per placement, in order; a full escape pays a large bonus
b: Arrives locked under three conditions that open in any order: its row completes, its column completes, and a card hits a mark in a line through its cell; a full escape pays a hand into the special bucket
c: Arrives locked under three conditions; each one you break pays a bonus, and breaking all three pays a much larger one

name: Turning the tip
head: A hidden objective revealed after the fact
a: Convert an audience faction into fame, with a hidden bonus objective revealed only once the show is cleared
b: Convert an audience faction into fame, with the bonus objective stated up front
c: Convert an audience faction into fame; the hidden objective is revealed after the show, and completing it later pays out retroactively

name: Guessing-game hidden target card
head: After the game Wordle: find the cell it is thinking of. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The distance of any empty cell is shown before you place, not after
a: A hidden target cell is chosen among the empty cells at each Entrance refill; each placement reports wrong, close (adjacent) or exact, and a card that hits the target cell's mark pays its match bonus three times
b: As (a), reporting only wrong or exact
c: As (a), and each placement reports its distance in cells, so the target narrows visibly

name: Quest-chain triggered stage acts
head: A story told in the right order
a: A quest chain where each stage unlocks only after the previous one's effect has been triggered
b: A quest chain where stages may be completed in any order, but completing them in sequence pays a bonus
c: A quest chain where each stage names the next only once the previous is done

name: The Metal Chain
head: A sequence that must be consumed in order. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card of the chain placed on a matched cell may be scored out of order
a: A named chain of ranks may only be scored in strict ascending order, and skipping one locks the rest
b: A named chain must be scored in order, and completing the whole chain pays enormously
c: The chain is the ranks of the marks along one row you name at show start, read left to right; cards of those ranks must be scored in that order, and finishing the row's chain pays a hand into the special bucket

name: The Three Tricks
head: This card earns its next stage. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its current objective may be completed by any card in a line through its cell, not only by this card
a: This card carries a chain of three objectives; completing one upgrades the card and reveals the next
b: This card carries a chain of three objectives, all visible; completing all three transforms it into a different card entirely
c: This card carries a chain of three objectives; completing one upgrades the card, and failing to finish the chain by show end resets it

name: The Three-Act Bill
head: Each objective is unlocked by the last
a: Three objectives are given in order; each becomes visible and claimable only once the one before it is done, and the third pays permanently for the run
b: Three objectives are given in order; each pays as it is completed, and the third pays permanently for the run
c: Three objectives are given in order, all visible from the start, and only the third pays anything

name: Built-in symmetric PvP mode
head: Same deck, same cards, higher score ⚑ *pair review: a duel needs an opponent, and a solitaire has none*
a: PvP: both players start with the same deck and draw the same cards, aiming for the higher score
b: PvP: both players share a deck and alternate taking cards from one Entrance
c: PvP: both players use the same deck and card order, and each sees the other's board as it builds

name: Crew formation battle / class legalization
head: Crew against crew
a: A formation battle against a rival crew, decided by whose formation scores higher
b: A formation battle against a rival crew, alternating one formation each until someone cannot answer
c: A formation battle against a rival crew; winning makes an outlaw class legal in that town for the rest of the run

name: Head To Head
head: Your line is matched against theirs, position by position
a: In a rival show, your line is compared to theirs card by card from one end, and the winner of each pairing scores
b: In a rival show, your whole line's total is compared to theirs, not card by card
c: In a rival show, your line is compared card by card, and a card that beats its opposite carries the surplus to the next pairing

name: One-upmanship duel (scissors dance)
head: Alternating melds until someone falls short ⚑ *pair review: a duel needs an opponent, and a solitaire has none*
a: Duel: you and a rival alternate melds, each having to beat the last; the first to fall short loses a card of their deck
b: Duel: you and a rival alternate melds; falling short costs one card rather than the whole wager
c: Duel: alternating melds, each having to beat the last, and you stake a card of your deck before seeing your opening board

name: The Eating Contest
head: An eating contest
a: A sanctioned outing where consuming cards race a rival to eat the town's offering fastest
b: An eating contest where the winner keeps everything eaten and the loser keeps nothing
c: An eating contest where you wager how much your card will eat before it starts

name: The Laughing Duel
head: Break the rhythm and you lose ⚑ *pair review: a duel needs an opponent, and a solitaire has none*
a: A pattern-matching duel against a town where breaking rhythm loses the show
b: A pattern-matching duel where each show's pattern is longer than the last
c: A pattern-matching duel where you set the pattern and the town must follow, alternating who leads

name: The Showdown
head: Same town, against a rival
a: Play the same town against a rival's score; the winner takes both crowds
b: Play the same town against a rival's score; the winner takes both crowds and one of the loser's cards
c: Play the same town against a rival, seeing their board as it builds

name: The Tent Challenge
head: Called out by name
a: A town champion calls out one of your cards for a duel: win for fame, lose a rank
b: A town champion calls out one of your cards; you may substitute another, which loses a rank
c: A town champion calls out your highest card for a duel, and refusing costs fame

name: The Apprenticeship
head: A quest the card sets itself. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Progress made on matched cells counts twice
a: Names an objective when acquired, drawn from a pool; finishing it makes this card's level 2 permanent, mark or no mark
b: Names an objective when acquired; finishing it lets you choose one of three permanent rewards
c: Names a new objective each time the previous one is finished, escalating, with a permanent reward each time

name: The Commission
head: The town sets you a task
a: Each town states one objective; completing it during that show grants a permanent run-scoped effect
b: Each town states one objective; completing it grants fame rather than a permanent effect
c: Each town states one objective, and you may accept it for a permanent reward or decline it for a smaller immediate one

name: The Long Game
head: An objective that spans the whole tour. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line through its cell that advances the objective also pays a step per point of progress so far
a: Names one objective at run start that can only be finished late in the tour, and pays enormously when it is
b: Names one objective at run start with a partial reward at each town you make progress in
c: Names one objective for the whole tour, and abandoning it at any point converts the progress made into fame

name: The Standing Order
head: Attaches a quest to any card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may swap its objective while the wearer sits on its mark
a: Attach an objective to any card you own; completing it permanently upgrades that card
b: Attach an objective to any card; completing it permanently upgrades that card and destroys this stamp
c: Attach an objective to any card; completing it upgrades that card, and the stamp then moves to a card of your choosing

name: Overshoot
head: Progress past the target is not wasted
a: Progress past an objective's target carries into the next objective
b: Progress past an objective's target is converted to fame
c: Progress past the target raises the reward rather than carrying forward

name: The Progress Report
head: Reading progress costs something
a: Cue: reveal the exact progress of one hidden objective, at the cost of discarding one Entrance card — **level 2:** The cue costs nothing
b: Cue: reveal the exact progress of every hidden objective, once per show — **level 2:** It also names the property each objective wants next
c: Cue: reveal one hidden objective's progress for free, but doing so raises what it requires — **level 2:** Revealing raises nothing

name: The Silent Tally
head: Progress you cannot see until it matters ⚑ *pair review: how quest progress is shown is interface; you rejected a UI-only effect at Q0038*
a: Quest progress is hidden until it passes halfway, then shown for the rest of the run
b: Quest progress is hidden entirely, and only completion is announced
c: Quest progress is hidden, and may be read once per show at the cost of discarding one Entrance card

name: The Tally Board
head: How a quest shows its progress ⚑ *pair review: how quest progress is shown is interface; you rejected a UI-only effect at Q0038*
a: Every active objective shows its exact progress at all times
b: Every active objective shows only whether it is close, not how close
c: Objectives show exact progress, but only while you are not in the middle of a placement

name: The Open Secret
head: Hidden objectives exist and are findable
a: A pool of hidden objectives is live every run; completing one reveals it and pays permanently
b: A pool of hidden objectives is live, and completing one reveals it permanently for all future runs
c: Hidden objectives are live, and any you complete stay hidden until the run ends

name: The Retroactive Clause
head: Pays for what you already did. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Landing on its own mark, it checks again and pays any objective met since
a: When acquired, checks what you have already done this run and immediately pays out any objective already met
b: When acquired, names an objective and counts progress made before you had it
c: When acquired, pays out for the single most impressive thing you have already done this run

name: The Sealed Brief
head: You can see how far along you are, but not what you are doing ⚑ *pair review: how quest progress is shown is interface; you rejected a UI-only effect at Q0038*
a: A hidden quest shows its progress bar from the start but never says what it is for until it completes
b: A hidden quest shows its progress bar, and one word of its text is revealed at each quarter
c: A hidden quest shows nothing at all, and completing it reveals both the quest and its reward at once

name: The Conflicting Notes
head: Two briefs that contradict each other
a: Two quests are offered whose conditions cannot both hold; progress on one erases progress on the other
b: Two contradictory quests are offered; progress on both is kept, but only the first completed pays
c: Two contradictory quests are offered, and abandoning one outright doubles the reward of the other

name: The Rival Contract
head: A quest a rival is also chasing
a: An objective is shared with a rival show; whoever finishes it first takes the reward
b: An objective is shared with a rival, and you can see how far along they are
c: An objective is shared with a rival; finishing second still pays, at a fraction

name: The Ultimatum
head: Take the quest or take the payout. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Landing on its own mark, the reward you declined is offered once more
a: Offers an immediate reward or an objective worth several times more; taking one removes the other
b: Offers an immediate reward or an objective; you may take the reward and still attempt the objective at a penalty
c: Offers an immediate reward or an objective, and the objective's value rises the longer you leave it unclaimed

name: Maximized
head: Only two ranks exist. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which of the two ranks each card counts as
a: Every face card counts as the same rank and every number card as the same rank
b: Every card counts as one of two ranks, chosen when this skill activates
c: Every card counts as one of two ranks, and which two changes each show

name: Pareidolia
head: Everything is a face card
a: Every card counts as a face card for every effect — **level 2:** A card on a mark it matches also counts, for melds, as the face rank you name
b: Every card counts as a face card, and face cards count as no rank at all for runs — **level 2:** Cards sitting on marks they match also keep their own rank for runs
c: Every card counts as whichever card type an effect is looking for — **level 2:** A card on a mark it matches also counts, for melds, as the face rank you name

name: The Backward-Backward
head: Cue: reverse one stack top to bottom. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may reverse any stack in a line through its cell
a: Cue once per show: reverse one stack top to bottom, so its bottom card is spotlit and the old top is buried
b: Cue once per Entrance refill: reverse one stack top to bottom
c: Cue once per show: reverse one stack top to bottom, and every card in it pays its match bonus again

name: The Blank
head: This card has no rank or suit: it can stack on anything and anything can stack on it, but it never melds and scores 0. It counts as matching every rank mark. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On a rank mark, it takes the mark's rank and suit, melds, and its lines score
a: Has no rank and no suit: anything stacks on it and it stacks on anything, but it never melds and scores 0. It counts as matching every rank mark
b: Has no rank and no suit for stacking, but counts as whatever the line needs when a meld is checked
c: Has no rank and no suit, and any line containing it scores as if it had four cards instead of five

name: Wild rank (copycat/understudy)
head: Copies whatever it can find. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Every card in a line through its cell counts as rank-matched
a: Rank 0 that also counts as any rank already present in your deck, for stacking and melds; behaves as blank with nothing to copy
b: Rank 0 that counts as any rank present on the board, updating as the board changes
c: Rank 0 that counts as the rank most common among the uncovered marks on its grid, changing as marks are covered

name: Gentleman juggling
head: Plain cards become juggling balls
a: Skill-less cards in this card's row count as the Balls suit — **level 2:** It reaches its column as well as its row
b: Skill-less cards anywhere on this card's grid count as the Balls suit — **level 2:** Skill-less cards on matched cells count as Balls and as their own suit
c: Skill-less cards in this card's row count as whichever suit this card is — **level 2:** It reaches its column as well as its row

name: The Colourblind Rule
head: Suits are compared by the way their prop travels. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on suit marks they match count as both paths
a: Suits are compared by their prop's path, along the row (Hoops, Knives) or along the column (Balls, Fire, Fireworks), so a flush needs only five of one path
b: Suits are compared by their prop's path for stacking, and by suit for melds
c: Suits are compared by their prop's path, and a five-card flush that is also one suit scores an extra step

name: The Rewritten Noun
head: Changes what a card counts AS, globally. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The marks are rewritten as well as the cards
a: Cue: name a suit and a second suit; for the rest of the show every card of the first counts as the second
b: Cue: name a rank and a second rank; for the rest of the show every card of the first counts as the second
c: Cue: name two values of one property - two suits, two ranks, two hats or two talents - and swap them across the whole board for the rest of the show

name: The Unsuited
head: A card that belongs to nothing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may take any suit you choose instead of none, once per show
a: This card counts as no suit at all: it breaks any flush it is part of, and nothing may be stacked on it by suit
b: This card counts as no suit, but its line ignores it entirely when working out the hand, scoring the other four
c: This card counts as no suit and cannot be targeted by any effect that names a suit

name: 31/99-style fixed point values
head: Odd values, aiming at a total
a: Ranks carry fixed odd values - ace 1 or 11, ten worth -10, King worth 99 - and lines score toward a target total
b: Ranks carry fixed odd values, and a line scores only if it lands exactly on the target total
c: Ranks carry fixed odd values you can see before placing, and overshooting the target scores nothing

name: Freakshow off-rank cards
head: No normal number. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Once per line, a line through its cell may count it as the rank the line needs
a: Freakshow cards carry no ordinary rank number and cannot be compared numerically
b: Freakshow cards carry no ordinary rank, but count as whatever their neighbours need for a run
c: Freakshow cards carry a rank outside the normal range, high or low, that no meld can include

name: Half-Step
head: This card has rank N and a half, letting it stack legally between rank N and N+1 in runs, but it never participates in poker melds
a: This card's rank is N and a half: it stacks legally between N and N+1, but never counts in a poker meld — **level 2:** It counts in poker melds too, as N
b: This card's rank is N and a half: it stacks between N and N+1, and shows down for melds — **level 2:** It may count as N+1 for melds as well
c: This card counts as either N or N+1 for any single check, chosen fresh each time — **level 2:** It may count as N-1 as well

name: Misrule show
head: Ranks upside down
a: Show: all ranks are reversed, 2 counting high and King counting low; winning pays large tips
b: Show: all ranks are reversed for one placement of your choosing, not the whole show
c: Show: all ranks are reversed, and you are told which placement it will happen in one placement ahead

name: The Spin (whirling)
head: Its rank turns; the change touches its lines, so a complete line through it re-scores at every placement. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may stop or restart its cycle whenever you choose
a: Cycles its rank by one each placement, wrapping from King back to 1
b: Cycles its rank by one each placement, and you may stop the cycle once per show
c: Cycles its rank each placement, but its lines re-score only when the new rank improves their hand

name: 5 starting suits
head: Five suits, not four
a: Fireworks join the standard suit roll, so every deck deals five suits, and a line holding all five scores as its own meld, the Rainbow — **level 2:** A line through a matched fifth-suit cell holding four suits counts as holding all five
b: Fireworks appear only on cards this skill creates, one per Entrance refill, into the slot you choose — **level 2:** A card this skill creates goes to the Entrance slot you choose
c: As (a), and the Rainbow counts as a flush for every effect that names one — **level 2:** A line through a matched fifth-suit cell holding four suits counts as holding all five

name: Harlequin
head: Counts as both printed suits for melds and stacking, and matches a mark of either. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: Fires both suits' props
b: Fires the prop of the suit its mark shows
c: Fires the prop of the suit its mark shows, twice

name: Ten-suit challenge deck
head: Ten suits. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on suit marks they match count as two suits ⚑ *pair review: a numeric reskin of Q1349, ten suits for five; only (c) is its own idea*
a: Ten suits instead of four, making flushes far harder and suit variety far easier
b: Ten suits, and any five distinct suits in a line counts as its own meld
c: Ten suits, of which five are active each show, so the roster changes

name: The Best Bower
head: This card counts as every suit for flush evaluation (but not for suit-stacking rules), and its prop identity is randomly one of the game's props each time. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On a suit match you choose which prop it fires
a: Counts as every suit for flush evaluation but not for stacking, and its prop is a random one of the game's props each time
b: Counts as every suit for both flushes and stacking, and fires no prop of its own
c: Counts as every suit for flushes, and fires the prop of whichever suit is most common on its grid

name: Rock Paper Scissors
head: Rock, paper, scissors. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On a suit match it wins every throw
a: At game start becomes rock, paper or scissors; stacking on another such card requires winning the throw, with ties broken by rank
b: At game start becomes rock, paper or scissors; stacking on another such card requires winning the throw, and a stack won on rank as well as on the throw pays a step
c: It re-rolls its throw every time it is placed, so its stacking legality changes each time

name: The Circle Of Suits
head: Suits beat each other in a ring. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack may run the ring either way
a: Suits form a ring in which each may be stacked on the next and on no other
b: Suits form a ring for stacking, and a line running the ring in order scores as a made hand of its own
c: Suits form a ring for stacking, and the ring rotates one step each placement

name: The Rank Wheel
head: High and low fold into each other ⚑ *pair review: straights already wrap through the Ace; only the stacking half is new*
a: Rank comparison is circular - the top rank is beaten by the bottom one, and every straight may wrap — **level 2:** Its stack may run the wheel either way
b: Rank comparison is circular for stacking legality but not for melds — **level 2:** Its stack may run the wheel either way
c: Rank comparison is circular, and a wrapped straight scores an extra step for having wrapped — **level 2:** Every straight through its cell scores as if it had wrapped

name: The Standoff
head: Three cards that cannot be ordered
a: While this card is spotlit, its line is compared as a ring: no card in it is highest, and the line scores as its best three-card hand instead — **level 2:** Its line scores as its best three-card hand or its full hand, whichever is higher
b: While this card is spotlit, comparisons in its line are non-transitive, and any effect that names the highest card in the line fails — **level 2:** An effect naming the highest card in its line names the card you choose instead
c: While this card is spotlit, comparisons in its line are non-transitive, and every card in it counts as beating exactly one other — **level 2:** You choose which card each beats

name: Clever Hans
head: Counts as a copy of its highest orthogonally-adjacent neighbor's rank; with no neighbors, its rank is 1. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On a side with no neighbour it reads that cell's uncovered mark instead, so it copies the plan as well as the board
a: This card's rank equals its highest orthogonally adjacent neighbour's rank, or 1 with no neighbours
b: This card's rank equals its lowest orthogonally adjacent neighbour's rank, or 1 with no neighbours
c: This card's rank and suit both copy whichever neighbour was placed most recently

name: Hanafuda Reskin
head: When a town outlaws a suit, all your cards of that suit count as the suit of the adjacent card for that show
a: When a town outlaws a suit, your cards of that suit count as their adjacent card's suit for the show — **level 2:** It also covers a suit a hazard disables
b: When a town outlaws a suit, your cards of that suit count as a suit of your choice for the show — **level 2:** It also covers a suit a hazard disables
c: Your cards always count as the suit of whichever orthogonal neighbour was placed most recently — **level 2:** It may copy from any orthogonal neighbour, not only the most recent

name: The Majority Rule
head: The board decides what a card is
a: A card with no card adjacent to it takes the suit that is most common on its grid — **level 2:** You may choose the second most common suit instead
b: Every card takes the suit that is most common in its own row, overriding its printed suit — **level 2:** You may choose the second most common suit instead
c: A card surrounded on all four sides by one suit becomes that suit permanently — **level 2:** Three sides suffice

name: The Turk
head: Borrows the rank underneath
a: This card's rank is the rank of the card directly beneath it in its stack, or 0 with nothing beneath — **level 2:** It may borrow from any card beneath it, your choice
b: This card's rank is the summed rank of everything beneath it in its stack, capped at 13 — **level 2:** Its sum wraps past the deck's highest rank back to 1, so the sum lands where you steer it
c: This card's rank is the rank of the card beneath it, and it also inherits that card's suit — **level 2:** It inherits the stamp beneath it too

name: The Wildcard
head: Becomes whatever its row already has. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may copy from any line through its cell, not only its row
a: On every board change, becomes a copy of a rank and suit already present in its row
b: On every board change, becomes a copy of whichever rank and suit is most common in its row
c: On every board change, becomes whichever rank and suit would score its row highest

name: The Abacus
head: Adds its neighbours together. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts diagonal neighbours too
a: This card's rank is the sum of its orthogonal neighbours' ranks, capped at the deck's highest rank
b: This card's rank is the sum of its orthogonal neighbours' ranks, uncapped
c: This card's rank is the sum of its neighbours' ranks minus its own printed rank

name: The Doubling Act
head: Twice the number, once the card
a: This card's rank counts as double its printed value for every check — **level 2:** Its rank triples instead of doubling
b: This card's rank counts as double for melds only, and normal for stacking — **level 2:** Its rank triples instead of doubling
c: This card's rank doubles each time it scores, until it exceeds the deck's highest rank and wraps to 1 — **level 2:** You choose whether it doubles when it scores

name: The Gap Card
head: Its rank is what separates its neighbours. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may compare as the gap or as its printed rank, whichever helps ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0080, which you wrote: the gap between the highest and lowest ranks in a line*
a: This card compares as the difference between the ranks of the cards on either side of it in its row
b: This card compares as the difference between the highest and lowest ranks in its row
c: This card compares as the difference between its printed rank and the rank of the card below it in the stack

name: The Halving
head: Splits the number in two
a: This card's rank counts as half its printed value, rounded down, for every check — **level 2:** You choose, per check, half or full
b: This card's rank counts as half for melds and full for stacking — **level 2:** The half it loses in melds goes to a neighbour you choose
c: This card's rank counts as half, and the other half is given to the adjacent card of lowest rank — **level 2:** You choose which neighbour receives the other half

name: The Bust
head: A line no better than High Card, or scoring nothing under a rule, is a bust, and feeds the next one
a: When a line busts, this card banks the summed ranks of its five cards and adds them as flat points to the next line that scores better than High Card — **level 2:** A bust through its cell banks double
b: When a line busts, the next line to score better than High Card scores double — **level 2:** Triple, when the bust ran through its cell
c: When a line busts, its five cards return to the Entrance — **level 2:** The returned cards go to the Entrance slots you choose

name: The Dropped Bit
head: A line that never finished is still worth something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One incomplete line through its cell that is one card short scores at End as a full hand, its uncovered mark standing in
a: At show end, every incomplete line pays a step per card it did hold
b: At show end, every incomplete line pays a step per card it holds into its own bucket, row, column or special, doubled for lines one card short
c: At show end, only the single closest incomplete line pays, and it pays as if it had completed with a blank

name: The Empty House
head: Failure is the axis; a line no better than High Card is a bust; a line no better than High Card is a bust
a: The show's combo counts lines that bust rather than lines that score better — **level 2:** Busts through its cell count twice
b: The show's combo counts both, so a mixed placement pays most — **level 2:** Busts through its cell count twice
c: A placement in which every line busts pays a large flat bonus — **level 2:** The flat bonus doubles when one of the busts runs through its cell

name: The Safety Net
head: Turns a bust, a line no better than High Card, into something. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A bust through its cell pays its highest rank twice
a: A line that busts instead pays flat points equal to its highest rank
b: A line that busts instead pays flat points and clears itself, freeing the cells
c: A line that busts may be re-formed once, and pays double if it scores the second time

name: The Silent Row
head: Paid for the line you deliberately never close
a: This card scores a step per Entrance refill for each line through it that remains incomplete, and loses the lot when one completes — **level 2:** When a line through its cell completes, the bank is paid into that line's bucket instead of lost
b: This card scores a step per Entrance refill for each incomplete line through it, and keeps what it banked when one completes — **level 2:** The bank is paid into the bucket of the line that completed, now
c: This card scores a step per Entrance refill for each incomplete line on the whole grid — **level 2:** Incomplete lines through matched cells count twice

name: The Cut List
head: Rewards cards for staying in. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, every card still in the stock of its Entrance slot at End gains the bonus twice
a: Any card that goes a whole show without being placed gains +1 rank permanently
b: Any card that goes a whole show without being placed gains a permanent bonus, lost the moment it is placed
c: Any card that goes three consecutive shows unplaced upgrades a rarity tier

name: The Standby
head: A card that is paid for waiting in the wings. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays double when it is finally placed on its mark
a: This card scores a step for every placement it spends in the Entrance, paid when it is placed
b: As (a), doubled if it is the last of its five placed
c: As (a); if the show ends with it still in the Entrance it upgrades permanently instead

name: Understaffed
head: The unplayed are counted against you
a: Cards left in the Entrance at show end each subtract from the final score — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, cards left in the Entrance subtract nothing
b: Cards left in the Entrance at show end are destroyed — **level 2:** While it sits on its own mark, you choose one of them to spare
c: Cards left in the Entrance at show end are carried into the next show's Entrance — **level 2:** The carried cards may be placed before the new ones

name: One Card Short
head: The hand you almost had
a: When a line completes, this card also pays for the best hand that line was one card away from — **level 2:** Lines through its cell count as two cards away, not one
b: When a line completes one card short of a better hand, this card pays the difference between the two — **level 2:** Lines through its cell count as two cards away, not one
c: When a line completes one card short of a better hand, this card pays as if it had reached it, once per Entrance refill — **level 2:** No per-refill limit for lines through its cell

name: The Glancing Blow
head: A prop that misses is worth more. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own props that miss are relaunched at double
a: Every prop that finishes its path without hitting anything scores a bonus
b: Every prop that misses scores a bonus, and this card gains a permanent bonus for each
c: Every prop that misses is re-launched once from the opposite edge

name: The Narrow Loss
head: Coming close to the target is not nothing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A show that ends while it sits on its own mark counts as within a tenth if it is within a fifth
a: A show that ends within a tenth of its target is not lost; it is replayed once with the board as it stood
b: A show that ends within a tenth of its target is still lost, but the run keeps the rewards
c: A show that ends within a tenth of its target is lost, and the shortfall becomes a permanent bonus to the next attempt

name: Leave No Trace
head: An empty board is the goal
a: Ending a show with no card but this one on the board pays an enormous bonus — **level 2:** One other card may remain, when it sits on its own mark
b: Ending a show with no card but this one on the board pays a bonus scaling with how many cards passed through it — **level 2:** One other card may remain, when it sits on its own mark
c: Ending a show with fewer than five cards placed pays a bonus scaling inversely with the count — **level 2:** Its own placement does not count

name: Room To Work
head: A card that wants space around it
a: This card scores a step for every empty cell orthogonally adjacent to it, checked when its line scores — **level 2:** It counts diagonal empties too
b: This card scores a step for every empty cell in its 3x3, checked when its line scores — **level 2:** It counts its row's and column's empties too
c: This card scores a step for every empty cell adjacent to it, and loses a step for every occupied one — **level 2:** It counts diagonal empties too

name: The Bare Stage
head: Paid for the cells you did not fill ⚑ *pair review: (c) needed a second grid*
a: Scores a bonus per empty cell on its grid when the show ends — **level 2:** Empty cells in lines through its cell count twice
b: Scores a bonus per empty cell in its own row and column — **level 2:** It counts the empty cells in its diagonals too
c: Scores a bonus per empty cell on its grid, paid at every refill instead of at show end — **level 2:** Empty cells in lines through its cell count twice

name: The Dead End
head: Cutting the board off has a cost. **Level 2, on its own mark:** While it sits on its own mark, cells in its lines are never destroyed ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you, and on a plain board every empty cell accepts any card, so it needs a legality rule to fire*
a: Any empty cell that no Entrance card can legally be placed in when the Entrance refills is destroyed and counts against the show
b: Any empty cell no Entrance card can legally reach at a refill is destroyed, but pays a small consolation
c: Any empty cell no Entrance card can legally reach at a refill is sealed rather than destroyed, and sealing enough cells triggers a bonus

name: The Gap
head: The empty cells are the thing you move. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A gap in its lines may be filled by any card
a: Cue: move a card into any empty cell whose left-hand neighbour is one rank below it; the gap moves to where the card was
b: As (a), and a gap at the start of a row takes any card
c: As (a); a gap no card can legally fill is sealed for the show and pays a step at End

name: The Reserved Seat
head: A cell you promise to leave alone
a: Consumable: name an empty cell; if it is still empty at End it pays its mark's rank once for every line through it that stayed incomplete, into the special bucket; if it was filled it pays nothing
b: As (a), and nothing may be placed there for the rest of the show
c: Name up to three empty cells; each pays as (a), and each filled one costs its mark's rank

name: The Reserved Space
head: Spends emptiness to finish lines to finish lines
a: Cue: seal exactly three empty cells for the show; every line whose only empty cell is one you sealed scores now, its mark standing in, and a sealed cell accepts nothing after — **level 2:** Sealed cells in its lines reopen at the next refill
b: Cue: seal three empty cells; every line whose only empty cell is sealed scores now, its mark standing in, and the cells reopen at the next refill — **level 2:** A sealed cell whose mark matches an Entrance card scores its line twice
c: Cue: seal any number of empty cells; every line whose only empty cell is sealed scores now at half, its mark standing in — **level 2:** A sealed cell whose mark matches an Entrance card scores its line twice

name: The Dead Air
head: A scoreless refill widens the Entrance. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A refill counts as scoreless when only its own lines scored nothing
a: An Entrance refill whose five placements completed no line widens the Entrance by one slot for the next refill
b: As (a), and the extra slot stays for the show; consecutive scoreless refills add one each
c: As (a), the slot staying for the show, and the extra slot's card pays no match bonus

name: The Patient Crowd
head: Silence is not always failure
a: When an Entrance refill's placements score nothing, one of its cards is shuffled back into the deck rather than spent — **level 2:** The card shuffled back goes on top of the stock you choose
b: When a refill scores nothing, one of its cards is shuffled back into the deck, but the show's goal rises a step — **level 2:** The card shuffled back goes on top of the stock you choose
c: The first scoreless refill of each show is free; every one after discards an extra card from the deck — **level 2:** The extra card discarded comes from the stock you choose

name: The Quiet House
head: A card that improves by being on stage for nothing
a: This card is permanently upgraded at the end of any Entrance refill in which no line completed anywhere — **level 2:** It upgrades twice
b: This card is permanently upgraded at the end of any Entrance refill in which its own line did not complete — **level 2:** It upgrades twice
c: This card is upgraded for the show after any scoreless refill, and the upgrades are made permanent if the show is won — **level 2:** The upgrades are permanent even if the show is lost

name: The Rebuilding Act
head: A scoreless refill is spent rebuilding instead
a: An Entrance refill that completes no line is followed by a free rebuilding phase - every card on the board may be moved once, at no cost — **level 2:** A card may be moved twice
b: An Entrance refill that completes no line is followed by a rebuilding phase in which up to three cards may be moved — **level 2:** Four cards may be moved
c: An Entrance refill that completes no line is followed by a rebuilding phase in which cards may be moved freely, and one card is discarded from the deck for it — **level 2:** The discard is waived

name: The Slow Burn
head: Banks the refills you wasted. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The bank pays out at double on the next line through its cell
a: Each scoreless Entrance refill banks a multiplier that is paid out on the next line that scores
b: Each scoreless refill banks a multiplier, paid out at show end whether or not anything scores after
c: Each scoreless refill banks a multiplier, and the bank is lost if two scoring refills pass without spending it

name: The Honk
head: No mechanical consequence at all. **Level 2:** none beyond the flat mult a match pays ⚑ *pair review: you rejected a UI-only effect at Q0038*
a: Cue for a noise and nothing else, unlimited uses, with no effect on play whatsoever
b: Cue for a noise; every fifth honk in a show pays a token bonus
c: Cue for a noise, and honking in the exact placement a line completes pays a hidden bonus

name: The House Band
head: Changes the show, not the score. **Level 2:** none beyond the flat mult a match pays ⚑ *pair review: you rejected a UI-only effect at Q0038*
a: While on the board, the music and background change, with no mechanical effect
b: While on the board, the music and background change, and the change signals which hazard is coming
c: While on the board, the presentation changes and the change is different per class of card that scored last

name: Chalk Dust
head: The mark pays twice for the card wearing it
a: Every property this card matches pays double — **level 2:** Every property matched in its lines pays double too
b: The first property this card matches each show pays double — **level 2:** The first two properties matched each show pay double
c: Every property this card matches pays double, but a miss on any property destroys this stamp — **level 2:** On a hat match, the properties it misses no longer destroy the stamp

name: Hitting It Cold
head: The first one is the one that counts. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The first match of every Entrance refill pays triple too
a: The first mark you match each show pays triple
b: The first mark you match each show pays triple, and every later match that show pays nothing extra
c: The first mark you match in each grid pays triple

name: The Double Take
head: One card, two marks. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It is compared against the diagonal neighbours' marks too
a: Cue when placed: this card is also compared against the uncovered marks of the four cells beside it; a neighbour's match holds while that cell stays empty
b: Cue when placed: this card is also compared against the uncovered mark of the cell one row up
c: Cue when placed: this card is also compared against any one uncovered mark you choose in its row

name: The Perfectionist
head: All four, or nothing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One missed property still counts as a full match
a: Pays a large mult when this card matches every property its mark prints, and nothing at all otherwise
b: Pays a large mult when this card matches every property its mark prints, and its ordinary bonuses otherwise
c: Pays a growing mult for each consecutive full match you land this show

name: The Rank Outsider
head: Its number is whatever the plan asked for. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays the rank bonus of both its printed rank and the mark's
a: This card counts as the rank of whatever mark it is placed on, for matching and for melding alike
b: This card counts as the rank of whatever mark it is placed on, for matching only - its meld rank is unchanged
c: This card counts as the rank of whatever mark it is placed on, and permanently becomes that rank

name: The Standing Ovation
head: Matching feeds the multiplier. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Matches in the cells beside it count double
a: Each property matched anywhere on the board this show adds to this card's mult, permanently
b: Each property matched in this card's own lines adds to its mult for the rest of the show
c: Each FULL match anywhere on the board adds to this card's mult, permanently

name: The Suit Case
head: A suit that carries its own permission. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The wearer's suit effect fires twice
a: The wearer's suit effect fires whether or not its mark agrees on suit
b: The wearer's suit effect fires whether or not its mark agrees, at half strength
c: The wearer's suit effect fires on ANY match, not only a suit match

name: The Understudy
head: Pays for being second best
a: When this card is placed on a mark it does NOT match, it still pays the rank bonus of whatever the mark wanted — **level 2:** Cards in its lines placed on marks they miss also pay that mark's rank bonus
b: When this card is placed on a mark it does not match, it pays half the rank bonus the mark wanted — **level 2:** Cards in its lines that miss pay the full rank bonus
c: When this card is placed on a mark it does not match, it pays the talent mult the mark wanted instead of the rank bonus — **level 2:** Cards in its lines that miss pay that talent mult too

name: The Amplifier
head: A mark that doubles the line. **Level 2, on its own mark:** When the wearer itself sits on its own mark, the doubling reaches the lines through the cells beside it too
a: As a mark: every line through this cell adds +2 to its bonus mult for as long as any card sits on it
b: As a mark: +2 while any card sits on it, +3 while a matching one does
c: As a mark: the first line through this cell each show adds +2 to its bonus mult

name: The Chorus Line
head: Marks that perform in concert
a: When two cards hit marks in the same line within one Entrance refill, both match bonuses pay again — **level 2:** The pair may lie in any line through its cell
b: When three do, all three pay again, and the line, if complete, scores again — **level 2:** The three may lie in any line through its cell
c: As (a), and each further hit in that line that refill grows the bonus a step — **level 2:** The pair may lie in any line through its cell

name: The Contract
head: A promise the board holds you to
a: As a mark: if this cell is still unmatched when you press End, the show scores nothing — **level 2:** If this card itself matches the mark, the show's score is doubled as well
b: As a mark: if this cell is still unmatched when you press End, the show's score is halved — **level 2:** If this card itself matches the mark, the show's score is doubled as well
c: As a mark: if this cell IS matched by the time you press End, the show's score is doubled — **level 2:** The doubling is banked the moment it matches, so an early End keeps it

name: The Reserved Cell
head: A mark nothing can cover
a: As a mark: no card may be placed on this cell until every other cell of its row and column holds a card — **level 2:** A card that matches the mark may be placed before the grid fills
b: As a mark: no card may be placed on this cell unless it matches the mark — **level 2:** When a matching card fills it, every complete line through the cell scores again
c: As a mark: no card may be placed on this cell until a line through it is otherwise complete — **level 2:** A matching card may be placed before the line completes, and the line it completes scores again

name: The Springboard
head: A mark that throws whatever lands on it
a: As a mark: the card placed on this cell scores as if it were one rank higher — **level 2:** If this card itself lands on the mark, it scores two ranks higher
b: As a mark: the card placed on this cell scores as if it were one rank higher, and two higher if it matched — **level 2:** Three ranks higher, and the rise lasts the show
c: As a mark: the card placed on this cell is moved one row up after scoring, stacking if that cell is occupied — **level 2:** If this card itself lands on the mark, it scores two ranks higher

name: The Stand-In
head: The mark performs instead of the card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The wearer's skill fires at level 2
a: As a mark: when any card covers this cell, the wearer's skill fires as though the wearer had been placed there
b: As a mark: when a MATCHING card covers this cell, the wearer's skill fires as though the wearer had been placed there
c: As a mark: when any card covers this cell, the wearer's skill fires and the mark is spent

name: The Trapdoor
head: A mark that takes what you give it ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (c) only cost you; it reads as a hazard*
a: As a mark: the first card placed on this cell is discarded instead, and the mark remains — **level 2:** This card itself is never trapped; a card the trapdoor takes while it sits on its mark goes to the Entrance slot you choose
b: As a mark: the first card placed on this cell is returned to the Entrance instead, and the mark remains — **level 2:** This card itself is never trapped; a card the trapdoor takes while it sits on its mark goes to the Entrance slot you choose
c: As a mark: a card placed on this cell that does not match it is discarded instead — **level 2:** A card the trapdoor discarded comes back at the next refill while this card sits on its mark

name: The Casting Call
head: Reads the board before you play it
a: Consumable: name a rank; every uncovered mark of that rank counts as matching any suit this show
b: Consumable: name a rank; every mark of that rank pays double when matched this show
c: Consumable: name a rank; every mark of that rank is re-dealt to a card of your choosing

name: The Dead Spot
head: Finds the plan's worst cell: the uncovered mark that shares neither rank nor suit with any other mark in its lines
a: Cue: names the cell whose mark contributes least to any line, and pays for covering it with anything — **level 2:** It names and pays for two cells
b: Cue: names the cell whose mark contributes least, and destroys that mark — **level 2:** It destroys two marks
c: Cue: names the cell whose mark contributes least, and re-deals it — **level 2:** It re-deals two cells

name: The Reader
head: Pays for lines the plan already made. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell pay the extra twice
a: When a line completes, pays extra if the marks under it would have made the same hand type
b: When a line completes, pays extra if the marks under it would have made ANY scoring hand
c: When a line completes, pays extra if the marks under it would have made a BETTER hand than you did

name: The Route Book
head: Scores for what the plan asked for, not for what you did
a: At show end, pays for every property of the plan still uncovered: the marks you never overwrote — **level 2:** Uncovered marks in its lines count twice
b: At show end, pays for every property of the plan you DID match — **level 2:** Properties matched in its own lines count twice
c: At show end, pays for every property of the plan you did NOT match — **level 2:** Properties left unmatched in its lines count twice

name: The Typecast
head: Rewards hitting a plan that repeats itself. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Such a match in its lines also re-scores that line
a: Gains a permanent mult each time a mark sharing its suit is matched
b: Gains a permanent mult each time a mark that is an exact copy of this card is matched
c: Gains a mult each show for the largest number of matched marks that share one suit

name: The Booking
head: Marks itself onto the board
a: At show start, this card's own mark is placed on a cell you choose instead of a random one — **level 2:** Landing on its own mark, it is marked onto two cells next show
b: At show start, this card is marked onto three cells instead of one — **level 2:** Landing on its own mark, you choose the three cells next show
c: At show start, this card's mark is placed on the cell that already has the most lines through it — **level 2:** Landing on its own mark, you choose the cell its mark is dealt to next show

name: The Cancelled Date
head: Destroys the plan for profit. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Twice per refill
a: Cue once per Entrance refill: destroy any unmatched mark and gain flat points equal to its rank
b: Cue once per Entrance refill: destroy any unmatched mark and gain a permanent mult
c: Cue once per Entrance refill: destroy every unmatched mark in one line and gain a large one-off score

name: The Rewrite
head: Redraws one cell of the plan
a: Consumable: re-deal the mark of any one cell from the deck
b: Consumable: re-deal the marks of any one line from the deck
c: Consumable: set the mark of any one empty cell to a card of your choosing from the deck

name: The Rolling Call
head: The plan grows as you play. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose the cell the new mark goes to
a: Every time you match a mark, one uncovered mark of your choice is re-dealt from the deck
b: Every time you match a mark, the NEXT card in the Entrance is marked onto an empty cell
c: Every time you fail to match, one uncovered mark of your choice is re-dealt from the deck

name: The Standing Set
head: The plan outlives the show. **Level 2, on its own mark:** At End, you choose which marks stand into the next show
a: The plan is not re-dealt between shows; the same marks stand until they are matched
b: Marks you matched stay matched across shows and pay a smaller bonus each time
c: The plan is re-dealt each show, but any mark you covered but never matched is dealt again to the same cell

name: The Swap
head: Two marks change places
a: Consumable: exchange the marks of any two empty cells
b: Consumable: exchange the marks of any two cells, covered or not
c: Consumable: exchange the marks of any two cells in the same line, and it is not spent the first time

name: The Colour Match
head: Near enough, for a suit
a: A card matches a mark's suit if both suits travel the same way: Hoops and Knives cross the row; Balls, Fire and Fireworks travel the column — **level 2:** Its own suit matches every suit mark
b: A card always matches a mark's suit, and every suit effect fires at half strength — **level 2:** Its own suit effect fires at full strength
c: A card matches a mark's suit if either card carries no talent — **level 2:** Its own suit matches every suit mark

name: The Loose Blocking
head: The mark does not have to be underneath
a: A card matches the mark of any cell orthogonally adjacent to the one it is placed in, if its own is unmatched — **level 2:** Its own card may match any mark in its row
b: A card also matches the uncovered marks of the cells beside it, on suit only — **level 2:** Its own card may match any mark in its row
c: A card matches the mark of any cell in its own line, once per line per show — **level 2:** Its own card matches in every line through it, with no once-per-line limit

name: The Near Enough
head: One step off still counts
a: A rank one away from the mark's rank counts as a rank match, at half the bonus — **level 2:** The cards beside it match one rank away at the full bonus
b: A rank one away from the mark's rank counts as a full rank match — **level 2:** The cards beside it match two ranks away
c: A rank one away counts, and a rank two away counts at half — **level 2:** The cards beside it match two ranks away at full

name: The Quick Change
head: Wears whatever the mark is wearing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On a mark that truly wears this hat, it counts as matching one more property you name
a: This card counts as matching the rank of any mark it is placed on
b: This card counts as matching the rank and suit of any mark it is placed on
c: This card counts as matching whichever single property you name when you place it, other than the hat

name: The Dark Cell
head: A cell the plan lost
a: A cell whose mark has been destroyed or withheld by an effect pays double for the card placed there, since nothing is planned for it — **level 2:** Dark cells in its lines pay triple
b: A cell whose mark has been destroyed or withheld by an effect scores nothing for the card placed there — **level 2:** Dark cells in its lines score normally
c: A cell whose mark has been destroyed or withheld takes the mark of the cell that scored most this show — **level 2:** You choose which mark a dark cell in its lines takes

name: The Empty House
head: Pays for the plan you ignored ⚑ *pair review: a mark never covered is an empty cell, which is Q1396*
a: At show end, pays a large amount for every mark that was never covered and whose card was never drawn — **level 2:** Such marks in its lines pay double
b: At show end, pays a large amount for every mark that was covered but never matched — **level 2:** Marks covered but never matched in its lines pay double
c: At show end, pays for every mark whose card left it again — **level 2:** Such marks in its lines pay double

name: The Missed Cue
head: Grows on failure
a: Gains a mult for the show for each card placed on a mark it matches nothing of; the next hit spends it into that hit's lines and resets it — **level 2:** Misses in its own lines count double
b: Gains a permanent mult every time a mark is destroyed unmatched — **level 2:** Marks destroyed in its lines count double
c: Gains a permanent mult for each show that ends with more than half the plan unmatched — **level 2:** Its own lines' unmatched marks count double toward the half

name: The Guest Director
head: Someone else blocks the show
a: Level: one line of the grid is marked by the level instead of by your deck
b: Level: half the grid is marked by the level instead of by your deck, in a scattered pattern
c: Level: the whole grid is marked by the level and your deck marks nothing

name: The House Deck
head: Marks of cards you have never owned
a: Level: the marks are drawn from a fixed house deck rather than from yours, and matching them still pays normally
b: Level: the marks are drawn from a house deck, and matching one adds that card to your deck for the run
c: Level: the marks are drawn from a house deck one rank above anything you own

name: The Rewritten Bill
head: The plan changes under you
a: Level: every fifth placement, one unmatched mark is re-dealt somewhere else
b: Level: every fifth placement, one unmatched mark is re-dealt to a different card
c: Level: every placement, the two lowest-value unmatched marks swap cells

name: The Bad Notice
head: Marks you are punished for hitting
a: Level: some cells carry a marked card that scores NEGATIVE when matched, shown before you commit
b: Level: some cells carry a mark that scores nothing when matched and pays double when deliberately missed
c: Level: some cells carry a mark that, when matched, disables that card's own effect for the show

name: The Fading Chalk
head: The plan expires
a: Level: a mark that has not been matched within a fixed number of placements disappears
b: Level: a mark that has not been matched within a fixed number of placements becomes a hazard cell
c: Level: the whole plan fades one cell at a time, oldest first, from the show's midpoint

name: The Poisoned Plan
head: The plan carries a status
a: Level: every mark of one named suit Exhausts, until the next Entrance refill, whatever covers it
b: Level: every mark Exhausts, until the next Entrance refill, a card that covers it without matching
c: Level: one cell's mark applies a status of the level's choosing, and it is visible

name: The Rent Book
head: The plan costs to use
a: Level: matching a mark sends the top card of the stock you drew from to the discard, and a card placed on a mark it matches may be placed as unmatched
b: Level: matching a mark sends the top card of every stock to the discard
c: Level: the first match each show is free; every later one discards the top card of the stock you drew from

name: The Understudy Riot
head: Ignore the plan and it acts on its own
a: Level: any cell whose mark you cover with a non-matching card places that mark's card onto the grid for you, somewhere else
b: Level: any mark still unmatched at show end is placed onto the board and scores against you
c: Level: covering a mark with a non-matching card discards the top card of the stock you drew from

name: The Kind House
head: The level hands you a good board
a: Level: the plan is dealt so that at least one line already forms a scoring hand if fully matched
b: Level: the plan is dealt so that every line forms at least a pair if fully matched
c: Level: the plan is dealt from your best cards rather than at random

name: The Open Rehearsal
head: The plan is negotiable
a: Level: before the first placement, you may re-deal any three cells of the plan
b: Level: before the first placement, you may swap any two marks, twice
c: Level: once per show you may re-deal one cell of the plan, at any time

name: The Solved Row
head: Part of the plan comes already done
a: Level: one line of the grid starts with its cards already placed and already matched
b: Level: one line starts with its cards already placed but unmatched, so you may improve on it
c: Level: one cell starts already matched, chosen at random

name: The Standing Invitation
head: Matching is worth more here
a: Level: every property matched pays double for the whole show
b: Level: every FULL match pays double for the whole show
c: Level: the mults from talent and hat matches are doubled, and flat rank bonuses are not

name: The Banned Number
head: Your own plan tells the level what to forbid
a: Level: the hand type the plan would most often make scores nothing this show
b: Level: the suit that appears most often in the plan scores nothing this show
c: Level: the rank that appears most often in the plan cannot be placed at all

name: The Critic
head: Judged against the plan rather than against a number
a: Level: the show is won by matching a stated fraction of the plan, and the score does not matter
b: Level: the show is won by beating what the plan would have scored, whatever that number is
c: Level: the show is won normally, but failing to match half the plan halves the reward

name: The Quoted Fee
head: The goal is set from your own plan
a: Level: the show's goal is a fraction of what the plan would score if every mark were matched
b: Level: the show's goal is set from what the plan's best single line would score
c: Level: the show's goal is fixed, but beating what the plan would have scored pays a bonus

name: The Typecaster
head: The plan decides what the level rewards
a: Level: whichever suit the plan carries most of pays double when matched
b: Level: whichever suit the plan carries LEAST of pays triple when matched
c: Level: the level names one property at show start and only that property pays

name: The Closed Rehearsal
head: A plan you cannot read
a: Level: every mark is face down and is revealed only when a card is placed on it
b: Level: every mark is face down and is revealed when a card is placed in an adjacent cell
c: Level: marks are face down until the first line scores, then all reveal at once

name: The Dark Grid
head: One board goes unplanned
a: Level: the marks are hidden until the first placement
b: Level: the marks are hidden until the Entrance is committed to the grid
c: Level: one grid's marks are shown only in the layer view, never on the board

name: The Fogged Plan
head: Reading it costs something
a: Level: the layer view may be opened a fixed number of times per show
b: Level: opening the layer view discards the top card of a stock
c: Level: the layer view shows only the lines through the last cell you placed in

name: The Partial Bill
head: Half the plan is legible
a: Level: a mark shows its rank but not its suit
b: Level: a mark shows its suit but not its rank
c: Level: a mark shows only whether it carries a talent or a hat, not which

name: The Cold Reading
head: A quest you are not told about
a: Objective: an unstated pattern of matches pays out when you happen to complete it
b: Objective: an unstated pattern, with a hint shown after the third match
c: Objective: an unstated pattern that is revealed the moment it becomes impossible

name: The Full House Call
head: A quest stated in marks
a: Objective: match every mark in any one line to win a permanent reward
b: Objective: match every mark in any one line, and the reward grows with the number of lines fully matched this show
c: Objective: match every mark in a row AND the column that crosses it

name: The Long Run
head: A quest across shows
a: Objective: match a stated number of marks across the whole run, counted between shows
b: Objective: match at least one mark in every show of the run
c: Objective: complete a show having matched every property at least once

name: The Understudy's Night
head: The boss condition is the plan
a: Boss: the show is beaten only by matching a stated fraction of the plan, whatever you score
b: Boss: the show is beaten normally, but every unmatched mark subtracts from the total
c: Boss: the show is beaten by matching every mark of one named property

name: Dress Code, as a mark
head: Ships in blinds.csv: some cells demand a named suit and refuse anything else. A mark already IS a cell asking for a suit
a: Keep it bespoke: a demanding cell stays its own rule, separate from marks
b: Fold it in: a demanding cell is a mark that REFUSES anything not matching its suit
c: Fold it in, and generalise: a mark may refuse on any one of its four properties, not only suit

name: Sight Unseen, as a mark
head: Ships in blinds.csv: every card is face down in the Entrance and only turns face up once placed. The plan is the mirror of this - the board is legible while the hand is not
a: Keep it bespoke: the Entrance blindfold has nothing to do with the plan
b: Pair them: the Entrance is blind AND the plan is fully visible, so the plan is the only information you have
c: Invert it: the Entrance is visible and the plan is blind

name: The Dye Vat, as a mark
head: Ships in blinds.csv: some cells convert whatever is placed on them to a named suit
a: Keep it bespoke: a converting cell stays its own rule
b: Fold it in: a converting cell is a mark that rewrites what covers it to its own suit
c: Fold it in, and generalise: a mark may rewrite any one property of what covers it

name: The Ranked Floor, as a mark
head: Ships in blinds.csv: scattered cells add or subtract from the rank of whatever is placed on them, shown before you commit
a: Keep it bespoke: a rank-shifting cell stays its own rule
b: Fold it in: the shift is the mark's own rank bonus, applied whether or not the card matches
c: Fold it in as the mirror: a mark you MISS applies its rank as a penalty instead of a bonus

name: The Sealed Envelope, as a mark
head: Ships in blinds.csv: one card starts face down somewhere in a grid and is revealed when a card is placed beside it
a: Keep it bespoke: the envelope stays a placed card, not a mark
b: Fold it in: the envelope is a face-down mark revealed by an adjacent placement
c: Fold it in, and pay for it: a face-down mark pays double when matched blind

name: The Understudy Fills In, as a mark
head: Ships in blinds.csv: any grid you place nothing into during a refill has a random card placed in it for you
a: Keep it bespoke: the random placement stays unrelated to the plan
b: Fold it in: the card placed for you is the one the plan marked for that cell
c: Fold it in: the card placed for you is the plan's mark, and it pays its match bonus twice

name: The Dead End
head: A rank nothing may cover. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The restriction does not apply to cards sitting on marks they match ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (c) only restrict you; it reads as a hazard*
a: Nothing may be stacked on a rank-1 card
b: Nothing may be stacked on a rank-1 card, and a rank-1 card pays double when its line scores
c: Nothing may be stacked on whichever card holds the highest rank on the board at the moment of placement

name: The Glued Run
head: Once joined, never parted ⚑ *pair review: only a restriction; it reads as a hazard*
a: Cards joined into an ordered run cannot be separated again, except the topmost card — **level 2:** A run through its cell may be split once
b: Cards joined into an ordered run cannot be separated again, and the run scores as one card of its top rank — **level 2:** A glued run through its cell scores as a made hand of its length
c: Cards joined into an ordered run cannot be separated for the rest of the Entrance refill — **level 2:** A run through its cell may be split once

name: The Golf Rule
head: One higher or one lower, any suit, wrapping, so a column can stack a straight
a: A card may be stacked on a card one rank above or one rank below it, any suit, and rank 1 wraps to rank 13 — **level 2:** A stack on a matched cell may also take a card two ranks away
b: A card may be stacked one rank above or below, any suit, and a stack pays its length into the special bucket at each refill in which no Entrance card could extend it — **level 2:** A stack on a matched cell may also take a card two ranks away
c: Each column names its own base card at show start, and only cards one rank above or below its current top may join it — **level 2:** A column whose base cell is matched may also take a card two ranks away

name: The Supermove
head: Move as many at once as you could have moved one by one. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match do not count toward the run's length ⚑ *pair review: only bounds a move Q0243 (The Packer) grants; alone it does nothing*
a: An ordered run moves as one unit only if its length is at most the number of empty cells on its grid plus one
b: An ordered run moves as one unit only if its length is at most the empty cells plus one, doubled for each empty column
c: An ordered run of any length moves as one unit, and each card beyond the empty-cell count costs one point

name: The Yukon Move
head: Move the whole pile from any card down, in order or not. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The moved stack may also land on any cell, occupied or not, whose mark its bottom card matches
a: Cue: move a stack from any card down as one unit, whatever order it is in, onto a card one rank above its bottom card
b: Cue: move a stack from any card down as one unit, whatever order it is in, onto any empty cell
c: Cue: move a stack from any card down as one unit, and every card in it that was out of order pays a point on landing

name: The Captives
head: The cards you need most start buried
a: Level: the four aces are dealt to the bottom of the Entrance stocks, and each one freed pays a bonus
b: Level: the four aces are dealt to the bottom of the Entrance stocks, and no line holding an ace scores until all four are on the board
c: Level: four cards named by the level are dealt to the bottom of the Entrance stocks, and freeing all four wins the show outright

name: The One-Use Pocket
head: A holding cell that works once. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The pocket reopens once when a card leaves it onto a mark it matches
a: One pocket beside the grid holds one card, and closes for the show once that card leaves it
b: One pocket beside the grid holds one card, which may leave it only into an empty cell; the pocket then closes for the show
c: Three pockets beside the grid each hold one card once per show, and a card leaving a pocket pays its rank

name: The Two-Suit Deck
head: A deck of only two suits, doubled
a: Cards are built from two suits only, each present twice over
b: Cards are built from one suit only, four times over
c: Cards are built from two suits only, and flushes pay half while straights pay double

name: The Cruel Redeal
head: Gather the board in order and lay it out again, unshuffled
a: Consumable: gather every grid card in reading order and re-deal them from the first cell, closing every gap; lines they complete score again
b: Consumable: gather every grid card in reading order and re-deal them column by column
c: Consumable: gather the Entrance stocks in order and re-deal them round-robin, unshuffled

name: The Flip-Three
head: Dig for the card beneath, at a cost. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Taking a lower card costs nothing: the cards above it stay put
a: Each Entrance slot shows the next two cards of its stock beneath the top one; only the top may be taken, and the two beneath are information
b: Each Entrance slot shows the next two cards of its stock beneath the top one; any of the three may be taken, and the cards above it go to the bottom of that stock
c: Each Entrance slot shows the next two cards of its stock beneath the top one; any of the three may be taken, and the cards above it are discarded

name: The Refill Gate
head: No new cards while a column stands empty
a: Level: the Entrance will not refill while any column of the committed grid is empty
b: Level: the Entrance will not refill while any column is empty, and the first card into an empty column pays a bonus
c: Level: the Entrance will not refill while any row or any column is empty

name: The Spider Deal
head: One card onto every column at once
a: Consumable: deal the top card of each stock into the lowest empty cell of the column below its slot; a full column is stacked on
b: Consumable: deal one card from the deck onto the lowest empty cell of the three leftmost columns; a full column is stacked on
c: Consumable: deal one card from the deck onto the lowest empty cell of every column, and any line it completes scores double

name: The Clock Face
head: Each column has a rank it must finish on
a: Level: each column is assigned a rank at show start; the column's line scores only while it holds a card of that rank
b: Level: each column is assigned a rank; a column holding its rank scores double, one without it half
c: Level: as (a), and the assignments rotate one column right at every refill

name: The Dealt Base
head: The rank a straight starts from is dealt at show start ⚑ *pair review: (b) only restricts you*
a: At show start one rank is dealt as the base, and a straight that wraps through the base pays its rank bonus again — **level 2:** A straight through its cell that starts on the base pays double
b: At show start one rank is dealt as the base, and only a card of the rank below it may be the first card into an empty column — **level 2:** A straight through its cell that starts on the base pays double
c: At show start one rank is dealt as the base, and a straight that starts on the base pays double — **level 2:** Any straight through its cell counts as starting on the base

name: The Osmosis Rule
head: A rank may enter a row only if the row above already holds it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own row places and scores freely ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (b) only restrict you; it reads as a hazard*
a: A card may be placed in a row only if the row above already holds a card of the same rank; the top row is free
b: A card may be placed in a row only if the row above already holds a card of the same rank, and the top row accepts one suit
c: Placement is free, but a card's row scores only if the row above holds a card of its rank; the top row is free

name: The Scorpion Count
head: Stacks headed by a king pay per card. **Level 2, on its own mark:** In its own column, any suit counts
a: A same-suit descending stack whose bottom card is a king scores as a hand into the special bucket every time a card is added, not only at multiples of five
b: As (a), and a full thirteen is removed from the board and scores once more
c: As (a) for a stack of any suits, at odd lengths only

name: The Starter
head: The last card of the deck belongs to every line. **Level 2:** none beyond the flat mult a match pays
a: The bottom card of the last stock the deal reaches is turned up at show start; it is never placed, and every complete line scores as the best five-card hand of its five cards plus the starter
b: The last card of the deck is never placed; it counts as a sixth card in every line, and a jack starter pays every line an extra point
c: The last card of the deck is never placed; it counts as a member of every line on one grid you choose

name: The Strategy Rule
head: Nothing pays until the deck is empty. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell score when they complete, and again at the end
a: Completed lines score nothing until the deck is empty; then every complete line scores at once, doubled
b: Completed lines score nothing until the deck is empty; then every complete line scores at once, and each counts as a first-of-its-class for the combo
c: Completed lines score nothing until the deck is empty; then every complete line scores once and the show ends

name: The Aces Up Cull
head: Of two spotlit cards of one suit, the lower may go. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may also discard either of two spotlit cards of one rank
a: When two spotlit cards share a suit, the lower may be discarded; aces count highest
b: When two spotlit cards share a suit, the lower may be discarded and pays its rank into the special bucket; aces count highest
c: When two spotlit cards share a suit, the lower is discarded automatically at the next refill; aces count highest

name: The Air Lock
head: Two of a rank, side by side, come off together. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may also remove a pair one cell apart
a: Two orthogonally adjacent cards of the same rank may be removed together; they pay twice their rank into the bucket of the line they lay along
b: Two orthogonally adjacent cards of the same rank, or one rank apart, may be removed together; they pay their ranks into the bucket of the line they lay along; ace and king count as adjacent ranks
c: Two orthogonally adjacent cards of the same rank may be removed together into the bucket of their line, and the last eight pairs removed pay their ranks again at End

name: The Rising Set
head: Each set removed pays more than the last. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A set in its own column counts as two sets ⚑ *pair review: a removal payout named no bucket*
a: Three cards of one rank in one column are removed and pay into the column bucket the rank times the number of sets removed so far this show
b: Three cards of one rank in one row or column are removed and pay into the bucket of the line they sat in the rank times the number of sets removed so far this show
c: Three cards of one rank in one column are removed and pay into the column bucket the rank times the number of sets removed so far this run

name: The Sandwich
head: Flanked by two of a kind, a card is taken. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Flanking cards sitting on marks they match make it pay double
a: A card whose two line-neighbours share a rank or a suit may be removed into the bucket of the line the flanking pair lies along for points equal to its rank
b: Two adjacent cards whose outer neighbours share a rank or a suit may be removed into the bucket of the line the flanking pair lies along together for their ranks
c: A card whose two line-neighbours share a rank or a suit pays its rank every time its line is touched, and stays

name: The Dealt-Full Grid
head: The grid starts full and every placement shoves one out
a: Level: the grid is dealt full from a house deck at show start; every placement enters from an edge, shoves its line one cell, and the card pushed off is discarded
b: Level: the grid is dealt full from a house deck at show start, and a placement replaces a card of your choice, which is discarded
c: Level: the grid is dealt full from a house deck at show start, with three single-use pockets beside it that hold a card each

name: The Emptied Fan
head: A cell once emptied stays empty ⚑ *pair review: (a) and (c) only restrict you; it reads as a hazard*
a: A cell a card has left cannot be filled again this show — **level 2:** Cells in its lines may be refilled
