b: A cell a card has left cannot be filled again this show, and each such cell pays its mark's rank at End — **level 2:** An emptied cell in its lines pays its mark's rank now, not at End
c: A column every card has left cannot be filled again this show — **level 2:** Cells in its lines may be refilled

name: The Forced Fill
head: A gap inside a row must be closed before you go on. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A slide onto a mark the card matches may be followed by one more slide
a: An empty cell with cards on both sides in its row must be filled by sliding an orthogonal neighbour into it before the next placement
b: After each removal you may slide up to two cards one cell each into empty cells
c: An empty cell inside a row is filled at once by the card to its right, and the rest of the row follows

name: The Shrinking Row
head: A cell vacated at the end of a row is gone for the show. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its row does not shrink ⚑ *pair review: only a restriction; it reads as a hazard*
a: When the card at either end of a row leaves, that cell is removed from the grid for the rest of the show
b: When the card at either end of a row leaves, that cell is removed for the show, and a row shortened to four cells scores four-card hands
c: When the card at either end of a row leaves, that cell is removed for the show and the deck loses one card with it

name: The Final Bow
head: The last card standing pays its rank
a: At End, every complete line through the last card placed scores again — **level 2:** If it sits on a mark it matches, its rank bonus pays again in each line
b: At End, if every card of the deck has been placed, every complete line through the last card scores again at double — **level 2:** If it sits on a mark it matches, its rank bonus pays again in each line
c: At End, each of the last five cards placed re-scores one complete line through it, your choice — **level 2:** Those sitting on matched marks re-score every line through them

name: The Royal Marriage
head: Bring the king to his queen
a: Objective: end the show with the 13 and 12 of one suit the level names orthogonally adjacent for a bonus
b: Objective: end the show with the 13 and 12 of one suit the level names adjacent, paid per card that was removed from between them in reading order
c: Objective: two cards named by the level must end the show adjacent, and the show is won when they do, whatever the score

name: The Strike
head: A clean frame is paid the next two frames' worth again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line through its cell always counts as within one refill of the previous one
a: A line completed in the same Entrance refill as the previous line, or the next also earns the score of the next two lines completed
b: A line completed in the same Entrance refill as the previous line, or the next also earns the score of the next line completed
c: A line completed in the same refill as the previous line, or the next pays its own score again plus the next two lines' scores; one that takes two refills pays the next one's

name: The Ten Pins
head: A row whose ranks never fall, left to right. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Columns count too
a: A new hand: a row whose ranks never decrease from left to right scores as a hand, and ranks may repeat
b: A new hand: a row whose ranks never decrease from left to right scores, paying more the fewer gaps its ranks have
c: A new hand: a row whose ranks never decrease from left to right scores, a card that fits nowhere in it counts as a miss, and three misses void the row

name: The Winnable Shuffle
head: A deal someone has already won
a: Level: the deck order is one a previous run won with, and the show's payout is reduced
b: Level: the deck order is one a previous run won with, shown as such, at full payout but a higher goal
c: Level: the deck is a fresh order, and winning it adds that order to a pool of winnable deals later runs can draw

name: The Average Night
head: A weak line is lifted to the show's average
a: Once per show, cue: a line that scored below the show's running average line score is raised to that average — **level 2:** A line through its cell that scores below average is raised without spending the cue
b: Every line that scores below the show's running average is raised halfway toward it — **level 2:** Lines through its cell are raised all the way to the average
c: Once per show, cue: a line is raised to the score of the BEST line so far this show — **level 2:** A line through its cell is raised without spending the cue

name: The Crowd Favourite
head: The commonest rank on the board is the star
a: Cards of the board's most common rank score extra — **level 2:** Cards sitting on rank marks they match count as the favourite rank
b: Cards of the board's most common rank score extra, and the placement that makes a new rank the favourite pays that bonus for every card of it on the grid at once — **level 2:** Cards sitting on rank marks they match count as the favourite rank
c: Cards of the board's most common SUIT score extra — **level 2:** Cards sitting on suit marks they match count as the favourite suit

name: The Debut
head: The first appearance of each rank pays
a: The first time each rank scores this show, +1 combo — **level 2:** A first that scores through its cell adds +2 instead of +1
b: The first time each rank and each suit scores this show, +1 combo — **level 2:** A first that scores through its cell adds +2 instead of +1
c: The first time each hand type completes this show, this card pays a large flat bonus — **level 2:** A hand type first completed through its cell pays the bonus twice

name: The Decrescendo
head: Paid for coming down
a: Gains a permanent multiplier when a line scores less than the previous line, and loses one when it scores more — **level 2:** It never loses a multiplier on the way up
b: Gains a permanent multiplier when a line completes as a weaker hand type than the previous line — **level 2:** Any weaker line counts, not only the previous one
c: Gains a permanent multiplier when a line scores less than the previous line; nothing on the way up — **level 2:** It also gains when a line scores exactly the same

name: The Echo Bill
head: Every line is paid as the last hand you made
a: Hazard: every completed line pays at the value of the most recently completed hand type, whatever it actually is
b: Hazard: every completed line pays at the value of the FIRST hand type completed this show
c: Hazard: every completed line pays at the value of the weakest hand type completed so far this show

name: The Emergency Fund
head: Saved for the night it goes wrong. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines through its cell are not taxed: paid in full and banked ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0037 and Q0074, which you wrote: bank score now, pay it later*
a: Banks a tenth of every line's score; the bank is paid out only if the show would otherwise end short of its goal
b: Banks a tenth of every line's score; the bank is paid out when you press End, doubled if the show fell short
c: Banks a tenth of every line's score; cue at any time to release it, but an unspent bank is lost at show end

name: The Encore Line
head: The same ranks, again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It looks back two lines, not one
a: A line whose ranks repeat the previous completed line's ranks in the same order pays double
b: Any rank that also appeared in the previous completed line pays extra
c: A line whose ranks are a permutation of the previous completed line's ranks pays double

name: The Ensemble Rate
head: Every card in the line is paid what the best one is paid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It reaches every line through its cell, not only one
a: Every card in this card's line pays what the highest-paying card in that line pays
b: Every card in this card's line pays the average of what the line's cards pay
c: Every card in this card's line pays what the LOWEST-paying card pays, and the line's multiplier doubles

name: The Even Bill
head: Paid when the kinds of line keep pace
a: Pays a step at each line completion while rows, columns and diagonals have each completed the same number of times this show — **level 2:** Counts within one of each other are enough
b: Pays a step per line kind (row, column, diagonal, height) not yet completed this show, so it pays most early — **level 2:** It pays once more when the last of the three flat kinds completes
c: When a line completion brings its kind's count level with the most-completed kind's, it pays a large bonus — **level 2:** A line through its cell that comes within one also pays

name: The Inverted Bill
head: Points become multiplier and multiplier becomes points
a: Hazard: every flat-point bonus from an effect is paid as multiplier instead, and every multiplier bonus as flat points
b: Hazard: every flat-point bonus from an effect is paid as multiplier instead; multipliers are unchanged
c: Hazard: at each line's payout, the line's flat points and multiplier swap values before they combine

name: The Levelling Crowd
head: The kind you lean on pays like the kind you neglect
a: Hazard: lines of the kind completed most this show pay half, and lines of the kind completed least pay double
b: Hazard: lines of the kind completed most this show pay half
c: Hazard: a line pays in full only if its kind is the one completed least this show, else half

name: The Loose Ends
head: Paid for the cards that are in no line yet. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Loose cards sitting on marks they match count twice
a: Pays a step per card on its grid that is not yet part of any completed line
b: Cards not yet in any completed line feed their rank into the multiplier while they wait
c: A card outside every completed line but flanked by two cards inside one pays double its rank

name: The Matinee Clock
head: Paid by the clock on the wall ⚑ *pair review: real time rewards stalling in a turn-based game*
a: Pays a bonus that grows with real minutes elapsed in this show — **level 2:** Its bonus grows twice as fast
b: Pays a bonus set by the real time of day, larger in the evening — **level 2:** Its bonus is always the evening rate
c: Hazard: every fixed number of real seconds, one random card on the board is discarded — **level 2:** Cards in its lines are never discarded

name: The Multiplier Suit
head: A suit that pays into the other bucket. **Level 1 is the plain suit; each option is its level 2**, firing on a suit match
a: Cards of this suit pay their rank into the multiplier instead of into flat points
b: Cards of this suit pay their rank into both buckets at half value
c: Cards of this suit pay their rank into the multiplier only when their line holds two or more of the suit

name: The Pendulum
head: It feeds one bucket, then the other. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which side it pays each time
a: Alternates between paying flat points and multiplier each time it scores
b: Cards in this card's line alternate paying flat points and multiplier in resolution order
c: Pays flat points on odd-numbered lines this show and multiplier on even-numbered ones

name: The Plain Company
head: Paid for the cards that carry nothing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Plain cards sitting on marks they match count twice ⚑ *pair review: the non-talent half of your Q0062 ruling: an effect scored on the number of cards with no talent*
a: Gains a multiplier per scoring card with no type, stamp or skill
b: Every scoring card with no type, stamp or skill pays double
c: Gains a multiplier per plain card on the board, scoring or not

name: The Spare
head: Its number lands on the next lines, not its own. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays its own line as well
a: This card pays nothing in its own line; the next two lines to complete anywhere on the grid each add its rank to their multiplier
b: This card pays nothing in its own line; the next line to complete adds three times its rank to its multiplier
c: This card pays nothing in its own line; every line completed for the rest of the Entrance refill in which it scored adds its rank to its multiplier

name: The Triple Entry
head: One line, another bucket
a: Every line this card completes pays into its own bucket and again into the special bucket — **level 2:** Lines through its cell pay the special bucket double
b: When placed, name a bucket; every line this card completes pays into that bucket instead of its own — **level 2:** You may rename the bucket at each Entrance refill
c: Every line on this card's grid pays into all three buckets at a third of its value each — **level 2:** Lines through its cell pay full value into each bucket

name: The Two Spotlights
head: Only two performers are lit
a: Hazard: at most two cards in a completed line score, the two of highest rank
b: Hazard: only the single highest-ranked card in a completed line scores
c: Hazard: at most two cards in a completed line score, chosen by you as it completes

name: The Uniform
head: Sameness pays, for once
a: Gains a multiplier per DUPLICATE rank in the scoring line, so five of a kind pays most — **level 2:** Duplicate suits count as well
b: Gains a multiplier if the scoring line holds two or fewer distinct ranks — **level 2:** Duplicate suits count as well
c: Gains a multiplier per duplicate rank in the line and per duplicate suit, so a flush of one rank pays most — **level 2:** A duplicate sitting on a matched cell counts twice

name: The Warm-Up Act
head: Whatever resolves after the named rank pays double
a: When a card of a named rank scores, every card that resolves after it in that line pays double — **level 2:** Cards that resolve before it pay double too
b: When this card scores, every card that resolves after it in its line pays double — **level 2:** Cards that resolve before it pay double too
c: When a card of a named rank scores, every card that resolved BEFORE it in that line is re-scored once — **level 2:** Cards before it are re-scored twice

name: The Wrong Spotlight
head: The line completes, and everything else is paid
a: Hazard: when a line completes, its hand is paid, but its flat points are the ranks of the cards on the grid outside the line, not its own
b: Hazard: as (a), and the line's own ranks pay at half on top
c: Cue, once per show: for one line completion, its flat points are the ranks of every card outside it

name: The Binary
head: Ones and blanks make a number. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which direction the line is read
a: A row or column of rank-1 and rankless cards, read as binary, creates a card of that rank in an empty Entrance slot; a value past King makes a King
b: A stack of rank-1 and rankless cards, read as binary, counts as one card of that rank
c: A line of rank-1 and rankless cards, read as binary, pays that many flat points

name: The Demotion
head: Every hand pays as the one below it
a: Hazard: every completed line pays as the next-weakest hand type
b: Hazard: every completed line pays as the next-weakest hand type, and a high card pays nothing
c: Hazard: the first line of each Entrance refill pays as the next-weakest hand type

name: The Double Count
head: One card in the line counts twice
a: When a line completes, one of its cards you choose counts twice for the hand, so a pair reads as a triple — **level 2:** Two cards count twice
b: When a line completes, its highest card counts twice for the hand — **level 2:** The two highest count twice
c: When a line completes, this card counts twice for the hand if it is in that line — **level 2:** This card counts three times

name: The Everything Hand
head: One line, every hand at once
a: Consumable: the next completed line counts as every hand type at once, paying the sum of them
b: Consumable: the next completed line pays for every hand type it actually contains, not only the best
c: Consumable: for the rest of the show, every completed line counts as the best hand type it is one card short of

name: The Full Mansion
head: A hand built across the whole board. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One of its parts may be a card short
a: When a placement brings a three of a kind and a four of a kind of different ranks onto the board at once, they score together as a full house into the special bucket, and again whenever a line through one of their cards scores
b: As (a), for two three of a kinds
c: As (a), for a straight of five and a flush of five

name: The Guardsman
head: The cards that made the hand fire for the ones that did not
a: Each card that contributed to the hand is retriggered once per card in the line that did not — **level 2:** Non-contributing cards on matched cells count twice
b: Each card that did NOT contribute to the hand pays its rank to the cards that did — **level 2:** Non-contributing cards on matched cells count twice
c: A line where every card contributed to the hand is retriggered once in full — **level 2:** A full-contribution line through its cell is retriggered twice

name: The Impostor Hand
head: One hand scores as another
a: Name two hand types; the first scores as the second — **level 2:** You may rename the pair once per show
b: Name two hand types; completing the first also fires every effect keyed to the second — **level 2:** You may rename the pair once per show
c: Every completed line scores as one hand type named when this card is placed, whatever it contains — **level 2:** You may rename the hand type once per show

name: The Material Flush
head: A hand made of matching materials, not matching pips
a: Five cards of one type in a line score as a flush of that material — **level 2:** Four of a type is enough through its cell
b: Three cards of one type and two of another in a line score as a full house of materials — **level 2:** Two of one type and two of another are enough through its cell
c: Five different types in one line score as a rainbow hand — **level 2:** Four different types are enough through its cell

name: The Mixed Company
head: No line of one suit, and no line of one rank
a: Hazard: a line must hold at least two suits to score
b: Hazard: a line must hold at least two suits and at least two ranks to score
c: Hazard: a line must hold at least three suits to score

name: The One-Night Stand
head: Each hand type gets one night. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A repeat through its cell is allowed once ⚑ *pair review: its restriction is Q0114, which you wrote as a boss*
a: Each hand type may score only once per show, and each distinct one raises this card's multiplier permanently
b: Each hand type may score only once per show, and completing all of them pays an enormous bonus
c: Each hand type may score only once per Entrance refill, and each distinct one adds +1 combo

name: The Prime Sum
head: A line that adds up to something special is a hand. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A line through its cell may be one off the sum ⚑ *pair review: a fourth line-sum detector beside your Q0075, Q0090 and Q0103*
a: A line whose ranks sum to a prime number scores as its own hand
b: A line whose ranks sum to a square number scores as its own hand
c: A line whose ranks sum to exactly zero, negative ranks included, scores as its own hand

name: The Redistribution
head: Levels are spread out, not piled up ⚑ *pair review: assumes hand types have levels, which only Q0128 (Burnt Joker) introduces*
a: Hazard: completing a hand drains half that hand type's level into the other hand types
b: Hazard: no hand type's level may exceed the average level of all hand types
c: Hazard: at show start, every hand type's level is pooled and spread evenly

name: The Reunion
head: The first cards of the last five lines meet again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which card of each line joins it
a: From the fifth completed line on, the first card of each of the last five completed lines forms a virtual line that scores as a hand into the special bucket at every line completion
b: As (a), the highest card of each
c: As (a), the card that completed each

name: The Rising Tide
head: Levelling one hand lifts its neighbours ⚑ *pair review: assumes hand types have levels, which only Q0128 (Burnt Joker) introduces*
a: When a hand type gains a level, the hand types directly above and below it on the ladder gain one too — **level 2:** Hand types two rungs away gain a level too
b: When a hand type gains a level, one fixed partner hand type gains one too — **level 2:** It names a second partner
c: When a hand type gains a level, every hand type in its family (pairs, runs, flushes) gains one too — **level 2:** The family gains two levels

name: The Status Meld
head: Cards that share an ailment match. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match count as carrying every status
a: Cards carrying the same status count as matching in rank for melds
b: A line of five cards all carrying a status scores as its own hand
c: Cards carrying the same status count as matching in suit for melds

name: The Underdog Bill
head: Every line is paid as your least-made hand
a: Every completed line scores as whichever hand type you have completed least this show — **level 2:** A line through its cell may keep its own hand if that pays more
b: Every completed line scores as either its own hand or your least-completed one, whichever pays more — **level 2:** It weighs the two least-made hands and takes the better
c: Once per show, cue: the next line scores as your least-completed hand type — **level 2:** A line through its cell may keep its own hand if that pays more

name: The Zero-Sum Ladder
head: A level gained is a level taken ⚑ *pair review: assumes hand types have levels, which only Q0128 (Burnt Joker) introduces*
a: When a hand completes, it gains a level taken from a random other hand type — **level 2:** You choose which hand type the level is taken from
b: When a hand completes, it gains a level taken from the highest-levelled other hand type — **level 2:** You choose which hand type the level is taken from
c: Cue, once per show: swap the levels of any two hand types — **level 2:** After the swap the lower of the two gains one level

name: The Bookends
head: What sits between two of a kind is retriggered. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Two cards of one suit count as bookends too
a: When a line holds two cards of one rank, every card between them is retriggered once
b: When two copies of this card sit in one line, every card between them is retriggered once
c: When a line holds two cards of one rank, every card between them is retriggered once per rank of the pair

name: The Centre Ring
head: A different act in a different seat
a: Pays a step anywhere on the grid; in the centre cell it instead adds +1 to the multiplier of every line through it — **level 2:** Its centre form also applies on its own mark, wherever that is
b: Pays a step anywhere; in a corner it instead pays a step per completed line through the corner's row, column and diagonal — **level 2:** Its corner form also applies on its own mark, wherever that is
c: Pays one step in row 1, two in row 2, up to five in row 5 — **level 2:** It uses the better of its own row and its mark's row

name: The Centrepiece
head: The middle card lends its material to the line. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It lends both type and stamp
a: The centre card of a completed line lends its type to every card in the line for that scoring
b: The centre card of a completed line lends its stamp to every card in the line for that scoring
c: The centre card of a completed line lends its type to the two cards beside it

name: The Cold Open
head: The first to resolve scores nothing
a: Hazard: the first card to resolve in each completed line scores nothing
b: Hazard: the lowest-ranked card in each completed line scores nothing
c: Hazard: the first card to resolve in each completed line is debuffed for the rest of the show

name: The Left Wing
head: Paid for the cards on one side of it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts both sides
a: Scores extra per scoring card to the left of it in its line
b: Scores extra per scoring card to the left of it in its line, and loses the same per card to its right
c: Scores extra per scoring card on whichever side of it holds more cards

name: The Neighbourly Rank
head: Paid for the rank next door. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Two ranks away counts too
a: A card scores extra when its line also holds a card one rank above or below it
b: A card scores extra when an orthogonally adjacent cell holds a card one rank above or below it
c: A card scores extra when its line holds BOTH the rank above and the rank below it

name: The Rabbit's Foot
head: Its neighbours never miss. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It reaches diagonal neighbours too
a: Every probability check on an orthogonally adjacent card succeeds automatically
b: Every probability check on an orthogonally adjacent card is rolled twice and keeps the better
c: Every probability check on a card in this card's row succeeds automatically

name: The Ringside
head: Worth more the nearer the edge it sits. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It measures distance from any cell you choose instead of the centre
a: Scores a step for each cell of distance from the grid's centre
b: Scores a step for each cell of distance from the grid's centre, and nothing in the centre itself
c: Scores a step for each cell of distance from the grid's centre, doubled in a corner

name: The Second Serving
head: The first of a rank pays nothing; the rest pay double. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The first of a rank sitting on a matched cell pays too
a: Among cards sharing a rank in a line, the first to resolve pays nothing and each later one pays double
b: Among cards sharing a rank in a line, the first to resolve pays nothing and the last pays triple
c: Among cards sharing a SUIT in a line, the first to resolve pays nothing and each later one pays double

name: The Shrapnel
head: When the wearer goes, something next to it goes too
a: When the wearer leaves the board, one random orthogonal neighbour is destroyed — **level 2:** You choose which neighbour goes
b: When the wearer leaves the board, the next occupied cell to its left is destroyed — **level 2:** You choose which neighbour goes
c: When the wearer is destroyed, every orthogonal neighbour is destroyed — **level 2:** You may spare one neighbour

name: The Spotlight Spill
head: A stamped card lights its neighbours. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Diagonal neighbours count too
a: Any card orthogonally adjacent to a stamped card is retriggered once when its line completes
b: Any card orthogonally adjacent to a stamped card has a chance to be retriggered, and the chance halves with each success
c: Any card orthogonally adjacent to THIS card is retriggered once when its line completes

name: The Sticky Stamp
head: A stamp that rubs off on the neighbours. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It copies onto a neighbour of your choice
a: When the wearer scores, this stamp copies itself onto one orthogonally adjacent card
b: When the wearer scores, this stamp has a one-in-three chance to copy itself onto each orthogonal neighbour
c: When the wearer scores, this stamp MOVES to an orthogonally adjacent card

name: The Tremor
head: When it scores, everything around it re-scores
a: When a card of this type scores, every completed line through an orthogonal neighbour that does not hold this card re-scores
b: When a card of this type scores, every completed line through any of its eight neighbours re-scores, and the card breaks
c: When a card of this type is placed, every completed line through an orthogonal neighbour re-scores

name: The Umbrella
head: Shelter for the wearer and its neighbours. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It shelters diagonal neighbours too
a: The wearer and its orthogonal neighbours ignore debuffs
b: The wearer's orthogonal neighbours ignore debuffs; the wearer takes them all instead
c: The wearer and every card in its row ignore debuffs

name: The Amalgam
head: A line becomes a card
a: Cue: collapse one completed line into a single card of the summed rank, keeping the completing card's suit; the other four cells empty — **level 2:** The new card lands on whichever of the five cells has a mark it matches
b: Cue: the card that completed a line absorbs the types and stamps of the other four, which are discarded — **level 2:** The completing card also takes their talents for the show
c: At show end, every card on this card's grid fuses into one card of the summed rank, carried into the next show — **level 2:** The fused card keeps this card's talent

name: The Boomerang
head: It never reaches the discard. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It returns to the stock you choose
a: When the wearer leaves the board it returns to an Entrance stock instead of the discard pile
b: When the wearer leaves the board it returns to the TOP of an Entrance stock
c: When the wearer leaves the board it returns to the bottom of its stock and pays its rank

name: The Bound Stamp
head: Wearers share one fate
a: When a wearer leaves the board, every other wearer gains a permanent step — **level 2:** Wearers sitting on matched cells gain two steps
b: When a wearer is destroyed, every other wearer is destroyed with it — **level 2:** A wearer sitting on a matched cell survives the others
c: Wearers on the same grid score together: when one scores, the others score too — **level 2:** The joint scoring repeats once

name: The Chaos Swap
head: Nothing stays where you put it
a: Hazard: every card you place swaps cells with a random other spotlit card
b: Hazard: every card you place swaps cells with the card you placed before it
c: Hazard: every card you place swaps cells with a random card in its row

name: The Exhausted Rank
head: Paid for the ranks you have used up
a: Gains a step for each rank with no copies left in the stocks — **level 2:** Suits count too
b: Gains a step the moment the last copy of any rank leaves the stocks — **level 2:** Suits count too
c: Gains a step for each SUIT with no copies left in the stocks — **level 2:** Ranks count too

name: The Flood
head: Fifty-two strangers join the deck
a: Hazard: a plain deck's worth of cards is added to the Entrance stocks for the show
b: Hazard: a plain deck's worth of cards is added to the stocks, and the goal rises by a third
c: Hazard: thirteen plain cards of one suit are added to the stocks for the show

name: The Fresh Lock
head: What just landed cannot be touched. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The lock also covers the cards beside it
a: A card cannot be moved, swapped, destroyed or discarded by any hazard or hostile effect for the two placements after it lands
b: As (a), for the rest of the Entrance refill
c: A card that an effect has just moved cannot be moved again until a line completes

name: The Ghost Partner
head: The discard scores along. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards in the discard of its mark's rank score with it too
a: When a card scores, any card of the same rank in the discard pile scores with it
b: When a card scores, the most recently destroyed card scores with it
c: A scoring card pays a step per card in the discard pile sharing its suit or rank

name: The Headcount
head: A pile is a card whose number is its height. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A stack on a matched cell may count as its height plus one
a: A stack counts as one card whose rank is the number of cards in it
b: A stack counts as one card whose rank is the number of cards in it, and whose suit is its top card's
c: Two stacks may be merged when their heights differ by one or less

name: The Loan From Tomorrow
head: Borrow a card now, return it or lose
a: Cue: draw any card from the stocks into an empty Entrance slot now; if it has not been placed within five placements the show is lost — **level 2:** It has two more placements
b: Cue: draw any card from the stocks into an empty Entrance slot now; an unplaced loan after five placements is destroyed instead — **level 2:** It has two more placements
c: Cue: draw the top card of any stock into an empty Entrance slot now; the next refill deals that slot nothing — **level 2:** The next refill deals its full five

name: The Lost Star
head: The best card in the discard still pays
a: Pays the highest rank in the discard pile when it scores — **level 2:** It pays the two highest ranks
b: Pays a step per card in the discard pile that outranks it — **level 2:** Cards of equal rank count too
c: Pays the highest rank in the discard pile, and that card is then destroyed — **level 2:** It pays the two highest ranks

name: The Next In Line
head: Paid by what is coming
a: Pays the rank of the next card due from a named stock when it scores — **level 2:** It pays the next two cards of that stock
b: Pays the summed rank of the next card due from every stock when it scores — **level 2:** It also reveals them
c: Pays double the rank of the next card due from its own stock, and that card is revealed — **level 2:** You choose which stock it reads

name: The No-Repeats
head: One of everything
a: Hazard: any card in the stocks that exactly matches another in rank and suit is set aside for the show
b: Hazard: any card in the stocks that shares a rank and suit with a card on the board is destroyed
c: Hazard: a card may not be placed if a card of the same rank and suit is already on the board

name: The Orbit
head: Columns drift out of phase. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may advance one column's phase each refill
a: Each column has a phase of three that advances when a card is placed in it; a line scores double when every column it crosses is in the same phase
b: Each column has a phase of three that advances on every placement in it; lines score only across columns in the same phase
c: Each column has a phase that advances when it scores; a column in phase three pays double and drops back to one

name: The Parity Build
head: Odd on even, even on odd. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its own stack may take either parity
a: A card may be stacked on a card of opposite parity, any suit
b: A card may be stacked on a card of opposite parity, and a stack that alternates all the way pays per card
c: A card may only be stacked on a card of the SAME parity

name: The Rails
head: Movement runs on one axis
a: Hazard: every effect that moves a card may only move it along its row this show
b: Hazard: every effect that moves a card may only move it along its column this show
c: Hazard: no effect may move, swap or rotate a card this show

name: The Restless
head: Paid for being moved. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A move onto a mark it matches gains two steps
a: Gains a permanent step every time you move it to a new cell
b: Gains a permanent step every time ANY effect moves it, and loses one when it stays put for a whole refill
c: Gains a permanent step every time you move it, up to a cap that rises by one each show

name: The Return Deal
head: A finished line goes back in the box
a: Hazard: when a line completes and scores, its five cards return to the bottoms of their stocks; a card returning for a second time is discarded instead
b: Hazard: when a line completes and scores, the card that completed it returns to the bottom of its stock and its cell is sealed for the show
c: Hazard: when a line completes and scores, its five cards return to the stocks and the line's cells are sealed for the show

name: The Rubber Stamp
head: One card prints itself down the stock
a: Consumable: choose a card in a stock; the three cards above it become copies of it
b: Consumable: choose a card on the board; the next three cards drawn from its stock become copies of it
c: Consumable: choose a card in a stock; every card above it takes its suit

name: The Scapegoat
head: A leaving card's number goes to someone still on stage
a: When a card leaves the board, its rank is added to a random card still on the board — **level 2:** The rank goes to a card you choose
b: When a card leaves the board, its rank is added to the card that has scored least this show — **level 2:** The rank goes to a card you choose
c: When a card leaves the board, its rank is added to this card — **level 2:** The rank it takes is doubled

name: The Siamese Pair
head: Place one, and the other comes too. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The partner may go onto any cell whose mark it matches instead
a: Cue: bond this card to another card in the Entrance; placing either places the other in the cell mirrored across the grid's centre, or the nearest empty cell to it
b: Cue: bond this card to another; placing either places the other in the orthogonally adjacent cell
c: Cue: bond this card to another; moving either moves the other the same way

name: The Skewer
head: Runs everything on one side through. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may pull from either side
a: Cue: every card to this card's right in its row is pulled into a stack on this card, in order
b: Cue: every card to this card's right in its row is pulled into a stack on this card, and this card consumes one of them per refill
c: Cue: every card in this card's column is pulled into a stack on this card

name: The Skyscraper
head: Paid for looking down
a: A scoring card pays a step per undrawn card of lower rank than it — **level 2:** It also counts undrawn cards of equal rank
b: A scoring card pays a step per undrawn card of the same rank — **level 2:** It also counts lower ranks
c: A scoring card pays a step per undrawn card of higher rank than it — **level 2:** It also counts undrawn cards of equal rank

name: The Spent Casing
head: Every card that left fires it again
a: A card of this type is retriggered once per card that has left the board this show
b: A card of this type is retriggered once per card that has left the board this refill
c: A card of this type is retriggered once per card of its own suit that has left the board this show

name: The Tourist
head: Paid for going somewhere new. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A new cell whose mark it matches counts twice
a: Gains a permanent step each show it is placed in a cell it has never occupied, and loses one when placed in a cell it has
b: Gains a step per cell it has ever occupied, checked when it scores
c: Gains a permanent step for each new cell, and resets when it has visited every cell of its grid

name: The Typecasting
head: Your favourites are buried
a: Hazard: the five cards you have placed most often this run are dealt to the bottom of their stocks
b: Hazard: the rank you have placed most often this run is dealt to the bottom of its stocks
c: Hazard: every card that scored last show is dealt to the bottom of its stock

name: The Wake
head: A departure that pays the room
a: When a card leaves the board, every other card on it gains a step for the show — **level 2:** Cards sitting on matched cells gain two steps
b: When a card leaves the board, it gains a permanent step for the next time it is placed — **level 2:** It gains two steps if it left a matched cell
c: When a card leaves the board, every card in its lines gains two steps for the show — **level 2:** Cards sitting on matched cells gain two steps

name: The Washout
head: Every line completed costs the deck
a: Hazard: when a line completes, that many cards are discarded from the stocks
b: Hazard: when a line completes, one card is discarded from each stock
c: Hazard: when a card leaves the board, one card is discarded from the stocks with it

name: The Wings
head: The ends of the Entrance perform from the wings. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The middle Entrance slot counts too
a: The cards in the leftmost and rightmost Entrance slots score alongside every line that completes
b: The card in the leftmost Entrance slot scores alongside every line that completes, then is discarded
c: The cards in the leftmost and rightmost Entrance slots join every row for melds: a row's hand is the best five of its five cards plus those two

name: The Word Backstage
head: Word reaches the cards still waiting
a: When a line completes, every card of the completing card's rank still in the stocks gains a permanent step — **level 2:** It also reaches the discard
b: When a line completes, every card of the same suit still in the stocks gains a permanent step — **level 2:** It also reaches the discard
c: When a line completes, the next card of the completing card's rank to be drawn scores double — **level 2:** The next two cards of that rank score double

name: The Ambiguous Card
head: It is whatever its neighbours leave it room to be
a: A card of this type has no rank or suit until its neighbours leave only one identity that fits every line through it, and then it becomes that card permanently
b: A card of this type has no rank or suit; when placed, it becomes whatever card would best complete the lines through it
c: A card of this type has no rank or suit; it becomes the card its row lacks for a straight, or stays blank

name: The Bequest
head: A destroyed card leaves its number to the neighbours
a: Cue: destroy one card on the board; its rank is split between the cards on either side of it in its row — **level 2:** You choose how the rank is split
b: Cue: destroy one card on the board; its rank is added to the card beneath it in its stack — **level 2:** The rank may go to the card above instead
c: When any card is destroyed, its rank is split between its orthogonal neighbours — **level 2:** You choose how the rank is split

name: The Chain Letter
head: It spreads across the grid. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its copy is placed on a cell whose mark it matches, if one is empty
a: The first time it scores each show, it places a copy of itself in an empty orthogonally adjacent cell
b: When placed, it overwrites the card to its left with a copy of itself; at show end it destroys any copy to its right
c: At show end it destroys its right-hand neighbour and replaces it with a stronger copy of itself

name: The Clear-Out
head: Sweeps the stage of everything that is not in a line. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on marks they match are spared
a: Cue, once per show: destroy every card on this card's grid that is not part of a completed line, paying a step per card
b: Cue, once per show: discard every card on this card's grid that is not part of a completed line, paying a step per card
c: Cue, once per show: destroy every card not part of a completed line, and gain a multiplier per five destroyed

name: The Colour Wheel
head: Suits move around the wheel. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose which way round the wheel it turns
a: When this card scores, its suit moves one step around a fixed cycle of the suits
b: When a line completes, every card in it moves one step around the suit cycle before scoring
c: When this card scores, every card in its line moves one step around the suit cycle after scoring

name: The Company Call
head: Everyone who has performed comes back on
a: When a line completes, every card that scored earlier this show is retriggered once — **level 2:** Cards that scored through its cell are retriggered twice
b: When a line completes, every card that scored earlier this refill is retriggered once — **level 2:** Cards that scored through its cell are retriggered twice
c: When a line completes, every earlier completed line this show pays again at a tenth — **level 2:** Earlier lines through its cell pay again at a fifth

name: The Crescendo
head: Retriggers grow along the line
a: Each card in a completed line is retriggered as many times as its position from the near end — **level 2:** You choose which end counts as near
b: Each card in a completed line is retriggered twice as many times as the card before it, starting from one — **level 2:** You choose which end counts as near
c: Every card in a completed line except the two endpoints is retriggered once — **level 2:** The endpoints are retriggered too

name: The Dye Bath
head: One suit for the whole board
a: Consumable: destroy one card on the board; every other card on the board takes its suit
b: Consumable: destroy one card on the board; every other card in its row and column takes its suit
c: Consumable: destroy one card on the board; every card in the stocks takes its suit

name: The Equaliser
head: Everyone in the line gets the average. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards sitting on rank marks they match keep their rank
a: When a line completes, every card in it becomes the line's average rank, rounded down
b: When a line completes, every card in it becomes the line's average rank, and the line re-scores
c: When a line completes, every card in it becomes the rank of this card

name: The Forgery Trap
head: Copy it and pay for it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its protection covers the cards beside it ⚑ *pair review: it only costs you: copy effects are your own cards'; it reads as a hazard*
a: Any copy effect that targets this card destroys the copier instead
b: Any copy effect that targets this card produces a rank-1 blank instead of a copy
c: Any copy effect that targets this card also copies a debuff onto the copier

name: The Fuse
head: Burns inward while the rank holds
a: When a line completes, destroy cards inward from one end while they share a rank, paying a step per card destroyed — **level 2:** You choose which end it burns from
b: When a line completes, destroy cards inward from one end while they share a suit, paying a step per card destroyed — **level 2:** You choose which end it burns from
c: When a line completes, destroy cards inward from BOTH ends while they share a rank, paying per card — **level 2:** Cards on matched cells in its path pay double

name: The Growth Hormone
head: Every rank raise is a little bigger. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Raises on cards sitting on marks they match go two steps further
a: Every effect that raises a card's rank raises it one step more
b: Every effect that grows a card's stored bonus grows it twice as fast
c: Every effect that raises a card's rank raises it one step more, and every effect that lowers a rank lowers it one step less

name: The Levelling Rank
head: Everything moves toward one number. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You choose, card by card, whether it moves
a: Every scoring card's rank moves one step toward a rank named when this card is placed, permanently
b: Every scoring card's rank moves one step toward this card's rank, permanently
c: Every scoring card's rank moves one step toward the rank most common on the board, permanently

name: The Merry-Go-Round
head: Three cards pass their numbers along
a: Consumable: choose three cards on the board; their ranks rotate one step among them
b: Consumable: choose three cards on the board; their suits rotate one step among them
c: Consumable: choose three cards on the board; their stamps rotate one step among them

name: The Mimic
head: Whatever was placed last, it is. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It may carry any of the last three skills placed
a: Always carries the talent of the most recently placed skill card
b: Always carries the talent of the most recently placed skill card, at half strength, in addition to its own
c: Carries the talent of whichever of its two orthogonal neighbours was placed more recently

name: The Overflow
head: Past the King, anything goes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On its mark, a card raised past King in its lines becomes wild at once
a: A rank raised past King, or lowered below Ace, becomes wild instead of stopping
b: A rank raised past King becomes an Ace of every suit
c: A rank raised past King becomes wild for one line completion, then returns to King

name: The Quick-Change Fan
head: Paid for every transformation. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Changes made to cards on matched cells bank twice
a: Banks a step every time any card's suit or rank is changed by an effect, paid when this card scores
b: Any card whose suit or rank has ever been changed by an effect scores extra
c: Banks a step every time any card's type or stamp is changed by an effect, paid when this card scores

name: The Rehearsal Run
head: The ending, early. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Twice per show
a: Cue, once per show: every effect that fires at show end fires now
b: Cue, once per show: every effect that fires at show end fires now, and again at show end
c: Cue, once per show: every effect that fires on an Entrance refill fires now

name: The Relay Tower
head: One consumable, every skill
a: A consumable used on this card applies to every skill card on the board — **level 2:** It also reaches stamp cards
b: A consumable used on this card applies to every card in its row — **level 2:** It reaches its column as well
c: A consumable used on this card is not spent, and applies to this card only — **level 2:** The consumable applies to every card in its lines

name: The Reverse
head: A number that turns the line around. **Level 2, on its own mark:** On a rank match you choose whether it reverses the line
a: A card of this rank in a completed line reverses the order in which that line's cards resolve
b: A card of this rank in a completed line makes the line resolve in reverse placement order
c: A card of this rank in a completed line makes the line resolve from itself outward

name: The Royal Issue
head: A king and a queen produce a jack
a: When a line holding a King and a Queen completes, a Jack of one of their suits is created in a stock — **level 2:** The Jack goes onto a cell whose mark it matches
b: When a King and a Queen sit orthogonally adjacent, a Jack of one of their suits is created in the Entrance — **level 2:** The Jack goes onto a cell whose mark it matches
c: When a line holding a King and a Queen completes, a Jack is created in the empty cell nearest them — **level 2:** The Jack takes the suit you choose

name: The Salvage
head: Nothing a dead card wore is wasted
a: When a card is destroyed, its stamp moves to a random other card on the board — **level 2:** You choose the card that receives it
b: When a card is destroyed, its type moves to a random other card on the board — **level 2:** You choose the card that receives it
c: When a card is destroyed, its stamp and type move to this card — **level 2:** It also takes the rank

name: The Stain
head: It leaves its material on the neighbours
a: When this card leaves the board, its type is copied onto the cards that were its orthogonal neighbours — **level 2:** You choose which neighbours take it
b: When this card leaves the board, its stamp is copied onto the cards that were its orthogonal neighbours — **level 2:** You choose which neighbours take it
c: When this card leaves the board, its cell keeps its type and gives it to the next card placed there — **level 2:** The next two cards placed there take it

name: The Tattoo
head: The costume becomes the number. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The folded stamp's effect stays for the show
a: Cue: fold a card's stamp and type into its rank permanently, removing them; each adds three ranks
b: Cue: fold a card's stamp into its rank permanently, removing the stamp; the card keeps its type
c: When this card scores, it folds its own stamp and type into its rank and loses them

name: The Transfusion
head: Rank moves from one card to another
a: Consumable: move up to three points of rank from one card on the board to another
b: Consumable: move one point of rank from every card in a row onto one card in that row
c: Consumable: move all of one card's rank onto another, leaving the first at rank 1

name: The Trim
head: The top and bottom of the line leave. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It spares cards sitting on marks they match
a: When a line completes, its highest- and lowest-ranked cards leave the board to the discard, and this card gains a permanent step per card
b: When a line completes, its highest-ranked card leaves the board, and this card gains that rank as a permanent bonus
c: When a line completes, its lowest-ranked card leaves the board to the discard, and the line re-scores with the uncovered mark beneath standing in for it (your Q0109 rule)

name: The Understudy's Break
head: The plain card that completed a nothing hand gets its chance
a: A skill-less card that completes a high-card line gains a random talent for the rest of the show — **level 2:** It chooses the talent from two
b: A skill-less card that completes a high-card line gains a random talent permanently — **level 2:** It chooses the talent from two
c: A skill-less card that completes any line gains this card's talent for the rest of the refill — **level 2:** It keeps the talent for the show

name: The Wild Hat
head: A stamp that is every stamp. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its wearer's hat match also pays the talent mult
a: This stamp counts as every stamp for any effect that checks a card's stamp, and its wearer matches any hat mark
b: As (a), but the hat match pays no mult of its own
c: This stamp counts as whichever stamp its orthogonal neighbours wear most, and matches only that hat

name: The Wildfire
head: A step that spreads down the row. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its bonus spreads to a neighbour of your choice
a: Gains a permanent step each show; at show end its steps are copied onto its left neighbour
b: Gains a permanent step each show; at show end its steps are copied onto every orthogonal neighbour
c: Gains a step at each line completion; at each completion its steps are copied onto its left neighbour and its own reset

name: The Balanced Line
head: Every suit present in equal measure
a: A completed line holding an equal number of each suit present pays a bonus — **level 2:** A line through its cell may be one card out of balance
b: A completed line holding exactly two suits in equal number pays a bonus — **level 2:** A line through its cell may be one card out of balance
c: A grid holding an equal number of each suit present pays a bonus at each line completion — **level 2:** The grid may be one card out of balance

name: The Black Cat
head: Enormous, until anyone misses
a: A large multiplier, and this card is destroyed the moment any probability check on the board fails — **level 2:** Only failures in its own lines count
b: A large multiplier, and this card is destroyed the moment one of ITS OWN probability checks fails — **level 2:** Its first failed check each show is ignored
c: A large multiplier that halves each time a probability check on the board fails — **level 2:** The multiplier halves only for failures in its own lines

name: The Blindfold Bargain
head: Big pay, blind draws
a: A large multiplier, and every time this card scores the next card dealt into the Entrance arrives face down — **level 2:** You may look at the face-down card before it arrives
b: Pays a step every time a card arrives in the Entrance face down — **level 2:** Face-down cards placed on marks they match pay double
c: Gains a permanent step every time a card that was dealt face down scores in a line — **level 2:** Face-down cards placed on marks they match pay double

name: The Carry-Over
head: The next line starts where the last one ended
a: Consumable: the next completed line starts from the previous completed line's score
b: Consumable: for the rest of the refill, each completed line starts from the previous line's score
c: Consumable: the next completed line starts from the show's best line score

name: The Coin Toss
head: Double, or nothing. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You flip twice and choose
a: Cue, once per show: flip a coin; the show's score doubles or drops to zero
b: Cue, once per show: flip a coin; the last completed line's score doubles or drops to zero
c: Cue, once per show: flip a coin; the show's score doubles, or this card is destroyed

name: The Crop Cycle
head: It grows, it ripens, and it needs resetting
a: Gains a step each Entrance refill until full, then scores nothing until an effect resets it to empty — **level 2:** It resets itself when a line through its cell scores
b: Gains a step each Entrance refill until full, then scores its whole growth once and resets itself — **level 2:** It scores its growth twice
c: Gains a step each line completed until full, then scores nothing until it is moved — **level 2:** It resets itself when a line through its cell scores

name: The Dead Heat
head: Two lines, one number. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Lines within one point count as equal
a: Pays a large bonus when two lines this show score exactly the same
b: Pays a large bonus when a line scores exactly what the previous line scored
c: Pays a bonus scaling with how close a line's score is to the previous line's

name: The Drift
head: The numbers will not hold still
a: Hazard: at each Entrance refill, a fifth of the cards on the board move one rank up or down at random
b: Hazard: at each Entrance refill, one random card on the board moves one rank up or down
c: Hazard: at each Entrance refill, every card on the board moves one rank toward the average rank

name: The Dyed Coat
head: Some suits are lying
a: Hazard: one card in three placed this show shows a false suit until it scores
b: Hazard: one card in three dealt to the Entrance shows a false suit until it is placed
c: Hazard: one card in three placed this show shows a false RANK until it scores

name: The Echo of an Echo
head: A retrigger that can retrigger
a: Every retrigger on the board has a one-in-three chance to retrigger again — **level 2:** Retriggers from matched cells rechain at one in two
b: This card's retriggers chain: each success rolls again at half the previous chance until one fails — **level 2:** Its chance does not fall on retriggers from matched cells
c: Every retrigger on the board has a one-in-three chance to retrigger again, and each success lowers the chance — **level 2:** Its chance does not fall on retriggers from matched cells

name: The Forbidden Three
head: Strong while you hold back. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Three of the rank are allowed when one of them sits on its own rank mark
a: Gains a multiplier per copy of a named rank in the deck; three of that rank on the board at once loses the show
b: Gains a multiplier per copy of a named rank in the deck; three of that rank on the board at once destroys this card
c: Gains a multiplier per copy of a named rank on the board; three of that rank in one line loses the show

name: The Four Colours
head: One flush of every suit. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A flush through its cell counts for two suits
a: Pays a step per distinct suit that has scored a flush this show
b: Pays a large bonus the moment every suit has scored a flush this show
c: Pays a step per distinct suit that has scored a flush this show, escalating at the fifth

name: The Holes
head: Paid for the ranks a line skipped. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It counts the holes in its column too ⚑ *pair review: overlaps Q0080, which you wrote: the gap between a line's highest and lowest ranks*
a: Pays a step per rank missing between a completed line's lowest and highest ranks
b: Pays a step per rank missing between this card's rank and its highest line-mate
c: Pays a step per rank missing from the board entirely

name: The Intensifier
head: Every status hits twice as hard. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Statuses on cards sitting on marks they match apply three times
a: Every status applied anywhere on the board is applied twice
b: Every status applied to a card in this card's row is applied twice
c: Every status applied anywhere is applied twice, and every status removed is removed twice

name: The Inverted Scale
head: Low is high
a: Every scoring card pays fourteen minus its rank instead of its rank — **level 2:** You choose per line which scale pays
b: Every scoring card in this card's line pays fourteen minus its rank instead of its rank — **level 2:** You choose per line which scale pays
c: Every scoring card pays whichever is larger of its rank and fourteen minus its rank — **level 2:** Cards on matched cells pay both

name: The Jinx
head: Nothing on the board ever gets lucky. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Checks made on matched cells are spared the jinx
a: Every probability check on the board fails; this card gains a permanent step per forced failure
b: Every probability check on this card's grid fails; this card pays a step per forced failure when it scores
c: Every probability check on the board fails while this card is spotlit, and succeeds while it is covered

name: The Achilles' Heel
head: After Superman's Kryptonite: one suit will kill it, and you are not told which. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It is shown the hidden suit
a: A large bonus; a hidden suit is chosen at acquisition, and completing a line of that suit destroys this card
b: A large bonus; a hidden RANK is chosen at acquisition, and scoring it in this card's line destroys this card
c: A large bonus; a hidden suit is chosen each show, and completing a line of that suit exhausts this card for the show

name: The Lantern
head: A light that never goes out
a: Hazard: a status that never clears is applied to one card per refill, and a line may hold at most one lit card to score
b: Hazard: a status that never clears is applied to one card per refill, and lit cards score nothing
c: Hazard: a status that never clears is applied to each card that scores, and a line of five lit cards pays double

name: The Mean
head: The average card is the star. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Cards within one rank of the average count
a: The card whose rank equals its completed line's average rank pays double
b: The card whose rank is closest to its line's average rank pays double
c: Every card whose rank equals its line's average rank gains a permanent step

name: The Narrow Act
head: A huge bonus that variety eats. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Hand types scored through its cell do not shrink it
a: A large flat bonus that shrinks by a fixed amount for every distinct hand type completed this run
b: A large flat bonus that shrinks for every distinct hand type completed this show, and resets each show
c: A large multiplier that shrinks for every distinct suit that has scored this show

name: The Persistence
head: It keeps rolling until it lands. **Level 2, on its own mark:** It pays two steps per reroll
a: Every probability check on the board rerolls until it succeeds; this card pays a step per reroll it took
b: Every probability check on this card rerolls until it succeeds, and the card is exhausted for the refill afterwards
c: Every probability check on the board rerolls once on failure

name: The Ratchet
head: Every gain adds a rule. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Breaking a ban through its cell costs nothing
a: Each time it scores it gains a permanent multiplier and bans the suit of the card that completed that line; a banned suit scoring resets both
b: Each time it scores it gains a permanent multiplier and bans the hand type just completed; breaking a ban resets both
c: Each time it scores it gains a permanent multiplier and bans one rank; breaking a ban destroys this card

name: The Reset Button
head: Back to the way it was printed
a: Consumable: revert one card to its printed rank, suit, type, stamp and skill, erasing all growth and decay
b: Consumable: revert one card's rank and suit to their printed values, keeping its modifiers
c: Consumable: revert every card on one grid to its printed identity

name: The Set List Card
head: It demands a suit, and the suit changes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may name the suit instead of advancing
a: Names a suit each show, advancing through the suits in order; complete a line of it or this card is destroyed at show end
b: Names a suit each show, advancing in order; completing a line of it pays a large bonus, missing it pays nothing
c: Names a suit each show, advancing in order; completing a line of it gains a permanent step, missing it loses one

name: The Silver Lining
head: A debuff is a costume
a: Any debuffed card on the board counts as wild for melds — **level 2:** Debuffed cards count as wild for suit matching too
b: Any debuffed card on the board counts as wild for melds, and the debuff clears when it scores — **level 2:** Debuffed cards count as wild for suit matching too
c: Any card a hazard suppresses retriggers its line instead of scoring nothing — **level 2:** A suppressed card on a matched cell scores as well as retriggering

name: The Trophy
head: It keeps a piece of every boss it beat. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The rule may be invoked twice a show
a: After a hazard show is won, cue once in any later show: that hazard's rule applies to the grid for one Entrance refill, and every line completed under it pays double
b: As (a), for the next show only
c: As (a), and each invocation adds +1 combo

name: The Unreliable Programme
head: A preview with one lie in it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** You may reveal the lie once per show
a: Reveals the next five cards of a named stock, exactly one of which is false
b: Reveals the next five cards of a named stock, each with a one-in-three chance of staying hidden
c: Reveals the next five cards of every stock, with one false card per stock

name: The Warmer, Colder
head: A secret cell, and you feel your way to it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The hidden cell is always one whose mark this card matches
a: A hidden cell is chosen each show; this card pays more the fewer cells it sits from it, and full only on it
b: A hidden cell is chosen each show; every card pays a step more the closer it sits to it
c: A hidden cell is chosen each show and revealed the first time a card is placed orthogonally next to it; a card on it pays triple

name: The Zigzag
head: Odd, even, odd, even. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A card on a matched cell counts as either parity
a: Gains a multiplier per consecutive card in a completed line whose rank parity flips from the one before
b: A line whose ranks alternate parity all the way along pays double
c: Gains a multiplier per consecutive card in a completed line whose suit differs from the one before, and double if the line uses only two suits, alternating

name: The Acid Bath
head: What leaves the board comes back blank
a: Hazard: any card that leaves the board loses its rank and suit
b: Hazard: any card that leaves the board takes a corrupted type that scores nothing
c: Hazard: any card that leaves the board loses its stamp and type

name: The Checkerboard
head: Half the board is awake at a time
a: Hazard: cards on even cells are live for one line completion, cards on odd cells for the next, alternating
b: Hazard: cards on even cells are live during odd-numbered Entrance refills, cards on odd cells during even ones
c: Hazard: only cards on cells matching the colour of the last placed cell are live

name: The Cooling Rank
head: The rank that just scored is spent
a: Hazard: the rank that most recently completed a line scores nothing until the next line completes
b: Hazard: the rank that most recently completed a line may not be placed until the next line completes
c: Hazard: the SUIT that most recently completed a line scores nothing until the next line completes

name: The Creeping Ban
head: Every line completed bans one more rank
a: Hazard: each completed line debuffs the next rank in order from Ace, so the banned set widens as you score
b: Hazard: each completed line debuffs the highest rank not yet debuffed
c: Hazard: each completed line debuffs one random rank

name: The Crowded Rank
head: Your commonest rank and its neighbours are off
a: Hazard: the rank you own most of, and the ranks one above and below it, are debuffed
b: Hazard: the rank you own most of is debuffed, re-read at each refill
c: Hazard: the suit you own most of is debuffed

name: The Dimming
head: Every suit that scores goes dark
a: Hazard: once a suit has scored this show, its cards are dealt face down for the rest of it
b: Hazard: every card carrying a type is dealt face down
c: Hazard: once a rank has scored this show, its cards are dealt face down for the rest of it

name: The Favoured Axis
head: The line kind you lean on stops paying
a: Hazard: the line kind (row, column, diagonal, height) completed most this show scores nothing until another kind overtakes it
b: Hazard: when a line of the kind completed most this show completes, its cards are discarded
c: Hazard: nothing scores until a line of the kind completed LEAST this show completes

name: The Fixed Odds
head: Nothing is rolled tonight
a: Hazard: no probability check rolls; every chance-based effect pays a flat step instead
b: Hazard: no probability check rolls; every chance-based effect simply fails
c: Hazard: no probability check rolls; every chance-based effect succeeds, at half strength

name: The Fresh Bill
head: Nothing from the last line may return
a: Hazard: a line may not share any rank with the previous completed line, except in the cell where the two cross, or it scores nothing
b: Hazard: a line may not share its hand type with the previous completed line, or it scores nothing
c: Hazard: a line that shares a rank with the previous completed line, the crossing cell excepted, scores half

name: The Kinship Rule
head: Only next to your own kind
a: Hazard: a card may only be placed orthogonally adjacent to a card sharing its suit or rank, or in an empty grid
b: Hazard: a card may only be placed orthogonally adjacent to a card sharing its suit
c: Hazard: a card may only be placed orthogonally adjacent to a card sharing its rank, or in an empty grid

name: The Locked Column
head: A column with a key
a: Hazard: two columns start locked; each opens once the two cells beside it in the neighbouring columns are filled
b: Hazard: two columns start locked; each opens once a line completes through the cell beside it
c: Hazard: one column starts locked and opens when a card of a named rank is placed anywhere

name: The Monotone Crowd
head: This audience hates variety
a: Hazard: the multiplier is divided by the number of distinct ranks on the board
b: Hazard: the multiplier is divided by the number of distinct suits on the board
c: Hazard: each line's multiplier is divided by the number of distinct ranks in it

name: The Neglected Rank
head: Bring the one you have been ignoring
a: Hazard: a line scores only if it holds the rank that has scored least this show
b: Hazard: a line scores only if it holds the suit least represented across the stocks
c: Hazard: a line scores double if it holds the rank that has scored least this show, and nothing otherwise

name: The One-Use Costume
head: A modifier works once
a: Hazard: a card's type and stamp are stripped after they score once
b: Hazard: a card's stamp is stripped after it scores once
c: Hazard: a card's type and stamp are stripped after they score once, and this pays a step per stripping

name: The Plain Clothes Ban
head: No costume, no pay
a: Hazard: a card with no type, stamp or skill scores nothing
b: Hazard: a card with no type, stamp or skill scores nothing, and a modified card scores double
c: Hazard: a line holding no modified card scores nothing

name: The River
head: Two banks, a boat, and a rule about who may be left together
a: Hazard: the grid is split into two halves; you may place only on the half you stand on, placing on the far half crosses you over, and a half may never hold two more cards of the named suit than of any other suit or the show is lost
b: Hazard: the grid is split into two halves; you may place only on the half you stand on, and every placement crosses you over
c: Hazard: a half may never hold two more cards of the named suit than of any other suit, or every card of that suit on that half is discarded

name: The Single Take
head: No second go
a: Hazard: every retrigger effect is disabled for the show
b: Hazard: every retrigger effect fires at most once per show
c: Hazard: every retrigger effect is disabled, and every card that would have been retriggered pays a flat step instead

name: The Sudden Death
head: Every placement must complete a line
a: Hazard: a placement is legal only if it completes a line, once the grid holds ten cards
b: Hazard: a placement that completes no line discards the placed card
c: Hazard: once the grid holds ten cards, three placements in a row that complete no line end the show

name: The Understudy Ban
head: No two of the same act
a: Hazard: of identical cards on the board, only the first placed keeps its talent
b: Hazard: of cards sharing a talent on the board, only the first placed keeps it
c: Hazard: a card identical to one already on the board may not be placed

name: The Veteran's Card
head: Only the cards that have been through the discard still work
a: Hazard: every card's talent is suppressed unless that card has passed through the discard pile at least once
b: Hazard: every card's talent is suppressed until that card has scored once this show
c: Hazard: every card's talent is suppressed unless that card has been moved at least once this show

name: The Weight Limit
head: Too heavy a line scores nothing
a: Hazard: a line whose ranks sum above a stated limit scores nothing
b: Hazard: a line whose ranks sum above a stated limit scores nothing, and the limit drops each refill
c: Hazard: a line whose ranks sum BELOW a stated floor scores nothing

name: The Circuit
head: Power runs through the cards
a: Cards of this type carry connectors on some sides; a card is powered only when linked through touching connectors to a King, and an unpowered card scores nothing
b: Cards of this type carry connectors; a completed line of powered cards pays double
c: Cards of this type carry connectors; every card in one powered network is retriggered when any of them scores

name: The Enclosure
head: Walls pay only when they close
a: Cards of this type are walls: a closed loop of walls pays a step per cell it encloses, and an open loop pays nothing
b: Cards of this type are walls: a closed loop of walls doubles every line inside it
c: Cards of this type are walls: a closed loop of walls protects every card inside it from hazards

name: The Garden Plot
head: Each suit grows in its own shape. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Harvested cards return to the Entrance instead of leaving
a: Cards of one suit arranged in that suit's shape (Hoop a ring of four, Knife a row of three, Ball a column of three, Fire an L, Firework two cells apart on a diagonal) with an average rank of seven are harvested: they score as a flush of their count into the special bucket and leave the board
b: Cards of one suit arranged in that suit's named shape are harvested, whatever their ranks
c: Any four cards of one suit in a two-by-two block with an average rank of seven are harvested

name: The Production Line
head: Raw, refined, consumed. Its tokens are ghosts: they leave the deck when the show ends
a: Three cards form a chain: when the first scores it makes a token; a token reaching the second is converted; the third consumes converted tokens for points — **level 2:** A chain card on its mark converts two tokens at once
b: Two cards form a chain: when the first scores it makes a token, and the second consumes tokens for points — **level 2:** The consumer on its mark pays double per token
c: Three cards form a chain along a row, and the chain pays only when all three score in the same refill — **level 2:** A chain through its cell may complete across two refills

name: The Rail Line
head: Everything on the line is next to everything else
a: Cards of this type are rails: every card touching one connected rail chain counts as adjacent to every other card touching it
b: Cards of this type are rails: a card touching a rail chain counts as a member of every line the chain crosses
c: Cards of this type are rails: a prop reaching a rail follows the whole chain

name: The Bullseye Streak
head: Consecutive hits build a streak that the next line cashes. **Level 2, on its own mark:** A miss in its own lines does not reset the streak
a: Each placement that lands a card on a mark it matches adds +1 to a streak; the next line to score adds the streak to its multiplier and spends it, and a miss resets it
b: As (a), but the streak survives one miss before it resets
c: As (a), but the streak is not cashed until it breaks, and then it pays its square as flat points

name: The Echo Mark
head: A hit copies its mark to a second cell, making a new target
a: When a card hits its mark, that mark is copied onto the mirrored cell across the grid's centre, if it is empty — **level 2:** It is also copied onto the cell mirrored across its row
b: When a card hits its mark, that mark is copied onto an empty cell beside it of your choice — **level 2:** The mark is copied to two cells instead of one
c: When a card hits its mark, that mark is copied onto the next empty cell in its row — **level 2:** The mark is copied to two cells instead of one

name: The Full Set
head: A line where every card hit its mark scores one hand higher. **Level 2, on its own mark:** One card of the line may miss
a: A completed line in which every card sits on a mark it matches scores as the next hand up the ladder
b: A completed line in which every card sits on a mark it matches scores double
c: A completed line in which every card matches its mark on the SAME property scores as the next hand up

name: The Hot Hand
head: Three hits in a row make the next card match anything. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Two hits in a row are enough
a: After three placements in a row that each land on a mark they match, the next card placed counts as matching any mark
b: After three hits in a row, the next card placed counts as matching any mark on one property you name
c: After three hits in a row, every card placed counts as matching its mark until a card is placed on a mark it matches on none of its own properties

name: The Relay Hit
head: Hits in one line pass their bonus down the line. **Level 2, on its own mark:** The relay also passes the first card's level 2 to the second card for that scoring
a: When a card hits its mark, the next card to hit a mark in the same line pays the first card's match bonus as well as its own
b: As (a), but the relay passes along every line through the first card's cell
c: As (a), and the relay keeps passing, growing by one step each time, until a card in that line misses

name: The Triangulation
head: Hits that form a shape fire their marks again. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Diagonal shapes count too
a: When three hits form an L of three cells, all three marks fire their match bonuses again
b: When three hits sit in one line with gaps between them, all three marks fire again
c: When four hits form a two-by-two square, all four marks fire again and the square scores as the best four-card flush or straight it holds, else High Card

name: The Chosen Property
head: You pick which property unlocks the wearer's level 2
a: When placed, name one property - rank, suit, talent or hat; a match on it unlocks the wearer's level 2 — **level 2:** The named property may be changed at each refill
b: When placed, name two properties; a match on either unlocks the wearer's level 2 — **level 2:** The wearer may name three properties
c: When placed, a match on ANY property unlocks the wearer's level 2 — **level 2:** The wearer's level 2 lasts until the next refill, even after it leaves its mark

name: The Contagious Talent
head: Level 2 spreads to the cards around it. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its options are its level 2; at level 1 it does nothing
a: While it is at level 2, cards in its lines that hit their own marks on ANY property fire their level 2, not only on the matching property
b: While it is at level 2, the cards beside it that hit their own marks fire their level 2 on any property
c: While it is at level 2, every card placed during that Entrance refill fires its level 2 on any property it matches

name: The Late Bloomer
head: Nothing at level 1, a lot at level 2. **Level 2, on its own mark:** Its options give both levels
